title: Steelers will put DL Derrick Harmon on injured reserve
summary: The Steelers will be without defensive lineman Derrick Harmon for at least four games.
full_text: The Steelers will be without defensive lineman Derrick Harmon for at least four games. Harmon had to be carted off the field after he suffered a foot injury in last Thursday's loss to the Browns and word over the weekend was that he would miss multiple games . Head coach Mike McCarthy confirmed that on Monday when he said at his press conference that Harmon will be placed on injured reserve. Harmon has 12 tackles, 1.5 sacks, and a forced fumble in four games this season. The Steelers also have Cam Heyward, Keeanu Benton, Sebastian Joseph-Day, Yahya Black, Gabriel Rubio, and Kevin Jobity on the roster at defensive line.
author: Josh Alper

title: Donovan Jackson out with torn meniscus, Christian Darrisaw in concussion protocol
summary: The Vikings remain undefeated at 4-0, but they will have to deal with some injuries along their offensive line.
full_text: '' The Vikings remain undefeated at 4-0, but they will have to deal with some injuries along their offensive line. Head coach Kevin O'Connell told reporters in his Monday press conference that left guard Donovan Jackson suffered a torn meniscus and will likely miss the rest of the regular season. Jackson is set to undergo surgery to repair the injury. O'Connell also noted that left tackle Christian Darrisaw is in the concussion protocol after Sunday's win over Miami. But tight end Ben Yurosek and offensive lineman Michael Jurgens are set to return to practice this week. Both players are currently on injured reserve. The Vikings will be on the road to play the Saints on Sunday.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Jesse Minter unsure of Lamar Jackson's availability for Week 5 vs. Falcons
summary: Minter told reporters that the team is still gathering information on the ankle injury Jackson suffered during Sunday's win over the Titans.
full_text: '' Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson had to exit Sunday’s win over the Titans with an ankle injury. Will he be on the field for the Week 5 matchup with the Falcons? “ I don’t know the chances yet ,” head coach Jesse Minter said in his Monday press conference. “We’re still gathering a lot of the information, imaging, things like that. Just dealing with a little bit of an ankle. We’ll kind of see where that shakes out. “Full trust and confidence in him that when it’s ready to roll, that we’ll roll, and go from there.” The Ravens may still be gathering information. But if Jackson is going to miss time, it sounds like it won’t be much. “I really don’t think it’s going to be crazy long term,” Minter said. “But, we’ll see what happens.” Jackson departed Sunday’s game after he suffered the injury on a sack late in the second quarter. Before his exit, he had completed 15-of-20 passes for 222 yards with two touchdowns. PFT reported on Sunday night that Jackson is believed to be week-to-week . He departed the stadium in a walking boot. In four games this season, Jackson has completed 70.8 percent of his throws for 967 yards with six touchdowns and one interception. He leads the league in yards per attempt (10.1) and yards per completion (14.2). Tyler Huntley would be in line to start if Jackson is unavailable. Additionally, Minter noted that he didn’t have updates on Durham Smythe, Andrew Vorhees, or Marlon Humphrey. The Ravens’ first injury report of the week will be released on Wednesday.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Bengals call Tee Higgins day-to-day with adductor injury
summary: The Bengals saw their top two receivers leave Sunday's 22-17 loss to the Jaguars with injuries and it's unclear if either one of them will be back for Week 5.
full_text: The Bengals saw their top two receivers leave Sunday's 22-17 loss to the Jaguars with injuries and it's unclear if either one of them will be back for Week 5. Head coach Zac Taylor told reporters on Monday that Tee Higgins is considered day-to-day after suffering an adductor injury late in Sunday's game. Higgins had 11 catches for 157 yards before his injury. One of the reasons that Higgins saw so many targets was the absence of Ja'Marr Chase, who left the game in the second quarter. Chase has been diagnosed with a concussion and will need to clear concussion protocol before he will be able to return to action. The 2-2 Bengals will be in Miami next weekend and they have a bye in Week 6.
author: Josh Alper

title: Robert Saleh: Cam Ward is going to be a damn good quarterback
summary: Saleh called Sunday's loss to the Ravens the best game Ward has played this year.
full_text: '' Titans head coach Robert Saleh says his team has its franchise quarterback in place. Asked if the coaching staff is confident in Cam Ward, Saleh insisted that Ward has already shown significant growth and is going to continue developing. "We have the utmost confidence in Cam," Saleh said. "We really do. I'm not trying to stand up here and show strength. The kid's gonna be a damn good quarterback. Everyone just needs to take a deep breath and let him grow. If you can't objectively sit down and watch tape and look at him from Week 1 of last year to Week 1 of this year to Week 4 yesterday, and not see improvement, and a young man who's trending in the right direction, then you're just being biased to your own opinion." In Sunday's loss to the Ravens, Ward completed 20 of 31 passes for 222 yards, with one touchdown and one interception. He also ran for 27 yards. Saleh was pleased. "I do think it was the best game he's played this year. When you look at it as a whole, he made a lot of plays with his feet, a lot of plays off schedule, did a good job hanging in the pocket," Saleh said. "I thought he did a lot of good things and he's done a nice job building off the positives that we've had each week." Ward has started all 21 games since the Titans took him with the first overall pick in last year's draft, and the Titans are 3-18 in those games. At some point, the Titans need Ward to play winning football. Saleh is confident he will, eventually.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Antoine Winfield Jr. out 2-4 weeks with rib fracture
summary: Already facing the challenge of a short week, the Buccaneers have yet another injury to a key player entering Week 5.
full_text: '' Already facing the challenge of a short week, the Buccaneers have yet another injury to a key player entering Week 5. Head coach Todd Bowles told reporters in his Monday press conference that safety Antoine Winfield Jr. has a fractured rib that will keep him out for 2-to-4 weeks. A Pro Bowler last season, Winfield has registered 24 total tackles and one QB hit so far in 2026. He finished last season with eight passes defensed, two interceptions, a sack, and four tackles for loss. Bowles also noted that linebacker SirVocea Dennis is still undergoing tests on his ankle injury to determine its severity. Tampa Bay will be on the road to face Dallas on Thursday night. The team’s first injury report will be released later on Monday.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Texans opening practice window for Tank Dell
summary: Texans wide receiver Tank Dell is getting closer to a return.
full_text: Texans wide receiver Tank Dell is getting closer to a return. Houston head coach DeMeco Ryans said today that he expects to open the 21-day practice window for Dell, which suggests that the Texans think Dell could be on the active roster within three weeks. Dell has not played since December of 2024, when he suffered a devastating knee injury. That injury caused him to miss the rest of 2024 and all of 2025, and in training camp this year he had a setback. The Texans picked Dell in the third round of the 2023 NFL draft, and he showed a lot of promise in his first two seasons, with 98 catches for 1,376 yards and 10 touchdowns through his first 25 career games before the injury. Whether he'll ever be back to full speed remains to be seen, but the struggling Texans would love to see him making plays in their offense again. Ryans said the Texans are also planning to open the practice windows for offensive tackle Braden Smith and defensive tackle Kayden McDonald.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Mike Vrabel: Efton Chism III has earned more opportunities
summary: On Sunday, OBJ met EC3.
full_text: On Sunday, OBJ met EC3. And the stellar, game-winning catch made by Patriots receiver Efton Chism III will result in more chances to make more next-level grabs. "Sure, of course," coach Mike Vrabel told reporters on Monday regarding whether Chism has earned more opportunities. "That's what happens. I mean, guys continue to take advantage of their opportunities, they get more opportunities. I mean, we've been finding ways to work Chis in there previously. And it's a balance, but he certainly did a lot of things well. I know that he'll continue to do things well for us and continue to know a bunch of different spots." On Sunday, Chism was on the field for 34 offensive snaps. Targeted four times, he had two catches for 42 yards, including the 23-yard clincher. In Week 1 against the Seahawks, Chism was inactive. In Week 2 vs. the Steelers, Chism had 10 snaps; he was targeted once, for minus-2 yards. In Week 3 at the Jaguars, Chism had 16 snaps. He had one catch on two targets, for one yard. So he has already been earning more work, one game at a time. And it looks like Chism will get even more. Which means that, contrary to the prediction from Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson, we probably will hear from him again .
author: Mike Florio

title: All five 0-3 teams fell to 0-4
summary: Sunday started with five 0-3 teams in the NFL.
full_text: Sunday started with five 0-3 teams in the NFL. It will end with five 0-4 teams in the NFL. Each of the winless teams lost again on Sunday — the Dolphins, the Titans, the Texans, the Chargers, and the Buccaneers. Only one team has ever recovered from 0-4 to make the playoffs. The Chargers did it in 1992. The good news is that one of the 0-4 teams is destined to not fall to 0-5. The Titans host the Texans next weekend, in the Something's Gotta Give Bowl. It's a deep hole, for all five winless teams. It helps to have a 17th game and seven playoff spots per conference. For the Chargers and Texans, it's a stunning slide. Both made the playoffs last year, and both were expected to do it again. They still could. Getting that first win would be nice.
author: Mike Florio

title: Another defendant in Terrion Arnold case pleads guilty, agrees to testify
summary: Seahawks cornerback Terrion Arnold remains on paid leave, as he faces eight felony counts arising from an alleged armed robbery and kidnapping.
full_text: Seahawks cornerback Terrion Arnold remains on paid leave, as he faces eight felony counts arising from an alleged armed robbery and kidnapping. A Monday development won't make it any easier for Arnold to defeat the charges. Multiple defendants in the case have previously pleaded guilty and agreed to testify against the remaining defendants. Via Dave Birkett of the Detroit Free Press, Boakai Hilton pleaded guilty on Monday . Under the deal, which results in a 10-year prison term for Hilton, he agreed to testify against Arnold, a first-round pick of the Lions in 2024. A July article regarding the incident characterized Hilton, 23, as a " childhood friend " of Arnold's. Hilton also was the alleged mastermind of the effort to confront the men who were suspected of stealing cash and other property from a house that had been rented by Arnold in Florida. From the moment the news of the initial arrests emerged in February, it seemed obvious that prosecutors would attempt to leverage guilty pleas into evidence against Arnold. With Hilton pleading guilty and agreeing to testify, the prosecution may have everything it needs to make a compelling case against Arnold.
author: Mike Florio

title: Report: Braxton Berrios will be placed on IR with foot injury
summary: The Giants will not have one of their key special teams players for at least the next four weeks.
full_text: ' The Giants will not have one of their key special teams players for at least the next four weeks. Braxton Berrios will be placed on injured reserve, ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports. Berrios suffered a foot injury during Sunday’s victory over the Cardinals. Charlie Jones came in to replace Berrios on punt returns. Tyrone Tracy also returned kicks on Sunday. New York will be on the road to face Washington in Week 4.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Tests confirm Packers LB Edgerrin Cooper tore his Achilles
summary: Packers linebacker Edgerrin Cooper's season is over.
full_text: '' Packers linebacker Edgerrin Cooper's season is over. Head coach Matt LaFleur said after Sunday's win over the Buccaneers that the team believed Cooper tore his Achilles during the game and multiple reports on Monday say that further tests confirmed that is the case. Cooper was having a big day before the injury knocked him out. He had nine tackles, an interception and a sack to help the Packers to a 17-14 victory that evened their record at 2-2. He had 21 tackles and two sacks in the first three weeks of the season. The Packers will have to adjust to Cooper's absence while their defense continues to wait for defensive end Micah Parsons to make his 2026 debut.
author: Josh Alper

title: CBS reporter Aditi Kinkhabwala heard no profanity from Trey McBride
summary: On any given Sunday of NFL games, expect the unexpected.
full_text: On any given Sunday of NFL games, expect the unexpected. Week 4 resulted in an unexpected exchange between line judge Jeff Seeman and Cardinals tight end Trey McBride. It happened after a non-call of pass interference late in the Cardinals-Giants game. It looked like a fairly clear foul. McBride made his case to Seeman. And while the cameras and microphones captured nothing McBride said, a CBS camera on the sidelines showed Seeman apparently saying to McBride, "Fuck you." Twice. NFL Players Association executive director JC Tretter issued a statement calling Seeman's behavior " unacceptable " and expressing hope that the league will hold the officials to the same standard that is applied to the players. Via Sam Neumann of Awful Announcing , CBS reporter Aditi Kinkhabwala witnessed the interaction. She heard no profanity from McBride. “I was standing right there,” Kinkhabwala said on Twitter. “What’s wild is that it all started with Trey McBride saying ‘please’ when pleading his case for a PI flag. He was heated for sure, but I never heard a curse from him. The harshest he got was, ‘You’re ruining the game.'” It was a bad call, to be sure. The latest in a recent epidemic of erroneous calls and non-calls of pass interference. The point is that, as players, coaches, and officials interact after such decisions are made, certain lines shouldn't be crossed. If McBride had said to Seeman what Seeman apparently said to McBride, there surely would have been consequences. During the Fail Mary misadventure of 2012, the NFL issued multiple fines to coaches for their conduct toward replacement officials. The league has said it will review the situation. There's not much that needs to be reviewed, however. The eye in the sky doesn't lie, and it doesn't take extensive lip-reading skills to understand what Seeman said to McBride.
author: Mike Florio

title: Marcus Mariota suffered MCL sprain on Sunday
summary: If Jayden Daniels is not ready to play in Week 5, rookie Athan Kaliakmanis may get more playing time.
full_text: If Jayden Daniels is not ready to play in Week 5, rookie Athan Kaliakmanis may get more playing time. According to Jeremy Fowler of ESPN, quarterback Marcus Mariota suffered an MCL sprain during Sunday’s loss to the Colts. Mariota previously suffered an MCL sprain during the preseason. Mariota went down during the first quarter of Sunday’s game in London and was not able to return. That came after Mariota was able to beat the defending-champion Seahawks in Week 3. In his three appearances with two starts this season, Mariota has completed 64.7 percent of his passes for 340 yards with four touchdowns and no interceptions. Kaliakmanis completed 15-of-33 passes for 186 yards with a touchdown and an interception on Sunday. As PFT reported on Sunday night, the Commanders are hopeful that Daniels will be able to play in Sunday’s game against the Giants. But practice participation will be a key factor in Daniels’ return from a dislocated left elbow. Daniels was limited in practice on Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday last week.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Report: Rashawn Slater believed to have a high-ankle sprain
summary: The Chargers saw left tackle Rashawn Slater get hurt in Sunday's loss to the Seahawks and the 0-4 team is reportedly set to be without him for a while.
full_text: The Chargers saw left tackle Rashawn Slater get hurt in Sunday's loss to the Seahawks and the 0-4 team is reportedly set to be without him for a while. Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports that the belief is that Slater suffered a high-ankle sprain. He'll have an MRI to confirm that diagnosis and he will likely miss multiple weeks if the team gets that confirmation. Slater missed all of the 2025 season with a torn patellar tendon and he missed most of the 2022 season with a torn biceps, so the Chargers have experience playing without him. They were also missing right tackle Joe Alt for most of last season and Alt suffered a neck injury on Sunday, so climbing out of the early hole they've dug themselves this season is not shaping up to be an easy task.
author: Josh Alper

title: Tyson Bagent is expected to start Week 5 vs. Packers
summary: Ben Johnson isn't going to play the, "Who's going to start?"
full_text: ' Ben Johnson isn't going to play the, "Who's going to start?" game this week. In a radio interview with ESPN 1000 Chicago on Monday, Johnson said Tyson Bagent will start at quarterback in the team's Week 5 matchup with the Packers. " Tyson will be the guy ," Johnson said, via Kevin Fishbain of TheAthletic.com. "We'll go from there. We're in good shape." Bagent technically was not the starter on Sunday, as Case Keenum took the first snap in a cheeky move from Johnson. But it was Bagent’s show the rest of the way, as he completed 25-of-34 passes for 268 yards with an interception. Caleb Williams is dealing with a hamstring injury suffered during the Week 2 loss to the Vikings. He has been considered week-to-week. In 14 career games with five starts, Bagent has completed 67.2 percent of his passes for 1,239 yards with three touchdowns and seven interceptions.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Broncos WR Pat Bryant is expected to miss time with sprained ankle
summary: The Broncos had a pair of players leave Sunday's loss to the 49ers with ankle injuries, but early word on both is that they avoided serious injuries.
full_text: The Broncos had a pair of players leave Sunday's loss to the 49ers with ankle injuries, but early word on both is that they avoided serious injuries. According to multiple reports, wide receiver Pat Bryant suffered a sprained ankle when he went down in the second half. Bryant is expected to miss a few weeks with the injury, but should be back to contribute to the team. Cornerback Pat Surtain II had the other ankle injury and reports are that he will also avoid a long-term absence . In addition those injuries, the Broncos also saw cornerback Riley Moss go down with injured ribs.
author: Josh Alper

title: Steelers sign CB Sean Murphy-Bunting off Bucs practice squad
summary: After the Steelers traded Joey Porter Jr. to the Cowboys, help is on the way for Pittsburgh’s secondary.
full_text: After the Steelers traded Joey Porter Jr. to the Cowboys, help is on the way for Pittsburgh’s secondary. Per Tom Pelissero of Netflix, the Steelers are signing cornerback Sean Murphy-Bunting off of the Buccaneers’ practice squad. Murphy-Bunting, 29, missed the 2025 season with a torn ACL. He had returned to the Buccaneers after he was released by the Cardinals at roster cuts in August. A second-round pick in 2019, Murphy-Bunting has appeared in 82 career games with 65 starts. In 2024, he registered 52 total tackles with three interceptions, five passes defensed, and two forced fumbles in 15 games for the Cardinals. He has 34 career passes defensed with 11 career interceptions.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Report: Kyle Juszczyk could miss a couple of weeks with knee injury
summary: 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk had to leave Sunday's win over the Broncos with a knee injury, but early indications are that he will avoid a long absence from the lineup.
full_text: 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk had to leave Sunday's win over the Broncos with a knee injury, but early indications are that he will avoid a long absence from the lineup. Head coach Kyle Shanahan said after the game that Juszczyk's ACL and other ligaments appeared to be intact. Adam Schefter of ESPN reports that initial tests showed that Juszczyk hyperextended his knee and that he is expected to miss a couple of weeks, but still needs to have an MRI to confirm that belief. Any missed time for Juszczyk would force Shanahan and the 49ers to alter some offensive plans, but they've become adept at that this year and in past years due to an extended run of injuries across the roster. Juszczyk had two catches for 28 yards Sunday and he has four catches for 55 yards and a touchdown this season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Klint Kubiak on taking made FG off the board: I don't regret it, I regret not getting a first down
summary: In the third quarter of Las Vegas’ matchup against Kansas City on Sunday, Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak made a choice.
full_text: In the third quarter of Las Vegas’ matchup against Kansas City on Sunday, Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak made a choice. Matt Gay had sent a 41-yard field goal through the uprights, making the score 16-10, Las Vegas. But the Chiefs had lined up with too many players on one side of the ball for an illegal formation. So, Kubiak elected to accept the penalty and go for it on fourth-and-2 from Kansas City’s 18. But the problem was the Raiders didn’t convert, as Kirk Cousins’ pass to Ashton Jeanty was broken up and fell incomplete. While the Raiders ended up losing 30-27, that choice to take three points off the board was far from the only reason for the ultimate result. “[O]bviously, there's a point there where I took three points off the board, and we were going to be aggressive going into the game,” Kubiak said postgame. “I don't regret it. I regret not getting it.” Kubiak later reiterated that he knew “we were going to be aggressive, and that was part of the game plan.” The Raiders have played well to get to their 3-1 record on the season, and Kubiak has made some strong coaching choices. Even if this choice didn’t work out, it doesn’t mean that Kubiak should change his process moving forward.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Win over Eagles was Matthew Stafford's 40th career fourth-quarter comeback
summary: The Rams were losing 20-10 to the Eagles in the fourth quarter on Sunday, but anyone who thought the game was over hasn't been watching Matthew Stafford over the years.
full_text: The Rams were losing 20-10 to the Eagles in the fourth quarter on Sunday, but anyone who thought the game was over hasn't been watching Matthew Stafford over the years. Stafford engineered a 10-play, 98-yard touchdown drive and followed that with a 10-play, 79-yard touchdown drive, and the Rams beat the Eagles 24-20. It was the 40th fourth-quarter comeback of Stafford's career, and he said after the game that he and his teammates never doubted that they could pull it out. "If you don't have belief, then what are we doing? That's what we put all this work in for," Stafford said. "We put all the work in Monday through Saturday so that when those instances come up on Sunday, we believe in each other. We understand, this guy has put the work in to do what we do. Not every game is going to go exactly how you want it, sometimes you're going to have to find ways to win football games and that's what we did today. I know I believe in everybody in that huddle." The only other players in NFL history with 40 fourth-quarter comebacks are Tom Brady with 46, Peyton Manning with 43 and Ben Roethlisberger with 41. Stafford had 31 fourth-quarter comebacks with the Lions, and Sunday was his ninth with the Rams. Stafford said those are special moments to share with his teammates. "We'd love to go out there and score every time we touch the ball and stop them three-and-out, and that's just not the case in the NFL," Stafford said. "But coming together as a team, finding a way to figure it out and get a win . . . Just proud of our group, proud of our team."
author: Michael David Smith

title: Tyreek Hill still has an active Personal Conduct Policy investigation
summary: Hill's looming return could move the case back to the front burner.
full_text: Receiver Tyreek Hill could be signing with an NFL team (possibly the Chiefs) very soon. There's an issue beyond the status of his knee that could impact his availability. Per the NFL, Hill remains under an active Personal Conduct Policy review. The investigation was sparked by the divorce filing initiated by his wife, Keeta Vaccaro. She has made specific allegations of domestic violence against Hill. The full details of her contentions came to light in October 2025. Hill's history complicates the situation. Past incidents, including a 2015 guilty plea to domestic assault and battery by strangulation in an incident involving his then-pregnant girlfriend, could result in an enhanced suspension — if the league finds a Personal Conduct Policy violation in connection with Vaccaro's allegations. The league rarely provides a timeline for Personal Conduct Policy investigations. The case almost always remains pending until it suddenly isn't. With Hill not playing, there's less urgency to resolve the situation. If/when he signs with a team, the probe could quickly move back to the front burner.
author: Mike Florio

title: Report: Commanders WR Jaylin Lane fractured, dislocated ankle on Sunday
summary: The ankle injury that knocked Commanders wide receiver Jaylin Lane out of Sunday's loss to the Colts in Europe is reportedly just as severe as it appeared to be on the field.
full_text: The ankle injury that knocked Commanders wide receiver Jaylin Lane out of Sunday's loss to the Colts in Europe is reportedly just as severe as it appeared to be on the field. Lane was carted off the field and ruled out almost immediately after being injured while returning a punt in the third quarter. Lane remained in London on Sunday night for further evaluation and Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports that he sustained both a fracture and a dislocation. Those injuries have been stabilized and Lane is having more tests done before he will return to the United States. The injury is likely a season-ending one for the 2025 fourth-round pick. Lane had two catches for 25 yards, but was playing a bigger role in the return game. He returned a pair of punts for touchdowns as a rookie, but it looks like he will have to wait until 2027 for a shot at adding to that total.
author: Josh Alper

title: Buccaneers coach Todd Bowles could be running out of time to turn things around
summary: The Buccaneers started the 2025 season at 6-2.
full_text: '' The Buccaneers started the 2025 season at 6-2. Since then, they're now 2-11. Sunday's 17-14 loss to the Packers has dropped the Bucs to 0-4. After the game, coach Todd Bowles was asked whether he's the right coach to lead the Buccaneers moving forward, and what he can do to change the recent trend. "I'm the head coach," Bowles told reporters. "I can do more. I can always do more. I'll always take the blame on that." He was then again asked what he can do to change things. "We're gonna fight, we're gonna stick together, and we're gonna figure this thing out, and I'll lead them to that," Bowles said. "That's my job." The good news is that every loss in 2026 has come in a one-score game. The bad news is they've won none of them. "We know what the problem is," Bowles said. "It's on us. We can't keep getting close to not winning. That's not good enough. Our record says what we are. We're 0-and-4, until we acknowledge that and we correct our own mistakes, you know, it's gonna keep happening. We talked about it as a team. We're gonna be a team, and we got to play tougher in the end and we got to execute the end. And that's the only way you can win the ball game." It won't get any easier on Thursday night, with a short-week trip to Dallas. The Cowboys are not easy to beat at home, and Tampa Bay will have an undrafted rookie at quarterback against Dak Prescott and company. Then comes the mini-bye, which provides an opportunity for the Bucs to make a coaching change. There's a benefit to an in-season termination; it gives the team a longer runway to search for the next coach. Working in Bowles's benefit is the fact that there's no clear candidate on his staff to serve as the interim head coach. There's no defensive coordinator. Offensive coordinator Zac Robinson is in his first year with the team, after being fired by the Falcons. The special-teams coordinator is Danny Smith. The Bucs could go outside the organization for an interim hire, like the Colts did in 2022 when Jeff Saturday replaced Frank Reich. Or the Bucs could just ride it out, quietly planning for a new direction in 2027 while allowing the balance of 2026 to play itself out. However it goes, it's not going well in Tampa. After playing the Cowboys, the Bucs face the Steelers, Panthers, Falcons, and Bears before the Week 10 bye. For now, they need to start digging out of the early-season hole. And they'll need to get used to plenty of empty seats for the six remaining home games — unless those otherwise empty seats are filled by fans of the visiting team.
author: Mike Florio

title: Aaron Glenn: Jets history will get brought up, we can't think about it in locker room
summary: The Jets opened the season with an easy win over the Titans, but the last three weeks have not been as pleasant for Aaron Glenn's club.
full_text: ' The Jets opened the season with an easy win over the Titans, but the last three weeks have not been as pleasant for Aaron Glenn's club. After blowing a lead in a painful loss against the Packers at home in Week 2, the Jets lost a close game in Detroit and then got dismantled by the Bears in Chicago on Sunday. The three-game losing streak calls to mind dismal Jets seasons of the past and the head coach was asked after Sunday's loss if he's worried about the roof caving in on his team in the weeks to come. “Well, that's exactly it, we have too many people that want to think about history," Glenn said, via a transcript from the team. "Inside of that locker room, I want our guys not to think about history, because history is going to be brought up so much. And they get it from the outside, just beating down on history so much. We just have to circle the wagons and not let any of that come inside our locker room. We've been working our butts off to change that. But our guys know because everybody's going to bring history in this. It brings so much negativity to us that we have to continue to be positive on what we've been doing. Improving on things, and then the things that we're not doing good at we have to continue improving that. So that's really the focus for us.” Browns head coach Todd Monken had a pointed response to those who brought up his team's own tortured history after a Week 1 loss and Cleveland has now rattled off three straight wins. Coincidentally, they're also next up on the Jets' schedule and Glenn will need to get a win in that game if he really wants to put any notions of another lost Jets season to rest.
author: Josh Alper

title: Kenneth Walker becomes third player ever to rush for at least 170 twice in first four games
summary: Kenneth Walker has obviously been a major piece of Kansas City's offense since signing with the team as a free agent this offseason.
full_text: Kenneth Walker has obviously been a major piece of Kansas City's offense since signing with the team as a free agent this offseason. But his performance in Sunday's win has catapulted his 2026 season into the realm of downright historic. According to NFL Research, Walker became just the third player in NFL history to rush for at least 170 yards twice within his team’s first four games. The other two players to accomplish the feat are Hall of Famers Jim Brown and O.J. Simpson. Notably, Brown (1958 and 1963) and Simpson (1973 and 1975) both did it twice. As for Walker, he put up 173 yards rushing in the Week 1 win over Denver and had 179 yards rushing in Sunday’s victory over the Raiders. He also had the league’s longest run of the year so far with his 76-yard scamper in the second half. Walker leads the NFL with 537 yards rushing, 6.2 yards per carry, and 621 total yards from scrimmage. While he isn’t No. 1 in carries, he’s close. Baltimore’s Derrick Henry has 89, while Walker has 87. Walker and the rest of the Chiefs will get a break in the coming days with a Week 5 bye.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Brock Purdy has thrown 113 passes, and still hasn't been sacked
summary: 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy has put up some impressive numbers this season, including leading the NFL with a 126.2 passer rating and 11 touchdown passes.
full_text: 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy has put up some impressive numbers this season, including leading the NFL with a 126.2 passer rating and 11 touchdown passes. But Purdy's most impressive number may be zero. That's how many times Purdy has been sacked this season: Despite throwing 113 passes, Purdy still hasn't been sacked. Every quarterback other than Purdy who has started all four games has been sacked at least five times this season. Purdy is the first quarterback since Peyton Manning with the 2005 Colts to start the first four games of the season and not get sacked in any of them. Up next for the 49ers is a game in Seattle against the Seahawks, who sacked Purdy three times the last time the teams met. Whether the Seahawks can do what other defenses haven't and sack Purdy will go a long way toward determining who wins the game — and who wins the NFC West.
author: Michael David Smith

title: NFL reviewing incident between Vikings' Eric Wilson and ref Adrian Hill
summary: An odd incident took place during Sunday's Vikings-Dolphins game when referee Adrian Hill got knocked to the ground and then got in the face of Vikings linebacker Eric Wilson.
full_text: An odd incident took place during Sunday's Vikings-Dolphins game when referee Adrian Hill got knocked to the ground and then got in the face of Vikings linebacker Eric Wilson. The NFL is reviewing the matter , according to ESPN. On the play in question, Dolphins running back Ollie Gordon was blocking Wilson after the play had been blown dead, pushing Wilson into Hill and knocking Hill down. Hill got up, got in Wilson's face, yelled at him and pointed him back to his huddle. Hill did not throw a flag, but many people watching the game thought Hill overreacted by yelling at Wilson. Wilson said after the game that he thought it was no big deal. "That was funny, honestly," Wilson said. "I ended up apologizing to him and explained the situation. He was cool about it. He understood what was going on. He just said he didn't want us fighting, me and [Gordon]. He said he was just trying to break us up." The altercation between Wilson and Hill was one of a few between players and officials on Sunday. Official Jeff Seeman appeared to shout obscenities at Cardinals tight end Trey McBride, and Patriots coach Mike Vrabel was flagged for using an obscenity toward an official.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Drew Rosenhaus: Tyreek Hill could sign with a team this week
summary: A return to the Chiefs could be in the cards for the wide receiver.
full_text: Wide receiver Tyreek Hill could be back in the NFL very soon. Hill's agent Drew Rosenhaus told ESPN that he plans to begin negotiations with teams about a contract for the wideout. Rosenhaus added that he does not expect it to take a long time for those talks to lead to an agreement. “I would anticipate Tyreek potentially signing with a team over the next few days,” Rosenhaus said. One of the teams that Rosenhaus is expected to be talking to is the Chiefs. Word on Sunday was that they have already reached out to show their interest in a reunion with Hill and their urgency to get something done went up when Tyquan Thornton dislocated his ankle during Sunday's win over the Raiders. Hill spent his first six seasons with the Chiefs and was a three-time first-team All-Pro while helping the team win the first of three Super Bowls under head coach Andy Reid. He was traded to Miami ahead of the 2022 season, but could be back with the Chiefs in the near future.
author: Josh Alper

title: Eagles' offense sputters with 68 net passing yards, 0-12 on third down vs. Rams
summary: The boo birds flew early and often in Philly on Sunday, thanks to an offense that couldn't get off the ground.
full_text: The boo birds flew early and often in Philly on Sunday, thanks to an offense that couldn't get off the ground. The final tally from Sunday's loss to the Rams: 172 total yards, 68 net yards passing, and 0-for-12 on third down. Over the last two games, the Eagles have converted only two of 21 third-down opportunities. After the loss to L.A., Eagles coach Nick Sirianni was asked whether the problems are a result of execution, play-calling, or scheme. "Obviously, everybody contributed to that," Sirianni told reporters. "Everybody. So, there's execution errors, there's coaching errors. Everybody contributes to it. It's an ultimate team game. You can't sustain drives and do the things that you want. Some of our problems offensively has been [that] we've been behind, but it wasn't quite the same case today where we were in second-and-long and all those different things. It was more we couldn't convert on third down for multiple different reasons. So again, there's always a lot of contributors to that. I need to go watch the tape before I react to anything. But I know when you're 0-for-whatever we were today, everybody has a hand in that. Our job is to figure out what happened and get better from it and not assign blame. That's what we'll be doing." Injuries had something to do with that. The Eagles didn't have receiver Devonta Smith or tight end Dallas Goedert. Right tackle Lane Johnson was a late scratch. Running back Saquon Barkley injured his hamstring on his only carry of the game. Quarterback Jalen Hurts didn't blame injuries. Or play-calling. Or scheme. “Poor execution," he said regarding the offensive effort, particularly in the second half. "Poor execution. Yeah, poor execution.” He was later asked what he means by "poor execution." "It's just you're finding your flow collectively as a unit," Hurts said. "I think it comes down to finding a flow, finding a rhythm as a unit, as a group, and going out there and executing at a higher level. We didn't do that today.” The next chance to do it comes in six days, in London. Against the 3-1 Jaguars. While the season isn't yet on the brink, it's clear that the Eagles aren't the team they've been in recent seasons. They're currently not dominant. They're currently not elite. They've got the Panthers and the Cowboys after the trip to England, followed by the Commanders and the Giants. The Eagles need to win at least three of the next five before their Week 10 bye. If they finish the first nine games at 4-5, 3-6, or 2-7, it could be very hard to get back to the playoffs. Even if they do, the 2026 Eagles don't look like a team that can make a climb up the playoff tree.
author: Mike Florio

title: Saints vs. Falcons prediction: Michael Penix Jr. leads Atlanta into New Orleans
summary: The NFC South rivals meet Monday night in New Orleans as Michael Penix Jr. and the Falcons look to build on their first win of the season
full_text:
In the Week 4 edition of "Monday Night Football," the New Orleans Saints host the Atlanta Falcons .
New Orleans is coming off a loss to the Las Vegas Raiders last week that dropped the Saints to 1-2. The Saints turned the ball over four times in the game and were carved up by Kirk Cousins and Brock Bowers on the other side of the ball. New Orleans lost running back Travis Etienne to injured reserve in that game as well. The Saints are now looking to rebound at home.
Atlanta is coming off its first win of the season, a destruction of the Green Bay Packers in Michael Penix Jr.'s first start of the year. Both Bijan Robinson and Drake London went completely berserk in Green Bay, with 194 yards on the ground and through the air, respectively. The Falcons are looking to get back to .500 after a dreadful start to the year with Cooper Rush filling in under center.
Will the Saints bounce back, or will the Falcons make it two in a row? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game.
The Falcons didn't make a single trip into the red zone in their first two games of the season, and they totaled just 524 yards in those two contests. They then came out in Week 3 and absolutely stomped on the Green Bay defense, piling up 498 yards on "Thursday Night Football" -- 256 through the air and 242 on the ground. They did all that while bouncing back from a game-opening interception by Michael Penix Jr., who was making his first start of the year after returning from his latest knee injury.
The New Orleans defense, meanwhile, has been lit up for over 30 points in two of its three games this season -- 31 by the Lions and 35 by the Raiders. The Saints, though, held the Ravens to 17 points in the other game and have dealt with poor opponents' field position in the two games where they got tagged, thanks to a combined seven turnovers by the offense. New Orleans' opponents have begun their average drive on the 34.8-yard line, the third-closest to the end zone of any team in the league.
The most fascinating matchup to watch in this one might be the one between Falcons wideout Drake London and Saints cornerback Kool-Aid McKinstry . London had just six catches for 80 yards through the first two games of the season with Cooper Rush under center, but he went off for nine catches and 194 yards against Green Bay last week. London has a monster target share in games where Penix has started, and he is clearly the top target for the lefty signal-caller.
McKinstry isn't a corner who just plays one side of the field; his snaps have been split just about equally between left and right cornerback, and I'd probably expect him to follow London whenever he lines up on the perimeter. The Falcons would do well to get London lined up in the slot more often than usual, because McKinstry has yet to play a snap in the slot this season, per Pro Football Focus. Shifting London inside would yield more advantageous matchups.
Of course, Atlanta's offense is still based around Bijan Robinson in the backfield. Robinson is averaging a career-best 5.3 yards per carry this season, thanks in large part to his 29 carries for 194 yards and two touchdowns a week ago. The Falcons have been clocked for an average of 4.7 yards per carry on running-back runs, according to Tru Media, the fourth-worst mark in the NFL.
Tyler Shough led the NFL in completions through the first three weeks of the year. Shough is 91 of 132 (68.9%) for 917 yards (6.9 per attempt), eight touchdowns and three interceptions so far. He's done most of his work in second halves as the Saints have worked to come back from deficits: he's just 32 of 53 for 278 yards, two touchdowns and an interception before the break, while he's 59 of 79 for 639 yards, six touchdowns and two picks after it.
The Falcons rank a surprising first in the league in pressure rate so far this season, generating a sack, hit or hurry on 45.2% of opponent dropbacks, per Tru Media. They were expected to have one of the worst pass rushes in the NFL coming into the year in the absence of both Jalon Walker (injury) and James Pearce Jr . (suspension), but instead, guys like Gervon Dexter (10), Brandon Dorlus (eight), Cameron Thomas (eight) and Samson Ebukam (seven) have been getting after it up front.
The Saints haven't had much in the way of success running the ball, and will be without Travis Etienne hereafter, as he went on injured reserve. Alvin Kamara and Kendre Miller are expected to share the load in the backfield with Etienne out, though CJ Donaldson could mix in as well. Kamara has been extremely inefficient on the ground for several years now, but he's at least a threat as a pass-catcher. Miller has only 140 carries in his career and has averaged south of 4.0 yards per attempt.
The Falcons looked much improved last week against the Packers, thanks in large part to the return of Michael Penix Jr. They hadn't even entered the red zone through the first two weeks of the season, then dropped 35 points on the Packers in Week 3. The Saints, meanwhile, could conceivably be 3-0 right now if not for backbreaking turnovers. They have two one-possession losses, both in games where they turned it over at least three times. If they can avoid giving the ball to the Falcons, I think they can win a close one here.
Prediction: Saints 23, Falcons 20
author: Jared Dubin

title: Caleb Williams to miss Bears' Week 5 rivalry game against Packers, Tyson Bagent set for second start
summary: The Bears are unbeaten without Williams in the starting lineup
full_text:
The Chicago Bears will be without quarterback Caleb Williams for at least one more game. Coach Ben Johnson said Monday on ESPN Chicago that Tyson Bagent "will be the guy" for the Week 5 rivalry game against the Green Bay Packers , which sets him up for his second consecutive start after he guided the Bears to a 23-12 win over the New York Jets on Sunday.
Williams remains on the mend from a hamstring strain and is poised to miss his third consecutive game. He suffered that injury in the Week 2 loss to the Minnesota Vikings , and in his absence, both Bagent and third-string quarterback Case Keenum stepped up to keep the offense rolling. They orchestrated plenty of success in back-to-back victories.
Bagent would have been in line to start against the Philadelphia Eagles in the first Williams-less game, but he spent most of Week 3 in the NFL's concussion protocol, which prompted Johnson to turn to Keenum. Now that Bagent is cleared, though, this is his offense until Williams returns. Chicago signed him to a two-year, $10 million contract extension in the offseason and regards him as a premier backup, so it was unsurprising that Johnson called his name even though Keenum was highly effective starting two games ago.
Bagent completed 25 of 34 passes against the Jets and amassed 268 yards through the air. He did not account for either of the Bears' touchdowns, though, and he threw one interception. Running back Kyle Monangai did the majority of the scoring with his two trips to the end zone on the ground.
"Some good and some that I think he wants back," Johnson said of Bagent's first start of 2026. "It's a little bit of a mixed bag. The best part is how he controlled the operation. I thought we had good tempo in and out of the huddle. I thought our guys played with a lot of confidence because of how he conducted himself. He found completions. I thought he played an efficient football game."
The hamstring strain Williams sustained in the Week 2 loss reportedly comes with a three-to-four-week recovery timeline , so even though the Bears initially labeled him as "week to week," there was always a real chance he would be unavailable for the NFC North battle against the Packers.
If Williams misses the full four weeks, he will also sit against the Atlanta Falcons in Week 6. That would set him up for a potential prime-time return against the New England Patriots on the Week 7 edition of "Thursday Night Football."
author: Carter Bahns

Everyone on the internet loves to overreact to things, and that's especially true when we're talking about the NFL. Personally, I overreact to everything. With that in mind, Zach Pereles decided to take a look at several things that happened during Week 4 to decide if we're all overreacting.
Statement: The Rams shouldn't be Super Bowl favorites. Overreaction or reality: Overreaction. There are two ways to view the Rams' 24-20 win over the injury-ravaged Eagles: "Wow, that was super unimpressive" or "Wow, that was an impressive comeback." It can be both. Los Angeles struggling to beat a Philadelphia team without DeVonta Smith, Saquon Barkley, Quinyon Mitchell, Zack Baun, Lane Johnson, Landon Dickerson and others was a bad look ... for 52-plus minutes. The score will lie about who dominated this game. The Rams had 415 yards of offense and averaged 5.4 yards per play, compared to 172 yards and 3.0 yards per play for Philadelphia. The Rams committed some horrible turnovers and penalties, but on a play-by-play basis, they were far superior. This was a crucial, crucial win, and one that should only prove Los Angeles can win when so much goes wrong.
Statement: The Cowboys will win the NFC East. Overreaction or reality: Reality. Speaking of important wins, the Cowboys just got their most important since the 2023 season: Dallas 34, Houston 30. Statement: Ben Johnson will win Coach of the Year. Overreaction or reality: Overreaction. Ben Johnson should be the frontrunner for Coach of the Year. He's now won games with Caleb Williams, Tyson Bagent and Case Keenum ... and it's only Week 4! According to CBS Sports research, only one other team has had three different quarterbacks throw for 200+ yards in a win through four weeks: the 1997 Jaguars.  Unfortunately for Johnson's Coach of the Year candidacy, the award tends to go to a coach whose team way overachieves. Basically, the external preseason expectations were likely too high for Johnson and the Bears for him to win the award this year, even if you could argue he's been the best coach in the sport so far.

title: NFL Week 4 injury panic meter: Concern for Ja'Marr Chase as Lamar Jackson gets good news
summary: We assess the latest injury news surrounding Lamar Jackson, Ja'Marr Chase, Saquon Barkley and the other prominent players hurt in Week 4
full_text:
Throughout the first month of the 2026 regular season, we were reminded not once, not twice, but by what felt like an avalanche of injuries sweeping over the league. And it's not just the number of injuries that have popped up over the opening month, but it's also been inflicted on some of the biggest names in the league at the most important positions in the sport.
For instance, leading up to Week 4, the NFL had already seen young phenoms like Caleb Williams (hamstring), Jayden Daniels (elbow) and Jaxson Dart (knee) suffer varying degrees of injuries. Meanwhile, Myles Garrett , the defending NFL Defensive Player of the Year and the centerpiece of arguably the biggest trade of the offseason, has yet to play for the Rams on American soil, landing on short-term IR after the opener in Australia due to a knee ailment. Then, there's Baker Mayfield (thumb), Justin Jefferson (ankle), Breece Hall (quad) and De'Von Achane (season-ending ACL tear), among other stars, dealing with injuries as well.
It's truly a who's who when they step into the NFL infirmary, and Week 4 only added to that total.
Below, we're going to highlight some of the biggest names in the NFL who went down with an injury in Week 4, assess their status, and give them a rating on our panic meter.
Panic meter barometer: 🔥🔥🔥 = Fears of a season-ender 🔥🔥 = Could miss a chunk of time 😬😬 = Could miss some time 😅 = Should be fine
The Ravens quarterback left Sunday's win over the Tennessee Titans with an ankle injury sustained just before halftime and was seen leaving M&T Bank Stadium in a walking boot. While Jackson being in a boot isn't exactly ideal for the two-time NFL MVP, it does sound more like a precaution than anything else. NFL Network reported on Monday morning that Jackson will undergo tests late today, but the initial thought is that he's day-to-day, signaling that the ailment doesn't appear to be too serious. Coach Jesse Minter also said that "there were some talks about that," referring to Jackson possibly reentering the game. The fact that it was a discussion about him going back in (even though he didn't) is another signal that Jackson avoided anything substantial.
Week 5 opponent : at Atlanta Falcons
Chase suffered a concussion in the second quarter of Sunday's loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars . After making a catch, the wideout was brought to the ground by his facemask by Jaguars corner Jarrian Jones (which drew a penalty), and he was hit again while being taken down. After sitting on the turf for a moment and being evaluated by the training staff, he was taken into the locker room and did not return. Chase is now in the league's concussion protocol, so he'll have to get over several hurdles this week to play next Sunday. Typically, it's a tight turnaround for a player to suffer a concussion and be back the next week, so there's a chance Chase misses at least a week.
Week 5 opponent : at Miami Dolphins
Higgins suffered an adductor injury during Cincinnati's final drive of the game after making a leaping catch. He stayed on the field for one snap after being hobbled on the reception before exiting. With this being a soft-tissue injury, it does feel like there's a possibility Higgins could miss some time. That said, there's no definitive word on the severity of the injury yet.
Week 5 opponent : at Miami Dolphins
It's been tough sledding for Barkley on the injury front this season. After already dealing with a stinger, the Eagles running back left Sunday's loss to the Rams due to a hamstring injury he suffered in the first quarter. Barkley seemed to pull up after running out of bounds on a carry during Philly's second possession. NFL Network reports that Barkley will undergo testing on Monday, but added that it doesn't appear to be overly serious. That said, as is the case with all soft tissue injuries, they won't know the full extent until they do testing.
Week 5 opponent : vs. Jacksonville Jaguars (in London)
The injuries continued to pile up for Philadelphia. On top of Barkley, All-Pro corner Quinyon Mitchell left the game in the third quarter on Sunday due to a knee injury. Mitchell got tangled up on the sideline while tackling Rams running back Blake Corum and appears to have taken a helmet to the knee. NFL Network reports that the hope is Mitchell hyperextended his knee and may have suffered a bone bruise, but testing on Monday will reveal the severity.
Week 5 opponent : vs. Jacksonville Jaguars (in London)
Mariota has been starting for Washington in place of the injured Jayden Daniels (left elbow), but he couldn't finish Sunday's loss to the Colts in London. The veteran reportedly aggravated his MCL injury and is now undergoing further testing, but he is expected to miss time. There's hope that Daniels will be back next week, but if he's unable to go, it could thrust rookie quarterback Athan Kaliakmanis , who came in under duress for Mariota, into the starter role.
Week 5 opponent : vs. New York Giants
Moore aggravated his shoulder injury in Sunday's loss to the Patriots , but ESPN reports that the injury is not considered to be a long-term issue right now. Head coach Joe Brady didn't give an update on Moore's injury postgame. The wideout, who initially injured the shoulder in Week 2 against the Lions ,  went down in the second quarter during Sunday's matchup. Before this aggravation, Moore didn't miss any time, but has been limited in practice. He'll have some extra time to recuperate as Buffalo plays on Monday night in Week 5.
Week 5 opponent : at Los Angeles Rams
The Packers fear Cooper, their standout linebacker, sustained a torn Achilles in the win over the Buccaneers . Coach Matt LaFleur acknowledged that the injury is "not good" and he'd "suspect" it will be a season-ending injury.
Week 5 opponent : vs. Chicago Bears
The Chiefs receiver was having the game of his life on Sunday against the Raiders , catching five passes for 111 yards and two touchdowns. Unfortunately, he suffered a gruesome ankle injury after making a sensational 55-yard catch and was carted off. Specifically, Thornton suffered a dislocated ankle. They were able to put the ankle back into place, and he did fly back with the team, but he is now out indefinitely. He will undergo an MRI on Monday to see if there is further damage.
Head coach Andy Reid said that Rice tweaked his hamstring in the first quarter and did not return. While the wideout did not get back into the game in Week 4, the injury doesn't sound too severe, with NFL Network characterizing it as a very minor hamstring injury. With Kansas City on the bye in Week 5, it appears that Rice may not miss much, if any, time.
Denver's star corner is expected to miss time with an ankle injury and will undergo further evaluation on Monday, according to NFL Network . At the time when Surtain went down in the second quarter with a non-contact injury, fears of a season-ender were hard to ignore. However, the injury is not as severe as it initially appeared. Surtian is still expected to be sidelined for a period of time -- NFL Network floated a couple of weeks or an IR stint -- but it is not expected to be season-ending, which is good news for the Broncos .
Week 5 opponent : at Los Angeles Chargers
Rashawn Slater left Los Angeles' Week 4 loss to the Seahawks in the fourth quarter due to an ankle injury and did not return. NFL Network reports that the Chargers' star left tackle is believed to have suffered a high ankle sprain based on initial exams. He's slated to undergo an MRI, but this is the type of injury that could leave a player out for several weeks and possibly place them on short-term IR.
Week 5 opponent : vs. Denver Broncos
Chicago will continue to be without Caleb Williams as the former No. 1 overall pick recovers from a hamstring injury he suffered in Week 2 against Minnesota. Head coach Ben Johnson announced on Monday that backup Tyson Bagent is expected to get the start in Week 5, ruling Williams out for another week. The Bears did not…
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: Patriots' Mike Vrabel fires back at Bills' C.J. Gardner-Johnson for jab at Efton Chism III
summary: Gardner-Johnson called Chism a 'practice squad player' and suggested the Patriots receiver could not replicate his spectacular game-winning catch
full_text:
The New England Patriots upset the Buffalo Bills in a key early-season divisional showdown on Sunday and got over the top in the close battle with help from an unlikely source. Wide receiver Efton Chism III secured the game-winning touchdown in the Patriots' 29-26 victory on the biggest play of his young career: A diving, one-handed catch in the end zone with 1:50 to play.
Bills cornerback C.J. Gardner-Johnson brushed off the highlight reception as a fluke. He called Chism a "practice squad player" and said that if the teams were to run that play over again, the wide receiver would not be able to replicate his stellar catch. It should be noted that Chism has been on the Patriots' 53-man roster since signing as an undrafted free agent in 2025.
"We're not going to get into no bulletin board material," Gardner-Johnson said postgame before promptly giving the Patriots plenty of bulletin board material. "An elevated guy made a hell of a catch. Probably won't hear from him again, respectfully. I say that with a lot of confidence, because it's like, he didn't put his confidence in his best player. If that was it, he would've threw it to Doubs or somebody. They won the game. Whatever. They ain't do s--- better than us. We gotta play better."
Patriots coach Mike Vrabel came to Chism's defense with his reaction to Gardner-Johnson's jab. He had a day to concoct the perfect response and delivered it Monday on his weekly radio appearance on WEEI.
"For a guy that's been on eight teams in four years? I guess he knows the drill," Vrabel said of the Bills defender . (For the record, Gardner-Johnson has been with seven teams in his eight-year NFL career, including spending time on the Bears and Ravens practice squads).
New England, for now, has the last laugh thanks to its coach's "mic drop" of a reply. The teams will meet again in Week 13, and Chism will have an opportunity to show Gardner-Johnson that he, in fact, can replicate the dazzling catch.
TOUCHDOWN PATRIOTS. What a catch by Efton Chism III to take the lead! @NEvsBUF on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/DtIZoenYNL
Chism is a second-year professional out of Eastern Washington, where he broke Cooper Kupp's school record for single-season receptions and earned FCS first-team All-American honors as a senior. The Patriots were one of multiple teams to target him as an undrafted free agent, and they kept him around on their active roster following an impressive rookie preseason. Chism made only a couple of appearances in 2025 but displayed his potential in Week 17 when he hauled in his first two career receptions.
With No. 1 receiver A.J. Brown out due to a high ankle sprain, Chism saw action in each of the last three games and made one start. He has four catches on the year for 41 yards and the highlight-reel touchdown.
author: Carter Bahns

title: Dan Campbell 'not talking about' defensive overhaul. Without one Lions are wasting their Super Bowl window
summary: With the defense bottoming out in 2026, Campbell needs to make changes in order to take his team back to the championship conversation
full_text:
Pull a random defensive statistic out of a hat, and there is a solid chance the Detroit Lions rank dead last in the NFL in that metric. Through Week 4, no team surrendered more points or yards than the Lions. This is now the second consecutive year in which Detroit's defense has been a liability, yet coach Dan Campbell is hesitant to make any significant changes to the unit's structure or leadership.
Following the 32-26 loss to the Carolina Panthers on "Sunday Night Football," Campbell admitted that the defense is a glaring issue. But instead of firing second-year coordinator Kelvin Sheppard , shaking up the play-calling duties or doing anything else to reconstruct the defense's framework, Campbell said he wants to "exhaust everything" with the players and coaches he has by his side.
"I'm not talking about all that," Campbell said after the game of a potential leadership change. "I'm talking about getting better right now with what we've got. That's what we're going to do. We're going to find a way to get better with what we've got. There are other things that we can do. We've tweaked a little bit every week here. There's still some things that we can try that we haven't yet to try to settle some things down and see if we can help. It's a work in progress."
None of the adjustments Campbell and his staff have made on the fly over the last year have produced the desired results. Sunday night was just the latest example. Carolina quarterback Bryce Young entered the game as the NFL's leading passer and only padded his advantage over the rest of the league's signal-callers with a 329-yard outing. Wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan enjoyed a career night with 14 catches, 192 yards and two touchdowns. On the ground, Chuba Hubbard racked up 122 yards and a pair of scores.
With each passing week, Detroit shows that no matter how excellent its offense may be, it is always in grave danger of losing. The Panthers, New York Jets , Buffalo Bills and New Orleans Saints each posted at least 24 points against this team. New Orleans tallied 30 in the second half and overtime of the season opener. Still, Campbell and his players stand up for Sheppard.
#Lions LB Jack Campbell on DC Kelvin Sheppard: “Shep works hard. Dan believes in him, I believe in him. He's made of the right stuff. We're going to get this figured out. We've just got to stay the course, stick together. Right now, it's us versus everybody.”
In Sheppard's defense, his personnel is less than fully stocked. The absences of Kerby Joseph and Brian Branch from the safety unit, plus Terrion Arnold's late-offseason departure, are undoubtedly key reasons why the Lions' secondary cannot get off the field. But the front is still full of Pro Bowl talent like Aidan Hutchinson and Jack Campbell .
The issues date back to before those defensive backfield personnel deficiencies, so it is clear that the troubles go much deeper.
Detroit has not been a defensive juggernaut at any point during the Campbell era, but there was a brief period at the height of his tenure where the Lions were nearly as effective at preventing opponents from scoring as they were at putting points on the board themselves. Former defensive coordinator Aaron Glenn built the group from the ground up and turned it into a top-10 unit before his departure to take the Jets' head coaching job.
Since then, it has been nothing but regression. The team as a whole suffered in turn. During Glenn's tenure, the Lions improved their win total every year. In his final season, they went 15-2 and reached the divisional round of the playoffs. Once Sheppard took over, Detroit instantly regressed to 9-8 and missed the postseason, and it is off to a mediocre start to 2026.
The Lions' offense is championship material. A few of the best players in the NFL at their respective positions reside on this unit. Jahmyr Gibbs is perhaps the top running back in the league. Penei Sewell might be the league's most elite tackle. Amon-Ra St. Brown is a top-flight wide receiver. Sam LaPorta is off to a tremendous start to his career at tight end. Holding the unit together is a commendable quarterback in Jared Goff , who logged the seventh 400-yard game of his career and the third of his Lions tenure in Week 4.
Winning shootouts is not a sustainable model, though. That was evident a year ago when the Lions finished just one game above .500. It is clear in 2026 as they open the campaign at 2-2. The offense can keep pace with nearly anyone, but the group on the other side of the ball is putting too much of the burden on Goff and his supporting cast.
There is foundational talent on the defense, too. Hutchinson and Campbell are the kinds of pieces that can anchor a formidable group. They just need more help on the back end and a play-caller who utilizes them more effectively.
Unless the Lions shake up their defensive leadership or make a splash personnel move, the group will continue to weigh down a team that, for so many reasons, should be in the Super Bowl conversation.

title: Travis Kelce closing in on NFL history, could climb to No. 5 on all-time receptions list in coming weeks
summary: Kelce is tied with Tim Brown for seventh in NFL history and needs nine catches to take sole possession of fifth place
full_text:
Kansas City Chiefs star Travis Kelce is already among the greatest tight ends in NFL history, and this week, he made his already impressive resume that much more convincing. Kelce came into Week 4 tied with wideout Tim Brown for the seventh-most receptions in NFL history with 1,094, meaning one catch from quarterback Patrick Mahomes and he would have sole possession of that mark.
Kelce finished with two receptions in their 30-27 win against the Las Vegas Raiders, meaning he claimed sole possession of that seventh spot.
Cris Carter is No. 6 on the all-time list with 1,101 receptions, just five more than Kelce. Marvin Harrison is at No. 5 with 1,102, six more than Kelce. When he hits seven more catches, Kelce will be at No. 5 on his own. He could move multiple spots in the coming weeks and has the chance to move up to No. 5.
In Week 1 against the Miami Dolphins , Kelce recorded two receptions on two targets. He registered nine receptions on 11 targets in Week 2 against the Indianapolis Colts, and caught three more balls on five targets in Week 3 against the Denver Broncos . He has 16 receptions total in the four wins, for an average of 4 catches per game.
If Kelce continues his trend of average receptions per game, he will pass Carter in Week 6 and will pass Harrison in Week 7. That said, the veteran always has a chance to have a big game and get those would-be historic receptions earlier.
If Kelce continues to average 4 receptions per game, he will finish the year with 68 catches if he plays all 17 games at the average. That would put him at 1,148 all-time, which would still put him at No. 5, as Jason Witten has 1,228 at No. 4.
To reach No. 4, Kelce needs 132 catches. The most receptions he has recorded in a single year is 110, and his 17-game average is 95 a year. If he plays in 2027 and continues at a similar level, he would likely pass Witten sometime next season.
At 36, Kelce will be hanging up the cleats sooner rather than later. While he hasn't announced whether he will retire after this year, after 14 seasons, it wouldn't come as a shock.

title: Jim Harbaugh defends Mike McDaniel despite 0-4 start, Justin Herbert earns ugly Chargers honor
summary: Los Angeles is struggling on offense and its franchise quarterback is a shell of himself
full_text:
Offensive execution continues to lack for the winless Los Angeles Chargers , partly due to schematic changes following the offseason hiring of former Miami Dolphins coach Mike McDaniel.
After Sunday's 30-23 loss to the Seattle Seahawks , coach Jim Harbaugh was peppered with questions about his team's struggles on that side of the football and whether he thought the Chargers could turn things around, with McDaniel calling plays.
Los Angeles has the fourth-worst scoring offense (16.8 points per game) in the NFL , and its passing offense (185.3 YPG) is on pace for its lowest full-season per game average since 1998.
"No, his job is not in jeopardy," Harbaugh said of the OC, via the Associated Press. "He's a skilled coach, and we're going to keep growing.
According to the NFL's stats department , Justin Herbert is the first Chargers quarterback with at least six interceptions and 10 sacks through the team's first four games since Ryan Leaf in 2000.
Herbert's never thrown six interceptions in his career this early in the season, and he's already been sacked 12 times, tied for the second-most in the league.
Like Harbaugh, however, Herbert's not putting the onus on his play-caller.
"I think (McDaniel) is the greatest and I want to make him proud and do everything I can to pick up the offense and do exactly what he asks," Herbert said. "But I think we've just got to go make plays. I've got to make plays out there and haven't done that, but I know we'll get it next time."
Last month, after a Week 3 loss to the Buffalo Bills , Harbaugh encouraged Herbert to "be better" as the orchestrator of McDaniel's offense. The former first-round pick acknowledged he needed to perform at a higher level.
But so much for Harbaugh attempting to energize his franchise player. Herbert turned it over three times in Sunday's loss, including a loss-clinching fumble after a sack on his team's final possession.
Herbert's QBR is a career-worst 27.9 through four starts, alarming for a signal caller whose efficiency usually rests in the 60s. He's only completing passes at a 59.7% clip, and two first-half interceptions against the Seahawks led to an early 17-point deficit.
McDaniel said after the Chargers' struggles against the Bills that the team's personnel was failing to do their "jobs" on offense and admitted he was part of the problem.
"I'm fully responsible," McDaniel said prior to his team's fourth straight setback, via ESPN . "I spend zero time trying to avoid blame. It's quite the opposite."
Harbaugh has a mess on his hands offensively if Herbert and McDaniel fail to get this ship turned in the right direction before the midseason mark in a couple of weeks.

title: Bryce Young shines again: How former No. 1 pick went from benched to leading NFL in passing
summary: Down two of his top wide receivers, Young threw for 329 yards and two scores on 'Sunday Night Football' vs. the Lions
full_text:
Sunday night, "MVP" chants rained down on Bryce Young as he led the Panthers to a 32-26 win over the Lions , his first prime-time win. It was both fitting -- Young threw for 329 yards and two touchdowns -- and a reminder of how far he has come. Just two years earlier, he wasn't even playing in games, let alone starring in them. He had been benched for Andy Dalton , with his chances of being an NFL starter seemingly in the balance.
How quickly things can change.
Young currently leads the NFL in passing yards and passing first downs. He's tied for third in passing touchdowns and seventh in yards per attempt. For a quarterback who doesn't have a rocket arm, he sure is making the most of it: He leads the NFL in completions of 10+ yards (55) and is tied for second in completions of 20+ yards (17).
And he's doing it all in far from ideal circumstances. The Panthers were without their No. 2 ( Jalen Coker ) and No. 3 ( Xavier Legette ) wide receivers Sunday. Rookie field stretcher Chris Brazzell suffered a season-ending injury in training camp. The offensive line, also battered by injury, is giving up pressure at a 46.3% rate -- only Justin Herbert is pressured at a higher rate.
So, what's working for Young? And more importantly, is it sustainable as the 2-2 Panthers look to make consecutive playoff trips for the first time in more than a decade?
This offseason, Dave Canales handed play-calling duties to offensive coordinator Brad Idzik. Idzik and Canales go back to 2019, when they were both with Seattle, but this is Idzik's first time calling plays. Still, one could have assumed it would look similar to Canales.
That's where assuming can be erroneous. The Panthers currently lead the NFL in pass rate over expected and are fifth in pass percentage. And they're not just passing a lot, but being aggressive doing so: Young is 12th in deep pass rate, ninth in air yards per attempt and sixth in explosives per dropback. It's a wild departure from Young's earlier career, even excluding his disastrous rookie season.
Bryce Young deep pass rate
Bryce Young air yards per attempt
Bryce Young explosives per dropback
Furthermore, Young is using play action on 31.5% of his dropbacks, the highest rate of his career. He's averaging 8.1 yards per play on those passes, also a career high. Here's one of his best throws from Sunday night:
Bryce Young is feelin' it @DETvsCAR on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/eJVA9QoIv2
Young not only makes a terrific throw, but he does so with a defender right in his face. Which leads us to ...
Young's superpower -- the thing that made him a Heisman Trophy winner at Alabama, the thing that made him the No. 1 pick despite his underwhelming physical profile -- is his ability to make the right reads and get the ball there on time. But the jump from being excellent at that in college and being excellent at that in the NFL is a huge one. Young appears to be making that jump.
Young is currently third in EPA per dropback on quick-game throws (thrown in 2.5 seconds or faster). That's an absurd jump.
Bryce Young EPA per dropback on quick throws
Here's one such throw from Sunday night: Young initially gets a Cover-2 look, but it's just a disguise, and the Lions end up playing Cover 3 with a deep safety. Young shreds it immediately with a dart to John Metchie III .
Young darts keep flyin' @DETvsCAR on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Yf2CbrL9oX
Furthermore, Idzik is implementing many different ways to attack. Sunday, for example, Young had three run/pass option throws, which resulted in three completions for 35 yards. It was Young's most RPO throws in a game since his rookie year. He had only three all season entering the game. Three isn't a big number, but adding wrinkles is crucial every week. Idzik clearly saw an area he wanted to attack and exploited it.
The game "slowing down" is a cliche, but it can be true. Young has just two interceptions, and his 1.2% turnover-worthy throw rate is sixth-lowest in the NFL. He's simply not putting the ball in harm's way as much. He's hitting first reads with confidence, and when things get mucked up, he's more composed.
EPA/dropback when pressured
Negative play rate when pressured
<< Ranks top 10 this season
It's not just negative play mitigation. How about this one from last night, in the biggest of moments?
T-MAC ARE YOU SERIOUS! @DETvsCAR on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/uIhOgbACgr
( Tetairoa McMillan rocks, by the way.)
Simply put, Young is playing on time. When it's not on time, it's not the disaster it was before. The biggest strengths of his game are shining, and the weaknesses are becoming either less weak or less important.
As fun as this excellent start has been, it's a very small sample size against a less-than-inspiring bunch of opponents. You can only play who's on your schedule, yes, but there's little doubt a start of Bears , Falcons , Browns and Lions is hardly Murderers' Row when it comes to pass defense.
The Browns were by far the best of that bunch, and Young struggled in that loss. He was inaccurate, took three sacks and couldn't produce explosive plays against a Cleveland defense heavy on press coverage. Young was under pressure all afternoon, and that's going to be an issue, too. The offensive line is without tackles Ikem Ekwonu and Taylor Moton and guards Brady Christensen and Damien Lewis . First-round rookie tackle Monroe Freeling left Sunday night's game and didn't return.
Carolina is currently 26th in PFF's pass blocking grades, and Young has faced 49 quick pressures this season, six more than anyone else.
It makes sense that Young has made strides against pressure, but making such a gigantic leap for an entire season seems unlikely -- especially as he faces some better secondaries, starting with the Eagles in Week 6 after the bye. Can the Panthers keep him clean (enough)? Can he continue to play this well under pressure? Will the wear and tear of a season begin to take its toll?
That's still to be determined. Still, Young has shown major strides. He might not play like a top-five or even a top-10 quarterback the rest of the season like he is now, but it's still trending toward making a very important step for both himself and the organization. Young didn't sign an extension this offseason and will enter the fifth-year option year of his rookie deal. Should he continue to play well -- even at a slightly lower clip than what he's currently doing -- Carolina will have much more confidence believing it's found its long-term answer at quarterback after nearly a decade of searching.
