full_text:
This is an article version of the CBS Sports HQ AM Newsletter, the ultimate guide to every day in sports. You can sign up to get it in your inbox every weekday morning here .
The list of undefeated NFL teams shrank by two, leaving the Chiefs , 49ers and Vikings as the only 4-0 squads. This top tier emerged from the pack in Week 4 while the Bills and Raiders suffered their first defeats of the season. What else do you need to know from the weekend that was in the NFL? Here are the rest of our takeaways:
Ohio State and Notre Dame came away from Week 5 victorious in more ways than one. Fighting Irish quarterback CJ Carr quietly added to his Heisman Trophy campaign in a dominant showing against North Carolina , but the Buckeyes made an even bigger statement and received an "A" grade on our report card . Superstar wide receiver Jeremiah Smith put on an absolute show in a 31-14 win over Iowa , and he hit the Heisman pose following his 36th career touchdown reception, which made him Ohio State's all-time leader . Smith's second consecutive 200-yard game cemented him among the greatest wide receivers in college football history .
The team on the other side of a legendary rivalry did not have as much fun this weekend. Michigan easily stands among Week 5's biggest losers because of its surprising loss to Minnesota and thus its 0-2 start to Big Ten play. Our Tom Fornelli wants to know why the Wolverines have such grave discipline issues , and there are now real questions about whether Bryce Underwood should continue as their starting quarterback .
In the ACC, only one team has a clear path to the College Football Playoff . And after what happened on Friday, even the top threat to Miami is in trouble. Pittsburgh emerged as the second-best team in the conference and earned itself top-25 recognition with a controversial shootout win over Virginia Tech , but quarterback Mason Heintschel sustained a season-ending knee injury in the triumph, which will make it difficult for the Panthers to capitalize on their potential as an ACC title hopeful.

title: NFL Week 5 early odds: Bears favorites at Lambeau, Bills underdogs to Rams
summary: Los Angeles is a slight favorite against Buffalo in a potential Super Bowl preview, while Chicago enters Lambeau Field favored over Green Bay
full_text:
Now that the first month of the season is in the books, it's time for the true contenders to begin separating themselves from the pack. That could happen as soon as Week 5, as there are several high-profile matchups on the docket.
Once again, Sunday's action starts a little early with the Eagles and Jaguars playing in London. Jacksonville travels to its home away from home as a favorite, while Philly will look to get its offense back on track after collapsing against the Rams in Week 4. After that, we have five divisional matchups, including Bears-Packers, with Chicago entering Lambeau Field as a road favorite. We then wrap up the entire slate on Monday for what could be a Super Bowl preview between the Bills and Rams from SoFi Stadium, so this slate packs quite the punch.
As we begin to turn our attention to Week 5, let's jump into the odds and see who the oddsmakers have coming out on top and which games could be high-scoring affairs.
Note : Kansas City and Carolina are on the bye in Week 5
All lines via DraftKings ; all games on Sunday unless noted
Buccaneers at Cowboys (Thursday)
Buccaneers +425, Cowboys -575
Eagles at Jaguars (in London)
Bengals -360, Dolphins +285
Raiders +154, Patriots -185
Giants +142, Commanders -170
Broncos -185, Chargers +154
Lions -250, Cardinals +205
Dallas is now a double-digit favorite over the Buccaneers, laying 10 points after the line initially opened at Coboys -9.5. This comes after we got our first glimpse of Jalon Daniels for Tampa Bay, and the undrafted rookie quarterback managed just two scoring drives in a loss to Green Bay. With Baker Mayfield still out, the Cowboys are rightfully being looked at as a heavy favorite, and they are riding high after a road win in Houston. Dallas is 3-1 ATS this season, including a cover in their home opener. The Bucs are 0-4 ATS through the first month.
Jacksonville has jumped out to a 4.5-point favorite over the Eagles, which is up from the 3-point spread they were laying at the open. The Jaguars are one of the more underrated teams in the NFL through the first three weeks, owning a 3-1 SU and ATS record with an average margin of victory of 12.8 points (second-highest in the NFL). They take on an Eagles team that has been banged up with injuries and saw Saquon Barkley leave Sunday's loss to the Rams with a hamstring injury. So far, the Eagles are 0-4 ATS. Because of the questions surrounding Philadelphia's offense, the total has dropped from 44.5 to 43.5.
Chicago opened as a 1.5-point road favorite over the Packers and that has since bumped up to -2.5. The Bears are both 3-1 straight-up and against the spread this season, and that's in spite of Caleb Williams suffering a hamstring injury. As for the Packefs, they've continued to look sluggish this season and, while they were able to beat the Bucs, it was hardly an inspiring victory and are 1-3 ATS this sesaon. If you're looking for a silver lining, however, Green Bay is 6-2 ATS as a home underdog under Matt LaFleur. That 75% cover rate is the highest in the NFL over that span.
Cincinnati is a 7.5-point road favorite on the road as they gear up to face the Dolphins. That's down from the 8.5-point spread at the open, which may be attributed to injuries plaguing the Bengals offense in Week 4. They lost Ja'Marr Chase due to a concussion, while Tee Higgins exited with an adductor injury. That leaves their availability for Week 5 in doubt, and the total has sunk to 42.5 (opened at 46.5) as a result. The Bengals are 1-1 on the road this season, while Miami is 0-1 ATS at home.
New York is 1-3 on the season, but they've been pesky. They're 2-1-1 ATS and now take on a Browns team that has been one of the surprises of the first month. They'll do so as a 2.5-point favorite, which is up from -1.5 at the open. They're 3-1 (SU and ATS) and are coming off a win against the Steelers on Thursday, so they'll have the rest advantage of New York. The Jets covered their lone game at MetLife Stadium this season, while Cleveland is 1-1 ATS on the road.
Las Vegas suffered its first loss of the season in Week 4 against the Chiefs and will look to rebound when they travel to Foxborough to face the Patriots. They'll enter Gillette Stadium as a 3.5-point underdog, however. New England got its season back on track with a last-minute win over the Bills in Buffalo to move them to 2-2 on the season. Since the start of last season, the Patriots are 7-4-1 ATS at home (1-0 ATS in 2026). The Raiders have covered both of their road games this season.
Houston is a 6.5-point road favorite in this AFC South matchup in Tennessee, but this may say more about the 0-4 Titans than the Texans. That said, Tennessee is 2-2 ATS on the season and 1-1 at Nissan Stadium, while the Texans are 0-4 ATS on the season. Under head coach DeMeco Ryans , the Texans are 5-6-1 ATS as a road favorite. Looking at the totals, the Under is a combined 5-3 between them this season.
This is quite the mismatch in terms of rest. Indy is coming back stateside after playing in London and will then have to travel to Pittsburgh to face a Steelers team that'll be on extended rest after playing last Thursday. That makes this 2.5-point spread in favor of Pittsburgh pretty interesting, especially considering they are 2-0 ATS at home this season. Indy is 1-0 ATS on the road this season.
The Commanders are a 3-point favorite over New York, but this line will be worth monitoring throughout the week. It's unclear if Jayden Daniels will make his return this week. If he doesn't, seventhr ound rookie Athan Kaliakmanis could get the nod after he relieved Marcus Mariota in London on Sunday due to a knee injury. If that proves to be the case, we could see more movement here. The Giants are 0-1 ATS on the road this season, while Washington is 1-0 ATS at home.
Minnesota is a 1.5-point road favorite over the Saints, who still have their Week 4 matchup on deck on Monday night. That said, the line does seem to be moving towards New Orleans as it originally opened at Vikings -2.5. Minnesota is 2-0 ATS on the road this season, but neither of those covers came with them as a road favorite. Before Monday's matchup, the Saints are 0-1 ATS at home and 2-1 ATS on the season.
Denver is a 3.5-point road favorite over the Chargers, who continue to struggle this season. On top of being 0-4 coming out of the first month, Los Angeles is still searching for its first ATS win (0-3-1). The Broncos are 2-2 ATS so far this season, but have yet to cover on the road. The total for this matchup sits at 43.5 and the Under could be in play as it's 6-2 between these teams this season.
Detroit has moved out to a 3.5-point road favorite over Arizona, which is up from the field goal spread at the open. They'll be looking to rebound after a loss in Carolina, where they were road favorites. The Cardinals have lost three straight after upsetting the Chargers in the season opener, but are 2-2 ATS entering Week 5. In their lone game as a home underdog, Arizona is 0-1 ATS.
The Seahawks are a field goal favorite at home as they host the undefeated 49ers in what is a key NFC West matchup. On top of being 4-0, San Francisco is 3-1 ATS and has an NFL-best 14.5 average margin of victory. On the road, they are 1-0 ATS. Meanwhile, Seattle is 1-1-2 ATS so far this season.
This line could change dramatically for a couple of different reasons. For one, the Falcons still have to play their Week 4 matchup on Monday night. Second, Lamar Jackson left Sunday's win over the Titans with an injury. If that causes him to miss time, you can almost guarantee this line won't continue to sit at Ravens -3.5 as it has since the open. The 44.5-point total will also move. This season, the Ravens are 1-3 ATS.
The Rams are a slim 2.5-point favorite as they gear up to host the Bills in a heavyweight matchup next Monday night. This line is down from the full field goal L.A. was laying at the open. The Rams are coming off a comeback win over the Eagles, while the Bills lost at home…

title: Cover 32: Packers don't instill any faith on possible playoff run, plus game balls, biggest gaffes from Week 4
summary: Tyler Sullivan dives into all the biggest items from Week 4 in the NFL, including CeeDee Lamb's historic day and Mike Vrabel's bizarre tiff
full_text:
With the first month of the season in the books, there are a few teams that haven't exactly lived up to the hype. Sure, you can look at teams like the Los Angeles Chargers and Houston Texans -- who are both still winless this year -- as some of the biggest disappointments through the early stages of the 2026 season, but don't sleep on the Green Bay Packers either. Despite emerging from the first month at 2-2, these Cheeseheads don't exactly pass the smell test.
It's been a slog for the Packers, and they haven't instilled much confidence as far as any serious threat in the NFC North. After coming into the year with the second-best odds to win the division and favored to reach double-digit wins on the year, their .500 record feels hollow, with their 17-14 victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 4 serving as the latest piece of evidence pointing to that fact.
They nearly let undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels -- who started in place of the injured Baker Mayfield -- beat them at the last minute because of self-inflicted wounds. For instance, they committed two fourth-quarter turnovers with a mere field goal lead, basically daring Tampa Bay to pull off the upset. The first was a fumble by Kaleb Johnson , and then, on the very next possession, Jordan Love needlessly tossed the ball into a high-traffic area, and the pass was picked off by Bucs corner Jacob Parish.
ANOTHER TAMPA BAY TAKEAWAY 🔥 @GBvsTB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/VVfqSCPHii
Despite those golden opportunities, Daniels and company couldn't capitalize, first punting, then turning the ball over on downs after those two turnovers. Had they been facing a more capable quarterback instead of a UDFA, we could be looking at a different result.
As has been the case throughout the year to this point, the Packers have had two adversaries every week: the opposition and themselves. On Sunday, they committed 10 total penalties, bringing their total to 42 infractions for the year (second-most in the NFL ). Their 344 total penalty yards also lead the league. That's not a characteristic of a true playoff contender.
When they're not having laundry thrown at them, the offense hasn't inspired much fear in opposing defenses. They average just 18.3 points per game, which is their lowest through the first four weeks of the season since 2006. They're also last in the NFL with a 26.1% conversion rate on third down, while their rushing yards per game average (3.2) is near the bottom of the barrel as well. Their defense is allowing a 48.2% conversion rate on third down (fourth-highest in the NFL), so it's not great on either side of the ball right now.
Yes, external circumstances are contributing to this lackluster beginning. They don't have Micah Parsons as he's continuing to rehab his season-ending ACL tear from last year, Josh Jacobs is on the commissioner's exempt list, and they continue to be inundated with injuries. After losing Jayden Reed and Zach Bako-Bewele in previous weeks, they also just saw linebacker Edgerrin Cooper go down in Week 4. It's been brutal from that front.
Even with that in mind, this team has enough talent that it shouldn't be this anemic, yet they're barely getting by despite facing backup and/or bottom-tier starting quarterbacks.
So far this season, Green Bay's two victories have come against the Buccaneers and Jets , who are a combined 1-7 through four weeks. As we mentioned, Tampa Bay started an undrafted free agent, while the Jets had Geno Smith (who nearly beat them in overtime). Meanwhile, their losses have come against the Carson Wentz-led Vikings and the Falcons, with Michael Penix Jr . making his first start since suffering his third career ACL tear.
Looking at their upcoming schedule, the offenses that they're set to face aren't going to give them much reprieve. Over the next three weeks, they'll face the Bears in Week 5, the Cowboys in Week 6, and the Lions in Week 7. At the rate at which they're going currently, it feels like an uphill climb for them to stay at or get over .500 on the season over that stretch.
Right now, the Packers are +225 to make the playoffs at DraftKings Sportsbook, which is a far cry from -146 odds they were before the season. I think that number will only continue to inflate as Green Bay moves forward throughout the rest of the year.
How Game Balls work: Six are awarded to standout players from the slate of teams that won their contests, and only one player on a team can get a game ball.
It was a monster day for the Cowboys receiver as Dallas went into Houston and pulled off a 34-30 win. Lamb was the straw that stirred the drink of the entire offense, and his 12-yard touchdown with 40 seconds left in regulation proved to be the game-winning score. Lamb is the first player in Cowboys history with at least 15 catches and 175 receiving yards in a game. He's also just the fourth player in NFL history to have a game with at least 17 catches, 180 receiving yards, and a touchdown.
WHO ELSE BUTE CEEDEE?!?! @DALvsHOU on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/ODeK70fSFH
The Giants defense generated three turnovers in the 36-24 win over the Arizona Cardinals , and rookie linebacker Arvell Reese was at the center of most of the action. The No. 5 overall pick at the 2026 NFL Draft was everywhere in Week 4, leading the Giants with nine total tackles and also breaking up three passes. One of which was an interception in the closing minutes of the first half. That runover helped springboard a touchdown by the offense two plays later.
ARVELL REESE TAKES IT🔥 📺: CBS/Paramount+ pic.twitter.com/vm6RQr629J
Monangai saw a massive increase in attempts during Chicago's Week 4 win over the Jets, particularly after D'Andre Swift fumbled on the first possession of the third quarter. The second-year back took the ball on 30 of Chicago's 54 rushing attempts on the day. Those attempts set a new career high, while his 146 yards rushing were the second-most of his career. This was also Monangai's first game with multiple touchdowns.
Not many are running it better than Kyle Monangai today 😤 NYJvsCHI on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/aOzQXt1CM5
Williams was instrumental for the Rams , who rallied from a 10-point deficit in Philadelphia to beat the Eagles . The veteran back scored both of the Los Angeles' fourth-quarter touchdowns, each of which came inside five minutes remaining in regulation. This was Williams' ninth-career multi-touchdown game and his 10 receptions set a new career high.
Kyren Williams POWERS IT IN FOR THE LEAD!! @LARvsPHI on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/LW85llHviL
Kenneth Walker III continues to dazzle this season and put on a show in Las Vegas as Kansas City remains perfect at 4-0. Walker set a new career high with 177 yards rushing and scored two touchdowns in the span of 20 seconds. He's the first Chiefs player to have at least 175 rushing yards and two rushing touchdowns in a game since Jamaal Charles in 2009.
K9 GOES 77 YARDS 🔥 @KCvsLV on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/1d8jxbAU0C
It was a career night for the Panthers receiver as he helped lead Carolina to a 32-26 win over the Lions. He set new career highs in both receptions and receiving yards. McMillan is also just the second player in franchise history with at least 10 catches, 150 receiving yards, and two receiving touchdowns in a game, joining Steve Smith Sr. in 2005.
BRYCE TO MCMILLAN FOR 6️⃣ @DETvsCAR on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/7Owb2F0Uni
After lobbying for a pass interference call on a third-down incompletion, one of the officials in the Cardinals-Giants matchup appears to use a profanity towards Arizona tight end Trey McBride . Various clips on social media appear to show the official saying "[expletive] you" to McBride, which was caught on camera during the broadcast.

title: Chiefs very interested in a Tyreek Hill reunion amid injuries at receiver, per report
summary: Kansas City has reportedly reached out to Hill's agent
full_text:
The Kansas City Chiefs are indeed interested in a reunion with Tyreek Hill . Speculation about a possible reunion with the 32-year-old Hill ramped up following Kansas City's win over the Raiders , which saw Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton leave the game with injuries.
Rice left the game after he suffered a hamstring strain in the second quarter that could sideline him for multiple weeks. Thorton, who had 111 yards and two touchdowns in Kansas City's 30-27 win, is out indefinitely after suffering a dislocated ankle that was put back into place by doctors.
Regarding Hill, The Athletic reports that the Chiefs are very interested in a possible reunion with Hill, who starred in Kansas City from 2016-21. The Chiefs have reached out to Hill's agent, Drew Rosenhaus, to express their interest.
Hill was one of the NFL's most explosive players during his first go-around with the Chiefs. He was a Pro Bowler in each of his six seasons in Kansas City and was a three-time All-Pro.
In Super Bowl LIV, Hill's 44-yard catch on a third-and-15 play helped ignite the Chiefs' comeback victory over the 49ers .
One year ago today, Mahomes called for Wasp 🔥 @PatrickMahomes @cheetah @Chiefs (via @NFLFilms ) pic.twitter.com/05oGavdr0f
In 2022, the Chiefs traded Hill to Miami, where he racked up two more All-Pro nods. Hill played through a wrist injury in 2024, and in 2025, he missed Miami's final 13 games after suffering a gruesome knee injury that included a knee dislocation and multiple torn ligaments. Hill is believed to be targeting a November return.
Several Chiefs, including Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce , endorsed the idea of Hill returning to Kansas City.
"I have no idea (if that would happen), but it'd be pretty cool," Mahomes said.
"That's out of my hands, but I know I'd love to have 'The Cheetah' back in this building," Kelce said. "He's a brother. He's one of those people who, when he sets his mind to something, he usually delivers. You saw that with Miami, when all the haters were saying he couldn't play and he went and had his best year. I'd be excited by what he could do (here)."
The Chiefs are 4-0 entering their Week 4 bye. Their first game after their bye will be against the winless Chargers .
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: NFL reviewing heated exchange between referee, Vikings' Eric Wilson
summary: The league is looking into two separate incidents involving a player and an official during Week 4
full_text:
An interaction between Minnesota Vikings linebacker Eric Wilson and referee Adrian Hill fell under the NFL's watchful eye in Week 4. The league said it is reviewing a play from the Vikings' 15-10 win over the Miami Dolphins in which Wilson and Hill collided.
Dolphins running back Ollie Gordon II shoved Wilson into the referee, who then fell backward to the ground. Wilson saw the referee take the tumble and extended his arms to help him up, but instead of taking the assistance, the referee stood up under his own power and began yelling at Wilson. It appeared that the referee took exception to the inadvertent collision and blamed Wilson, while Wilson pointed at Gordon and said that it was the Dolphins player who initiated the contact.
A second official stepped in to separate Wilson from the referee after they exchanged words and pointed in opposite directions. The referee appeared to be instructing Wilson to return to his side of the field.
NFL referee Adrian Hill had a strong reaction when Vikings LB Eric Wilson offered to help him up after their inadvertent collision. (📺 FOX) pic.twitter.com/azDgsIZESY
This is not the only play involving an official and a player that raised eyebrows on Sunday. The NFL is also reviewing an interaction between an official and Arizona Cardinals tight end Trey McBride . McBride pleaded for a pass interference penalty, to which the official appeared to deliver a profane response. That incident prompted a response from NFL Players Association president JC Tretter .
"This kind of behavior from an official towards a player is unacceptable," Tretter said. "Players are consistently held accountable when the roles are reversed. We expect the NFL to hold officials to the same standard."
New England Patriots coach Mike Vrabel also had a heated moment with an official over a pass interference situation. Vrabel was said to have told a down judge that he made "a f---ing terrible call," which drew an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty. Vrabel called the official "a little sensitive" for issuing the flag.
author: Carter Bahns

title: NFL reviewing incident between official and Cardinals' Trey McBride, NFLPA issues statement
summary: The altercation between the two went viral following New York's win over Arizona
full_text:
The NFL is reviewing an incident that took place between an official and Cardinals tight end Trey McBride during Sunday's game between Arizona and the New York Giants .
McBride initially voiced his displeasure after he thought pass interference should have been called on a third-down incompletion, and the referee seemed to respond with an expletive. Cameras caught the official's response to McBride, which quickly went viral.
The NFL said it is reviewing the situation in which an official appears to use profanity at Cardinals TE Trey McBride. The NFLPA Executive Director JC Tretter called for the NFL to hold the official accountable. pic.twitter.com/NuueChAmrx
The altercation caught the attention of JC Tretter , the president of the NFL Players Association.
"This kind of behavior from an official towards a player is unacceptable," Tretter wrote on X . "Players are consistently held accountable when the roles are reversed. We expect the NFL to hold officials to the same standard."
CBS Sports sideline reporter Aditi Kinkhabwala was in close proximity to the incident. She shared her observations on X.
"What's wild is that it all started with Trey McBride saying 'please' when pleading his case for a PI flag," she wrote . "He was heated for sure, but I never heard a curse from him. The harshest he got was, 'You're ruining the game.'"
Ironically, Patriots coach Mike Vrabel was penalized after saying something similar to an official during New England's win over the Buffalo Bills . The penalty helped set up a Buffalo touchdown.
"I've said that 87 times since I've been a head coach," Vrabel said afterward. "There's nothing derogatory. You know, you'd have to ask him. I think he was a little sensitive. ... I probably shouldn't have sworn, but I can tell you that in my history of being on the sidelines as a head coach, I've said that, and I apologized to him."
It'll be interesting to see how the NFL handles this situation.
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: Eagles' offense completely collapses vs. Rams: Who's to blame and what needs to change
summary: The offensive meltdown after having the chance to deliver the knockout punch to Los Angeles highlights an uncomfortable truth in Philadelphia
full_text:
The Philadelphia Eagles ' 24-20 collapse at home against the Los Angeles Rams in Week 4 on Sunday is a five-alarm fire for the back-to-back NFC East division champions.
Philadelphia had Los Angeles on the proverbial ropes. The Eagles led 20-10, and they had the ball on the two, just a couple of yards from scoring a touchdown that would land the knockout punch and put the game entirely out of reach with under eight minutes to play. At that moment, the NFL's Next Gen Stats assessed the Rams had a win probability as minuscule as 3.2%.
But Los Angeles stuffed quarterback Jalen Hurts on Philadelphia's famed "Tush Push" play before he threw incomplete on fourth-and-goal to force a turnover on downs. From that moment on, on their final two drives, the Eagles' offense lost a combined 14 yards. The Rams mounted consecutive, 10-play touchdown drives capped by rushing touchdowns from running back Kyren Williams .
The Eagles lost for the first time with Hurts when up double-digit points in a game's final five minutes, per CBS Sports Research. They were previously a perfect 41-0 in such situations (including the playoffs). The last time the Eagles lost in regulation when leading by at least 10 in the final five minutes was all the way back in a 2018 game against the Carolina Panthers , with Carson Wentz starting at quarterback.
So how did we get here? Let's take a look.
What killed the Eagles was a couple of things, starting with injuries and head coach Nick Sirianni's inability to assemble an offense that provides easy answers for Hurts. Running back Saquon Barkley , the player Philadelphia built its offense around, exited the game with a hamstring injury. Even before kickoff, the Eagles knew they would be without top wide receiver DeVonta Smith , tight end Dallas Goedert , offensive guard Landon Dickerson and right tackle Lane Johnson .
With all those players sidelined, Sirianni and offensive coordinator Sean Mannion couldn't build a game plan that provided Hurts and Co. with easy answers in high-leverage situations, particularly third down. The Eagles didn't convert on any of their 12 third downs, which is Philadelphia's most third-down attempts in a game without a conversion in the past 35 seasons, per CBS Sports Research. It's also the most third-down attempts without a conversion by any team in a game this decade, per NFL Media Research .
"Oh-for on third down, it hurts your drives. It hurts your being able to do the things you want to do on offense," head coach Nick Sirianni said postgame . "It can put you in a pressing situation at times. ... That to me is where we had our biggest issues here today was there."
How much did the Eagles' third-down inefficiency kill the offense? According to The Ringer , Philadelphia's 172 total yards of offense ranked as its lowest in a game in the last 12 years, while its 68 net passing yards are its lowest in a regular-season game in 23 years. On all of Philadelphia's third-down plays, it's clear Hurts didn't have the opportunity to execute key plays. He chalked it up to execution by the players, not an issue with the coaching staff.
"Poor execution. I don't think there's any other way to put it. ... I have to be better. I have to figure it out. However it looks, whatever that means," Hurts said postgame .
We'll save you the trouble of digging into every third-down play from the Eagles because it was ugly. But on third-down attempts, they had:
The most glaring execution issue came on the third-and-goal from the 2-yard line, in which the Eagles had a chance to put the game out of reach for good. Left guard Cam Jurgens, being too early coming off the line of scrimmage, threw off the timing of the Eagles' quarterback run play, and the Rams stuffed it for no gain. A play later, a Hurts incompletion led to a turnover on downs before Philadelphia netted minus-14 yards across their final two possessions.
Found it. Went through all the camera angles. The reason why the Eagles run failed on 3rd and goal from the 2 (which likely would have scored) is because Cam Jurgens slightly false started, but it wasn't called. He was on top of Hurts too quickly as he pulled, and his hand hit… pic.twitter.com/FnecKiGg2G
Including the goal-line miscue, the Eagles had six offensive possessions in the second half, and they ended as follows: punt, punt, turnover on downs, turnover on downs, punt, and turnover on downs.
However, Sunday afternoon's offensive woes after halftime weren't unique to Week 4. In their 24-22 Week 1 win over the Washington Commanders , they scored 10 points. In their 24-20 Week 2 win at the Tennessee Titans , they scored 10 points. Across the last two weeks, a blowout "Monday Night Football" loss vs. the Chicago Bears and the loss against the Rams, Philadelphia went scoreless after halftime. The Eagles are now the league's worst second-half offense as a result.
Expected points added (EPA) per play
New offensive coordinator Sean Mannion came to Philadelphia after spending last season as the Green Bay Packers quarterbacks coach under Matt LaFleur. He also played for Sean McVay and the Rams and Kevin O'Connell and the Minnesota Vikings across his nine-season playing career.
He is a branch off the Shanahan-McVay coaching tree, which tends to have offenses that display heavy doses of motion, quarterbacks lining up under center and play-action passing. The scheme wants the looks for runs and passes to appear the same to defenses. That way, the quarterback should be able to easily run a given play as called and then take advantage of a defense that can't tell what's coming.
In Mannion's offense under Sirianni, the Eagles are just average in motion rate (45.2%, 15th in the NFL) while ranking bottom-five in under-center rate (31.3%, 28th) and dead last in play-action rate (14.5%). Running the Shanahan-McVay offense without its core staples is like trying to win the lottery: The odds are that it isn't going to work out for you.
In addition to needing better health across the board, the Eagles need Sirianni to let Mannion fully incorporate every element of his playbook that he would like. Otherwise, the easy answers won't be present in Philadelphia.
"I have a ton of confidence in Sean [Mannion]. He's going to wear a lot of this, no doubt. I'm going to wear a lot of this," Sirianni said postgame . "Our offense is going to wear a lot of this. You win together, you lose together. I have no complaints with what happened there today. There's opportunity for us to grow."
Sirianni's confidence in Mannion and what he wants to do needs to be more than lip service going forward. Otherwise, he'll have to explain why the Eagles missed the playoffs for the first time in his tenure come January.
author: Garrett Podell

title: NFL Week 4 winners and losers: Drake Maye delivers, Texans' season slips away
summary: Maye rediscovered his 2025 form against the Bills, while Houston's latest loss left its playoff hopes hanging by a thread
full_text:
A pair of reigning playoff teams from the AFC needed to get up off the mat in Week 4. One side did so in resounding fashion while the other suffered the kind of loss that could effectively end its hunt for a return to the postseason. The New England Patriots took down the conference's best team for a get-right win, and the team they beat in last year's divisional round, the Houston Texans , fell to 0-4 to continue a miserable start to the season.
That dichotomy underscores how high the stakes are as the 2026 season enters its first month. This is one of those weeks when the NFL learns which teams are for real and which are bound to compete at the bottom of the league ladder. The separation built between Super Bowl hopefuls and No. 1 draft pick contenders on Sunday was eye-opening.
Week 4 has also been a brutal one from an injury standpoint. Players, unfortunately, get hurt every week. But the name value of those who dropped out of action this weekend was as significant as that of any of the previous three slates of games.
Here are the NFL's biggest winners and losers from Week 4.
There might have been no bigger disappointment across the NFL through three games than Drake Maye , whose regression from MVP runner-up to the league's second-worst quarterback by passer rating was a puzzling fall from grace. The 2025 version of Maye reappeared in the New England Patriots' 29-26 upset of the Buffalo Bills . He passed for 269 yards and three touchdowns and led the Patriots in rushing with another 54 yards.
Losing A.J. Brown to a high ankle sprain in Week 1 seemed to throw Maye off. His return is near, but importantly, Maye might have finally found a groove with his other targets. He spread the ball around to seven receivers on Sunday, tossed a pair of touchdowns to Romeo Doubs and got a little help from Efton Chism III on a one-handed catch for what proved to be the game-winning score. This should be a major confidence builder for a quarterback who could not get out of his own way to begin the year.
Maye's rounding into form is, of course, a crucial development for a Patriots team that could have ill-afforded to drop into a 1-3 hole. Getting up off the mat on the heels of a blowout loss was important, and doing it against the Bills was a best-case scenario, considering Buffalo is arguably the best team in the NFL and the Patriots' stiffest AFC East competition.
Since the Houston Texans reversed course last year to reach the playoffs after an 0-3 start, hardly anyone fully counted them out when they lost the first three games in 2026. But now? A 34-30 loss to the Dallas Cowboys leaves minimal room for optimism.
Defense was supposed to be Houston's calling card this year. It certainly was not on Sunday when it surrendered three touchdowns to Javonte Williams in the second half alone and had no answers for CeeDee Lamb . The Cowboys' star wide receiver racked up 17 catches to finish just one grab behind Jason Witten for the single-game franchise record, and he did it against what should be one of the NFL's stingiest defensive backfields. The Texans were no stalwarts on that side of the ball in any of their previous three losses, either.
Houston should finally grab its first win of the campaign next week when it meets the Tennessee Titans in a matchup of two winless AFC South teams. It might, however, already be too late to save a disastrous start to the year.
Fans in London did not have much reason to cheer for the Washington Commanders in Sunday's international game. The Indianapolis Colts pulled away from them in a 30-13 rout at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium and did so comfortably as it was clear the Commanders would not be able to maintain pace once Marcus Mariota went down with a game-ending knee injury . Washington took a 6-0 lead with him on the field and was outscored 30-7 from that point forward.
Rookie Athan Kaliakmanis, out of Rutgers, stepped into action and completed just 15 of 33 passes with a touchdown and an interception in his professional regular-season debut. He also took a sack and sustained multiple hard hits. The Commanders are stretched so thin at quarterback that if Kaliakmanis left the game for any reason, tight end Colson Yankoff would have had to step in as the emergency signal-caller.
Moving forward, the Commanders will either have a backup quarterback on the field or a less-than-healthy Jayden Daniels . There is no telling how effective he will be when he comes back from his elbow injury , which will require offseason surgery and which forces him to play with a brace on his non-throwing arm.
Coach Aaron Glenn, the New York Jets defensive personnel and their frustrated fanbase can finally sleep easily. To whatever extent possible, at least, in the wake of a 23-12 loss to the Chicago Bears . They undoubtedly would have preferred a win, but they did get a huge monkey off their back in the second quarter of that defeat when five-time Pro Bowl safety Minkah Fitzpatrick picked off Tyson Bagent for the franchise's first interception in 637 days . At long last, the drought is over.
The 20 games New York went between interceptions was an NFL record. It was a defining element of the team's defensive ineptitude last year and carried over into the first month of 2026, even as the unit showed modest signs of improvement. What remains clear is that there is still a lot of work to be done on that side of the ball, considering the takeaway was not enough to keep Chicago and its backup quarterback in check.
The Philadelphia Eagles made the wrong kind of franchise history in Week 4 with the worst third-down execution in their 94 years of existence. Never before had the offense gone 0-12 in third-down situations until Sunday's 24-20 loss to the Los Angeles Rams . Making matters worse, the Eagles found it difficult to move the chains on fourth down, too, with just one conversion on four tries. Those three turnovers on downs were costly in their scoreless second half.
First-year offensive coordinator Sean Mannion was always going to be heavily scrutinized this season because of the high-pressure situation he walked into. Sunday's performance was no resounding endorsement of his scheme nor his play-calling abilities. Perhaps it speaks more to Jalen Hurts and his shortcomings, though. Or maybe it was a product of Saquon Barkley missing nearly the entire game with a hamstring injury .
Regardless of who is most to blame, the Eagles cost themselves this game. They held a 10-point lead with four minutes to play and lost because they could not tack onto their advantage in the second half and could not stay on the field to drain the clock in the final period.
Brock Purdy is in the midst of his best football to date, which is a primary reason why the San Francisco 49ers are off to a perfect start. It is a whole lot easier to play the quarterback position at a high level when you do not have to worry about defenders invading your space, and Purdy can speak to that. The 49ers are the first team since the 2005 Indianapolis Colts to open a season at 4-0 without allowing a sack.
That caliber of offensive line play (plus quarterback escapability, wide receiver route-running and everything else that goes into sack prevention) is notable in a vacuum. It is even more impressive considering the caliber of opponent San Francisco faced in Weeks 1-4. They defeated the Denver Broncos on Sunday, 24-14, and held a defense that last year posted the fifth-most sacks in NFL history to zero.
Barkley is not the only household name who departed from action in Week 4. Lamar Jackson also missed the second half of the Baltimore Ravens ' victory with an ankle issue, and Ja'Marr Chase suffered a concussion in the second quarter of the Cincinnati Bengals ' loss. And on defense, Patrick Surtain II sustained a non-contact ankle injury and did not return for the Denver Broncos in their loss to the San Francisco 49ers. Each of those players is at least a top-three player at high-profile positions…
author: Carter Bahns

title: Week 4 overreactions: Should Rams still be Super Bowl favorites? Cowboys to win NFC East?
summary: Plus, why Ben Johnson won't win Coach of the Year
full_text:
Sean McVay's visceral reaction to the Rams ' 24-20 comeback win over the Eagles is one small part of what makes the NFL so great. Think these early-season games don't mean anything? Think winning a game you "should" win shouldn't elicit celebration? Think again.
The margins in the NFL are tiny. Entering the late-afternoon window, seven of the 10 games played in Week 4 were decided by one possession. Another game -- Cardinals at Giants -- came down to the final snap, when Deonte Banks ' pick six made it a multi-score game. Teeny, tiny differences matter so much.
And that's why the Rams' win matters. The Super Bowl favorites were staring down a 1-3 start and a long, long list of questions. They still have questions, sure, but they'll feel a lot better addressing those questions after a win.
And that's why you see McVay high-fiving his players and celebrating as if he had just won a Super Bowl — a celebration he has, in fact, done before. His reaction is an earned one, not an overreaction.
Speaking of overreactions -- or not ...
Overreaction or reality: Overreaction
There are two ways to view the Rams' 24-20 win over the injury-ravaged Eagles:
It can be both. Los Angeles struggling to beat a Philadelphia team without DeVonta Smith , Saquon Barkley , Quinyon Mitchell , Zack Baun , Lane Johnson , Landon Dickerson and others was a bad look ... for 52-plus minutes.
But the last 7:26? Super impressive:
Matthew Stafford , against Eagles' defensive coordinator Vic Fangio and in the rain, struggled. Those are two factors he has always struggled with. In fact, this was his first win over a Fangio-coached defense. But when the Rams had to have it, they got Stafford at his best: 12-for-15 for 140 yards over the two late, lengthy scoring drives. Kyren Williams pounded in two touchdowns.
The score will lie about who dominated this game. The Rams had 415 yards of offense and averaged 5.4 yards per play, compared to 172 and 3.0, respectively, for Philadelphia. The Rams committed some horrible turnovers and penalties, but on a play-by-play basis, they were far superior. Puka Nacua had nine catches for 125 yards and ran for a score. They won without Myles Garrett , Aaron Donald and Jaylen Watson on defense. This was a crucial, crucial win, and one that should only prove Los Angeles can win when so much goes wrong.
Overreaction or reality: Reality
Speaking of important wins, the Cowboys just got their most important since the 2023 season: Dallas 34, Houston 30.
This game had a little bit of everything and a lot of one thing in particular: CeeDee Lamb . He had 17 catches for 189 yards and a touchdown against the Texans ' normally terrific defense. He was unstoppable everywhere, a true superstar at his peak. Dak Prescott was absolutely outstanding with 335 passing yards, a touchdown (to Lamb, naturally) and no interceptions or fumbles.
The issues in the secondary remain, but the Cowboys held the Texans to a 31.6% rushing success rate. That is Dallas' second-lowest rate allowed this season. Yes, I know it's the Texans, but it's a start.
This is a game the Cowboys needed to win, and they found a way to do so. Looking around the division, the Eagles' offense remains a mess, the Giants are 3-1 but not likely to threaten with Jameis Winston under center, and the Commanders are in a world of trouble.
Simply put, Dallas, with a defense that should only improve and an offense that can go toe-to-toe with any, should win this division. If it can't, there should be major questions from the top down ... again.
Overreaction or reality: Overreaction
Last week, I said the Seahawks losing Kenneth Walker III was the worst loss of the offseason . I have been a huge Walker fan since he arrived in the NFL -- you simply cannot teach the talent he has -- and I was an even bigger fan of him landing in Kansas City. The match of his talent, now in a full-time role, plus the Chiefs' offensive line is *chef's kiss*.
What do I mean by chef's kiss? How about 22 CARRIES, 177 RUSHING YARDS AND TWO TOUCHDOWNS. Yes, stat lines like that require all caps, especially when they come on runs like this:
K9 GOES 77 YARDS 🔥 @KCvsLV on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/1d8jxbAU0C
ANOTHER K9 TD 😱 @KCvsLV on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/vXoi9BkCfD
Walker has already proved himself a top-tier running back after just four games in Kansas City. He is phenomenal.
But I'd still take Bijan Robinson and Jahmyr Gibbs , if ever so slightly, over Walker. The biggest reason is they're a little more consistent down-to-down. That's been a difference historically and even this season, when Walker's situation has been better than ever before.
You know what I also wrote last week? That it's a great time to watch running backs. We can all agree there.
Overreaction or reality: Overreaction
Ho hum. Another week, another win for the Jaguars , who have won 11 of their last 12 regular-season games going back to last year. This time, it was a 22-17 win over the Bengals in Cincinnati. Yes, the Bengals lost Ja'Marr Chase to a concussion early in the game, but this is a really impressive win over another AFC team with playoff aspirations.
Trevor Lawrence had another strong game -- 18 for 23 for 227 yards (9.9 yards per attempt) with a touchdown and no interceptions -- and the Jaguars ran for 111 yards while allowing just 23. Foyesade Oluokun and Jourdan Lewis both picked off Joe Burrow .
DraftKings has the Jaguars with the fourth-shortest odds to win the AFC (+590), behind the Ravens (+390), Bills (+395) and Chiefs (+405). The Jaguars probably belong among those teams, but not as the definitive favorite. It's a crowded group, and that doesn't even include the Broncos or Patriots .
Two things can be true: The Jaguars look like the best team in the AFC right now, and I'm not sure I would take them as my pick to represent the AFC in the Super Bowl at the moment.
Still, it's absurd how much they're being overlooked. Only the 49ers have a better line-of-scrimmage expected points added, and they've played a much easier schedule. This is a really, really good team.
Overreaction or reality: Overreaction
The Packers eked out a 17-14 win over the Buccaneers to get to 2-2 on the season, but major problems persist.
And in new negative developments, CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz reports that the Packers fear standout linebacker Edgerrin Cooper has torn his Achilles .
The biggest positive for Green Bay (after winning the game, of course) was that Love took no sacks. The offensive line was much better. But this team is still miles away from looking like a playoff contender, and that goes for both sides of the ball.
Overreaction or reality: Overreaction
Ben Johnson should be the frontrunner for Coach of the Year. He's now won games with Caleb Williams , Tyson Bagent and Case Keenum ... and it's only Week 4! According to CBS Sports research, only one other team has had three different quarterbacks throw for 200+ yards in a win through four weeks: the 1997 Jaguars.
Unfortunately for Johnson's Coach of the Year candidacy, the award tends to go to a coach whose team way overachieves: Mike Vrabel's Patriots last year, Kevin O'Connell's Vikings (with Sam Darnold ) in 2024, Kevin Stefanski's Browns in 2023, Brian Daboll's Giants in 2022.
Basically, the external preseason expectations were likely too high for Johnson and the Bears for him to win the award this year, even if you could argue he's been the best coach in the sport so far.
Overreaction or reality: Reality
There are a lot of things Dan Quinn cannot control. He can't control that Jayden Daniels is hurt, nor that Marcus Mariota got hurt Sunday, forcing the Commanders to turn to seventh-round rookie Athan Kaliakmanis under center. He cannot control that the team has injuries pretty much everywhere up and down the roster. He can't control a litany of other problems, including that there simply isn't enough talent, period.
But the things he can control aren't going his way,…

title: Jayden Daniels update: Dan Quinn says 'the hope' is for Commanders QB to return in Week 5
summary: The plan is for Daniels to practice in full this week
full_text:
Amid another spate of injuries for his Commanders , Dan Quinn had one positive update following Washington's 30-13 loss to the Colts in London: He's hoping quarterback Jayden Daniels will be back for Week 5 against the Giants
"That's the hope for us for sure, [Jayden] coming back," Quinn said. "He'll have a full week of practice Wednesday, Thursday, Friday. That's the goal that he could get into that space. Once we see where Marcus [Mariota] is ... we'll have a better understanding. That's the goal for Jayden to throw a full week. He was able to do some limited this week, and this week would be the plan for him to do all the reps."
Mariota is believed to have aggravated a preseason MCL injury in the first quarter of Sunday's contest when he went down awkwardly on a sack . With Daniels already out, Washington had to turn to third-string quarterback Athan Kaliakmanis , a seventh-round rookie out of Rutgers. Though he threw his first NFL touchdown pass, he also had a costly interception, and Washington only scored once across Kaliakmanis' 10 drives.
"Athan came in after 12 plays; that's not the ideal space to begin it, but I thought he also showed a lot of confidence, some fearlessness with that, and made some of the throws to highlight why he is where he is," Quinn said.
Quinn said that Mariota would undergo further testing, but ideally, it'll be Daniels getting the start next week. Daniels dislocated his left elbow — his second such injury in less than a year — in Week 2 against the Cowboys when he got stepped on by left guard Chris Paul and fell awkwardly.
The No. 2 overall pick in 2024 played in just seven games last year, and his injuries, plus Washington's lack of success, have raised questions as to whether Daniels can protect himself and if the team can provide him enough support. Regarding the latter, the Commanders are already in a tough spot: Left tackle Laremy Tunsil tore his triceps in training camp, right guard Sam Cosmi is still recovering from a concussion he suffered in Week 2, and Terry McLaurin (hamstring) was out in Week 4 as well. Furthermore, Commanders running backs had just 49 yards on 18 carries Sunday.
"For us, having run game is going to be a big deal," Quinn said. "Hopefully, Sam's on his way back up too. So, when you're putting those two together, to me, that's the sweet spot where you can balance both of them together. We don't want to make it where he's a dropback player and 'Do all your magic every time.'"
Daniels missed four weeks (three games plus a bye) after suffering his first dislocated elbow in 2025. In his first game back, he re-aggravated (but did not suffer any further damage to) the elbow. With the Commanders out of the playoff picture, Daniels did not return for the rest of the season after the re-aggravation.

title: Mike Vrabel calls out official after being penalized during Patriots win over Bills
summary: Vrabel's team overcame his penalty, which led to a Bills touchdown
full_text:
While the Patriots recorded a 29-26 win over the Bills , one of the biggest storylines after the game was on Mike Vrabel's 15-yard penalty that led to a Buffalo score just before halftime.
Vrabel's infraction occurred with 1:48 left in the second quarter and the Bills facing a third-and-goal on New England's 16-yard line. Josh Allen threw an incomplete pass on the play, but Buffalo was awarded a first down after Vrabel was flagged 15 yards for unsportsmanlike conduct.
Allen ran for a game-tying touchdown five plays later.
Patriots coach Mike Vrabel was hit with an Unsportsmanlike Conduct penalty. The Bills tied the game a few plays later. pic.twitter.com/6JsrQWfAeA
Fortunately for Vrabel, his team bailed him out by outplaying the Bills in the second half. New England started the half with a 14-play scoring drive and finished it with a game-clinching interception of Allen. The win evened the Patriots' record at 2-2 and prevented Buffalo from taking a two-game lead in the division.
Afterward, both Vrabel and official Bill Vinovich addressed the incident.
"He was out of the box, came up to the official and said, 'That was a f---ing terrible call," Vinovich said when asked about his decision to penalize Vrabel.
As a follow-up, Vinovich was asked whether that situation usually warrants a warning rather than a penalty. "I don't know how you're going to give a warning," he replied. "It's not something that is going to happen twice. When you use language like that, it's pretty much a given."
Vrabel, however, doesn't think that his actions warranted a penalty.
"I've said that 87 times since I've been a head coach," Vrabel said. "There's nothing derogatory. You know, you'd have to ask him. I think he was a little sensitive. ... I probably shouldn't have sworn, but I can tell you that in my history of being on the sidelines as a head coach, I've said that, and I apologized to him. And again, players, responded. It was unfortunate, and I have to be better in those moments."
It's been a tumultuous several months for Vrabel, who started off 2026 by leading the Patriots to an AFC title in just his second season in New England.
In April, reports surfaced regarding Vrabel's relationship with NFL reporter Dianna Russini. Shortly thereafter, Vrabel announced he was entering counseling.
New England's 2026 season has been a roller coaster so far. The Patriots lost in Seattle in Week 1, defeated the Steelers convincingly in Week 2, and were blown out by the Jaguars last Sunday .
On Sunday, the Patriots received a much-needed bounce-back performance from quarterback Drake Maye , who struggled during New England's first three games. Maye threw three touchdowns in Sunday's win over Buffalo.
Maye's performance earned him a game ball from Vrabel.
“We are gonna fight until they cut our hands off” 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/Wri16XInsp
"Hey! We ain't taking no more f-----g s--t!" Vrabel was heared shouting to Maye in an exchange that Vrabel won't be penalized for.

title: CeeDee Lamb makes Cowboys history, caps career day with winning TD vs. Texans
summary: The five-time Pro Bowler erupted for 11 catches and 140 yards after halftime before scoring the decisive touchdown with 40 seconds remaining
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys (2-2) looked doomed at halftime in Houston, trailing the Texans (0-4) by double digits.
Then, CeeDee Lamb put on his Superman cape.
Lamb, sitting on six catches for 49 yards, erupted in the second half for 11 more catches, 140 more receiving yards and the game-winning 12-yard receiving touchdown to finish with 189 yards receiving, a touchdown and 17 catches in a 34-30 Dallas victory. Those 17 catches rank as the most in a single game by a wide receiver in Cowboys history, and only Jason Witten ever caught more passes in a Cowboys game, back in 2012. Lamb is also the only Cowboy with 15-plus catches and 175-plus yards in a game. Prescott finished the afternoon with 335 yards and the touchdown to Lamb on 32 of 45 passing.
"I just want Schotty [coach Brian Schottenheimer] to know that I got his back. I'm with him. I'm one of his strongest soldiers," Lamb said postgame on Sunday, via The Dallas Morning News . "It's just going to battle with each other. I feel like once you have that confidence and know who you're going to battle with, just shoot your gun, and I feel like he shot it."
After realizing the wordplay he pulled off in talking about Schottenheimer taking his "shot," or rather his "schot," by continuing to dial plays for him, it hit Lamb exactly how locked in he was on Sunday, both on and off the field.
"Wow," Lamb said, via The Dallas Morning News . "That's fire."
Perhaps one of the craziest things about Lamb's day is that Lamb had multiple catches against six different Texans defensive players on Sunday, per the NFL's Next Gen Stats via SB Nation. Houston literally had no answers for No. 88 in blue.
Dallas Cowboys WR CeeDee Lamb was targeted on 21/45 routes during Sunday's win in Houston, the most targets by any receiver to have run 45 or fewer routes in a game during the Next Gen Stats era (since 2016). CeeDee had multiple receptions when matched up against 6 different… pic.twitter.com/wPlKSbBBmT
Most importantly, Lamb caught the game-winning touchdown to give Dallas the victory over Houston.
"As soon as it was called, I knew it was a touchdown," Prescott said postgame, via The Dallas Morning News .
CEEDEE LAMB'S CAREER GAME IS CLUTCH FOR THE COWBOYS 🔥 📺: FOX/FOX ONE pic.twitter.com/fixkANRDjA
Sunday was the Cowboys' 11th game allowing 30-plus points since the start of the 2025 season. Perhaps new Cowboys cornerback Joey Porter Jr . can help get things turned once he is able to play a full game's worth of snaps. He missed the first three games of the 2026 season while in a contract standoff with the Pittsburgh Steelers . In his Dallas debut on Sunday, he played on 42.3% (22 of 52) of the Cowboys' defensive snaps, and Porter Jr. wasn't targeted during his 17 coverage snaps.
Porter Jr. and the rest of the Cowboys roster might end up watching an all-time season from Lamb should he keep up the pace he's on through the first four games of the 2026 season. Lamb is up to 498 yards receiving and four receiving touchdowns on 37 catches at the moment. That has him on pace for 2,116 yards receiving and 17 receiving touchdowns on 157 catches. All three of those figures would shatter the Cowboys' single-season receiving record for each of those statistics, while 2,116 yards receiving and 157 catches would stand alone atop the NFL's single-season record books. His 498 yards receiving are now the most in Cowboys history through the first four games of a season.
In years past, the Cowboys had bell cow running backs like Tony Dorsett, Emmitt Smith and Ezekiel Elliott . Today, Lamb, in tandem with Prescott, is the powerful playmaker that could drag Dallas' entire franchise, struggling defense and all, back to the postseason for the first time since 2023.

title: Packers fear Edgerrin Cooper suffered torn Achilles in win over Buccaneers
summary: Matt LaFleur called the injury "not good" after the game, and the emerging defensive star is suspected to miss the rest of the year after being carted off against Tampa Bay
full_text:
Although the Packers secured a 17-14 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday , Green Bay suffered a big loss as well.
While the injury is still being evaluated, the Packers fear that star third-year linebacker Edgerrin Cooper sustained a torn Achilles tendon against Tampa Bay, sources tell CBS Sports.
Green Bay head coach Matt LaFleur confirmed CBS Sports' report during his postgame press conference, noting that Cooper's Achilles injury is "not good" and that he'd "suspect" it will be a season-ending injury.
The 24-year-old Cooper, a second-round draft pick in 2024 out of Texas A&M, had been continuing to emerge as one of the young linebackers in the NFL . After tallying 205 total tackles during his first two seasons with the Packers, Cooper had 30 tackles and three sacks through the first three-and-a-half games of this season before the injury.
He had nine tackles and a sack Sunday against Tampa Bay before sustaining the injury and having to be carted off the field.
Green Bay, which improved to 2-2 with the win over the Buccaneers, faces the 3-1 Bears next week.

title: Lamar Jackson injury: Ravens QB being monitored, considered day-to-day after exiting vs. Titans

full_text:

Jackson suffered the injury on the second-to-last play of the first half, when Jermaine Johnson II sacked him and appeared to twist his ankle. The two-time NFL MVP completed 15-of-20 passes for 222 yards and two touchdowns before exiting, to go along with 20 yards rushing.
Jermaine with the sack 📺: @NFLonCBS pic.twitter.com/zL6SHLHckO
Head coach Jesse Minter told reporters after the game that the team doesn't know the extent of Jackson's ankle injury, but they did discuss allowing him to re-enter the game in the second half. NFL Network reports that Jackson is considered day-to-day and the Ravens will continue to monitor and treat him this week.
Huntley completed 8-of-9 passes for 63 yards and rushed four times for 16 yards in the final two quarters, but the Ravens did not score any points. Derrick Henry led the offensive attack with 73 rushing yards and one touchdown on 23 carries vs. his former team.
Jackson entered Sunday with 745 passing yards, four touchdowns and one interception through three weeks. He leads the league in yards per attempt (9.8) and yards per attempt off play-action (13.4).

title: NFL investigating referee cursing at Cardinals’ TE McBride
summary: The NFL has begun an investigation regarding a sideline referee cursing at Arizona Cardinals TE Trey McBride during the 36-24 loss to the New York Football Giants in New Jersey. The NFL Players Association, plus the NFL Referees Association, have gotten involved. RELATED: BEAKS & GEEKS CARDINALS VS. GIANTS If you watched the game, you […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 27: Trey McBride #85 of the Arizona Cardinals takes a drink of water during warm ups (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL has begun an investigation regarding a sideline referee cursing at Arizona Cardinals TE Trey McBride during the 36-24 loss to the New York Football Giants in New Jersey. The NFL Players Association, plus the NFL Referees Association, have gotten involved. RELATED: BEAKS & GEEKS CARDINALS VS. GIANTS If you watched the game, you know what this moment was. The fourth quarter was winding down, and the Giants were clinging to a 27-24 lead, but had to punt. The kick was signaled a fair catch by KR Devin Duvernay at the 13-yard line, but instead, he let it hit the turf at the 15-yard line, and it was downed at the three-yard line. Now, the Cardinals had to drive the field in the hopes of getting into field goal range. QB Jacoby Brissett gained seven yards after being flushed from the pocket. On second down, RB Tyler Allgeier was tackled by NT DJ Reader after just a one-yard gain. This brought up third-and-two from the 11-yard line. Brissett dropped back to pass, and flung it in the direction of McBride just past the first down marker on the left side. Giants nickelback Dru Phillips picked up McBride off the line, grabbed his jersey, released, and was able to bat away the pass. He was obviously all over McBride and made physical contact without the tight end catching the ball. Before the ball even arrived, McBride was falling. Editor’s note: This play begins at the 13:07 mark McBride got to his knees while on the turf with his arms up at the 19-yard line, waiting for a pass interference call. None was thrown. McBride got to his feet and started barking at the line judge, Jeff Seeman, who was stationed at the 13-yard line in perfect view of the play. McBride then began to walk towards the line judge, jawing the entire time. The referee, who is situated behind the offense, also had a good view and did not throw his flag either. In the live feed, McBride was livid. Cardinals personnel had to pull him away from the line judge. Arizona was forced to punt. Since the conclusion of the Giants game, the NFL is in full review of the official’s apparent use of profanity directed at McBride in their little back-and-forth. Seeman was caught on camera cussing out McBride, who most likely was cussing out Seeman. It appears Seeman yelled out “F*** you” twice. Seeman is wearing a microphone. The NFLPA is asking the NFL to hold Seeman accountable for the verbal tirade. This kind of behavior from an official towards a player is unacceptable. Players are consistently held accountable when the roles are reversed. We expect the NFL to hold officials to the same standard. pic.twitter.com/vawHA8Jrlt — JC Tretter (@JCTretter) October 4, 2026 NFL players go through similar situations and suffer the consequences. The incompletion to McBride was obvious as Phillips pulled the tight end down as the ball approached. McBride normally has a pretty calm and cool demeanor during games, but it was evident what had happened with Seeman only six yards away from the action. The NFL Referees Association has not responded to any inquiries regarding this incident.

title: Beaks & Geeks: Cardinals, Giants Winners & Losers: Arizona on the doorstep again
summary: The Arizona Cardinals find themselves at a crossroads with their Week 4 matchup against the New York Football Giants. At 1-2-0, a loss would send the team into the abyss and getting to the surface wouldn’t be likely. There are a lot of exceptional teams on the Cardinals’ schedule coming up, so a win is […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - OCTOBER 04: Chad Ryland #38 of the Arizona Cardinals kicks a 60-yard field goal against the New York Giants during the first quarter at MetLife Stadium on October 04, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Arizona Cardinals find themselves at a crossroads with their Week 4 matchup against the New York Football Giants. At 1-2-0, a loss would send the team into the abyss and getting to the surface wouldn’t be likely. There are a lot of exceptional teams on the Cardinals’ schedule coming up, so a win is crucial. Having to travel and play on the road adds to the fact that Arizona needed a win in the worst way. RELATED: CAN THE CARDINALS TAKE ADVANTAGE OF AN AILING GIANTS ROSTER? The Cardinals were blown out by the Seattle Seahawks earlier in the season, but otherwise stayed in the game against the undefeated San Francisco 49ers last weekend. The team had plenty of opportunities to pull out a victory, but untimely penalties and trading field goals for touchdowns killed their offensive attack. Against the Giants, Arizona had several leads and was on the Giants’ four-yard line with 18 ticks left in the game, and could not score the touchdown in four downs in the 36-24 loss. So, who played well for the Cardinals? Who didn’t? ——————————————————————————– BEAKS Opening drive – This was a thing of beauty, and it looked like more of the same was on the way. Right off, KR Devin Duvernay ran the opening kickoff all the way back to Arizona’s 42. On third-and-10, QB Jacoby Brissett found WR Michael Wilson for 13 yards and into Giants territory. And that’s a Marv tuddy 🤫 📺: CBS pic.twitter.com/vLeYVCPB6c — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) October 4, 2026 Two great runs by RB Jeremiyah Love of 16 and 9 yards now put Arizona on New York’s 23. Two plays later, Brissett threw a dart to WR Marv Harrison in the back of the end zone for six. 8 plays, 58 yards, 3:52 of clock, and six points to start the contest. K Chad Ryland – In the UFL this past season, any kick of 60+ was worth four points. Ryland showed off his leg by nailing a 60-yarder as time expired right before halftime. Was also 3-3 on PATs, and only four of his kickoffs were returned. Great job. 🔒 @garrettismynam3 pic.twitter.com/WMDTM62gZA — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) October 4, 2026 NB Garrett Williams – As the first quarter was winding down, Williams nailed TE Isaiah Likely for a two-yard completion and then a one-yard completion that forced a field goal. With 10:07 left in the second quarter, Williams slapped the ball away from WR Braxton Berrios on a third-and-three that forced a punt. On the ensuing possession, he destroyed Likely, who had the first down. Had a solid second half. LB Jack Gibbens – The defender that nobody is talking about led the Cardinals in tackles once again with eight, and went bonnet to bonnet with RB Cam Skattebo in the third quarter, who only gained three. DT Walter Nolen – Very aggressive and played havoc with the Giants’ run game. Forced QB Jameis Winston to leave the pocket, which became a sack for DE Josh Sweat early in Quarter 1. Then on New York’s next possession, Nolen beat rookie RG Francis Mauigoa for his own sack. Four tackles, two tackles for loss, one QB hit, and the sack. Good penetration for much of the contest. Yeaaaaaah Budda 🗣️ 📺: CBS pic.twitter.com/s0FQTh3LI9 — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) October 4, 2026 S Budda Baker – All eyes on his pick. Destroyed WR Darnell Moody in the second quarter that could be heard out in the parking lot. Had five tackles and two pass defenses. ——————————————————————————— GEEKS The play that lost the game – Yes, the Cardinals were on the Giants’ four-yard line with 18 seconds left and down by six. But the series before was the game-killer. With 3:07 remaining, Arizona was down by three points and had a third-and-two at their own 11-yard line. An incomplete pass to TE Trey McBride forced the Cardinals to punt. The kick was down at the 50-yard line, which simply moved the Giants into field goal range and converted. This meant that now, instead of getting into field goal range for the tying points, it forced the Cardinals offense to score a touchdown. Which, they did not. This one play ended a drive that had over three minutes of clock left, gave New York excellent field position, and then basically gifted them three points. C Hjalte Froholdt – The seasoned veteran had no answer for NT C.J. Okoye, who was in the backfield on a ton of plays. Had one sack and five pressures. Lack of tight end play – McBride has a vertical jump of 33”. Elijah Higgins’ vert is 35”. Yet when Arizona gets inside the 10-yard line, not once did they lob the ball for a jump ball to either player. For one, they are being covered by a linebacker. Can a linebacker jump three feet off the ground? McBride had 12 targets and caught just seven. Brissett’s aim was off in today’s game. Higgins was having a great game, and then all of a sudden, the offense forgot about him. Two targets, two receptions mean he is focused and making a contribution, right? Higgins had that sensational catch-and-run in the fourth quarter and then in the third quarter corralled the touchdown pass. Pretty good numbers for just two catches, and crickets in the first half. Offense second quarter – Absolutely a dark time in this game. INT, punt, punt, INT, punt, FG. How does any team win games with those type of series? Play calling final four plays – The Cardinals offense was now down by six points. 2:11 was left on the clock with one timeout and the two-minute warning. Brissett completed several passes to Wilson and McBride, had an eight-yard sneak for a key first down, and was now on the Giants’ 26 with 55 seconds remaining. Two short completions and an 18-yard pass interference call on D Banks placed the ball on New York’s four-yard line with a first-and-goal and 27 seconds left. Four-down territory. Incomplete short left to Wilson. Incomplete short right to Wilson. Incomplete to a well-covered McBride. Then Brissett threw the pick that was intended for Wilson. The Cardinals have a 6’-4” tight end in McBride who can jump, and a 6’-3” tight end in Higgins who can jump, and yet all four passes were thrown chest high. Ally oop in the end zone had a much better chance of becoming the game-winner. QB Jacoby Brissett – Such a wonderful beginning, and such a horrible ending. Brissett was off on so many passes that we failed to keep up. With 6:20 in the first quarter, he threw a dart to Wilson for 20 yards, and then on the next possession he chunked it deep to Harrison, who was double-covered and had zero chance of making the catch. His second interception was simply a batted ball that landed in the hands of DE Arvell Reese, but the pick at the end of the game wasn’t even close to his target, Wilson. BANKS CLOSED ON SUNDAYS 📺: CBS/Paramount+ pic.twitter.com/Adh3ijHUwo — New York Giants (@Giants) October 4, 2026 He was sacked twice, but that number could have been three times that if Brissett hadn’t been nimble enough to get out of harm’s way. 21 of 35 for 166 yards, two TDs, three picks, and a 55.2 QB rating. Third down efficiency – When a team goes 4 for 12 in this category, nothing good happens. ———————————————————————————– Bird Seed – I’m afraid to say what’s next, because it might be worse… P Blake Gillikin – Not much distance on his punts today. He had six kicks as the Cardinals’ offense had issues maintaining drives. Gillikin’s average was a measly 43.2, with just one punt landing inside the 20 and zero touchbacks. He did sail one punt 52 yards. TOUCHDOWN 🏡 📺: CBS/Paramount+ pic.twitter.com/e9Tsph0lMX — New York Giants (@Giants) October 4, 2026 LB Mack Wilson – Was very active in the run-stoppage game, but the dude could not cover the tight end in today’s game. He bit on too many head bobs and found himself too many steps behind his guy. Finished with seven total tackles with one tackle for loss, and had…

title: Jacoby Brissett throws game away in Cardinals loss to Giants
summary: For the Arizona Cardinals it started out so promising. They ran 14 plays for 132 yards and two touchdowns to get out to a 14-3 lead. Then it seemed like nothing went right or their way the rest of the day. When you have a really questionable call on a defensive holding on a field […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - OCTOBER 04: Jacoby Brissett #7 of the Arizona Cardinals scrambles with the ball against the New York Giants during the fourth quarter at MetLife Stadium on October 04, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images) | Getty Images For the Arizona Cardinals it started out so promising. They ran 14 plays for 132 yards and two touchdowns to get out to a 14-3 lead. Then it seemed like nothing went right or their way the rest of the day. When you have a really questionable call on a defensive holding on a field goal, and then what seemed like an egregious non-call on a Jacoby Brissett pass attempt to Trey McBride, it is easy to say the referees were the reason for the loss, instead of looking at the issues. However, the issues were obvious. The Cardinals offense after the first two drives had 93 yards from scrimmage before the final drive of the game. The defense forced three turnovers and still gave up 30 points to a bad New York Giants offense. And in the biggest moment of the game, Jacoby Brissett and Mike LaFleur both folded. For the Arizona Cardinals, the 36-24 loss to the Giants was actually worse than the score. They were inept on offense, defense and special teams today, and that is why they are now 1-3. Trey McBride was once again a running back more than a receiver, with seven catches for 31 yards. Jeremiyah Love and Tyler Allgeier combined for 22 carries for 105 yards. And Michael Wilson had seven catches for 95 yards. Yet, when your quarterback goes for 166 yards passing on 35 attempts and throws three interceptions it’s going to be very difficult to win games. Onto the Detroit Lions.
