title: Browns Shedeur Sanders trade rumors: Logical, but unlikely based on Monday report
summary: The NFL schedule seems to always be in warp drive. With the first quarter of the season over (technically, that will not come until the end of the first quarter of Week 5), the Cleveland Browns are in first place in the AFC North and have the fourth seed in the current AFC playoff picture. […]
full_text: The NFL schedule seems to always be in warp drive. With the first quarter of the season over (technically, that will not come until the end of the first quarter of Week 5), the Cleveland Browns are in first place in the AFC North and have the fourth seed in the current AFC playoff picture . The return of QB Dillon Gabriel also leads to questions about how the team will handle their roster and potentially four quarterbacks. The Browns also still have two first-round picks, but the Los Angeles Rams also winning kept both of those picks far away from the Top 10 . For now, the focus is on the current season mostly. Besides a somewhat easy schedule for Cleveland , the second quarter of the NFL season leads into the NFL trade deadline on November 10th. If the Browns continue their winning ways, GM Andrew Berry could be apt to be a buyer at the deadline. Berry is also creative in his process, so Cleveland could also be a seller if offers make sense. As we’ve already seen in the NFL, the deadline isn’t the only thing that has spurred trade action. For the Browns, Gabriel’s pending return could lead to fellow QB Shedeur Sanders being on the move. Rumors kicked off once Sanders lost the quarterback battle with starting QB Deshaun Watson . This week, Dan Graziano of ESPN fueled those rumors a bit more : Young guys such as Anthony Richardson Sr., Stetson Bennett IV or, yes, even Shedeur Sanders could be interesting to teams looking for a developmental QB who needs a change of scenery. Always watch for under-the-radar QB trades at this time of year. Again, we’ve already had one. With Watson playing well and Gabriel returning, Berry could find a trade he finds acceptable for Sanders. There has been some conversation that Watson’s positive, not perfect, performance could be a positive indication for Sanders’ development. Mary Kay Cabot of Cleveland.com threw cold water on the embers of the Sanders rumors: Amid national and local speculation that the #Browns might trade Shedeur Sanders, throwing this report from last week out there again: #Browns have no plans to trade Shedeur Sanders or Dillon Gabriel. Same goes for WR Jerry Jeudy: –> https://t.co/1XlNTrTdAV — Mary Kay Cabot (@MaryKayCabot) October 5, 2026 As always, if someone makes them an offer they can't refuse, they'll pivot. But they currently don't intend to trade these 3. — Mary Kay Cabot (@MaryKayCabot) October 5, 2026 Astute Browns fans have already noted the similarity between this “no plans” language and that which was used surrounding DE Myles Garrett in the months prior to him being dealt. As always, it takes two to tango. While Sanders had his moments in 2025, his overall performance has been ranked at the bottom of the league multiple times . Sanders completed 57% of his passes last year as a rookie, for 1,400 yards, seven touchdowns, and 10 interceptions. The surrounding cast and offensive system did not help any of Cleveland’s quaterbacks last year, including Sanders. HC Todd Monken’s work with Watson, and Sanders pushing the veteran throughout training camp, could raise his stock in the league. The NFL has also seen injuries to quarterbacks each week, which could create an opening for a team to see what they have with Sanders. For now, Sanders rumors are smoldering and could heat up at any moment, especially whenever Gabriel is cleared to return to practice with his 21-day window opened. Do you think Sanders rumors will heat up and he’ll eventually be traded or think Cleveland will try to keep all four of their quarterbacks (active, practice squad and/or IR) through at least the trade deadline this year? title: Browns schedule: Road to 6-2, 7-1 is possible
summary: After a 3-1 start, the Cleveland Browns have an opportunity to extend their win streak over the next several weeks. Looking at the next four weeks of the Browns’ schedule, can they win three of their next four games to bring their record to 6-2? Duplicating the results from the first quarter of the season […]
full_text: After a 3-1 start , the Cleveland Browns have an opportunity to extend their win streak over the next several weeks. Looking at the next four weeks of the Browns’ schedule , can they win three of their next four games to bring their record to 6-2? Duplicating the results from the first quarter of the season would certainly multiply the excitement around Northeast Ohio heading into the holiday season. This stretch of games kicks off with an away game against the 1-3 New York Jets. Although playing on the road can be challenging, this should be a winnable game for Cleveland. The Jets’ offense struggled in their most recent matchup against the Chicago Bears, managing just 12 points. The Browns defense should look to make some big plays. The next game is a home game against the Baltimore Ravens. Cleveland is 3-2 against the Ravens at home over the last five seasons. Baltimore is also sitting at 3-1 right now, so this will certainly be a challenging matchup, but a win is not out of the question. The Tennessee Titans have yet to record a win this season, so the Browns should certainly be looking to get that win on the road. The Cleveland defense will give them a lot of problems. The final matchup in this stretch is a road game against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Playing in Pittsburgh is always a challenging environment. The Browns already have one win against the Steelers this season, so they will have a level of confidence going into this game. A win in Pittsburgh would be a massive accomplishment for this team. “The 6-2 (or 7-1) Cleveland Browns” on November 1st has a nice ring to it. The team will take the “one game at a time” moniker, but we get to look ahead and imagine what could be. Let me know what you think in the comments – Can the Browns win 3 of their next 4 games? full_text: (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns have a major opportunity to change the narrative about the team over the next two weeks. With Sunday’s game in the books, the Browns start the week tied with the Baltimore Ravens for first place in the AFC North Division. Up next for the Browns are the 1-3 New York Jets, a team in perpetual turmoil and riding a three-game losing streak. Beat the Jets, and that sets up a huge showdown at home the following week against the Ravens. That is putting the cart before the horse, of course, as things have not gone well for the Browns in their last two road games against the Jets. In 2020, COVID wiped out Cleveland’s wide receiver room, leaving quarterback Baker Mayfield throwing to Ja’Marcus Bradley and Marvin Hall in a seven-point loss. Last year, it was breakdowns on special teams – the Jets returned a kickoff and a punt for a touchdown – along with a defense that could not stop a New York offense unable to complete a pass to save its life, for another seven-point loss. If the Browns want to be taken seriously as contenders and not have Thursday’s win over the Pittsburgh Steelers be the highlight of the season, they need to stay focused on the task at hand and take care of business against the Jets. Then we can start talking about that first-place showdown with the Ravens. On to today’s edition of the Daily Dawg Chow! title: How many snaps for Jerry Jeudy, Jaleel McLaughlin have for Browns offense in win over Steelers?
summary: Finally, we saw a productive first half from the Browns’ offense, as they put 21 points on the board in the second quarter. That built a cushion that allowed them some breathing room when things didn’t go their way in the third quarter; but they still added two field goals late, thanks to the reliable […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - OCTOBER 1: Jaleel McLaughlin #38 of the Cleveland Browns reacts against the Pittsburgh Steelers prior to an NFL football game at Huntington Bank Field on October 1, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Finally, we saw a productive first half from the Browns’ offense, as they put 21 points on the board in the second quarter. That built a cushion that allowed them some breathing room when things didn’t go their way in the third quarter; but they still added two field goals late, thanks to the reliable leg of Andre Szmyt . Below, we analyze the snap counts and stats on offense for the Cleveland Browns ’ Week 4 game against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Quarterback Pos Player Plays % Snaps Stats QB Deshaun Watson 64 100% 24-of-33 (72.7%) for 268 yards, 1 TD, 1 INT. 7 carries, 22 yards (3.1 YPC), 1 fumble. This was another respectable performance by Deshaun Watson , with his 268 passing yards being the third most he’s had in a single game with Cleveland. His second quarter (along with the rest of the offense) was particularly great, and he again made enough plays on the final drive to get in position for a game winning field goal. In between, there were three rough plays: getting stripped by T.J. Watt on a read option, throwing an interception on the next series, and missing a wide open Harold Fannin late in a game that could’ve sealed the win sooner. The Fannin miss was the biggest issue. The turnovers sucked to see, but were relatively understandable in the realm of NFL turnovers, as opposed to the old, ‘wtf are you doing?’ plays. Watson received a grade of 62.9 from PFF. Running Back Pos Player Plays % Snaps Stats RB Quinshon Judkins 42 66% 17 carries, 53 yards (3.1 YPC), 1 TD. 6 catches, 43 yards (7 targets). RB Raheim Sanders 22 34% 2 carries, 9 yards (4.5 YPC). 2 catches, 7 yards (2 targets). FB Michael Burton 9 14% No stats registered. RB Jaleel McLaughlin 1 2% 1 carry, 28 yards (28.0 YPC), 1 TD. How about that stat line for Jaleel McLaughlin ? One snap, one carry, and it goes for a 28 yard touchdown run. The blocking by the receivers on that play was very nice. Quinshon Judkins ran a hair better this week, but there’s still lots of room for improvement. He looked better when he was in space catching a career-high 6 passes. In their 9 pass blocking snaps, Judkins and Raheim Sanders graded horribly against the Steelers, per PFF. Wide Receiver Pos Player Plays % Snaps Stats WR Denzel Boston 61 95% 4 catches, 89 yards (7 targets). WR KC Concepcion 59 92% 6 catches, 43 yards (7 targets). WR Jerry Jeudy 24 38% 3 catches, 36 yards (3 targets). WR Malachi Corley 14 22% No stats registered. WR Isaiah Bond 7 11% No stats registered. I wouldn’t call it a rough start for Denzel Boston , but Watson put two long balls right on the money for him, and he wasn’t able to haul either one in. They stuck with him, and it paid off. His hands are great to watch, the confidence that he’ll secure those clutch catches. KC Concepcion got the ball in space and made some guy miss. When he gets more acclimated to the speed of the NFL, I think we’ll see more of those plays with success. The reps for Jerry Jeudy took a further hit this week, down to 38%. But he also caught all 3 passes that went his way late, and they were big grabs. Hopefully the combination of winning, and seeing how his timely grabs can make a big impact, keeps him motivated, because he can still be a huge asset. He was the team’s third-highest graded player on offense by PFF, grading out to a 79.9. Malachi Corley received the reps that Tylan Wallace was getting, and he did a nice job on a few blocks. Tight End Pos Player Plays % Snaps Stats TE Harold Fannin 57 89% 3 catches, 27 yards (5 targets), 1 TD. TE Blake Whiteheart 22 34% No stats registered. TE Carsen Ryan 1 2% No stats registered. It was another productive day for Harold Fannin , who caught a short touchdown. On the play he was wide open on late, if Watson connected with him, that probably could’ve gone for like 40 yards. Blake Whiteheart did not fare well in his run blocking. You have to wonder at some point if the team will try to get a better run blocking tight end. Offensive Line Pos Player Plays % Snaps Stats OL Spencer Fano 64 100% OL Zion Johnson 64 100% OL Elgton Jenkins 64 100% OL Austin Barber 64 100% OL Tytus Howard 64 100% OL Zak Zinter 1 2% It was a rebound performance for rookie RG Austin Barber, who was the Browns’ top-graded player on offense by PFF, grading out to an 82.6. In the breakdown, his run blocking was excellent, but his pass protection was actually among the lowest graded. It was also a hell of a job by C Luke Wypler filling in. He was the Browns’ second-highest graded player on offense by PFF, grading out to a 79.9. You don’t want to ship away quality backup linemen often, but with the team drafting Parker Brailsford , that’s the type of performance by Wypler to where if a team’s center goes down, he might be a trade candidate.

title: Cowboys perfect red zone day enough to even record in Houston
summary: The 0-3 Houston Texans may have been the team carrying the “desperate” label into Sunday’s early kickoff against the Dallas Cowboys, but after the first 30 minutes of play, the visiting Cowboys at 1-2 sure found themselves in a desperate spot as well. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer’s team was back on the field for the […]
full_text: Photo by Tim Warner/Getty Images | Getty Images The 0-3 Houston Texans may have been the team carrying the “desperate” label into Sunday’s early kickoff against the Dallas Cowboys, but after the first 30 minutes of play, the visiting Cowboys at 1-2 sure found themselves in a desperate spot as well. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer’s team was back on the field for the first time since that loss in Brazil, one that fell in the lap of coaching at large, the offense squandering a great opportunity to take a late lead, and defense giving up one too many gash plays. Through 30 minutes in Houston, it looked like the Cowboys hadn’t learned any lessons in any of these areas, and trailed 16-6 to a Texans team that was never going to flinch at being 0-3, having been in this spot a year ago. There were also few indicators from the first half that the Cowboys would fight back into a very similar position from the Ravens game, the ball in Dak Prescott and the offense’s hands in the red zone with a chance to take the lead at the end. The Cowboys did play themselves into this spot though, and this time got the go-ahead touchdown on CeeDee Lamb’s 17th catch of the game, plus the stop to follow to win 34-30. From ESPN Research: The Cowboys had lost 32 straight road games when trailing by double digits in the second half, which was the longest active streak of its kind in the NFL. — Todd Archer (@toddarcher) October 4, 2026 Let’s get to our notes on how it happened, with the Cowboys now facing a short week to prepare for another winless team – the now 0-4 Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Corner Up, Corner Down The Cowboys were very depleted in the secondary coming into this game, and to make matters worse for them the Texans welcomed their star wide receiver Nico Collins back to the lineup to face this banged up pass defense. This mismatch showed itself very early, in fact as early as possible with Collins making a 45-yard catch on the first play from scrimmage. Houston caught Reddy Steward lined up against Collins for this big play, and then hit Collins again in the red zone against DaRon Bland to cap off the drive with seven points. Bland did not have his best game, but part of the reason why is actually encouraging in an overall sense for Christian Parker’s defense. The higher volume of throws that Bland faced was partly a result of the newly traded for Joey Porter Jr. inserting himself into the lineup and having a great debut. There were questions about how Porter would fit this scheme, but he came in and played well immediately. This shifts some of those scheme fit concerns to the veteran Bland, who has battled through injury to be part of multiple scheme changes defensively in Dallas. Joey Porter Jr. in his Cowboys debut, per @SumerSports : 24 snaps 0 targets 0 receptions allowed 0 yards allowed — Underdog NFL (@UnderdogNFL) October 5, 2026 There have been multiple big plays allowed by Bland this season where he appeared not on the same page with the rest of the coverage, or playing the wrong leverage. This happened on Collins’ touchdown, where Bland and rookie Caleb Downs were out of sync. The Cowboys defense is still searching for it’s first interception of the season, and teams being forced to throw near Bland more can bring takeaways in bunches, but right now his inconsistencies on a down-to-down basis paired with an inconsistent pass rush are worrisome for how well this defense can hold up for long stretches. Defending Long Fields Speaking of the defense holding up, the Cowboys defense was handed multiple gifts early in this game via Texans special teams penalties that backed them up and gave them long fields. If there was any doubt about it before this game, there should be zero now that this Cowboys team is again built to play through their offense. The defense supporting this by flipping some of these long fields into short fields for Dak Prescott would be a very welcome sight, but also for the second week in a row they had trouble doing so. The Texans got points on their first two drives of the game that started at their own 15- and 8-yard lines, as well as the fourth quarter touchdown to put them up 30-27, starting at their 13. The splash negative plays from this defense are coming in later downs or short-yardage situations, which is still a very good thing, but opposing offenses are leaning on this defense with their run games in early downs and getting them off-balance in manageable down and distances. The drive that started at the eight-yard line for Houston and ended in a field goal had a field-flipping play against Bland, when Jaylin Noel beat him on an out and up route for 52 yards. The Cowboys had Von Miller and Malachi Lawrence on the field for this play as their edge rushers, and neither got remotely close to Stroud, allowing the double move deep route to develop. Not Picking up the Defense The counterpoint to this is that the Cowboys offense continued on a concerning trend carrying over from the Ravens game as well. In that loss, the defense forced three separate three and outs. The offense got the ball back in these spots and kicked a field goal in the red zone, missed a field goal, and went three and out themselves. In Houston, the Dallas defense got back-to-back three and outs in the second quarter, and the offense punted after the first one and missed a field goal after the second on Will Anderson’s block. The Cowboys would miss another long range field goal on their next drive following this sequence too, and to the defense’s credit they bowed up and held Houston to six points out of the two drives where the Texans had their best starting field position of the game. The Cowboys punt would come even after they escaped a 3rd-and-22 and intentional grounding penalty thanks to a Texans penalty. Schottenheimer getting too cute with the play calls again would pop up at an inopportune time, losing five yards on first down to a CeeDee Lamb reverse, then asking Jake Ferguson to block Will Anderson on second down – another incomplete pass to Lamb. Ferguson’s blocking at the point of attack has been a major red flag within the heavier personnel sets the Cowboys have still been at their best offensively in. Ferguson needs to be included in the downfield passing concepts, but defenses should continue to force him to block out of these looks after seeing the Texans tape. Late in the fourth quarter, the Cowboys offense had the ball back with a four point lead and chance to really seize control of the game by at least chewing some more clock. They possessed it for only 1:45 on a three and out of their own, after Ferguson had a terrible chip block against Anderson on third down. All his block did was give Anderson more of a direct rush past Terence Steele and into Prescott’s lap, deflecting Dak’s pass incomplete. Red Zone Excellence The Cowboys immediately cut into the Texans lead coming out of the locker room with a four-play touchdown drive, and the play sequencing was a thing of beauty – starting with a nice return by KaVontae Turpin as well. A play-action pass to Lamb got them into the red zone, and Javonte Williams finished it off with his first of three touchdowns. We already mentioned Steele’s inconsistency at right tackle, and on the left side Tyler Guyton had a plus game, but it was the Cowboys interior offensive line that struggled most often in this game. Instead of bashing their head against the wall in the red area where things are condensed, the Cowboys pulled guard T.J. Bass and center Cooper Beebe to take the Texans interior defenders out of the play by design. These two linemen paved the way on a toss for Williams to score. Dallas would need more of these scores from Williams after the Texans got a big kick return of their own and answered back with another Nico Collins touchdown, and his second touchdown took the Cowboys off the hook a little bit for not-as-great sequencing in the red zone this time. George Pickens had the 54-yard catch to get…

title: Cowboys at Texans: CeeDee Lamb is currently the NFL’s best wide receiver
summary: After a demoralizing loss in Brazil to the Baltimore Ravens, the Dallas Cowboys came into Sunday’s matchup against the Houston Texans as a desperate team. Since the 2015 season, 14.9% of teams have made the playoffs after starting 1-3 (13 of 87) versus 43.3% of teams that started 2-2 (45 of 104).  If Dallas lost […]
full_text: (Photo by David Buono/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images After a demoralizing loss in Brazil to the Baltimore Ravens, the Dallas Cowboys came into Sunday’s matchup against the Houston Texans as a desperate team. Since the 2015 season, 14.9% of teams have made the playoffs after starting 1-3 (13 of 87) versus 43.3% of teams that started 2-2 (45 of 104). If Dallas lost this game and fell to 1-3, their playoff hopes would start to slip away just four weeks into the regular season. Thankfully, the Cowboys bounced back in a big way from the heartbreaking loss last Sunday, delivering a 34-30 victory over the Texans. Dallas’ offense was the star of the show in the second half of Sunday, led by five-time Pro Bowl receiver CeeDee Lamb. The seven-year pro put the Cowboys on his back, posting a career day and earning this week’s game ball award. Lamb put together one of the best receiver performances of the past decade in Houston. The 27-year-old caught a career-high 17 passes for 189 yards to go with scoring the game-winning touchdown late in the fourth quarter. HUGE CEEDEE TD 🔥 #DallasCowboys | @_CeeDeeThree 📺: #DALvsHOU on FOX 📲: Stream on NFL+ https://t.co/XM2vIx7C1d pic.twitter.com/pQcMzqN4BZ — Dallas Cowboys (@dallascowboys) October 4, 2026 While this was undoubtedly his best performance of the year, Lamb’s performance on Sunday was a continuation of an unbelievable start to his 2026 campaign. Four games in, Lamb has recorded 37 receptions for 498 yards, both the most in the NFL, to go with four receiving touchdowns. Lamb’s has already surpassed his previous career-high of 332 receiving yards through four regular-season games from last season. CeeDee Lamb's first four games: 2020 – 21 Rec, 309 Yds, 2 TD 2021 – 20 Rec, 264 Yds, 1 TD 2022 – 23 Rec, 288 Yds, 2 TD 2023 – 23 Rec, 309 Yds, 1 TD 2024 – 20 Rec, 316 Yds, 2 TD 2025 – 21 Rec, 332 Yds, 1 TD 2026 – 37 Rec, 498 Yds, 4 TD pic.twitter.com/NpejrEvtYH — Bobby Belt (@BobbyBeltTX) October 4, 2026 There is no denying that Lamb looked like the best receiver in the National Football League on Sunday in Houston. He did everything a true generational receiver is supposed to do, including taking over the game when his team needed him most. There is some hope that the Cowboys will figure things out defensively as the season unfolds, but it is becoming increasingly clear that this team is going to have to be carried by its offense. That may seem like a tall task, but if Lamb continues to play at this level, he has the ability to make up for the team’s shortcomings on defense and help lead Dallas to a historic season on the offensive side of the ball. For now, the message is simple: CeeDee Lamb is playing on a different level, and the Cowboys are going to go as far as he can carry them. Right now, it’s CeeDee Lamb’s world—and everyone else is just living in it.
author: Matthew Holleran

title: Cowboys at Texans Stock Report: CeeDee Lamb leads the way
summary: The Dallas Cowboys won the Texas State Championship on Sunday, and whether or not beating the in-state Houston Texans means anything extra to you, it stands to reason that wins in general do. Sunday’s victory was very needed for the Cowboys to stop the bleeding that began down in Rio when they lost to the […]
full_text: Mandatory Credit: Thomas Shea-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Dallas Cowboys won the Texas State Championship on Sunday, and whether or not beating the in-state Houston Texans means anything extra to you, it stands to reason that wins in general do. Sunday’s victory was very needed for the Cowboys to stop the bleeding that began down in Rio when they lost to the Baltimore Ravens. There is no rest for the weary though as they are back in action just a few days from now on Thursday night against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Before we fully shift focus to Tampa Bay, we need to properly tie a bow on the win in Houston. Several players really shined where others left us wanting more. Here is our stock report from Sunday’s win. Let’s begin. Stock Up: CeeDee Lamb What can you really say at this point? CeeDee Lamb was a true and total alpha in Houston. He did whatever he wanted, and Next Gen Stats noted that he recorded multiple receptions against six different Texans defenders . Think about how absurd that is. Lamb was entrusted with the game on the line, and well before it, to deliver and he absolutely did. He is living up to all hype and fanfare that people have had around him, and it feels like we are seeing the best version he has ever offered throughout his Cowboys career which is really saying something. Stock Up: Joey Porter Jr. It took all of five seconds for everyone involved to realize/remember that JPJ is the best cornerback on the Cowboys roster. All told it was still a wading in for Porter as he was just acquired by the Cowboys this past week, but he played 19 snaps while in coverage and did not allow a single reception against a single target. It was evident that Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud was avoiding him at all costs. That is what the Cowboys paid for. They went out to get someone to neutralize one side of the field, and they have it now. Stock Up: Tyler Guyton There really was a time, not too long ago, when we doubted whether or not Tyler Guyton would actually be the left tackle on this team. Heck, head coach Brian Schottenheimer openly declared in the offseason that Nate Thomas was competing with Guyton for the job. That is the same Nate Thomas who got traded to the Texans in roster cutdowns and was inactive for this game. Having the left side of the offensive line so stable is such a peaceful thing. It will improve even more when Tyler Smith returns to the lineup. Don’t forget about that. Stock Up: George Pickens Four games into this season we have yet to see George Pickens have the exact same impact that CeeDee Lamb has, but he is easily making his mark. Consider that the Cowboys’ game-winning drive would not have happened to the extent that it did without a huge gain from Pickens. Heck, consider that his 53-yard reception early in the second half was part of what woke the offense up at large. Pickens is giving the Cowboys his all and delivering when called upon. Stock Up: Ryan Flournoy This was arguably Ryan Flournoy’s best game since joining the Cowboys. The sample size there isn’t exactly large, but we have long believed that he could/should exist as a proper third option in the passing game and that’s exactly what he was in Houston. Sometimes the opposing defense is taking so many things away and wreaking havoc in a number of different directions. You have to have that person who helps keep things moving right along, and that’s what Flo was in this game. Stock Up: Quinnen Williams The last two games have shown the Quinnen Williams who the Cowboys traded for and extended. He is turning into the defensive game-wrecker that his reputation said he was with the New York Jets. Maybe it was a matter of gelling across time, but it feels fair to assume that this is the player who is here to stay. Clearly we hope that. is the case. Williams kept things in check, especially as the second half wore on and the game got tight. That’s his job and he did it very well. Static Stock: Brian Schottenheimer It has been a while since I handed out a static stock, but I believe Brian Schottenheimer is deserving in this instance. The first half was pretty terrible. Specifically, the sequence at the end of it. Schottenheimer gambled in letting Brandon Aubrey attempt a 65-yard field goal right after having a 62-yard one blocked, and the miss gave Houston short field position that they converted into a field goal to send everyone to their respective locker rooms. But Schotty locked in as the game wore on. He pledged all week to not let last week, as in the Ravens loss, define him. He said he would not hold the team back the way that he believed he did against Baltimore in Rio. Eerily, the Cowboys faced almost an identical situation as the game wore on. Their offense went three and out when they could have iced the game with a four-point lead, and they took over with around two minutes left down by three. This time, unlike last, Schotty entrusted and enabled his superstars and the Cowboys won as a result. That is legitimate growth. So the beginning was rough, but the end was great. So long as they are in that order and lead to a win, that’s what matters. Stock Down: DaRon Bland This is another instance where there really isn’t a ton to say. Joey Porter Jr. is incredible, but his incredible-ness means that opposing quarterbacks are going to attack DaRon Bland early and often. C.J. Stroud did so and was highly successful as a result of it. There is no question that Bland is among the weaker points of the Cowboys roster at the moment. That is a huge issue that they are going to have to address if they don’t want to be in similar circumstances moving forward. Stock Down: Brandon Aubrey You can certainly argue that his 62-yard field goal was blocked because Will Anderson Jr. is incredible, and you can similarly claim that a 65-yard field goal is difficult to pull off and that being asked to do it right after a block is not ideal. But it feels like we move the goalposts a lot for Aubrey, no pun intended. It feels like we let his reputation tell us we are being too harsh when moments of constructive criticism come up. It can be true that those circumstances were not ideal and that as the NFL’s highest-paid kicker he should be successful nonetheless. He wasn’t and that’s a problem. Stock Down: Nick Sorensen At the moment the Cowboys have one of the worst and least efficient special teams operations across the NFL. Nick Sorensen has been under fire even dating back to last year, and that temperature is only rising as a result of the messes we are seeing. We regard the Cowboys’ special teams as great because of the visible pieces in the aforementioned Aubrey, KaVontae Turpin, and even Bryan Anger. But the operation is clunky. How? How can this really be possible? Are they missing a veteran on the field in C.J. Goodwin? Does Nick Sorensen need to do more? Whatever the answer is, they have to find it immediately.

title: 5 key plays from Cowboys win over the Texans
summary: Another week, another harrowing finish for the Dallas Cowboys. They needed this one desperately to avoid a 1-3 start, and through the heroics of CeeDee Lamb and Dak Prescott, they hung on in a 34-30 thriller. Even better, the Los Angeles Rams did them a favor by beating the Philadelphia Eagles, so it was a […]
full_text: Another week, another harrowing finish for the Dallas Cowboys. They needed this one desperately to avoid a 1-3 start, and through the heroics of CeeDee Lamb and Dak Prescott, they hung on in a 34-30 thriller. Even better, the Los Angeles Rams did them a favor by beating the Philadelphia Eagles, so it was a good day as the Cowboys won and it wasn’t so sunny in Philadelphia. The clutch victory came down to several pivotal moments. Here are the five key plays that delivered the much-needed win. Lamb’s 30-yard pickup jump-starts the second-half offensive flurry Down 16-6 at the break, the Cowboys had themselves largely to blame. A blocked 62-yard field-goal attempt late in the second quarter gave Houston a chance to tack on three more points, and the Texans took a 10-point lead into intermission. For most of the first half, Dallas’ offense couldn’t do anything right against Houston’s pass rush. The tide turned on the opening possession of the third quarter. After a pair of successful runs, the Cowboys dialed up play-action. Prescott sold the fake, stepped up to elude Will Anderson and the edge pressure, and found an open Lamb in a soft spot in the middle of the defense for 30 yards. That connection put Dallas deep in the red zone. On the next snap, Javonte Williams scored the first of his three touchdowns behind strong offensive-line blocking. The play ignited an offense that stayed on fire the rest of the afternoon. Lassiter lassoes Pickens There are few things George Pickens does better than catching contested balls and drawing flags. After hauling in a spectacular 53-yard grab over Kamari Lassiter, Pickens kept working. On third-and-7 deep in the red zone, Lassiter was flagged for defensive pass interference as Pickens worked off the line, giving the Cowboys a fresh set of downs at the one. Lassiter looked stunned, as did many of the Houston fans. Three plays later, on fourth-and-goal, Lassiter grabbed Pickens’ jersey for a holding penalty that kept the drive alive. Williams punched it in on the next play to cut the deficit to three. Without those two flags, Dallas likely would have failed to score on the possession. Given how the Cowboys’ defense has performed this season, Houston could easily have answered with a long drive to widen the gap even further. Lassiter’s inability to play clean football proved costly. Parker dials up the right call Christian Parker’s tenure as defensive coordinator has drawn plenty of criticism, even with the unit depleted by injuries. Communication breakdowns and coverage issues have been recurring problems, especially in zone. After the Cowboys closed the gap to 23-20, Parker needed a stop. Facing third-and-8 from their own 42, Houston was one conversion away from field-goal range for Ka’imi Fairbairn. Parker sent pressure that overloaded the middle and brought Dee Winters off the edge. The blitz was in C.J. Stroud’s face immediately; the quarterback had just enough time to scramble and throw the ball away. Dallas capitalized on the ensuing possession to take its first lead of the game. Pitre can’t come up with the pick The comeback nearly died before it fully arrived. On the game-winning drive, Prescott went looking for Lamb in a tight window. Jalen Pitre broke on the throw and had a real chance at the interception, but the ball slipped through his hands. Had Pitre secured it, the Cowboys would have faced roughly 2:10 remaining and needed a defensive stop after already burning a timeout on a failed challenge earlier. Instead, the drive stayed alive, and Dallas eventually took the lead for good. Houston’s 13 penalties created multiple self-inflicted wounds, but none will haunt them more than the one that got away. Dak to Lamb for the win Of course the game-winner has to close the list. Time and again, Dallas found Lamb in favorable matchups against the Texans secondary. With the game on the line, they went back to the well one more time. Isolated in the slot against Pitre, Lamb got separation. Prescott, with solid protection, scanned the field and delivered a strike into the end zone. The 12-yard touchdown with 40 seconds left gave Lamb his 17th catch of the day, a career high and the second-most receptions in a single game in franchise history. Dallas held on through Stroud’s final Hail Mary attempt to improve to 2-2. Lamb’s performance felt like something out of a movie, and the final catch delivered the Hollywood ending the Cowboys desperately needed.
author: LP Cruz

title: 10 thoughts on the Cowboys win over the Texans
summary: Did you really expect anything less from the Dallas Cowboys than a game that would push your heart rate to maximum capacity? At times it was frustrating, other times exhilarating, but in the end, the Cowboys pulled off a thrilling 34-30 come-from-behind victory over the Houston Texans, providing fans with another wild late-game finish. There […]
full_text: Photo by Alex Slitz/Getty Images | Getty Images Did you really expect anything less from the Dallas Cowboys than a game that would push your heart rate to maximum capacity? At times it was frustrating, other times exhilarating, but in the end, the Cowboys pulled off a thrilling 34-30 come-from-behind victory over the Houston Texans, providing fans with another wild late-game finish. There is never any shortage of excitement with this football team. Regardless, they got the win, and here are 10 thoughts on this almost disappointing, but then very satisfying, chaotic game. 1. Better late than never It was a tale of two offenses for the Cowboys. In the first half, all they could muster was field goal attempts, and a couple of those did not go well. All the Cowboys had to show for their efforts was six measly points in the first half. Sideline reporter Pam Oliver mentioned at halftime that offensive coordinator Brian Schottenheimer was not fazed, and considering what we saw next, we now understand why. The Cowboys offense completely came to life, scoring four second-half touchdowns, including three straight to start the half and the game-winner to close it out. Thank you, offense. 2. CeeDee is sensational If there was any doubt that CeeDee Lamb had not returned to his spectacular self, today’s game served as another reminder. He was all over the field, finishing the game with 17 catches for 189 yards and a touchdown. He came just one catch shy of tying the single-game reception record for the Cowboys set by Jason Witten with 18 back in 2012. Lamb was incredible, coming up with big catches and huge runs after the catch. The Texans had no answer for him. 3. Finishing The Cowboys’ offense had some questionable play-calling last week as the unit sputtered near the goal line on a couple of drives when they abandoned the running game. Not this week. Dallas attacked the goal line with far more ferocity, resulting in not one, not two, but three rushing touchdowns by Javonte Williams. It was nice to see them finish things off with some physical football instead of trying to get cute and petering out. 4. Giving up big plays The Cowboys’ defense just can’t help itself sometimes, constantly giving up big plays. On each of Houston’s first two drives, the defense allowed a play of 45 yards or more. First, C.J. Stroud connected with Nico Collins for a 45-yard completion. On their next possession, DaRon Bland got beat on a double move, resulting in a 52-yard completion to Jaylin Noel. Coming into this game, the Texans hadn’t had a single play over 35 yards all season. Leave it to the Cowboys’ defense to help an opponent break a dry spell. 5. Can’t block on FGs For the second straight week, the Cowboys special teams unit has allowed a defender to sneak through and block a field goal. Last week, we could point our fingers at a possible offsides penalty, but this week, there were no excuses. The interior line allowed Will Anderson Jr. to waltz through and get his hands up to block the kick from Brandon Aubrey. That was a costly six-point swing as it took away a field goal from Dallas and eventually led to one for Houston. 6. Special teams struggles The special teams struggled on several occasions in this game. Besides the block, Aubrey also missed a field goal that gave the Texans great field position, resulting in a field goal late in the first half. This group was also highly influential in the return game for both teams. The Cowboys opened the second half with a nice return from KaVontae Turpin, and the offense quickly turned that into a touchdown. Unfortunately, the Texans answered immediately with a great kickoff return of their own from Jaylin Noel, which also resulted in a touchdown. 7. Defensive groove It was a struggle at times, but the Cowboys’ defense did eventually start to settle in and make stops. If you don’t count the instances where the special teams left them with terrible starting field position, the defense had a nice stretch where they were making plays. In those situations, they put together four straight possessions where they allowed four plays or fewer and forced the Texans’ offense off the field. That was a welcome sight. 8. Another late collapse? Unfortunately, all those key defensive stops did not mean as much when they allowed the Texans to drive down the field and put together what almost became the game-winning drive. Houston moved the ball 87 yards on nine plays and was aided by a clever hook-and-ladder play on a crucial third-and-14. It felt like the defense was finally going to make a big stop, but allowing them to convert on third and long was a kick to the stomach. The Texans scored on the very next play on a six-yard touchdown run by Woody Marks, putting Dallas in a major hole. 9. Finding a way When the Texans scored the go-ahead touchdown to go up 30-27 with just over two minutes left, it looked eerily similar to last week’s game when the Ravens jumped ahead late. Cowboys fans were asking themselves the exact same question they asked last week, which was whether the offense had one last drive left in them. Just like last week, the answer was yes, but unlike last week, the Cowboys finished things up with a touchdown rather than settling for the tying field goal. We enjoyed that much better. 10. Always a sweat Admit it, you were on pins and needles when the Texans got the ball back with 37 seconds left in the game. The odds were certainly in favor of Dallas, but after what we witnessed last week, we were not taking anything for granted. While we could not rest easy until we saw the ball hit the ground on the final Hail Mary attempt, it always has to be a sweat with this team.
author: Dan Rogers

title: Cowboys news: Dallas wins a shootout on a game-winning drive by Dak Prescott
summary: Following the last-second heartbreak last week, and staring down the barrel of a tough upcoming schedule, the 1-2 Cowboys needed a win in week three. And they got it. Behind CeeDee Lamb’s career day, Dak Prescott posting a great second half, and the defense closing it out when they needed them, Dallas got it done. […]
full_text: Photo by Alex Slitz/Getty Images Following the last-second heartbreak last week, and staring down the barrel of a tough upcoming schedule, the 1-2 Cowboys needed a win in week three. And they got it. Behind CeeDee Lamb’s career day, Dak Prescott posting a great second half, and the defense closing it out when they needed them, Dallas got it done. Joey Porter Jr., Dallas’ recent acquisition, not only played but, according to NextGen stats, had a great debut. Cowboys 34 Texans 30: A Needed Win- Cody Warren, Inside The Star Falling to 1-3, even this early in the season, would have put the Cowboys in an early hole. However, the offense got the job done and the defense did just enough to escape Houston with a win. The defense finally settled down enough in the second quarter to force consecutive three-and-outs. After the frustrating first quarter, I will give them credit. They gave the offense chances they didn’t take advantage of. Instead, we watched Brandon Aubrey trot out four different times. He made 39 and 50-yard field goals. Followed by a Will Anderson Jr. blocked 62-yard attempt and missed from 65. I can’t blame Aubrey for the miss, but I am irritated the offense couldn’t do anything. 8 instant reactions to Cowboys’ heart-stopping win vs. the Texans- Jerry Trotta, The Landry Hat With another week in the books, we now have a clearer picture of who the 2026 Dallas Cowboys are. So what did we learn during week four’s exciting victory? 1. Why is DaRon Bland covering Nico Collins in the red zone? The Texans polished off a commanding eight-play, 85-yard opening drive with a Nico Collins touchdown from C.J. Stroud. Returning from a two-game absence, Collins beat DaRon Bland off the line of scrimmage, and Caleb Downs traveled with the underneath crossing route, leaving Bland in 1-on-1 coverage. title: Cowboys vs. Texans: The good, the bad, and the ugly from Week 4
summary: For the second week in a row, the Dallas Cowboys played a game down to the wire. Thankfully, they were able to do enough to improve to 2-2 on the season and hopefully it will help kickstart a long-lasting win streak. Only time will tell though. Getting the “W” in the interstate rivalry with Houston […]
full_text: Photo by Tim Warner/Getty Images | Getty Images For the second week in a row, the Dallas Cowboys played a game down to the wire. Thankfully, they were able to do enough to improve to 2-2 on the season and hopefully it will help kickstart a long-lasting win streak. Only time will tell though. Getting the “W” in the interstate rivalry with Houston Texans was the main goal, but it wasn’t always pretty. Below is our good, bad, and ugly from Week 4. THE GOOD – WR CeeDee Lamb Javonte Williams deserves a shoutout here for his three touchdown performance, but it was CeeDee Lamb who had the biggest impact on the game as well as ultimately sealing the victory for the Cowboys. No. 88 had himself a day against the Texans Sunday afternoon, catching a career-high 17 passes resulting in 189 receiving yards and scoring the game-winning TD. He continues to be Dak Prescott’s favorite target/security blanket in the passing game and hopefully continues to be highly productive as the season progresses. THE BAD – RT Terence Steele The Cowboys entire offensive line struggled against the Texans defensive front Sunday afternoon, but Terence Steele played poorly in this Week 4 matchup and had to get help much of the game. No. 78 has been somewhat of a liability in pass protection for what seems like years now, and yet, the Cowboys haven’t had a better option to replace him. They traded for Broderick Jones, but so far it looks like they don’t think he is any better. THE UGLY – Penalties for the Texans The Cowboys are usually the team getting beat because of penalties. Not on Sunday. The Texans committed 13 penalties for 90 yards in the game. They committed them in the endzone to gift Dallas a score. They gave the Cowboys four first downs on penalties. They put themselves in terrible field position with penalties on kickoff returns. The timing of some of their penalties couldn’t have been worse. It was ugly.

title: Both CB Pat Surtain II and WR Pat Bryant suffered short-term ankle injuries
summary: Great news! According to NFL Network’s lead league insider Ian Rapoport, both cornerback Pat Surtain II and wide receiver Pat Bryant suffered short-term ankle injuries during Sunday’s loss to the 49ers. Surtain II left the field after suffering a non-contact ankle injury. Many feared the worst there, but thankfully, he avoided a serious injury. As […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 4: Pat Surtain II #2 of the Denver Broncos gets set during the second quarter of an NFL football game against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium on October 4, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Great news! According to NFL Network’s lead league insider Ian Rapoport, both cornerback Pat Surtain II and wide receiver Pat Bryant suffered short-term ankle injuries during Sunday’s loss to the 49ers. Surtain II left the field after suffering a non-contact ankle injury. Many feared the worst there, but thankfully, he avoided a serious injury. As for Bryant, we already learned he will miss a “few weeks” due to a sprained ankle , but this confirmation is great to hear. ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler is reporting that Surtain II is “week-to-week” and that one source believes he will be sidelined for about two weeks. The #Broncos received some good news on both star CB Pat Surtain II and on WR Pat Bryant from their MRIs today, sources say. They avoided worst-case scenario on both of their ankle injuries and both absences are expected to be short-term. pic.twitter.com/2V6vduTbew — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) October 5, 2026 Honestly, this is great news for both players. After a tough loss to the 49ers and their pesky injury-creating substitution, the fear was that the Broncos may have lost both players for the entire season. Surtain II suffered a non-contact injury and was unable to put much weight on his ankle and needed to be helped off the field. As for Bryant, his knee/ankle bent awkwardly, and he was eventually carted off the field. It did not look great for either player, but again, this is great news. It remains to be seen if one or both players will be placed on the short-term injured reserve, but we should find that out in the coming days. With Surtain II sidelined, look for 2025 first-round pick Jahdae Barron to fill in as a starter. He came in as relief for Surtain II on Sunday and played well. He made a few nice plays in coverage and also had a few big hits on 49ers ball carriers. A lot has been made of his limited snap counts this season, but now he will have an opportunity to prove himself against the Chargers and Seahawks. We still haven’t had an update on Riley Moss and his ribs, but if he cannot play, Kris Abrams-Draine will fill in for him as he did on Sunday. The Broncos corner depth will be tested early on this season. I already touched on the loss of Pat Bryant, but the fact it is only a short-term injury is great news. Bryant has become one of the more productive and consistent pass catchers on the team, and his loss is a hit to the already inconsistent Denver Broncos passing game. Reserves Troy Franklin, Marvin Mims Jr., and Lil’Jordan Humphrey will be tasked with filling in for Bryant these next couple of games, at least. At the end of the day, this is the best-case scenario for the Broncos. Both injuries looked bad, but they escaped major injuries and are expected back sooner rather than later.
author: Scotty Payne

title: Broncos WR Pat Bryant suffered a sprained ankle and will miss a ‘few weeks’
summary: According to ESPN’s lead NFL insider Adam Schefter, Denver Broncos wide receiver Pat Bryant suffered a sprained ankle during the Broncos’ loss to the 49ers on Sunday and is expected to miss “a few weeks”. Bryant was carted off the field after the injury, which did not look all that good on the replay, and […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 4: Pat Bryant #13 of the Denver Broncos is carted off of the field due to an apparent injury during the third quarter of an NFL football game against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium on October 4, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to ESPN’s lead NFL insider Adam Schefter, Denver Broncos wide receiver Pat Bryant suffered a sprained ankle during the Broncos’ loss to the 49ers on Sunday and is expected to miss “a few weeks”. Broncos WR Pat Bryant sprained his ankle during Sunday’s loss at San Francisco, and now is expected to miss “a few weeks” per source. pic.twitter.com/uwZA3UYou2 — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) October 5, 2026 Bryant was carted off the field after the injury, which did not look all that good on the replay, and he seemed to have suffered a potentially serious knee injury. However, we learned late last night that the belief was that neither he nor cornerback Pat Surtain II suffered season-ending injuries, and for Bryant, that was confirmed today. Honestly, this is about as best-case as you can get with this injury. It looked bad, and I assumed Bryant’s season was done. Thankfully, it’s just a sprained ankle, and he will miss a few weeks. It remains to be seen if Bryant will land on the short-term injured reserve or not, but we will learn that in the coming days. The Broncos play the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday and then play the reigning Super Bowl Champion Seattle Seahawks on a short week on Thursday Night Football. Bryant will likely be sidelined for both of these games, at least, but after that, we will have to see. This is still a tough loss for the Broncos’ scuffling offense. Bryant has been one of their more consistent and productive playmakers in recent weeks and just finished making a big play before suffering this sprained ankle. So, they will need Troy Franklin, Marvin Mims, and/or Lil’Jordan Humphrey to step up while he is sidelined. We are still awaiting word on the severity of CB Pat Surtain II’s ankle injury and CB Riley Moss’s rib injury. Again, the belief is that Surtain II did not suffer an Achilles injury, which is great, but he is still expected to miss some time. We will have that update when we get more information, but in the meantime, we can be thankful that Bryant escaped with just a sprained ankle and should be back on the field after a few weeks.

title: Denver Broncos Stock Up, Stock Down: Week 4 loss to the 49ers
summary: After having two thrilling comeback wins vs. the Jaguars and Rams at home, the Broncos headed west to take on the San Francisco 49ers, and things did not go as well. The offense once again started slow, but the Broncos’ defense played tough against a tough 49ers offense and kept the game close. However, after […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 4: RJ Harvey #12 of the Denver Broncos carries the ball during the third quarter of an NFL football game against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium on October 4, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images After having two thrilling comeback wins vs. the Jaguars and Rams at home, the Broncos headed west to take on the San Francisco 49ers, and things did not go as well. The offense once again started slow, but the Broncos’ defense played tough against a tough 49ers offense and kept the game close. However, after some calls and bounces went the 49ers’ way, they took a lead and never looked back. The Broncos did start to mount a comeback, but unfortunately, a long George Kittle touchdown reception ended any hopes of a comeback. Stock up and stock down is a weekly series where I go through the Denver Broncos’ 53-man roster and tell which Broncos players’ stock is going up, down, or remains unchanged. After a tough loss to the 49ers, we are going to see some stocks trending the wrong way. Quarterback Bo Nix – Stock down: Was it all on Nix? Not really. There were some costly drops, no run game, play-caller questions, and, of course, penalties. However, Nix did not play great either. He routinely dumped it off, was off target at times, and led the Broncos offense to just 3 points through three quarters. They did score 11 points in the 4th quarter, but it was too little too late for them at that point. The entire offense, play caller, quarterback, playmakers, and offensive line need to be better. Jarrett Stidham – Unchanged: Broncos backup quarterback. Sam Ehlinger – Unchanged: Broncos third-string quarterback. Running Back JK Dobbins – Stock down: He doesn’t seem right; his role seems reduced, and the production is not there. For what it is worth, he did get things going late on the Broncos’ lone touchdown drive, but overall, it was another disappointing effort by the Broncos veteran running back. RJ Harvey – Stock up: The numbers will not blow you away, but he was used like the starter and produced like a starter. He only had 25 yards on the ground, but did have 68 yards receiving, which led the team. He ran tough, showed some speed, broke some tackles, and was the Broncos’ most consistent playmaker. Tyler Badie – Stock up: Badie has been productive. He had yet another 20+ yard catch-and-run, had 2 carries for 7 yards, and scored the Broncos’ two-point conversion. His role remains as the third-down pass blocker, but he’s producing when called on and, honestly, deserves some more touches moving forward, Adam Prentice – Unchanged: He played just 7 offensive snaps on Sunday while playing 62% of the special teams snaps. Wide Receiver Jaylen Waddle – Unchanged: Waddle did catch his first touchdown as a member of the Denver Broncos, but his usage remains puzzling. He had 5 receptions for 35 yards and only saw 6 total targets throughout the game. I assumed they would manufacture more touches for him, and we saw that a little bit this week, but still, not what I envisioned when they traded for him. Courtland Sutton – Stock down: He didn’t get the start, only had 1 catch for 4 yards, and like Dobbins, just doesn’t look like himself out there. This is a wide receiver who has topped 1,000 yards and averaged 10 or so touchdowns in recent years, but we haven’t seen that player this year. He isn’t making the wow plays and isn’t thriving like I thought he would with the addition of Jaylen Waddle. Pat Bryant – Stock down: This sucks. Bryant was going to be a stock-up player and someone who should be more involved moving forward. However, after making a big play, he suffered a knee injury and had to be carted off the field. Thankfully, it doesn’t sound like it will be season-ending, but still, he’s going to miss time. Troy Franklin – Stock up: Franklin played 48% of the snaps on Sunday and figures to see a larger role with Bryant sidelined. The Broncos will need him to step up and make some plays moving forward. Marvin Mims Jr. – Stock down: What a disastrous start to his contract year. He has been dealing with multiple injuries but finally returned to the field on Sunday, and it did not go well. Mims played 27% of the offensive snaps and had 1 catch for 10 yards. However, his fumble on a punt return is what flipped the momentum in the 49ers’ favor. I would argue that Mims was down, but the NFL disagreed and the 49ers would go on to score the go-ahead touchdown off that turnover and never look back. Tight End Adam Trautman – Unchanged: His role is what it is. Evan Engram – Stock down: He played 67% of the offensive snaps and had 1 catch for 6 yards on 6 targets. He’s playing a lot, but the production is minimal. Nate Adkins – Unchanged: He played 21% of the snaps on offense but did not see a target on offense. Dallen Bentley – Unchanged: Was inactive. Offensive Line Garett Bolles – Unchanged: He’s a top LT in the league, but he did have some penalty issues on Sunday. Ben Powers – Unchanged: I did not notice him specifically, but the 49ers were able to get some pressure up the middle (also not an OL expert). Luke Wattenberg – Unchanged: Like with Powers, I did not notice him specifically, but he had some off-target snaps (again), and there was some pressure up the middle at times. Quinn Meinerz – Stock up: He’s a dog in the run game and played well from what I saw. Mike McGlinchey – Unchanged: He did get dinged up a little bit but played alright overall from my perspective. Alex Palczewski – Unchanged: Played 1 offensive snap and 3 special teams snaps. Matt Peart – Unchanged: Played just 3 special teams snaps. Alex Forsyth – Unchanged: Played just 3 special teams snaps. Kage Casey – Unchanged: Was inactive once again. Defensive Line Zach Allen – Stock up: Remains one of the best interior defensive linemen in the NFL and played well again on Sunday. DJ Jones – Unchanged: I say this each week, but I never really notice him during the game, and the Broncos allowed 100+ yards rushing again. Malcolm Roach – Unchanged: Roach had a PBU but overall did not do anything noteworthy throughout the game. Eyioma Uwazurike: Unchanged: Played 65% of the snaps on defense and remains a valuable rotational player for the Broncos. Jordan Jackson – Unchanged: Was active again and played 21% of the snaps, and remains ahead of Sai’vion Jones and rookie Tyler Onyedim. Sai’vion Jones – Stock up slightly: I only say slightly because he was playing some edge-rusher for the Broncos since they were down Dondrea Tillman. He only played 20% of the snaps, but the usage was interesting. Tyler Onyedim – Unchanged: Remains a weekly inactive. Edge Rusher Nik Bonitto – Stock down: The 49ers offensive line is the best in the NFL right now, but the Broncos pass rushers NEED to get to the quarterback. This defense is built around its pass rush, and it has currently taken a step back this season. Jonah Elliss – Stock down: He was out-snapped by Que Robinson, and his impact on the field has not been there. He had a good summer, but the production has not been there, unfortunately. Que Robinson – Stock up: While the Broncos’ pass rush failed to get to Brock Purdy, his usage increased, and he outsnapped Jonah Elliss, who has been playing more than him. He has flashed more on the field than Elliss in my opinion, and deserves more playing time. Dondrea Tillman – Unchanged: Was inactive with a hamstring injury. Linebacker Alex Singleton – Stock up: This was a fairly good game for Alex Singleton. I do not recall him struggling in coverage, and he made some impact tackles in the run game. Overall, I thought this was his best all-around game, which probably isn’t saying much, but still. A solid effort by the Broncos’ leader on defense. Justin Strnad – Unchanged: He didn’t really stand out to me, but he has been playing well overall. Jordan Turner – Stock up: Forced a fumble on a kick return, but it bounced right back to the 49ers, which…

title: With injuries, Broncos need to quickly shift gears
summary: Overshadowing the loss on Sunday to the San Francisco 49ers, the Denver Broncos lost a great deal more to injury. Pat Surtain II (ankle), Riley Moss (ribs), and Pat Bryant (leg/ankle) all left the game and it looks like all could miss more than a little time, if not the whole season. While I appreciate […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 4: Pat Surtain II #2 of the Denver Broncos stretches on the field prior to an NFL football game against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium on October 4, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Overshadowing the loss on Sunday to the San Francisco 49ers, the Denver Broncos lost a great deal more to injury. Pat Surtain II (ankle), Riley Moss (ribs), and Pat Bryant (leg/ankle) all left the game and it looks like all could miss more than a little time, if not the whole season. Non-contact injury for Pat Surtain. A closer look pic.twitter.com/p0Pmy0qXRv — Arye Pulli (@AryePulliNFL) October 4, 2026 🚨🚨HEARTBREAKING🚨🚨 #Broncos WR Pat Bryant was carted off the field after this ankle injury. This is GRUESOME… watch with caution. 😬😬 pic.twitter.com/LNMJEUTHBm — MLFootball (@MLFootball) October 4, 2026 While I appreciate the Klis report late Sunday night of Broncos brain-trust optimism regarding the extent of Surtain and Bryant’s injuries, there’s not much of a silver lining. No matter how you look at it, the Surtain injury has all the hallmarks of what’s tipically a season-ending Achilles injury. Pat Bryant’s ankle was wrenched the wrong way and, while it may not be a season-ender, he will most certainly miss more than a few weeks. Riley Moss’ previous rib injury took him out of action in the preseason for a couple weeks and it’s possible this could be more of the same (best case scenario)… but it’s also possible there is a bone fracture or cartilage damage, which could mean 3-6+ weeks of recovery. What do you do when you lose both your starting corners and a reliable offensive contributor at wide receiver? First of all, the defense can no longer be counted on to keep games close. For the first time in Bo Nix’s career, the defense is no longer the security blanket that will allow Davis Webb to fart around with the offense for 3 quarters. The offense now has to lock in when the game starts and get off to fast starts. The run game, and sustaining drives, has never been more important. This affinity for wasting downs in 3 and out possessions is only going to stress a depleted secondary and will most certainly yield horrific results. Sure, Davis Webb is finding his way as a play caller and it’s been a neat little adventure, watching him wobble and stumble like a toddler learning to walk. With the injuries on Sunday, the time for stumbling is over. The Broncos offense has got to strike first and strike hard to cover for a defense that suddenly finds itself without their starting cornerbacks. Sustaining offensive pressure through 4 quarters of football has never been more crucial than it suddenly is for the Denver Broncos. While these injuries don’t necessarily signal the end of the Broncos Super Bowl dreams in 2026, they absolutely don’t help. It’s time for the Broncos offense to show up when the game starts and not when they’re behind in the 4th quarter. In order for Bo Nix to ascend to the legendary echelon of Broncos quarterbacks, he’s going to need to put this team on his back and will them to victory, injuries be damned. …and so begins the next chapter of Bo Nix’s story.

title: Broncos are hopeful that Pat Bryant avoided a season-ending injury
summary: According to 9NEWS Denver’s Mike Klis, the Denver Broncos are hopeful that both cornerback Pat Surtain II and wide receiver Pat Bryant avoided season-ending injuries. He adds that both still need to undergo MRIs, but the belief is that both players will return to the team at some point this season. The positive update regarding […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 04: Pat Bryant #13 of the Denver Broncos is carted off the field after an injury in the third quarter against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium on October 04, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Lachlan Cunningham/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to 9NEWS Denver’s Mike Klis, the Denver Broncos are hopeful that both cornerback Pat Surtain II and wide receiver Pat Bryant avoided season-ending injuries. He adds that both still need to undergo MRIs, but the belief is that both players will return to the team at some point this season. Won’t know til MRIs on Monday but for now there is hope neither Pat Surtain or Pat Bryant suffered season-ending ankle injuries per source. May well miss some time but team as of now hopes to have them back this year. — MikeKlis9NEWS (@mikeklis9news) October 5, 2026 The positive update regarding Surtain II dropped earlier this evening , but Klis provided a late positive update on Bryant. Unlike Surtain II, who was able to walk off the field, albeit gingerly, Bryant was carted off, and it did not look good. It seemed like the Broncos were in danger of losing both Surtain and Bryant for the season, which obviously would be major blows to their lofty Super Bowl goals. Thankfully, that was not the case, and both are expected back at some point this season. Bryant will undergo an MRI tomorrow to determine the severity of his injury, but it seems like he will miss time regardless. This will be a major blow to an already underperforming Denver Broncos offense. He has turned into one of their more reliable pass catchers this season while also helping out as a run blocker. The Broncos will need Troy Franklin, Marvin Mims, and likely Lil’Jordan Humphrey to step up in his absence. It also puts more pressure on Jaylen Waddle, Courtland Sutton, Evan Engram, and the Broncos’ running game to step up their game. Waddle has had a surprisingly slow start to his Broncos career, Sutton and Engram barely contribute, and the run game has been mostly non-existent this season. Bryant has been one of the few bright spots, but now he will likely be sidelined for at least a few games. Like with Surtain II, the Broncos are fortunate that this doesn’t appear to be a season-ending injury for Bryant. The replay did not look good and anytime a playmaker is carted off the field, you fear the worst. Hopefully, Bryant will not miss much time and can return to the field sooner rather than later for the Denver Broncos.

title: Pat Surtain II injury update: Broncos star CB has reportedly avoided a long-term injury
summary: According to multiple reports, including NFL insider Tom Pelissero, Denver Broncos star cornerback Pat Surtain II reportedly avoided a long-term injury. Surtain II suffered a non-contact injury during the Broncos’ loss to the 49ers on Sunday, and it didn’t look good for the former Defensive Player of the Year. Thankfully, it sounds like Surtain II […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 04: Pat Surtain II #2 of the Denver Broncos sits on the field being assisted in the second quarter against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium on October 04, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Lachlan Cunningham/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to multiple reports, including NFL insider Tom Pelissero, Denver Broncos star cornerback Pat Surtain II reportedly avoided a long-term injury. Surtain II suffered a non-contact injury during the Broncos’ loss to the 49ers on Sunday, and it didn’t look good for the former Defensive Player of the Year. Thankfully, it sounds like Surtain II has avoided a major season-ending injury. Broncos star CB Patrick Surtain II is believed to have avoided a long-term injury Sunday, per sources. Surtain will undergo further testing for the non-contact injury to his ankle. But his Achilles is intact and all indications are that he avoided any worst-case scenario. pic.twitter.com/H78Vwjp1wJ — Tom Pelissero (@TomPelissero) October 5, 2026 While Surtain II appears to have avoided a long-term, season-ending injury, he still seems likely to miss time and could even spend time on the injured reserve. He needed the assistance of two trainers and was walking pretty gingerly to the locker room, so we will have to see what his exact injury is and how much time he is expected to miss. Surtain II wasn’t the only Broncos corner to leave Sunday’s game. Riley Moss, the Broncos’ other starting corner, suffered a rib injury and was sidelined for the entire second half. He was later ruled out for the game, and we are still awaiting an injury update on him. With Surtain II and Moss sidelined, the Broncos turned to former first-round pick Jahdae Barron and Kris Abrams-Draine at corner. While the 49ers were not throwing much, both corners held their own, and Barron had a few physical tackles in the game. With Surtain II and likely Moss expected to miss time, both players could see significant playing time moving forward. With Moss and Ja’Quan McMillian on expiring contracts, this will be a big opportunity for both corners to prove they can be trusted to start moving forward. The Broncos will face the 0-4 Los Angeles Chargers next Sunday, followed by a home game vs. the Seattle Seahawks on a short week on Thursday Night Football. Both Barron and Abrams-Draine will likely be counted on in those games at least and will need to play well if the Broncos want to have success moving forward. At the end of the day, it’s great news that Surtain II appears to have avoided a season-ending injury. Non-contact injuries are often bad, so the Broncos and Surtain II may have lucked out here.

title: Winners and Losers from the Denver Broncos’ 24-14 loss to the San Francisco 49ers
summary: Well, that sucked. The Denver Broncos started slow, suffered some tough injuries, did not have luck go their way, and could not complete the 4th quarter comeback vs. the 49ers. It was a tough game, but a winnable one for the Broncos that they let slip away late. They are now 2-2 and will have […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 04: George Kittle #85 of the San Francisco 49ers runs with the ball after a catch to score a touchdown in the fourth quarter against the Denver Broncos at Levi's Stadium on October 04, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Lachlan Cunningham/Getty Images) | Getty Images Well, that sucked. The Denver Broncos started slow, suffered some tough injuries, did not have luck go their way, and could not complete the 4th quarter comeback vs. the 49ers. It was a tough game, but a winnable one for the Broncos that they let slip away late. They are now 2-2 and will have an AFC West Divisional matchup vs. the Chargers next week to avoid falling under .500. As for winners and losers, it’s mostly the same story. Offense started slow, defense held tough, penalties sucked, injuries sucked, offense came alive late, but the defense could not close it out for the Broncos. So, here are your winners and losers for the Denver Broncos after their 24-14 defeat to the San Francisco 49ers. LOSER – Injuries Pat Surtain II – Non-contact and carted off Riley Moss – Missed the entire second half with a rib injury Pat Bryant – Was carted off with what looked to be a bad leg injury The Broncos caught the injury bug today, and it hit some big names. Surtain II had a non-contact injury and needed to be helped off the field by two trainers. Not what you want. Riley Moss suffered a rib injury for a second time this season and missed the entire second half. Then, Pat Bryant was carted off with what looked like a bad leg injury. We do not have updates on their statuses moving forward just yet, but we will keep you updated on any injury updates throughout the week. LOSER – Marvin Mims Jr. Was he down? It sure looked like it, but at the end of the day, they ruled it a fumble and the Niners’ ball. This led to a touchdown by the 49ers and flipped the momentum in their favor for the rest of the game. The Broncos could never recover from this, and ultimately, it was the point when they lost control of the game. This Was Ruled A Fumble After Marvin Mims’ Forearm Clearly Hit The Ground 👀 They Said The Ball Is Part Of His Hand, But I Don’t Know… I Think He’s Down. This Is Weird. pic.twitter.com/gy9E30SHrm — SM Highlights (@SMHighlights1) October 4, 2026 It has been a very forgettable start to the season for Marvin Mims Jr., who is playing for a new contract this season. He has missed multiple games due to injury and now has a costly fumble on his ledger. Not great. LOSER – Broncos offense All the talk this week was about starting fast. Well, that did not happen. They had just 3 points through three quarters before coming alive in the 4th quarter. Unfortunately, it was too little, too late for the Broncos. Nix was hit or miss throughout the game; the run game was not there until very late, and the Broncos’ playmakers did not make plays for the most part. They also had no answer for the 49ers’ sending the blitz and gave up some quick pressures throughout. They cannot continue to rely on late 4th quarter comebacks against good teams. They do it well, but it’s going to bite them at times, and it happened today. This was a winnable game but the Broncos simply could not get anything going on offense. We did see some good late, but that has been the story. We need to see this good throughout the game. WINNER – RJ Harvey The numbers are not great, but Harvey was the Broncos’ lone playmaker throughout the game. He had 7 carries for 25 yards but led the team with 10 receptions for 68 yards and also had a nice kick return late. Again, it is nothing to write home about, but he is the Broncos’ most productive running back right now. He’s making plays in space, running hard, breaking tackles, and looks better than JK Dobbins who simply doesn’t look right. LOSER – JK Dobbins We need more. Dobbins had some nice runs late, but finished with 11 carries for 40 yards and was mostly unproductive throughout the game. A lot of 3-yard gains and a cloud of dust. I don’t know if he’s injured or what, but he seems to be lacking some of that juice we saw last season. He doesn’t look right, and we need more from him, or else the Broncos need to make a change in that running back room. Rookie Jonah Coleman will be out the next two weeks at least. WINNER – Tyler Badie Again, it wasn’t a great day, but he made plays. 2 carries for 7 yards, 2 receptions for 32 yards, and converted a two-point conversion. He’s making a case for more touches moving forward. Either way, the Broncos need more from their running backs. LOSER – Broncos defense This is a tough loser call because they played tough throughout, but they came up short when they needed them the most late. They allowed 358 total yards, 218 passing yards, and 140 yards on the ground. They had no answer for Deebo Samuel throughout the game, allowed the Niners to get chunk plays on the ground, and allowed a long George Kittle touchdown late to put the nail in the coffin. Also, their attempt to lead the NFL in sacks for a third straight season is in danger. Their pass rush has taken a step back this season and struggled to get consistent pressure on Brock Purdy throughout this game and was not able to bring him down for a sack. Purdy has yet to be sacked this season, and that streak extends into Week 5. LOSER – Courtland Sutton Sutton has been the Broncos’ longtime WR1, but he’s having a tough start to the 2026 season. The impact plays are not there, and today he had just 1 catch for 4 yards. The hope of him giving the Broncos an explosive pairing with Jaylen Waddle seems to be dead right now. LOSER – Davis Webb The offensive struggles continue. How much longer can the Broncos allow him to call the plays before they need to make a switch? They sit at 2-2 and play the Chargers next week and then the Seahawks on a short week. They need to improve and improve quickly. Other notable winners and losers WR Jaylen Waddle – WINNER: Caught his first touchdown as a member of the Denver Broncos. TE Evan Engram – LOSER: The production simply isn’t there. CB Jahdae Barron – WINNER: Made some nice plays and will see plenty of playing time moving forward it seems. DL Zach Allen – WINNER: Blocked a field goal and was disruptive throughout the game. S Talanoa Hufanga – LOSER: Whiffed on a few tackle attempts. EDGE Nik Bonitto/Jonah Elliss/Que Robinson – LOSER: We need some pass rush. P Jeremy Crawshaw – WINNER: He has been booming punts all season. Penalties – LOSER: 7 flags for 44 yards while the Niners had just 1 for 5 yards.
