title: Travis Glover passes the test in first significant playing time since 2024
summary: After upending their offensive line over the post-Thursday Night Football mini bye, the Packers coaching staff reached into a hat and pulled out a new name to start at right guard for Sunday’s game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Instead of Kevin Zeitler or Donovan Jennings or Jacob Monk or Jager Burton, it was Travis […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - AUGUST 18: Travis Glover #79 of the Green Bay Packers steps up to block during an NFL football game against the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High on August 18, 2024 in Denver, CO. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images After upending their offensive line over the post-Thursday Night Football mini bye, the Packers coaching staff reached into a hat and pulled out a new name to start at right guard for Sunday’s game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Instead of Kevin Zeitler or Donovan Jennings or Jacob Monk or Jager Burton, it was Travis Glover getting the nod between Sean Rhyan and Anthony Belton. A 2024 sixth round pick, we haven’t seen Glover on the field for a game that matters in quite some time. The last time he made an appearance was in the Packers’ loss to the eventual Super Bowl champion Philadelphia Eagles, when he came in at left guard in relief of an injured Elgton Jenkins, who dropped out after just four plays. Facing off against a ferocious Philadelphia front, Glover was penalized three times before he was ultimately benched in favor of Kadeem Telfort. However, after an injury to starting center Josh Myers forced Sean Rhyan to take over at center, Glover got back into the game at right guard. All told, he played 33 snaps and had a dreadful day, posting a pass blocking grade of just 1.8 according to Pro Football Focus. For comparison, Donovan Jennings and Jacob Monk put up pass blocking grades of 40.0 and 48.2, respectively, in the Packers’ Week 1 loss to the Vikings this season, and that was one of the single-worst blocking performances we’ve ever seen. You can and should take PFF grades with a grain of salt, but that’s a startling difference. Glover missed all of the 2025 season with a back injury, but was back in action this preseason lining up primarily but not exclusively at right tackle. He played 39 snaps on the outside against just 28 at right guard, but with Jennings struggling, Monk unavailable due to injury, and Burton’s experience coming primarily at right guard, those 28 snaps apparently represented enough time on task to give Glover the start. How did Glover do? It wasn’t a spectacular day for the Packers on the ground or through the air, but Glover came close to achieving a lineman’s ideal day: by and large, he was seen but not heard. In 60 snaps of work, surrendered just one pressure and was penalized one time, a holding penalty on the Packers’ first offensive play of the fourth quarter. A 19-yard completion to Jonnu Smith on the next play erased that penalty and then some, though, so ultimately it was of little consequence. Pro Football Focus gave Glover a 59.4 grade overall, bolstered mainly by his 71.4 grade as a pass blocker (they gave him a 53.8 grade for his run blocking). That aligns well with the eye test of the Packers’ offensive line as a whole; by and large, they did a good job protecting Jordan Love but struggled to get much push in the ground game. It wasn’t necessarily Glover’s fault, but you can see some of the struggles the Packers had on the ground in a 2nd and 3 play in the second quarter. Jordan Morgan gives up ground to Buccaneers’ defensive lineman Rakeem Nunez-Roches so quickly that Glover, coming right to left as a pulling guard, ends up smacking Morgan in the face. For a second, it looks like Glover and Morgan are giving each other a hug as Nunez-Roches takes Kaleb Johnson down for a two-yard loss. But in a game where the Packers’ offensive line looked relatively competent, especially compared to the rest of the season, Glover, at the very least, was not obviously bad. That’s a step in the right direction. And hopefully, it’ll be the last the Packers see of him for a while. It was probably unrealistic to expect newly arrived Kevin Zeitler in the lineup this week, but going forward, he’ll hopefully be ready to go. Whatever workouts he’s been doing on his own were almost assuredly not enough to get him from “active, but sitting at home” to “ready to play in an NFL game” in roughly three days of practice, one of which would have been at walkthrough speed. He was always going to need some time, and hopefully another week will do it. But if he can’t go, the Packers should at least feel good putting Glover out there again. He wasn’t a clear detriment to the team’s performance, and given what we’ve seen from his teammates this year, that’s a huge compliment.
author: Jon Meerdink

title: NFL officials are calling more penalties than ever
summary: If you’ve been feeling like NFL football fields have been awash in yellow this season, your eyes have not deceived you. NFL officials are calling more penalties per game than they have in any season dating back to 2009, and it’s not particularly close. According to data from NFLPenalties.com, NFL officials are calling a little […]
full_text: OAKLAND, CALIFORNIA - DECEMBER 08: A yellow penalty flag lays on the field during the second half of the game between the Oakland Raiders and the Tennessee Titans at RingCentral Coliseum on December 08, 2019 in Oakland, California. (Photo by Lachlan Cunningham/Getty Images) | Getty Images If you’ve been feeling like NFL football fields have been awash in yellow this season, your eyes have not deceived you. NFL officials are calling more penalties per game than they have in any season dating back to 2009, and it’s not particularly close. According to data from NFLPenalties.com , NFL officials are calling a little more than 17 penalties per game this season, the most we’ve seen in any single year since 2009. The average game includes 15 accepted penalties, also the most we’ve seen in any single year in that same time span. The previous highs in both of those categories are 16.2 total flags per game and 13.7 accepted penalties per game, both of which happened in 2015. The Packers, as you no doubt are aware, are one of the hardest hit teams in this ongoing festival of penalties, averaging 10.5 penalties per game. And for those inclined to say this is a long-term issue for Matt LaFleur’s teams, it really isn’t. Outside of this year, LaFleur’s Packers have typically been right in line with the league average for individual team penalties per game; they’ve never averaged more than 6.2 accepted penalties per game in any season since 2019. In short, NFL games have been flag fests. What’s causing the increase? There are a few specific penalties to blame, but it’s all on the offense’s shoulders. Offensive holding, false start, and delay of game have all seen the biggest increases in per game calls from 2025 to 2026. Holding is being called, on average, 3.13 times per game leaguewide, up from 2.4 per game last year. We’re seeing 2.78 false start flags per game this year, up from 2.39 last year. And to round things out, we’ve seen an average of 0.97 delay of game penalties per week, an increase from 0.64 last year. Those penalties alone don’t account for the increase, though it comes pretty close. But in general, NFL games are seeing more and more penalties; across the 49 different infractions already called at least once this year, 26 are being called at a higher rate than last year. Just 15 are being called at a lower rate. Generally speaking, if you’re tuning in to watch NFL football this season, chances are good you’re going to see more penalties than ever before.
author: Jon Meerdink

title: Packers Film Room: Long snapping on kicks in Week 4
summary: In this space, we look at the snap-to-hold operation on field goals and extra points. We only have 3 that we’re looking at this week, so it’ll probably be a quick one. No blocked field goals to break down like we did last week. As we always do, we’ll start with the snap location for […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - NOVEMBER 28: Long snapper Matt Orzech #42 of the Green Bay Packers warms up prior to an NFL game against the Miami Dolphins at Lambeau Field on November 28, 2024 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images In this space, we look at the snap-to-hold operation on field goals and extra points. We only have 3 that we’re looking at this week, so it’ll probably be a quick one. No blocked field goals to break down like we did last week . As we always do, we’ll start with the snap location for the holder. How did it look this week? The exact same as last week in terms of breakdown. Two up and into the body, one over the hold spot. Let’s look at the individual kicks, with the snap-to-hold operation slowed down to 30% speed. Kick 1: Extra Point (Made) Snap up and to the body of Whelan. Clean catch and hold. No wind and extra point distance, so we get a slight lean forward and away from the kicker on the hold. It’s worth noting that the block last week was a result of Donovan Jennings being late out of his stance. Travis Glover is in that spot this week, and he is able to make himself big and not allow pressure from his outside shoulder. One other thing to keep an eye on: Karl Brooks is the outside man on the left side of your screen. He’s slightly late to react to the snap and doesn’t force Zyon McCollum [27] wide, which allows McCollum to bend the edge and almost get a hand on the ball. Kick 2: 58 Yard Field Goal (Made) Great snap. Up and over the hold spot (slightly into the body, but I’m counting it as over the hold spot). With the distance of the kick, the lean on the hold is slightly more forward than we saw on the extra point. Brooks is on the right side of the screen. Once more McCollum is looking to bend the edge, but Brooks gets a hand on him and is able to disrupt him just enough. Good snap. Good hold. Booming kick from Smack. Kick 3: Extra Point (Made) Good snap, up and into the body. Good hold by Whelan. Smack splits the uprights. Once again, McCollum is on the edge vs Brooks (right side of the screen). Brooks has seen this movie before. With Belton slowing down the gap between him and Brooks, Brooks turns and gives McCollum a nice knock, sending him to the turf. Albums listened to: Nine Inch Nails – Ghosts V: Together
author: Dusty Evely

title: Packers By The Numbers: Stats from the Week 4 win over the Bucs
summary: As we do every week in this space, we’re looking at some stats from the Green Bay Packers game, courtesy of SumerSports. Offense Last week saw the Packers needing to lean heavy into 11 personnel and the passing game, due to getting behind early and also lacking any ability to run. This week saw them […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 4: Xavier McKinney #29 of the Green Bay Packers celebrates a sack against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the game at Raymond James Stadium on October 4, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images As we do every week in this space, we’re looking at some stats from the Green Bay Packers game, courtesy of SumerSports . Offense Last week saw the Packers needing to lean heavy into 11 personnel and the passing game, due to getting behind early and also lacking any ability to run. This week saw them with a little more balance, both in terms of personnel usage and in run/pass ratio. This week, the Packers were in 11 personnel (1 RB, 1 TE, 3 WR) on just 47.3% of their snaps (down from 81% last week). They were in 12 personnel on 23.6% and 13 personnel on 29.1% of their snaps. That 13 personnel rate (1 RB, 3 TE, 1 WR) was their highest usage of that personnel package this year, and it was also their best passing package. When operating out of 13 personnel, Jordan Love was 5/5 for 76 yards for an EPA per Play of +1.04 (basically, they generated a little more than 1 point every time they passed out of this grouping). They had a 100% Success Rate when passing out of 13 personnel. It was also their best running group (11 attempts, 52 yards, -0.09 EPA per Play). I’m excited to dig into the film on that and see what they were doing when in that personnel group. On the run/pass ratio, the Packers passed 56.4% of the time and ran 43.6% of the time. That’s a far cry from the 85.7% pass rate we saw against the Falcons. The pass game (+0.14 EPA per Play) far outperformed the run game (-0.35). While an 85.7% pass rate is a bit extreme, I’d certainly like to see the pass rate be a little closer to 65% rather than 55%. Love was still getting the ball out quickly (he averaged 2.17 seconds to throw, a full 0.5 seconds below the NFL average), with an EPA per Play of +0.14. That’s far and away his best passing performance of the year. Before this, his best performance was in the Vikings game in Week 1, where he posted an EPA per Play of -0.02. For the first time this year, Love took 0 sacks. There were some plays he’d like to have back and there were (once again) a couple drops, but this is the most competent the Packers offense has looked all year. Love also looked good against the blitz. That’s been an issue all year (mainly because, against the line through the first 3 weeks, a blitz meant an automatic pressure), but Love did well this week. Against the blitz, he was 7/9 for 62 yards (+0.14 EPA per Play). It was also an encouraging performance from Tucker Kraft. He caught 6 of his 7 targets for 42 yards and a TD, good for +0.79 EPA per Reception. He had an ADOT (Average Depth of Target) of 0.57 yards and he averaged 6.83 yards after the catch. He wasn’t asked to stretch the field very much (his targets were on Hitches and Quick Outs), but when he got the ball in his hands he got upfield and was looking to make something happen. He still doesn’t look like the Tucker Kraft we were used to seeing last season, but this was the first time all year we really got a good glimpse of that guy. Overall, Kraft had a 22.6% target share. He was a heavy target in the Red Zone (42.9% target share) and saw a decent amount of looks on early downs (27.3% early down target share). Kraft also had an EPA per Play of +1.93 on rush attempts, thanks to his successful 4th down sneak. Here’s what the running game numbers looked like from Gap Outcomes, by running back. Chris Brooks: Kaleb Johnson: MarShawn Lloyd: Brooks is their most limited runner in terms of burst/wiggle, but, if the line can block it up, he’s been their most effective because he can read his blocks and hit the hole. Let’s take a quick look at the guards before moving to the other side of the ball. Last week, Jacob Monk (LG) allowed 8.3% pressure rate, with a 22.2% pressure rate against blitz, 5.3% pressure rate vs stunts. On the other side, Jager Burton (RG) allowed an 18.2 pressure rate, with an 11.1% pressure rate against the blitz and 20.8% vs stunts. This week, we had Travis Glover (RG) giving up a 3.3% pressure rate, 0% rate against the blitz, 0% against stunts. New Packer Laken Tomlinson gave up a 3.3% pressure rate, 11.1% against the blitz, 0% against stunts. I’m not going to sit here and proclaim that the interior of the line has been fixed, but, against a pretty good Tampa Bay front, Glover and Tomlinson performed well. Defense The Packers lived in Nickel in this game, posting a 90.2% Nickel rate (30.38% above the NFL average). That seems high, until you look and see they were just matching the Bucs’ personnel. The Bucs were in 11 personnel on 90.2% of their snaps. When the Bucs brought out a 3rd WR, the Packers were matching in Nickel. The Packers defense was zone heavy, but not quite as much as they had been. They played Man Coverage on 39.4% of their snaps, their highest rate of the year (their previous high was 13.3% against the Vikings). The Man snaps were primarily Cover 1 (man-to-man across the board, with a single-high safety), but they also ran 2 snaps of Cover 0 (all-out blitz with man coverage). This was also the highest blitz rate the Packers had all year. They blitzed the Bucs on 47.22% of their snaps, 17.09% above NFL average. Their previous high was 34.69% against the Jets. The defense has been a bit uneven at times (which is putting it a bit nicely), but I have been quite happy with Gannon’s blitz approach. Coming into the year, Gannon was known as a defensive coordinator who didn’t blitz very often. This year, he has dialed it up more than we’ve seen in his career, and has leaned heavier into the blitz depending on the gameplan. Seeing that type of flexibility in attack has been really fun. Lukas Van Ness had a nice performance, but not quite as impactful as we had been seeing. He notched 2 solo tackles, 2 assisted tackles and 0 tackles for loss. I’d like to see his pressure rate higher (his 8.7% pressure rate was 3.23% below NFL average), but that was due to a quick release and screen-heavy plan from the Bucs. His Average Time to Pressure was 2.36 seconds, right around NFL average. Albums listened to: Alex G – Camp Miasma Soundtrack; Poppy Ackroyd – Liminal

title: Green Bay Packers News: Cooper’s injury makes win over Bucs a pyrrhic victory
summary: “We’ve been kind of hit with some type of curse.” Those were Sean Rhyan’s words after the Green Bay Packers’ 17-14 victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday afternoon. Yes, the Packers got back in the win column. Yes, the team is back to 2-2 and still right in the thick of the NFC […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 4: Linebacker Edgerrin Cooper #56 of the Green Bay Packers has to be carted off the field in the third quarter against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium on October 4, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Parker S. Freedman/Getty Images) | Getty Images “We’ve been kind of hit with some type of curse.” Those were Sean Rhyan’s words after the Green Bay Packers’ 17-14 victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday afternoon. Yes, the Packers got back in the win column. Yes, the team is back to 2-2 and still right in the thick of the NFC North race. Yes, the offensive line looked much better, bolstered by changes at both guard positions and facing a team with a fairly dismal pass rush. But when Edgerrin Cooper went down with a non-contact injury in the third quarter, it felt like a massive gut punch for the entire team. Rhyan’s sentiments echo what Packers fans were surely feeling: the likely season-ending loss of yet another essential player on the Green Bay roster. Last year it was Tucker Kraft and Micah Parsons, both of whom were playing at an All-Pro level when they tore their ACLs (and Parsons still managed to be an All-Pro anyway). This year, it has been Jayden Reed and Zach Bako-Bewele, both of whom weren’t quite at that level but who were key cogs on the offense. Now it’s Cooper, who has been pushing for All-Pro consideration as well through the first month of the season. Cooper was even in the midst of arguably his finest game so far this season. Before his injury, he had racked up 9 tackles, a sack, and an interception, the second of his career. It’s probably no coincidence that on the Bucs’ drive immediately following Cooper’s injury, they put together a 12-play, 89-yard touchdown drive to cut the Packers’ lead to three points. Somehow, the defense did just enough to overcome a pair of fourth-quarter turnovers from the Green Bay offense, forcing a punt and a turnover on downs late to preserve a narrow three-point win. But moving forward, the Packers’ defense will be without one of its most dynamic young playmakers, presumably for the rest of the season. Sean Rhyan Nailed It Following Crushing Injury to Packers Star Edgerrin Cooper | SI.com Ryhan isn’t the only Packer who’s feeling down about Cooper’s injury. Isaiah McDuffie, Evan Williams, and Tucker Kraft all spoke about it after the game as well. Rapid reaction: Packers get win, but still ‘hurting ourselves’ | Packers.com Meanwhile, Matt LaFleur wasn’t his usual self at the podium following a win. Quite the opposite: he was fiery and frustrated by the team’s continued mistakes — turnovers and penalties, especially in the fourth quarter, very easily could have led to yet another blown double-digit lead. With Edgerrin Cooper out, Evan Williams shines for Packers | ESPN The Packers’ defense found a closer on Sunday in Williams. After a first-quarter interception, he made his way into the backfield three times on the Bucs’ final series, coming up with his first career sack and another QB hit to force a bad throw on the final, decisive fourth down. G ood, bad and ugly coming out of Packers’ Week 4 win over Buccaneers | Packers Wire There’s not a ton of good here, though improved offensive line play is certainly something to build on. title: Packers vs. Bears odds: Opening lines for Week 5 matchup
summary: It is particularly unusual for the Green Bay Packers to be underdogs at home in recent years. Since the start of the 2024 season, the Packers have been home underdogs just twice, and one of those games featured the significant unknown of the team starting a backup quarterback. Both of those games came during the […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - DECEMBER 07: Luther Burden III #10 of the Chicago Bears and Carrington Valentine #24 of the Green Bay Packers react after the play during the second quarter at Lambeau Field on December 07, 2025 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images It is particularly unusual for the Green Bay Packers to be underdogs at home in recent years. Since the start of the 2024 season, the Packers have been home underdogs just twice, and one of those games featured the significant unknown of the team starting a backup quarterback. Both of those games came during the 2024 season. Week two saw the Packers — with Malik Willis set to make his first start in relief of an injured Jordan Love — getting 2.5 points against the visiting Indianapolis Colts. Green Bay won that game 16-10, thanks to an efficient 12-for-14 passing day from Willis and 151 rushing yards from Josh Jacobs. The second time that a visiting team was favored at Lambeau Field that year was a few weeks later when the Detroit Lions came to town, and the Lions won 24-14 as 2.5-point favorites. On Sunday in Week 5, the Chicago Bears come to Lambeau likely to feature a backup quarterback, but given the two teams’ recent results, it’s understandable that Chicago is favored at the start of the week. As of Monday morning, FanDuel Sportsbook has the Bears favored by that familiar 2.5-point spread for the two teams’ meeting in the early slate on Sunday. After sitting out the Bears’ prior game against the Eagles with a concussion, backup Tyson Bagent returned in Week 4 and helped lead his team to a 23-12 victory over the New York Jets, throwing for 268 yards and one interception. The Bears completely dominated the game, however, owning the football for nearly 43 minutes of game clock and running a whopping 89 offensive plays to the Jets’ 32. Kyle Monangai was the biggest star for the Chicago offense, toting the football a whopping 30 times for 146 yards and two touchdowns. If the Packers can’t sustain drives on offense and keep their own defense fresh, it could be a very long afternoon next Sunday. Edgerrin Cooper’s absence will likely be a significant blow to the defense as well, particularly with the third-year linebacker having played at an extremely high level to this point in the season. If the Packers offense can find a way to keep Jordan Love clean, there should be opportunities downfield, but the books see only a moderate expectation of offensive firepower; the over/under for total points this week is set at 44.5. Will the Packers be able to overcome this spread while sporting their Rivalries uniforms on Sunday? Keep it here at APC for more updates as the week goes on. Go Pack Go—wherever you go! title: Packers Winners and Losers: Week 4 vs. the Buccaneers
summary: The sky has been falling for the Green Bay Packers so far through the first few weeks of the 2026 season. It still might be falling, just a little more slowly at the moment, because the team left Raymond James Stadium with a .500 record after a 17-14 win against the winless Buccaneers. There’s a […]
full_text: (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The sky has been falling for the Green Bay Packers so far through the first few weeks of the 2026 season. It still might be falling, just a little more slowly at the moment, because the team left Raymond James Stadium with a .500 record after a 17-14 win against the winless Buccaneers. There’s a lot to talk about. Let’s dive in. Winner: Edgerrin Cooper (Loser: all of us) One of the NFL’s brightest young stars, Cooper maintained that status as he had quite the game on Sunday. He forced a punt in the Bucs’ opening drive with a huge third down stop on QB Jalon Daniels. As Tampa looked to score before halftime, he had another huge play: an interception, and a big 18 yard return to go along with it. COOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOP 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/kApADhGYbt — Green Bay Packers (@packers) October 4, 2026 Then, midway through the third quarter, the earth stood still as Cooper went down with a non-contact injury. The cart was immediately brought out, and it was later confirmed that the star LB had suffered an Achilles injury, and that it looked to be season-ending. The impact of this loss cannot be overstated: the defense has immediately gotten worse. With the news this week that Micah Parsons might not be ready to go for another month, this is about as “worst-case scenario” as it gets for the team. Here’s to a speedy recovery for future 2027 Comeback Player of the Year Edgerrin Cooper. In the last 336 days: Micah Parsons: Torn ACL + meniscus Zach Bako-Bewele: Torn patella Jayden Reed: Neck surgery Edgerrin Cooper: likely torn Achilles Tucker Kraft: Torn ACL — Andy Herman (@AndyHermanNFL) October 4, 2026 Winner: Evan Williams The safety had himself a DAY in Tampa. To start things off, just as the Bucs seemed to get a drive going for themselves, Williams came in with one of the best picks I’ve seen in some time, creating a massive momentum shift which saw the Packers score the first points of the game on the next drive. Evan Williams with a CRAZY INT 😯 @GBvsTB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Rg88hMIRN8 — NFL (@NFL) October 4, 2026 Then, on the same drive as Cooper’s interception, Williams had a colossal PBU on 3rd and 1 (the Bucs would pick up the first down on the next play, but that wasn’t Williams’ fault now was it?). During the Buccaneers’ final drive of the game, Williams got his first NFL sack (can’t believe it) for a loss of 6 yards. Two plays later, he applied heavy pressure on Jalon Daniels, which led to a turnover on downs after a dropped pick by Nixon. Williams finished the day with 7 tackles, 1 sack, 2 QB hits, and 1 INT. The kid’s a star. Not Losers: The Offensive Line POP THE CHAMPAGNE; THEY WERE FINE. Loser: Guys with Hands There were some really great moments from the pass catchers today. TE Tucker Kraft had some big first downs early in the game, and a really nice TD catch to cap off the team’s opening drive of the second half. Let's go! 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/ew9PERp3ey — Green Bay Packers (@packers) October 4, 2026 You know what wasn’t nice? THIS DROP. Tucker Kraft brutal drop pic.twitter.com/R3SJrRrfj7 — Ian Hartitz (@Ihartitz) October 4, 2026 We’ve also got WR Matthew Golden, who had a gorgeous TD catch in the second quarter to give the team their first points of the day. That was electric! 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/VLkxJO2SFL — Green Bay Packers (@packers) October 4, 2026 You know what wasn’t gorgeous? THAT DROP, FOR WHICH I CONVENIENTLY CAN’T FIND THE FOOTAGE. And then we have WR Bo Melton, who dropped an absolute dime of a pass from Love. Oh, Bo. A perfect throw from Love but Bo Melton drops it. This doesn’t do justice to the ball placement. pic.twitter.com/i2UlWQQJoe — Rob Demovsky (@RobDemovsky) October 4, 2026 I am simply begging for someone to give Jordan Love a break at this point. If it’s not the offensive line, it’s the pass catchers. If it’s not the pass catchers, it’s the run game. Oh, it was indeed the run game today! Loser: The RB Room Congratulations, you’ve fixed your offensive line, and now your RBs all have The Itis™. On 25 rushes today, the Packers had 86 yards. You may be thinking “Sam, that’s 3.4 YPC. That doesn’t seem THAT bad”. Dear reader, two of those rushes went for a combined 58 yards. What does that mean? The Packers had 23 carries for a total of 28 yards, which amounts to a whopping 1.2 yards per carry. Not only are they slow and lacking vision, but they also can’t hold onto the ball. This Kaleb Johnson fumble is about as brutal as it gets. FUMBLE! Bucs Ball 🏈 @GBvsTB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/qGdaMniTQH — NFL (@NFL) October 4, 2026 Aside from the team giving us their two longest rushes of the season (Johnson: 31 yards, Brooks: 27 yards), the one bright side from today’s RB room: MarShawn Lloyd gave us one of the funniest hurdles I’ve ever seen. Even this was in slow motion. He looks like me trying to hop over a baby gate. MarShawn Lloyd with an INSANE hurdle 📺: FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/WWDsYOLtMI — FOX Sports: NFL (@NFLonFOX) October 4, 2026 The Packers face one of their biggest tests of the season next week, as they head back home to face off against the Chicago Bears during Sunday’s early slate of games. The 3-1 Bears could very well still be missing QB Caleb Williams, who suffered a season-ending week to week injury in Week 2. The 2-2 Packers will likely have yet another variation of starting offensive linemen for this game, as Kevin Zeitler is brought up to speed after signing with the team this week. Can Green Bay pull off the upset?
author: Sam Kallien

title: Packers Week 4 Snap Counts: MarShawn Lloyd leads the way in the backfield
summary: It’s Week 4, so we know a good amount about the Green Bay Packers, but there are still some moving parts. This week, the team made some expected moves, and they also made some decisions that seemed out of nowhere. Let’s go position-by-position through the team’s offensive and defensive snap counts, explaining what did or […]
full_text: (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s Week 4, so we know a good amount about the Green Bay Packers, but there are still some moving parts. This week, the team made some expected moves, and they also made some decisions that seemed out of nowhere. Let’s go position-by-position through the team’s offensive and defensive snap counts, explaining what did or did not change for each position (if there was anything notable that happened on Sunday against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers). Quarterback Jordan Love: 55 snaps Running Back MarShawn Lloyd: 30 Kaleb Johnson: 15 Chris Brooks: 10 The running back unit was feast-or-famine, relying on explosive plays. While the Packers had their best rushing game of the season on Sunday, the two longest runs from Kaleb Johnson and Chris Brooks totaled a combined 58 yards. On the 17 other runs from the backs in Week 4, they mustered just 17 carries for 27 yards. Brooks actually got the “start” in the game, but was shut down in the first half due to injury (head coach Matt LaFleur was not asked about Brooks’ injury in his post-game press conference). Because of that, MarShawn Lloyd, who had been splitting touches with Brooks prior to his injury, took over as the clear RB1 for the remainder of the game. Receiver Matthew Golden: 50 Christian Watson: 36 Skyy Moore: 22 Bo Melton: 10 J. Michael Sturdivant: 2 Nothing too shocking here, as Skyy Moore remains the team’s slot receiver — as a replacement for the injured Jayden Reed. Tight End Tucker Kraft: 50 Mark Redman: 25 Josh Whyle: 13 Jonnu Smith: 12 Offensive Line Jordan Morgan – LT: 55 Laken Tomlinson – LG: 55 Sean Rhyan – C: 55 Travis Glover – RG: 55 Anthony Belton – RT: 55 The Buccaneers came in with the 4th-highest blitz rate in the NFL (44%), but blitzed Jordan Love just 17% of the time. Not coincidentally, the Packers also had a season-best 53% Pass Block Win Rate per ESPN Analytics/NFL Next Gen Stats. They had a win rate of just 16% the first… — Rob Demovsky (@RobDemovsky) October 4, 2026 The Packers had their best pass protection day of the season on Sunday, as the team made changes to their guard positions. Laken Tomlinson stepped up as a left guard, while Travis Glover played right guard — displacing Donovan Jennings and Jacob Monk, respectively. After the game, LaFleur stated that he wanted bigger bodies in front of quarterback Jordan Love to protect him. Love was hit just two times on Sunday. For reference, Glover had been on the bench for three weeks, while Tomlinson was poached from the Dallas Cowboys’ practice squad after the team’s loss to the Atlanta Falcons. LaFleur also said that Kevin Zeitler, the team’s preferred starting option at right guard, needs more time to ramp up before game action. Zeitler was the only healthy player scratched for Week 4’s action against the Buccaneers. Defensive Line Karl Brooks: 34 Javon Hargrave: 28 Chris McClellan: 24 Devonte Wyatt: 23 Jonathan Ford: 13 Devonte Wyatt dropped out of play twice with injury, but returned to the field for the Packers. That’s one reason why he was fourth in the pecking order on the defensive line (by a slim margin) on Sunday. Nose tackle Jonathan Ford didn’t play much, as the team mostly lived in their nickel defense (more on that later) against Tampa Bay. Edge Defender Lukas Van Ness: 44 Barryn Sorrell: 32 Brenton Cox Jr.: 24 Dani Dennis-Sutton: 23 Dani Dennis-Sutton received the second-most snaps among edge defenders in Week 3, but that appears to be a one-off game. The rookie fourth-round pick was fourth in the pecking order on Sunday, essentially a split role with Brenton Cox Jr. — as it has been for most of the season. Barryn Sorrell continues to start opposite Lukas Van Ness. Linebacker Zaire Franklin: 61 Edgerrin Cooper: 33 Isaiah McDuffie: 24 Ty’Ron Hopper: 5 It looks like the team is worried that Will linebacker Edgerrin Cooper tore his Achilles , which would be a season-ending injury. The next man up behind Cooper is Isaiah McDuffie, who left Sunday’s game with an eye injury before going back in. The McDuffie injury (after the Cooper injury) is how Ty’Ron Hopper (the next Will linebacker up) got into the game for five snaps. Cornerback Keisean Nixon: 61 Brandon Cisse: 52 Carrington Valentine: 9 Brandon Cisse went out against Tampa with a neck injury and was evaluated for a concussion. LaFleur was not asked about Cisse’s status in the post-game press conference, so there’s no information on how serious Cisse’s injury was. The next man up behind Cisse, who has been starting at right cornerback this year, is Carrington Valentine. Safety Evan Williams: 61 Xavier McKinney: 61 Javon Bullard: 58 Slot defender Javon Bullard was on the field for 95 percent of the defense’s snaps on Sunday, an incredible amount. It’s not uncommon for Bullard to be off the field for about half of the game, depending on the opponent. The Buccaneers lived in 11 personnel (three-receiver sets), which allowed the Packers to deploy Bullard more than usual. The nickelback was nearly an every-down player for Green Bay in Week 4.

full_text: (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images Green Bay Packers starting Will linebacker Edgerrin Cooper was carted off against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers for what appears to be a non-contact ankle injury. Cooper dropped to the ground awkwardly on a third-down blitz versus the Buccaneers, grabbed his ankle and needed assistance to leave the field. You can find the video of the play linked below. ❌ 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/fTtoHm43fp — Green Bay Packers (@packers) October 4, 2026 Cooper’s replacement at the position has been Isaiah McDuffie, who backs up both the Mike (Zaire Franklin) and Will (Cooper) positions on defense. McDuffie is also a core special teamer who is a year-long team captain on that unit. If there were ever another injury at the position, it’s likely that Ty’Ron Hopper would take over the Will position with the remaining healthy linebacker (be it Franklin or McDuffie) playing the Mike. So far, the Packers haven’t made an announcement about Cooper’s injury. We’ll keep you updated when any new information drops on his status. Green Bay also dealt with two other injuries on Sunday, as running back Chris Brooks and defensive tackle Devonte Wyatt were both banged up in Tampa. — Update: Cooper has been ruled out, and the Packers are calling it an Achilles injury. LB Edgerrin Cooper has been ruled out with an Achilles injury. — Green Bay Packers (@packers) October 4, 2026 Update #2: #Packers star third-year linebacker Edgerrin Cooper is still being evaluated but the initial fear is that he suffered a torn Achilles today vs. the Buccaneers, sources tell @CBSSports . Terrible development. Had 30 tackles and three sacks through three-and-a-half games this… pic.twitter.com/RbETHnjgHa — Matt Zenitz (@mzenitz) October 4, 2026 According to CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz, the Packers’ “initial fear” is that Cooper tore his Achilles. Update #3: Head coach Matt LaFleur said it’s “not good” for Cooper and that he suspects Cooper has a season-ending injury.

title: Value of Things: In the rearview mirror
summary: Luckily this comes out the next day. My comrade gets to do the day after the day after. He is even luckier. There are some losses that hit harder than others. It is a close game and nail biter in the end. Sometimes the game means more in the standings because of the playoff push. […]
full_text: Luckily this comes out the next day. My comrade gets to do the day after the day after. He is even luckier. There are some losses that hit harder than others. It is a close game and nail biter in the end. Sometimes the game means more in the standings because of the playoff push. Sometimes it is a bitter rival you just don’t want to lose to. Occasionally, all of those intersect into one event that just guts you beyond belief. I will post the numbers and the numbers by themselves tell a great deal of the story, but they are never all of the story. Most of the story is the emotional toll these games take week in and week out. I’d have to look it up, but I don’t think the Texans have ever been 0-4, so at least they are making history. Being a Texans fan is its own special hell. Most 0-4 teams are ready to fold up shop and start playing for next year, but this outfit has had enough miraculous comebacks where you don’t want to fully give up on the season. You can talk yourself into a winning streak. It is the hope that kills you. These numbers by themselves mean little. The Texans have lost in a variety of different ways this season. This isn’t the utter defensive collapse that was 2010. It isn’t the pick six festival that was 2013. It hasn’t been any one thing and that is the most maddening part of it. The only consistent thing has been an inability to make the one or two key plays that winning reams make. Three of the four losses were one score games. We might as well call them the “Almost” Texans. The Key Numbers Total Yards: Texans 52/397, Cowboys 73/399 Rushing Yards: Texans 19/62, Cowboys 25/75 Passing Yards: Texans 33/335, Cowboys 48/324 Third Down Conversions: Texans 3/10, Cowboys 5/14 Fourth Down Conversions: Texans 0/0, Cowboys 1/1 Sacks: Texans 3, Cowboys 2 Turnovers: Texans 0, Cowboys 0 Penalties: Texans 13/90, Cowboys 6/47 Time of Possession: Texans 28:33, Cowboys 31:27 These numbers tell a story, but it might not be the story of the game. The stories are usually when these things happen. For instance, two sacks is not terrible. I’m sure Nick Caley would gladly take only two sacks allowed per game for the rest of the season. Unfortunately, it is about when these sacks happened. They happened at a stage in the game when they desperately needed sustained drives and instead they were three and outs. However, that spills us into the good, bad, and ugly. The Good We will get to Stroud in his own special section, so this one goes to Will Anderson yet again. Officially he had only a half a sack and five tackles but a couple of those were tackles for loss. As the Texans ponder their future they will need building blocks. These seasons reveal a ton about character. There are players that consider it a night at the office and make business decisions in key moments. Then there are players like Anderson. J.D. Clowney also had half a sack in his return to the field. Whatever is happening on defense, it is not happening on the defensive line. Throw in Danielle Hunter and you have a group of players getting constant pressure on Dak Prescott. Unfortunately, the units behind the defensive line didn’t play as well, but we as fans notice the players that show up and play hard and they will always be called out for their effort. The Bad I cannot completely torch Nick Caley for this effort. Any time you score 30 points and you don’t turn the football over it is a good day. However, there are still key points in these games when protections break down and play calls don’t make sense. More than anything, I hate days like today. They are the days that get stat heads like me (yup, I’ll cop to this one) to say that things are going well overall because they scored a ton of points in two games. The most important thing is that the Cowboys were yet another weak defensive team that struggles against the run. Yet, they looked like the 1985 Bears against the run. The Texans rushed for more than 100 yards in the first game and haven’t sniffed that since. For a hard-nosed physical football team that is pretty anemic. The offense deserves their portion of the blame for the defensive debacle. They couldn’t posses the ball long enough to keep the Cowboys offense off the field. You cannot let them run 70+ plays and live to tell about it. The Cowboys ran 20 more plays than the Texans and that is a recipe for disaster. The Ugly Someone needs to explain this to me like I’m a four year old. How do you allow a player to catch 17 passes in a football game? Yes, I know that Kamari Lassiter should have been a Pro Bowler and Derek Stingley was a Pro Bowler. The operative word there is was. They aren’t playing like that now for whatever reason. They aren’t bad football players per se. They still make plays and do good things, but they are not playing on the level they were last season. At a certain point you have to scrap what you are doing and do something else. The drive that pulled the Cowboys within 23-20 was the key drive of the game. The Texans stopped them twice inside the ten only to have penalties extend the drive. The first defensive holding/contact penalty on Lassiter was EXTREMELY questionable. George Pickens initiated most of the contact, so it was a horrible flag. The second penalty was not egregious. The Texans literally turned them over on downs after another set of downs where the Cowboys were ready to settle for a field goal. That was eight plays inside the ten. Even the Texans could score a touchdown in those conditions. That segment probably was the whole football game. It also encapsulates the season as a whole. Focus on Stroud I’ll have more to say on this later in the week, but the Texans have some huge decisions looming and none are bigger than the decision on Stroud. Yet, today was the first day I honestly considered Stroud’s point of view. Does he really want to be here? If he keeps ballin’ like he has the first four weeks the answer could be no. No, he is not going to make anyone forget Peyton Manning, Drew Brees, or Tom Brady, but he has mustered five touchdown passes in four games and thrown zero picks. He is one of three quarterbacks not to throw one. I could nitpick in this one, but what would be the point? Stroud threw for nearly 350 yards without a run game. He needed a drive at the end of the game and gave his team a lead with two minutes left. I’m not sure what else anyone wants from him. I will own up to my part in this whole thing. I questioned his abilities coming into the season saying that he is not an elite quarterback. I still don’t know that he is, but this 0-4 start is not on him. He is doing what they are asking him to do. That of course brings up the next obvious question. Are they using him to his most effective use? The answer is almost clearly no. We will have more on this later in the week as the whispers at 0-2 and 0-3 become raised voices at 0-4. They will become shouting and screaming with future losses. There is no joy in Mudville. The Texans are strung out.
author: Scott Barzilla

title: The State of the 2026 Houston Texans
summary: The Houston Texans just dropped their fourth straight game, this time falling to the Dallas Cowboys at home in another frustrating loss. The offense did its job, putting 30 points on the board and giving Houston the lead late in the fourth quarter. At some point, that has to be enough to win a football […]
full_text: The Houston Texans just dropped their fourth straight game, this time falling to the Dallas Cowboys at home in another frustrating loss. The offense did its job, putting 30 points on the board and giving Houston the lead late in the fourth quarter. At some point, that has to be enough to win a football game. The problem this season has not been the offense nearly as much as it has been the defense. In three of their first four games, the Texans’ offense has put the team in a position to close out the game, and the defense simply has not delivered when it mattered most. That is extremely concerning considering how much talent Houston has on that side of the ball. This is a unit filled with elite players at several positions, and coming into the season, the defense was expected to be one of the biggest strengths of this team. Instead, they have been majorly underwhelming through the first four weeks. The most frustrating part is how these games are being lost. Houston has had opportunities late in games to make one stop and walk away with a win, but they have consistently failed to do so. When you are trying to compete with the best teams in the AFC, those are situations where your best players need to step up. A lot of Houston’s issues this season can also be traced back to the coaching. Whether it is questionable decisions, a lack of adjustments, or simply not getting enough out of an extremely talented roster, something is clearly not working. At this point, it feels like changes need to be made in an attempt to salvage the season before it is too late. Starting 0-4 does not completely end your season, but the margin for error is now incredibly small, and Houston cannot afford to continue making the same mistakes every single week. This team is far too talented to be winless through four games, especially considering three of those games were played at home. There is still plenty of football left to be played, but eventually, talent on paper has to translate to wins. For the Texans, that needs to happen very soon.
author: Nickschwager

title: RECAP: Texans lose Battle of Texas to the Cowboys
summary: This was the Houston Texans’ 25th anniversary game. All of the team’s fan favorites were in attendance: Andre Johnson, DeAndre Hopkins, Arian Foster, Billy Miller, Brian Cushing, all were there (or so I was told). And this was the game they got to see: a perfect, and I do mean perfect, distillation of the Houston […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TEXAS - OCTOBER 04: Ka'imi Fairbairn #15 of the Houston Texans celebrates with teammates after making the kick for the point after a touchdown against the Dallas Cowboys during the third quarter at NRG Stadium on October 04, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Alex Slitz/Getty Images) | Getty Images This was the Houston Texans’ 25th anniversary game. All of the team’s fan favorites were in attendance: Andre Johnson, DeAndre Hopkins, Arian Foster, Billy Miller, Brian Cushing, all were there (or so I was told). And this was the game they got to see: a perfect, and I do mean perfect, distillation of the Houston Texans’ entire existence: a tremendous disappointment for all the same reasons. 25 years of this. This was supposed to be the year, right? The year they finally break through the divisional round into the conference finals and maybe, dare I say without laughing, their first Super Bowl appearance. 25 years of disappointment. This was THE team to do it. They had a dominant defense. They had a retooled (yet again) offensive line which was supposed to be better, a running game built for this offensive line, and a wide receiver corps that could stand up to anybody’s. 25 years of this game. The Texans lost yet another heartbreaker, though if you’ve been paying attention at all this season it came as little surprise. The Texans racked up 13 penalties for 90 yards, some deserved, some very much not (Brad Allen is an idiot). C.J. Stroud lived up to the level of play we’ve come to expect of him, going 21/31 for 347 yards and two touchdowns. Nico Collins proved to be the best part of the offense not named C.J. Stroud by grabbing those two touchdowns. 25 years of waiting till next year. But a bad offensive line performance and worse play calling by offensive coordinator Nick Caley stunted the Texans’ chances of playing well; of which we saw plenty last year. What we DID NOT see last year was a miserable effort by the Houston Texans defense to stop the Cowboys from putting the ball wherever the hell they wanted from the start of the third quarter onward. 25 years of Houston Texans football summed up with the usual shortcomings (the defense didn’t show up when it mattered, the offensive line was bad again, they couldn’t run the ball. It’s been 25 years and so little has changed for this team. The Texans are now 0-4 on the season and any chance of righting the ship, assuming it can be righted, is now moving into the realm of wishful thinking. 25 years. We’ve watched this for 25 years, folks. And this is what we have to show for it. They’re frauds. They will continue to be frauds as long as Nick Caley is calling plays. Because while the defense was bad, the offense has been bad under Nick Caley and no meaningful improvement has come from his time as the Texans OC. 25 YEARS. A quarter of a damn century of Texans football and I don’t think I’ve ever been more disappointed in this team. I still love this team, because I’m stupid and I make bad life decisions, but I’m tired of having to say wait until next year. Aren’t y’all? Vent to your heart’s content in the comments.

title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter alludes to Colts, among suitors, who have called on Marvin Harrison Jr. regarding trade availability
summary: According to ESPN’s Adam Schefter on ‘The Pat McAfee Show,’ the Indianapolis Colts are among the league suitors who have already called the Arizona Cardinals on the trade availability of underperforming young wideout Marvin Harrison Jr. ahead of the NFL’s upcoming Tuesday, November 10th trade deadline: Originally the 4th overall pick of the 2024 NFL […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CA - SEPTEMBER 27: Marvin Harrison Jr. #18 of the Arizona Cardinals heads to the locker room before an NFL game against the San Francisco 49ers on September 27, 2026 at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, CA. (Photo by Matthew Huang/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images According to ESPN’s Adam Schefter on ‘The Pat McAfee Show,’ the Indianapolis Colts are among the league suitors who have already called the Arizona Cardinals on the trade availability of underperforming young wideout Marvin Harrison Jr. ahead of the NFL’s upcoming Tuesday, November 10th trade deadline: Who's calling about Marvin Harrison Jr… The Indianapolis Colts are calling #PMSLive https://t.co/Ogpi7ipwdA pic.twitter.com/QBTdCDdb3x — Pat McAfee (@PatMcAfeeShow) October 5, 2026 Originally the 4th overall pick of the 2024 NFL Draft by Arizona, and widely considered a “can’t miss,” if not a generational wideout prospect, the 24-year-old wideout has largely (and surprisingly) struggled in over 2 seasons with the Cardinals—having been an increasing afterthought within their offense compared to their other starting receivers. Of course, he’s also the namesake of his legendary father, Marvin Harrison Sr., who’s a Pro Football Hall of Famer and the all-time greatest wide receiver in Indianapolis franchise history, as the leader in nearly all of their major statistical receiving categories. However, Jr.‘s much bigger than his famous pops, at 6,‘3”, 220 pounds, but otherwise, it’s not hard to miss the uncanny physical resemblance between the two wideouts. There’s been unnamed speculation that Harrison’s Jr. trade value has fallen to a ‘quality Day 3 pick,’ as in some anonymous league circles, he’s viewed more as a “3rd wide receiver with upside.” That being said, it’s hard to envision the Cardinals actually moving him elsewhere, unless they get meaningful trade value in return, in some ways, similarly to the Colts have handled backup quarterback Anthony Richardson’s availability to-date. For what it’s worth, Harrison Jr. just had his first touchdown reception of the season in Week 4, but otherwise, has underwhelmed to just 5 receptions for 85 total receiving yards collectively through Arizona’s first four games. It seems like a combination of maturity, underperformance, and not being properly utilized by the Arizona offense. While I won’t get too into the weeds again of why Harrison Jr. makes sense for the Colts , it’s clear that after losing lead wideout Alec Pierce to injured reserve and veteran Keenan Allen now banged up, having missed last weekend’s game, that Indianapolis could use some immediate positional reinforcements, especially with veteran pickup Darius Slayton still not active through two weeks of being with the team. Harrison Jr. would be a legacy here, and the hope is that Colts wide receivers coach Reggie Wayne, who formed one of the most prolific wide receiver duos in NFL history alongside Harrison Jr.‘s father, could coach some “tough love” into the still young and talented wideout, who may just need a change of scenery to reach his full playing career potential. If nothing else, it seems like a fairly favorable ‘buy-low’ opportunity for a former top wideout prospect, who almost every team coveted not too long ago ahead of the 2024 NFL Draft— with the Colts being among them .

title: Horsepower or Horseplay? Colts’ performances from Week 4 win across the pond
summary: After an initial sloppy start, the Indianapolis Colts (2-2) righted the trolleybus offensively, took advantage of a rookie 3rd-string quarterback defensively, and bested the Washington Commanders (1-3), 30-13, in London this past Sunday—now back to playing .500 football for the first time this season. We’ll look at some of the studs, duds, and maybe a […]
full_text: Oct 4, 2026; Tottenham, ENG; Indianapolis Colts defensive tackle DeForest Buckner (99) hits Washington Commanders quarterback Athan Kaliakmanis (16) during the second quarter at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Geoff Burke-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect After an initial sloppy start, the Indianapolis Colts (2-2) righted the trolleybus offensively, took advantage of a rookie 3rd-string quarterback defensively, and bested the Washington Commanders (1-3), 30-13, in London this past Sunday—now back to playing .500 football for the first time this season. We’ll look at some of the studs, duds, and maybe a little in between regarding their latest international win: Horsepower RB Jonathan Taylor: The Colts star workhorse continues to shine overseas, recording 95 total rushing yards and 2 rushing touchdowns on 20 carries (4.8 ypc. avg.). With starting quarterback Daniel Jones clearly shaky play early on (which we’ll get to here in a bit), the Colts went “back to the basics,” and that was riding the efficient Taylor in this one (with some rookie rusher Seth McGowan sprinkled in as a change-of-pace back). Taylor is now the all-time international leading rusher (6 touchdowns) and rushing yards leader (408) in league history, and whether it was “drinking tea” or “waving like the queen” following his two touchdowns runs on the day, he celebrated in London style. DT DeForest Buckner: With the Colts offense spiraling early on (with a fumble lost, three straight punts, and an interception on their first five offensive drives), Buckner, to me, almost single-handedly kept the Colts in this football game defensively with his hustle, impact, and leadership. Whether it was stopping the run, creating pass pressure, or just all-out effort , Buckner played like a man on a mission, and was a huge reason why the Indianapolis defense held the Commanders to just two field goals on their first two offensive drives, despite being gifted a short field on their first possession because of the weird Jones’ fumble. Buckner deserves to be a Colts’ Ring of Honor player when it’s all said-and-done, and his collective impact on Sunday is a big reason why. That was a performance to remember, one day looking back at his standout career here in Indianapolis. While we’re on the position, I’d also like to give backup defensive tackle Ade Adebawore an honorable mention, who made his pass rushing presence felt in limited action again, with 0.5 sacks and 2 QB hits. He continues to be a menace as a subpackage interior pass rusher. LB Jaylon Carlies: The Colts much maligned starting linebacker unit has taken its fair share of lumps and growing criticism to begin the 2026 campaign, but arguably had their best performance of the season on Sunday. In particular, Carlies showcased his best, and elite athleticism, by somehow batting an Athan Kaliakmanis pass to himself for the interception early in the 3rd quarter . CB Charvarius Ward : The Colts secondary had its fair share of coverage gaffes, by allowing a handful of explosive big plays to the rookie Kaliakmanis, but wearing the guardians cap again, Ward arguably had his best game of the season in coverage. Specifically, he allowed just two receptions for 13 total receiving yards on 7 targets in coverage (28.6 catch rate) with 3 pass breakups . PK Spencer Shrader: Regarding what was a narrowly won offseason competition, the Colts absolutely made the right call by naming Shrader the victor, who was a perfect 3 for 3 from field goal range again including makes from 48 yards, 52 yards, and 44 yards. That’ll certainly play on special teams! Horseplay QB Daniel Jones : For the first 1.5 quarters in this one, Jones looked like how a lot of Colts fans may have thought he’d look coming off last year’s season-ending torn Achilles in Week 14 with no preseason reps. He has to take better care of the football on the weird sack fumble, and the interception off his back-foot under duress to Commanders veteran cornerback Rasul Douglas is just a play that can’t happen at this level. Jones has to either feel the pressure earlier or “eat the sack,” rather than throw a gifted lollipop in coverage. Jones looked closer to the failed franchise quarterback hopeful who was too turnover prone with the New York Giants than the breakout quarterback we surprisingly saw during the first half of last season in his Indianapolis debut. No idea if the Colts coaching staff was ever seriously contemplating an in-game change, but one more offensive drive that ended in another Jones brutal turnover, and as fans, we were realistically getting close to advocating for seeing Anthony Richardson again—if we weren’t already. Jones absolutely cannot play that way again in Pittsburgh next week, which has been a historical franchise house of horrors. CB Sauce Gardner: Whether you want to argue that Gardner has not lived up to his billing so far in Indianapolis, after the Colts surprisingly surrendered two first round picks, it’s fair game—although Gardner himself did not make that trade. In London, he clearly played his worst game as a member of the Colts. He allowed 4 receptions for 117 total receiving yards and a touchdown reception on his 5 pass coverage targets , although I will also contend that his safety help (i.e., rookie A.J. Haulcy) and the Indy pass pressure didn’t do him favors either by leaving him on a coverage island for so long. Even with his lack of interceptions, the Colts need Gardner to be a shutdown #1 cornerback, and on Sunday, he was far from it, as he was openly picked on by Kaliakmanis on two explosive passing plays deep.
author: Luke Schultheis

title: Colts Monday Morning Awards: Week 4 vs Commanders (London)
summary: The Colts shook off an ugly first quarter and leaned on their run game to walk out of Tottenham Hotspur Stadium with a convincing 30-13 win. Was the first month of the season pretty? Absolutely not, but the Stampede Blue Community would have taken a 2-2 record after a tough stretch against the Ravens, Chiefs, […]
full_text: London, United Kingdom - October 4: Robert Henry Jr. of Washington Commanders is tackled by Indianapolis Colts linebacker Jaylon Carlies during the Indianapolis Colts and Washington Commanders match at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on October 4, 2026 in London, United Kingdom. (Photo by Vince Mignott/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty Images) | DeFodi Images via Getty Images The Colts shook off an ugly first quarter and leaned on their run game to walk out of Tottenham Hotspur Stadium with a convincing 30-13 win. Was the first month of the season pretty? Absolutely not, but the Stampede Blue Community would have taken a 2-2 record after a tough stretch against the Ravens, Chiefs, Texans and Commanders, in that order. The defense has stepped up in consecutive games and dominated third down, while the rushing attack took over and Jonathan Taylor continued cementing his name into the record books as an international superstar. Here’s to a new edition of Monday Morning Awards. MVP of the Game: Jonathan Taylor Who else deserves it other than the best player on the roster? Taylor rushed for 95 yards and two touchdowns on 20 carries, becoming both the NFL’s all-time leading rusher and scorer in international games. After he bounced left for a 5-yard score to give the Colts a lead they would never relinquish, he celebrated his fifth touchdown of the season by sitting criss-cross applesauce to veritably sip tea in front of a roaring crowd in London. TAYLOR TOUCHDOWN #INDsWAS on NFLN pic.twitter.com/p1WfMtYoA4 — Indianapolis Colts (@Colts) October 4, 2026 With 75 career touchdowns, Indy’s 27-year-old tailback joined Jim Brown, Emmitt Smith, and LaDainian Tomlinson, as the only running backs to reach that mark before turning 28. Taylor doesn’t turn 28 until after the regular season and wild card weekend ends. Dud of the Game: Daniel Jones performance The dud of the game came from Daniel Jones, who was strip-sacked by Odafe Oweh and lost the fumble, giving Washington possession near the Colts’ red zone on the second snap from scrimmage. Jones later threw an interception off his back foot to cornerback Rasul Douglas, marking his eighth turnover-worthy play through four games and putting the Colts in an early deficit before he finally settled in. The veteran QB finished 19 of 34 for just 143 passing yards, but scrambled for a 4-yard touchdown to put the Colts ahead by two scores early in the fourth quarter. Daniel Jones!!! #INDvsWAS on NFLN pic.twitter.com/5AYd8dcQVP — Indianapolis Colts (@Colts) October 4, 2026 Worst Play of the Game: Turnover terminates opening drive The worst play of the game has to be the opening sequence as the Colts had the ball for just two snaps before Jones fumbled and gave Washington a chance to seize an early lead on a short field. Oweh rushed from the right edge and drove left tackle Bernhard Raimann straight into Jones’ dropback, which knocked the ball loose before Oweh recovered it himself. Best Play of the Game: Jaylon Carlies interception If the first half was hard to stomach, any doubt of leaving London without a victory vanished when the defense finally got the momentum-shifting turnover it needed to start the third quarter. Washington was pushed backward from a penalty and faced with third-and-17, then linebacker Jaylon Carlies reached up to tip a pass from opposing QB Athan Kaliakmanis, hauled in his first career interception and returned it to the Commanders’ 27-yard line. Four plays later, Taylor plunged into the end zone to give Indianapolis a 17-6 lead. Heck of a play from @Colts LB Jaylon Carlies @INDvsWAS on NFL Network Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/am18AmEMmD — NFL (@NFL) October 4, 2026 Best Position Group: Defensive line The defensive front combined for 14 stops and 11 QB hits, then made life miserable as the Commanders were able to convert just 2-of-15 third downs. Laiatu Latu and Adetomiwa Adebawore combined for a sack that knocked opposing starter Marcus Mariota out of the game, while Latu added two more quarterback hits. DeForest Buckner had three quarterback hits of his own, and collected his 100th career tackle for loss. The biggest difference was the pressure as Washington could not move the sticks with its emergency third-string QB. Unsung Hero: Spencer Shrader Kicker Spencer Shrader made all three field goals from 48, 52, and 44-yards out to keep the Colts ahead with enough cushion to maintain a lead. His 52-yarder in the third quarter pushed the Colts’ lead back to seven after Washington had trimmed the deficit to 17-13. Shrader quietly put together one of those games where you don’t notice the kicker until you look at the scoreboard and realize he has as many points as the opponent. Along with three extra points, Shrader collected 12 points while the Commanders left 13 on the scoreboard. Rookie of the Week: Seth McGowan Rookie running back Seth McGowan didn’t need a huge workload, but his 10 touches were more than enough to make an impact. With Taylor doing most of the heavy-lifting, McGowan carried the ball six times for 31 yards, averaging 5.2 per carry. Two of those six carries resulted in first downs as McGowan provided a nice change of pace and showed why he’s capable of getting more opportunities. McGowan also returned four kickoffs for a combined 102 return yards, with the final return stopping the Commanders’ momentum and ultimately led to a field goal. Honorable Mention: Justin Walley Sunday was Justin Walley’s best game of his young career. He finished with eight tackles and a key sack on an blitz that forced a fourth down and knocked the Commanders out of field-goal range. Walley came screaming uncovered from the blindside and dropped Kaliakmanis for a 9-yard sack that forced Washington to punt. Walley posted a 75.4 coverage grade, which ranked among the top 10 cornerbacks who played at least 10 coverage snaps in Week 4. Watch out for Walley 👀 #INDvsWAS on NFLN pic.twitter.com/ymbykBpdUA — Indianapolis Colts (@Colts) October 4, 2026 Charvarius Ward deserves credit when its due, too. Washington completed only two catches against him on seven targets, while Ward recorded three forced incompletions. His three forced incompletions and 41.0 snaps per reception was third among cornerbacks through Sunday in Week 4. Indy struggled to start the game, but played complementary football in the second half. The Colts finished with just one penalty compared to Washington’s 10 and won the turnover battle after the early mistake. Between the clean play, dominance on third down and pounding the rock with their marquee tailback, the Colts stuck to their playstyle and return stateside with an even 2-2 record. The Colts travel to Pittsburgh to face the Steelers (2-2) next Sunday, with kickoff set for 1 p.m.
author: Thomas Butler-Guerrero

title: The Colts won, but Daniel Jones needs to get a grip
summary: The Indianapolis Colts found some much-needed fortune in London as they managed to beat the Washington Commanders and climb to 2-2. Yes, there was skill and preparation involved, but there was a lot of luck as well. Daniel Jones tested that luck throughout the game, but if the Colts are going to keep winning, they […]
full_text: London, United Kingdom - October 4: Tim Settle of Washington Commanders and Daniel Jones of Indianapolis Colts battle for the ball during the Indianapolis Colts and Washington Commanders match between Indianapolis Colts and Washington Commanders at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on October 4, 2026 in London, United Kingdom. (Photo by Vince Mignott/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty Images) | DeFodi Images via Getty Images The Indianapolis Colts found some much-needed fortune in London as they managed to beat the Washington Commanders and climb to 2-2. Yes, there was skill and preparation involved, but there was a lot of luck as well. Daniel Jones tested that luck throughout the game, but if the Colts are going to keep winning, they need to reserve some in the tank. The best way to do that is for Jones to stop turning the ball over. Jones fumbled on the second play of the game in a highly unusual fashion. It wasn’t as bizarre as the “butt fumble”, but it looked just as sloppy. The defender bull rushed Bernhard Raimann and had them both in Jones’ face, but to fumble the ball like that was simply odd. Just like against the Texans, he threw off his back foot under pressure and was intercepted. It was a dispiriting quarter and a half as the offense was dreadful. Luckily, the Colts weathered the early storm. The defense held strong and kept the Commanders out of the endzone to limit the damage to six. Additionally, facing a third string quarterback didn’t hurt either. That isn’t always going to be the case, however. The better teams in this league will make the Colts pay for their errors. Jones has to be better. He has to protect the ball and play smarter. He cannot turn the ball over at this rate if the Colts hope to survive. Daniel Jones has seven turnovers across four games with five in the last two. That looks like the second half of 2025 Jones, but the Colts can’t win with that version. An occasional turnover is understandable, but at least two of the fumbles and both of the interceptions were avoidable. Those must be cleaned up. Jones has to find a way to get a grip.

title: Colts-Steelers opening odds:  Steal one in the Steel City
summary: The Indianapolis Colts are heading to a dark place. Game day may be bright and sunny with the perfect temperature and the right amount of wind, but it is sure to send a chill down the spine of Colts Nation. Facing the Pittsburgh Steelers in Pittsburgh has almost never gone well, but the Colts get […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 27: A detailed view of aPittsburgh Steelers helmet on the field prior to an NFL football game between the Cincinnati Bengals and Pittsburgh Steelers on September 27, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Indianapolis Colts are heading to a dark place. Game day may be bright and sunny with the perfect temperature and the right amount of wind, but it is sure to send a chill down the spine of Colts Nation. Facing the Pittsburgh Steelers in Pittsburgh has almost never gone well, but the Colts get a chance to right some wrongs next week. FanDuel Sportsbook has the Colts as underdogs at +1.5 points in the spread. The money line starts at +112 while the over/under comes in at 41.5. The Colts have gotten their season back on track after an 0-2 start. Wins against the Texans and Commanders have them pointed in the right direction. Concerning play from Daniel Jones continues to be a mild theme as turnovers and a lack of positive ball movement were the story for the offense in the first half. Luckily, Jonathan Taylor wears a horseshoe, and the defense kept this one close enough for the Colts to pull comfortably ahead and reach .500. The Steelers found themselves on the rare side of an “L” to the Cleveland Browns. It’s a rivalry that’s actually become more of a true division battle over the years than it used to be, though. The old Browns would have rolled over after falling behind 0-7 to start, but this is the 3-1 Browns. They scored the next 21 and held the Steelers off with a late-game field goal. The Steelers will be looking to get that taste out of their mouths. This is a huge game for the Colts. A 2-3 to start the year with their schedule is something most fans would have taken. Now that they are at 2-2, however, 3-2 sounds much better. It will be a chance to continue their streak and build contender status in the league by picking up a solid win against an opponent that causes them fits. This could mark a major season shift.
author: Jon Spradley

title: Colts cruise past Commanders 30-13 for third straight international win
summary: The Indianapolis Colts found their rhythm Sunday morning in London, overcoming an early deficit to cruise to a commanding 30-13 victory over the Washington Commanders at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. A sluggish start featured a fumble on the second snap from scrimmage and an interception from quarterback Daniel Jones. Commanders linebacker Odafe Oweh rushed left tackle […]
full_text: LONDON, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 04: Jonathan Taylor of the Indianapolis Colts is tackled by Nick Cross of the Washington Commanders during the NFL match between Indianapolis Colts and Washington Commanders as part of the London NFL Series 2026 at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on October 04, 2026 in London, England. (Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Indianapolis Colts found their rhythm Sunday morning in London, overcoming an early deficit to cruise to a commanding 30-13 victory over the Washington Commanders at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. A sluggish start featured a fumble on the second snap from scrimmage and an interception from quarterback Daniel Jones. Commanders linebacker Odafe Oweh rushed left tackle Bernhard Raimann into Jones’ stepback, forcing a fumble that Oweh recovered near the red zone. Washington capitalized with a pair of chip shots from kicker Drew Stevens to take a 6-0 lead midway through the opening frame. Indy’s offense began to settle in the second quarter as Jones connected with tight end Tyler Warren for a 12-yard gain on third down to move past midfield. After an unnecessary roughness penalty extended the drive, Jones fed running back Jonathan Taylor to follow his blockers and bounce left for a 5-yard touchdown run to give the Colts their first lead, which they never relinquished. The international star tailback led the Colts with a game-high 95 rushing yards on 20 carries and scored two touchdowns, becoming the NFL’s all-time leading rusher in International Series games. TAYLOR TOUCHDOWN #INDsWAS on NFLN pic.twitter.com/p1WfMtYoA4 — Indianapolis Colts (@Colts) October 4, 2026 The Colts carried that momentum into the final two-minute drive to close the first half. Jones connected with Warren and Ashton Dulin to move the offense into enemy territory before kicker Spencer Shrader drilled a 48-yard field goal as time expired giving Indianapolis a 10-6 halftime lead. The Colts defense terminated the Commanders first drive of the second half with a takeaway. After forcing Washington into third-and-17, linebacker Jaylon Carlies tipped a pass on the run from emergency third-string quarterback Athan Kaliakmanis and came down with his first career interception at Washington’s 27-yard line. Taylor made the Commanders pay, capping off the ensuing drive with his second 5-yard touchdown run to extend Indianapolis’ lead to 17-6. His 408 rushing yards on 75 carries and six touchdowns in International Series games are also the most in league history. Carlies caught THAT. #INDvsWAS on NFLN pic.twitter.com/y0FdbDLmBM — Indianapolis Colts (@Colts) October 4, 2026 Washington answered with an explosive play as Kaliakmanis found Treylon Burks wide open deep for a 47-yard touchdown to trim the deficit to 17-13. The Colts defense did let up a few monstrous gains, but held firm with the pass rush as cornerback Justin Walley recorded his first career sack, while Laiatu Latu and Adetomiwa Adebawore combined for another sack. Shrader drilled a 52-yard field goal to restore a seven-point cushion before the Colts took control in the fourth quarter, then he sealed the victory with a 44-yarder midway through the fourth. Indianapolis leaned on Taylor and the punishing ground game to sustain a long drive into the red zone. Jones mastered the run-pass-option and kept it himself to stroll into the end zone for a 4-yard touchdown run, pushing the lead to two possessions. Jones finished 19-of-34 for 143 passing yards, but threw an interception and lost a fumble. Indianapolis (2-2) now turns its attention to Pittsburgh, where the Colts visit the Steelers (2-2) next Sunday at 1 p.m. in a Week 5 matchup.
