title: Colts win ugly in London, as overcome sloppy start vs. Commanders and eventually settle in
summary: The Indianapolis Colts (2-2) overcame a sloppy start to beat the Washington Commanders (1-3), 30-13, in London in Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, to begin playing .500 football for the first time in the 2026 season. In particular, the Colts and starting quarterback Daniel Jones got off to a dreadful start, as Indianapolis had only 1 offensive […]
full_text: LONDON, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 04: Jonathan Taylor of the Indianapolis Colts celebrates a touchdown during the NFL match between Indianapolis Colts and Washington Commanders as part of the London NFL Series 2026 at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on October 04, 2026 in London, England. (Photo by Alex Pantling/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Indianapolis Colts (2-2) overcame a sloppy start to beat the Washington Commanders (1-3), 30-13, in London in Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, to begin playing .500 football for the first time in the 2026 season. In particular, the Colts and starting quarterback Daniel Jones got off to a dreadful start, as Indianapolis had only 1 offensive yard collectively its first three offensive drives. Jones had one of the weirdest fumbles you’ll see on the Colts opening drive , after starting left tackle Bernhard Raimann got ‘blown up,‘ and Indianapolis, collectively, with a banged up receiving corps and surrendering constant interior pass pressure, couldn’t muster much of anything offensively early on. After the shaky Jones inexplicably threw an interception off his backfoot under pressure to Commanders veteran cornerback Rasul Douglas with 9:59 left in the second quarter, the Colts’ first 5 offensive drives were a fumble lost, 3 punts in a row, and then the Douglas interception, which obviously, won’t get it done. Fortunately, the Colts defense bent, but did not break during that same period of time, only allowing two field goals on the Commanders two opening drives (*the first on a short field) and were aided by the fact that Commanders starting quarterback Marcus Mariota (knee) left early in this one, with Washington 3rd-string quarterback Athan Kaliakmanis taking over the rest of the way in relief of Mariota, beginning with 5:20 left in the first quarter. For the Colts offensively, star running back Jonathan Taylor, who’s now the NFL’s all-time leading in scorer regarding international football, had 20 carries for 95 total rushing yards and 2 rushing touchdowns, while Indianapolis mixed in backup running back Seth McGowan more, who had 6 carries for 31 total rushing yards, purely to help limit some of Taylor’s workload throughout the long season. Passing wise, Jones completed 19 of 34 pass attempts for 143 total passing yards, 0 touchdowns, and an interception and a fumble lost, while veteran wideout Laquon Treadwell led the Colts in receiving with 5 receptions for 42 total receiving yards. While Jones settled down a bit, he was not very good in this one. Defensively, the Colts were largely good going against the Commanders rookie third-string quarterback. Colts defensive tackle DeForest Buckner deserves a lot of credit for his constant hustle, impact, and pass pressure, as he kept Indianapolis in this one defensively early on until the offense finally settled in midway through the 2nd quarter. He had 4 tackles (2 solo), a tackle for loss, a pass defensed, and 3 QB hits. Colts subpackage defensive tackle Ade Adebawore also added some interior pass pressures off the bench, finishing 0.5 sacks and 2 QB hits. Colts linebacker Jaylon Carlies had an athletic interception off Kaliakmanis which he batted to himself early in the 3rd quarter and set up Taylor’s 2nd touchdown run of the day, as Indianapolis was able to start pulling away. Although they got off to a bit of a slow start themselves, the Colts defense was a strength of the team for much of the day, which they rightfully should be going against a rookie 3rd-string backup quarterback, with no NFL prior NFL experience. That being said, Colts cornerback Sauce Gardner surprisingly struggled on two deep Kaliakmanis’ throws, although it looked like there may have been at least some miscommunication or a blown coverage assignment by rookie safety AJ Haulcy regarding expected over-the-top help on the 47-yard Treylon Burks touchdown reception early in the 3rd quarter. It’ll be interesting to see if the Colts will clarify what happened this week on that ‘stop-and-go’ by Burks on Gardner that led to an easy big score. Lastly, Colts kicker Spencer Shrader continues to be ‘money in the bank’ so far this early season with makes of 48 yards, 52 yards, and 44 yards in this one, while successfully converting all 3 of his extra point attempts.

title: 3 Numbers to Know From the Jaguars’ Win Over the Bengals
summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars eeked out a win over the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 4 to move to 3-1 on the season. Hooray! Here are a few stats that stand out from the victory. 125 That’s how many yards the Jaguars were penalized on Sunday. It’s the most by Jacksonville since Week 7 of the 2019 […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OHIO - OCTOBER 4: Ventrell Miller #51 of the Jacksonville Jaguars celebrates during the third quarter of a game against the Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium on October 4, 2026 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Jacksonville Jaguars eeked out a win over the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 4 to move to 3-1 on the season. Hooray! Here are a few stats that stand out from the victory. 125 That’s how many yards the Jaguars were penalized on Sunday. It’s the most by Jacksonville since Week 7 of the 2019 season… when the Jags beat the Bengals in Cincinnati, 27-17. Head coach Liam Coen said after the game, “I’ve never been a part of anything like that before in my life.” Liam Coen didn’t want to get fined commenting about penalties in the first half 🤣 “I’m not going to say anything to get fined. That was just mental. I’ve just never seen something quite that much in the first half of a football game.” #Jaguars #DUUUVAL pic.twitter.com/MgJVds9JyW — Action Sports Jax (@ActionSportsJax) October 4, 2026 The Jaguars had 10 penalties for 125 yards, and the Bengals weren’t far behind (11 for 108). And the teams really weren’t that sloppy. Sure, there were a few obvious calls, but most of the flags should’ve been picked up. Or not called in the first place. Jacksonville had two touchdowns, an interception, and a lengthy kickoff return nullified by penalties. They still found a way to get the job done. Though they may not have beaten the “can’t stop great passers” allegations, they did quiet the “can’t finish ball games” concerns. 23 That’s how many rushing yards the Jaguars allowed on Sunday. It’s the fifth-fewest in franchise history. Fewest single-game rushing yards allowed by #Jaguars in franchise history (regular season/playoffs) … 10 by KC (Oct. 2007) 14 by Arizona (Nov. 2013) 14 by Detroit (Nov. 2016) 21 by MIami (Jan. 2000) 23 by Cincinnati … today Per @pfref — Ryan O'Halloran (@ryanohalloran) October 4, 2026 Jacksonville has now gone 21 straight games without allowing a single rusher to reach 75 yards on the ground. That’s the fourth-longest streak by any team in the Super Bowl era, per ESPN . Bengals starter Chase Brown couldn’t get anything going — he finished with 10 rushing yards on 9 carries. Joe Burrow and Samaje Perine chipped in 6 and 7 yards, respectively, on 3 carries apiece. That adds up to 1.5 yards per rush for Cincinnati. Burrow may have thrown for 428 yards, but he wasn’t all that efficient. The Jaguars held him to 7.9 yards per attempt. He had more interceptions (2) than touchdowns (1). By completely shutting down the run, Jacksonville forced Cincinnati to be one-dimensional on offense. Burrow couldn’t get the job done. 3:1 That’s the ratio of how often Jarrian Jones was targeted in coverage compared to Travis Hunter on Sunday. Hunter was targeted 6 times, per PFF. He allowed 3 catches for 20 yards while notching 2 pass breakups. Jones was targeted EIGHTEEN TIMES, allowing 11 catches for 133 yards. He had 1 pass breakup. Jones finished with a 59.6 coverage grade, which seems about right, but there should probably be a grading curve. The guy was going against some elite receivers in Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. After Chase left the game in the first half with a concussion, Higgins became the focal point of Cincinnati’s offense, and Jones matched up against him for much of the game. Half of Jones’ targets in coverage went to Higgins. He finished with 4 catches for 56 yards against Jones, compared to 7 catches for 101 yards against all other Jaguars defenders. It was far from Jones’ best game — but it’s not like he was burned over and over again. He did just enough to help Jacksonville pull out a road victory against a playoff contender. He didn’t come close to acing the test, but in my book, he passed it. For context, JJ was playing boundary CB all day. He was primarily aligned over Tee Higgins since he is the Bengals’ X receiver. With Chase leaving the game early, more targets went to Higgins. Also, the Jags played a lot of Cover 2 and Cover 6 (1/4, 1/4 and 1/2) wirh JJ playing… https://t.co/sVJKr2Jn0h — Bucky Brooks (@BuckyBrooks) October 5, 2026 Hunter had an easier assignment than Jones, but man oh man, he passed this week’s test with flying colors. He had a teach tape PBU , a leaping PBU , a colossal tackle , and a filthy interception negated by a penalty. The Heisman Trophy winner earned an 80.8 coverage grade from PFF. Other numbers to know: 9 . That’s how many consecutive games the Jaguars have with an interception. It’s the longest streak in franchise history and the longest active streak in the NFL. 38 . That’s how many points off takeaways the Jaguars have this season. It’s the most in the NFL. 3 . That’s how many redzone takeaways the Jaguars have this season. No other team has more than 1. 0 . That’s how many first half touchdowns the Jaguars have allowed this season. They’re the first team to do so in each of their first four games since the 2022 49ers. 95 . That’s how many receiving yards Brenton Strange had on Sunday. It is a new career-high for him. 25 . That’s how long Chris Rodriguez’s rushing touchdown was on Sunday. It is a new career-high for him. 100% . That’s how often Travis Hunter was on the field for Jacksonville’s defensive snaps on Sunday. It is a new career-high for him. 0% . That’s how often Travis Hunter was on the field for Jacksonville’s offensive snaps on Sunday. It is a new career-low for him. 55 . That’s how many consecutive games Jakobi Meyers has had a 1st down catch. It’s the longest active streak in the NFL. 81 . title: Jaguars Winners And Losers From Week 4: Defense Leads In Tough Road Win
summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars might have something cooking. On a Sunday where the Jags had to not only beat the Cincinnati Bengals but the NFL Zebras, they did so anyway, defeating Cincy on the road 22-17. It wasn’t pretty, but it was gritty, proving the Jags aren’t only capable of winning on the road but winning […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OHIO - OCTOBER 04: Defensive end Myles Murphy #99 of the Cincinnati Bengals is penalized for a face mask on running back Bhayshul Tuten #33 of the Jacksonville Jaguars during the second quarter of an NFL game at Paycor Stadium on October 04, 2026 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Jeff Dean/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Jacksonville Jaguars might have something cooking. On a Sunday where the Jags had to not only beat the Cincinnati Bengals but the NFL Zebras, they did so anyway, defeating Cincy on the road 22-17 . It wasn’t pretty, but it was gritty, proving the Jags aren’t only capable of winning on the road but winning when things are not going 100% their way. There is no denying that this defense is legit after four games this season. And this offense is extremely effective when given the chance. Beating the Bengals doesn’t mean Jacksonville has the automatic path to the Super Bowl, but teams have to win those types of games if they are to have a legit chance at winning it all. The Jags now seem like they have the mettle to do it. WINNERS Mentality Sometimes you just need to get the monkey off your back. For some reason, the Bengals have been a thorn in the side of Jacksonville for a handful of years. Whenever these two teams meet all hell just breaks loose for some reason. While this matchup was no different, the score was in favor of the Jags this time. Losing to the Broncos stung. It stung even more when the team came home and pummeled the Patriots. I think Jacksonville needed a bit of a “prove it” road win to really put a stamp on the front part of the year and make it known far and wide this team can travel. The Jags don’t play in Jacksonville for quite some time now as they prepare to ship off to London. Earning a win like that could be an excellent boost as they embark overseas. Just listen to how head coach Liam Coen talks about this one. You need wins like this to really bring it all together. Tough team. Tough win. pic.twitter.com/ydMV36wo8c — Jacksonville Jaguars (@Jaguars) October 4, 2026 Travis Hunter, Jourdan Lewis and Jarrian Jones It’s not often cornerbacks are winners when facing a Cincy offense featuring Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. Despite what the stats may say, these guys played lights out. Hunter is now stacking consecutive great games on defense after ripping down his first pick last week. He had an athletic pick called back Sunday, but did only allow three catches for 21 yards to go with two pass breakups and a huge hit along the sideline. The second-year corner was the second highest graded player on the team according to PFF. Travis Hunter with a big hit, he's fired up! pic.twitter.com/yEWpTbNa9W — Fitz (@LaurieFitzptrck) October 4, 2026 As for the others, Jarrian Jones was second on the team in tackles (seven) and had a tackle for loss and this nice PBU . Jourdan Lewis took down a pick and almost housed it. This cornerback room rose to the challenge in a difficult circumstance, especially considering Higgins and Chase were catching a lot of balls for a lot of yards. That never broke the confidence in the corners and it was a humongous factor in why Jacksonville won. A big shoutout also goes to safety Rayuan Lane, who not only led the team in tackles but made the game-ending over field tackle to seal it. Ray Lane with the stop that wins the game for the Jaguars on 4th and 10 pic.twitter.com/iBYb7HTUoy — Fitz (@LaurieFitzptrck) October 4, 2026 Running The ball On the offensive side, Jacksonville had a solid time running the rock against Cincy’s pretty solid defensive line. Jacksonville rushed for 111 total yards and one ground score from Chris Rodriguez. Bhayshul Tuten led the game in rushing with 73 yards on 17 carries. Speaking of PFF grades, Tuten ended up being the highest graded player when all was said and done. Tuten now has back to back games over 70 yards rushing and three straight games with two catches. This running back core is coming together quite nicely after a bit of a quiet start. Chris Rodriguez makes it a two-score game with a 25-yard TD! JAXvsCIN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/EocORsZ5jR — NFL (@NFL) October 4, 2026 Jacksonville needs to be able to run the ball effectively to set up its huge passing game. Conversely, the team needs to be able to stop the run in order to sell out to stop the pass which… Stopping The Run Jacksonville did that on Sunday! Cincinnati had absolutely nothing going on the ground, finishing the game with just 23 combined yards rushing. Cincy had just one run over four yards, the second time in franchise history the team was able to limit a rushing attack in such a manner. Arik Armstead had a big game. DaVon Hamilton had another bulldozing afternoon. Those guys sold out to stop the run and in turn were in the lap of Burrow all day. Again, the stats may not jump off the page because Burrow passed for over 400, but he had to because the Jags were not going to allow any run game to beat them. Bend but don’t break. Mission accomplished. Cam Little Obligatory Cam Little appreciation section. Little nailed three field goals with a long of 55. He is 4-6 on the year on kicks and perfect under 50 yards. Little’s leg was integral to victory on Sunday and he deserves a little bit of praise, like always. Al’s Pizza For the second straight week, the defense triggered the Al’s Pizza and Big Cat Country promo. Courtesy of interceptions by both Foye Oluokun and Lewis, customers can get 50% off their Al’s Pizza order through Oct. 6. Get some pizza and watch whatever the hell unfolds between the Saints and the Falcons on Monday night. Please forgive me for interrupting, but the defense has made two interceptions, so Al’s Pizza is offering 50% off pizza! Offer code “PIZZAPICKOFF” is valid for 48 hours after the game on https://t.co/VQgsy0KG5d 🐆 pic.twitter.com/XXlQ6qJiww — Big Cat Country (@BigCatCountry) October 4, 2026 The Pass Catchers In a game with some of the biggest wide receivers in football, it’s funny to me that Parker Washington didn’t have a bigger game. Instead, it was Brenton Strange who led the pass catchers. Strange had 95 yards on seven catches. It was a Strange catch that set up Rodriguez’s score and a Strange catch that extended Jacksonville’s last drive to eat up more clock. Lo’ and behold, it was Josh Cameron who was second on the team in receiving with 42 yards, coming ever so close to scoring yet again. Even Brian Thomas Jr. (yes, him!) scored on Sunday. It was an everybody eats type of afternoon for the pass catchers and it was exactly what Jacksonville needed. Josh Cameron gets inside the 5 on a catch-and-run 😤 JAXvsCIN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/CmTUPhSj6A — NFL (@NFL) October 4, 2026 LOSERS Penalties Holy shit was a showing from the NFL referees. There were 24 accepted penalties in that game, 13 of which going against the Jags. Multiple touchdowns were called back. A Hunter interception was called back. Years of our lives were taken away because of how many flags made it to the ground. And we were not even the only game to have trouble with the refs . The damn cover photo for this article features a penalty by the way. It was all just so unreal to watch, even the penalties that actually were really penalties. Good on Coen for being diplomatic after the game because he could have exploded. At least the Jags won. Imagine if we lost AND had 13 penalties. Liam Coen didn’t want to get fined commenting about penalties in the first half 🤣 “I’m not going to say anything to get fined. That was just mental. I’ve just never seen something quite that much in the first half of a football game.” #Jaguars #DUUUVAL pic.twitter.com/MgJVds9JyW — Action Sports Jax (@ActionSportsJax) October 4, 2026 The Rest Of The AFC South There is no reason to really pile on the rest of the AFC South after four weeks but I’m going to anyway. Houston is winless, losing three games at home already. Thankfully for them, they have to…

title: 3 reasons why the Jaguars beat the Bengals
summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars are starting to make a habit of this. A week after dismantling the defending AFC champion New England Patriots 35-6, Jacksonville walked into Paycor Stadium and left with another victory over an AFC contender, beating the Cincinnati Bengals 22-17 to move to 3-1 on the season. It was not particularly pretty. Trevor […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OHIO - OCTOBER 04: Chris Rodriguez Jr. #24 of the Jacksonville Jaguars runs into the end zone against the Cincinnati Bengals during the fourth quarter of the game at Paycor Stadium on October 04, 2026 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Jacksonville Jaguars are starting to make a habit of this. A week after dismantling the defending AFC champion New England Patriots 35-6, Jacksonville walked into Paycor Stadium and left with another victory over an AFC contender, beating the Cincinnati Bengals 22-17 to move to 3-1 on the season. It was not particularly pretty. Trevor Lawrence threw for 227 yards and a touchdown, the Jaguars managed only 111 rushing yards, and they committed an extraordinary 13 penalties for 125 yards. Joe Burrow threw for 428 yards, nearly twice Lawrence’s total, and yet Jacksonville controlled enough of the game to win it. The Jaguars are finding different ways to win, and Sunday’s victory offered another three reasons to believe this team could be considerably more dangerous than many expected when the season began. Here are three reasons why the Jags added another W to the win column in Week 4: Jacksonville brought the kind of physicality that borders on chaos Ja'Marr Chase had his facemask pulled and then took a big hit right after. Chase is being evaluated for a concussion and is questionable to return. (🎥: CBS) pic.twitter.com/ddAgYK0fqt — Football Forever (@fballforeverhq) October 4, 2026 There is playing physically, and then there is whatever the Jaguars were doing in Cincinnati. Jacksonville entered the game having been penalized only 15 times through its first three games. It then committed 10 penalties for 100 yards before halftime alone, eventually finishing with 13 penalties for 125 yards. Two of Bhayshul Tuten’s touchdown runs were wiped out by penalties, while a roughing-the-passer penalty on Arik Armstead erased what would have been an interception by Travis Hunter. It was hardly disciplined football. It was, however, extremely physical football. Armstead’s hit on Joe Burrow in the first quarter was penalized for helmet-to-helmet contact, while Jarrian Jones was flagged for grabbing Ja’Marr Chase’s facemask on a four-yard reception early in the second quarter. Chase went down awkwardly, was subsequently hit by Ventrell Miller and was ruled out with a concussion. He finished with three catches for 26 yards. There is an important distinction here. The Jaguars should not be celebrated for injuring an opponent, and some of their aggression flirted with crossing the line. The point is that Jacksonville made the Bengals uncomfortable from the opening whistle. This was not a defense sitting back and hoping Burrow would make a mistake. It was a defense attacking, tackling and challenging Cincinnati’s offense on virtually every possession. Hunter was involved in the action throughout, finishing with four tackles and a pass defended, while Jourdan Lewis supplied the first of Jacksonville’s two interceptions. The Jaguars entered the game already tied for third in the NFL in takeaways and left Cincinnati with eight through four games. Perhaps the most impressive part was that Jacksonville managed to absorb its own mistakes. Giving away 100 yards in penalties before halftime should normally be catastrophic. Instead, the Jaguars went into the locker room 13-3 ahead. Cincinnati had opportunities, but Jacksonville repeatedly disrupted drives, forced negative plays and made the Bengals work for everything. That physical edge eventually produced the decisive moments. Foye Oluokun intercepted Burrow early in the fourth quarter with Cincinnati threatening, preserving a 16-10 lead, and the Jaguars’ defense then held the Bengals to a fourth-down stop on the final meaningful possession of the game. This is not a defense that is simply accumulating numbers against bad teams. It has allowed three or fewer points in the first half of all four games this season, a start matched by only the 2019 Patriots over the past several years. Jacksonville has also intercepted a pass in nine consecutive games, the longest streak in franchise history. The Jaguars may need to clean up the penalties. But there is something valuable in having a defense that plays with this kind of edge. Trevor Lawrence doesn’t have a favorite target – and that’s the point With today's 23-yard reception, @BrentonStrange has nine receptions of 20-plus yards in his last 11 games. That is tied for the second most in the NFL in that span (since Week 12 of 2025) among tight ends. pic.twitter.com/tjNBliDEpI — JaguarsPR (@JaguarsPR) October 4, 2026 There was a moment during Sunday’s game that summed up Jacksonville’s offense rather neatly. Parker Washington, who entered the afternoon as the Jaguars’ leading receiver, finished the game with just one catch. That would have been a major problem for plenty of NFL offenses. It wasn’t for Jacksonville. Instead, Brenton Strange became a major part of the passing attack, Jakobi Meyers produced important plays, Josh Cameron supplied a 29-yard reception and Brian Thomas Jr. caught the touchdown that gave Jacksonville its halftime lead. Seven different Jaguars caught passes during the game, with Lawrence completing 18 of 23 attempts for 227 yards and a touchdown without throwing an interception. This distribution is not an accident. Through the first three games, Washington had established himself as Lawrence’s most productive receiver with 15 catches for 221 yards and two touchdowns. Meyers had 10 catches for 132 yards and two scores, while Strange and Thomas Jr. had seven receptions apiece. Bhayshul Tuten, Josh Cameron, Ameer Abdullah, LeQuint Allen Jr., Nate Boerkircher, Travis Hunter and Quintin Morris had also already recorded receptions. And then Washington effectively disappeared from the box score in Cincinnati. But whether that was down to the Bengals gameplanning for the receiver, or just an off-day for Parker, Jacksonville simply moved on. That is what makes the construction of Liam Coen’s offense so interesting. There is no obvious volume receiver that a defense can remove and expect the entire passing game to collapse. The Jaguars can attack underneath with their tight ends, get Meyers involved on intermediate routes, take shots to Thomas Jr., use Washington from the slot and involve their backs in the passing game. Strange, in particular, is becoming an increasingly important piece. His 23-yard reception on third-and-18 was one of the early highlights of the game, and the tight end finished as one of Lawrence’s most productive targets. The result is an offense that does not necessarily need a 10-catch performance from its biggest name every Sunday. That matters over a 17-game season. Defensive coordinators can spend an entire week trying to remove Washington or Thomas Jr. from the game, only for Meyers, Strange or one of the backs to exploit the space that creates elsewhere. It also takes some of the pressure off Lawrence. He doesn’t need to force the ball to his best receiver simply because that player is his best receiver. He can take what the defense gives him, and the Jaguars have enough variety around him to make that approach work. That is exactly what happened in Cincinnati. Expect a similar story when the Jags head to London to face the Eagles and Texans the next two weeks. Maybe the Jaguars are the best team in the AFC? With the @Jaguars win against the Bengals, Trevor Lawrence has now won against every AFC team. @Jaguars | #DUUUVAL pic.twitter.com/RD1k82kYGT — NFL+ (@NFLPlus) October 4, 2026 It sounds ridiculous. And it’s not necessarily a reason they won. But it might also be time to at least ask the question – are the Jaguars just REALLY good? Jacksonville is 3-1 after beating the Browns, losing narrowly to Denver, destroying New England and now beating Cincinnati on the road. The Jaguars have won their last two games by a combined 57-23 and have now beaten two teams…

title: Jaguars Grind Out Cincy Win and Keep Rolling
summary: It wasn’t pretty. It wasn’t perfect. And for much of the Jacksonville fanbase, it may have been downright frustrating to watch. But Jacksonville Jaguars fans and players are walking into Victory Monday at 3-1 and atop the AFC South, following a road victory over the Cincinnati Bengals. Here’s everything you need to know from Jacksonville’s […]
full_text: Jacksonville Jaguars cornerback Jourdan Lewis (2) intercepts a pass in the second quarter of the NFL Week 4 game between the Cincinnati Bengals and the Jacksonville Jaguars at Paycor Stadium in Cincinnati on Sunday, Oct. 4, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co It wasn’t pretty. It wasn’t perfect. And for much of the Jacksonville fanbase, it may have been downright frustrating to watch. But Jacksonville Jaguars fans and players are walking into Victory Monday at 3-1 and atop the AFC South, following a road victory over the Cincinnati Bengals. Here’s everything you need to know from Jacksonville’s Week 4 22-17 road victory over the Cincinnati Bengals. Favorite Highlight: Whether it counted or not, Duval remembers that Travis Hunter picked off Joe Burrow in this one. It didn’t count but my god Travis Hunter sent Tee Higgins to the shadow realm pic.twitter.com/4vMXrQdCp1 — SleeperNFL (@SleeperNFL) October 4, 2026 Bhayshul Tuten’s second quarter 44-yard touchdown looked to be a thing of beauty, however, one of many first half penalties negated this one also. Of course it just has to be a flag. pic.twitter.com/tXsWpSOeyr — Nash Henry (@NashJagsNats22) October 4, 2026 In Case You Missed It The early quarter of the game was easily dictated by penalties, with both offenses struggling to land in the end zone over the first 28 minutes of the day. Jacksonville was called for 100 yards of first-half penalties on ten flags, negating two touchdowns and a Travis Hunter interception. With under two minutes remaining in the half, the game’s first turnover, a Jourdan Lewis interception, kicked off the scoring. Lewis’s interception of Joe Burrow, assisted by a Josh Hines-Allen quarterback hit and a Dennis Gardeck tipped pass, set Jacksonville up inside the Bengals’ red zone. Lawrence connected with Brian Thomas Jr. just four plays later for the game’s first touchdown. A wide open Brian Thomas Jr. makes it a two-score game! JAXvsCIN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/uXT47Yp4vh — NFL (@NFL) October 4, 2026 Halftime Stats: Halftime Score: 13-3 Jacksonville Third Down Defense: 1/5 Jacksonville, 2/5 Cincinnati Defensive Sacks: 1 to 1 Turnovers forced: 1 to 0 Jacksonville Rushing yards: 52 to 16 Jacksonville Passing yards: 129 to 130 Cincinnati Redzone: 0/1 Jacksonville, 1/2 Cincinnati Penalties: 10 for 100 yards for Jacksonville, 6 for 49 yards for Cincinnati Points off turnovers: 7-0 Jacksonville QB Trevor Lawrence ended the half with 9/12 for 136 yards (11.3 avg) with a touchdown and no turnovers (139.6 passer rating). RB Bhayshul Tuten had 9 carries for 39 yards (4.3 YPC) and tight end Brenton Strange led the team in receiving with 49 yards on three catches (16.3 YPR). Following the half, the Cincinnati offense awoke, immediately putting together a 12-play, 67-yard, 6:16 touchdown drive with 30 yards on the drive from Bengals’ receiver Tee Higgins. The drive cut Jacksonville’s halftime lead to three. After Jacksonville added a field goal, Joe Burrow looked to be leading the Bengals down the field for a go-ahead fourth-quarter touchdown when his second mistake of the day occurred. Linebacker Foye Oluokun stepped in front of Burrow’s first down, red zone attempt for Jacksonville’s second interception of the day. Foye's interception via eagle eye view. Hes been able to step into the middle of the field after Armstead puts the pressure on Burrow. pic.twitter.com/3lsWRBQJfF — Fitz (@LaurieFitzptrck) October 4, 2026 Following back-to-back fourth-quarter punts, Chris Rodriguez made it a two-score game with a 25-yard fourth-quarter scamper. Chris Rodriguez makes it a two-score game with a 25-yard TD! title: Andy Reid says special teams was Chiefs’ best phase in win over Raiders
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs needed a full-game effort to outlast the Las Vegas Raiders in the Week 4 bout that finished 30-27. The offense came alive in the fourth quarter with 20 points while the defense made enough stops to hold the Raiders down. However, head coach Andy Reid called the third phase of the […]
full_text: (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs needed a full-game effort to outlast the Las Vegas Raiders in the Week 4 bout that finished 30-27. The offense came alive in the fourth quarter with 20 points while the defense made enough stops to hold the Raiders down. However, head coach Andy Reid called the third phase of the game “the best” in his opening statement after the game. At the podium, Reid detailed the impact of special teams coordinator Dave Toub’s unit. “I think special teams was the best part of the three phases today,” Reid said. “(Punter) [Matt] Araiza with the fake punt did a nice job there. We didn’t capitalize on it offensively, but what a job he did there, and then the punt down there at the end, I thought, was nice.“ Araiza was locked in from the jump, which included the fake, where he sprinted to the right with the ball and took a big hit after moving the chains. After that, he punted five times; the Raiders produced only four yards off those kicks, which averaged nearly 47 yards. Rookies finishing off a masterpiece by Araiza 💣 pic.twitter.com/2uHPFiaDH4 — Arrowhead Pride (@ArrowheadPride) October 4, 2026 The last of his five punts seemingly iced the game, pinning the Raiders’ offense at their own one-yard line with only 1:16 of game time and no timeouts to move down the field for a game-tying field goal. Rookie running back Emmett Johnson made an athletic play to toss the ball back to rookie safety Xavier Nwankpa in order to finish off the on-target punt by Araiza. Reid noted Johnson’s “great instincts” and pointed out that he is still learning and growing as a special-teams player, benefiting from Toub’s and assistant special teams coach Porter Ellett’s direction. “Emmett is doing running back, and he’s working the special teams, which he hasn’t done a lot of in his career,” Reid said. “But Dave has been teaching him and pushing him along there; he and Porter.” It wasn’t just punt coverage; the team also made plays on kickoffs. Reid pointed out the forced fumble by second-year linebacker Jeffrey Bassa in the fourth quarter as a pivotal play. Veteran linebacker Jack Cochrane secured the turnover. “The play of the game was Bassa punching the kickoff out,” Reid noted. “Then Cochrane getting it back there. What a great job he did on that with the forced fumble, and like I said, probably the biggest play of the game.” In a road divisional matchup, the little things matter in a game of inches. Kansas City’s young special teams unit has plenty to clean up with penalties, but the third phase of the game made a difference in the close win on Sunday.

title: Who gets your game ball from the Chiefs’ win over the Raiders?
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs are 4-0 after a 30-27 win over the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 4! Wide receiver Tyquan Thornton currently leads the poll for his heroic effort on Sunday, totaling 111 yards on five catches with two red-zone touchdowns. He gained 42 yards on a second-quarter play that set up a field […]
full_text: (Photo by Steve Marcus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs are 4-0 after a 30-27 win over the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 4! Wide receiver Tyquan Thornton currently leads the poll for his heroic effort on Sunday, totaling 111 yards on five catches with two red-zone touchdowns. He gained 42 yards on a second-quarter play that set up a field goal before halftime, then caught and ran for 55 yards on a third-down play in the fourth quarter that ended with a very unfortunate injury. However, defensive end George Karlaftis was a menace for the Raiders’ offensive line. He finished with five total tackles — including a tackle for loss — a pass defended and six quarterback hits! He accounted for more than half of the team’s hits on Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins. Running back Kenneth Walker’s 76-yard run was just one of his difference-making plays in Las Vegas. He finished with 177 rushing yards over 22 attempts and scored two touchdowns. The team’s commitment to the run game allowed Walker to break loose and virtually put the game away in the fourth quarter. Rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane finished as the team’s leading tackler (10) while also breaking up a pass and making one tackle behind the line of scrimmage. Here are the top comments from the post-game poll: NCRaiderHater I know you can’t give Delane the nod here, but it turns out this young man is really, really good at football. Sticky in coverage and great at the run D as well. I have a feeling he’s going to be viewed as one of the best corners in football very soon. Steve Soper Bassa. I feel like he made the play of the game that won it for KC. afflatusmisery Even if he hadn’t gotten hurt, Thornton was making clutch play after clutch play. I would say he had a slight edge over K9, but the injury while making a game changing play seals it for me imo. RunningFree Hard to hand it to anyone but the guy who had a career day before disaster struck. 138 of Mahomes 225 total passing yards were the 3 long completions to Thornton and Worthy. With some time to sleep on it, who gets your game ball from Week 4?

title: Chiefs Week 4 snap count analysis: Chamarri Conner returns as starter
summary: Welcome to Arrowhead Pride’s weekly snap-count analysis! Let’s take a closer look at the Kansas City Chiefs’ playing time in the 30-27 win over the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 4. The starting lineups are courtesy of NFL Game Stats and Information, and the snap-count data comes from Pro Football Focus’ premium stats. Starters (offensive): LT Kahlil […]
full_text: (Photo by Candice Ward/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to Arrowhead Pride’s weekly snap-count analysis! Let’s take a closer look at the Kansas City Chiefs ’ playing time in the 30-27 win over the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 4. The starting lineups are courtesy of NFL Game Stats and Information, and the snap-count data comes from Pro Football Focus’ premium stats. Starters (offensive): LT Kahlil Benson, LG Mike Caliendo, C Creed Humphrey, RG Trey Smith, RT Jaylon Moore, QB Patrick Mahomes, WR Tyquan Thornton, WR Rashee Rice, WR Xavier Worthy, RB Kenneth Walker and TE Travis Kelce Starters (defensive): DE George Karlaftis, DT Chris Jones, DT Khyiris Tonga, DE Felix Anudike-Uzomah, LB Nick Bolton, LB Drue Tranquill, LB Jack Cochrane, CB Mansoor Delane, CB L’Jarius Sneed, S Alohi Gilman and S Chamarri Conner Did not play: LG Kingsley Suamataia, QB Justin Fields Inactive: TE Jared Wiley, QB Garrett Nussmeier (Emergency third QB), DB Jadon Canady, DE Jack Pyburn, OT Diego Pounds, LT Josh Simmons (Back) The big takeaway: Jalen Royals, not Cyrus Allen, steps up With the injuries of two starting receivers, second-year wide receiver Jalen Royals stepped up and played the second-most snaps of his career (38), only behind the season finale last season in Las Vegas (43). Royals didn’t record a catch over two targets (and 22 pass plays), but he was the next man up over rookie wideout Cyrus Allen, who only played five snaps. Allen saw one target, but it came on a drawn-out play that felt closer to a desperation heave from quarterback Patrick Mahomes than an in-rhythm play. Without Rashee Rice, Royals’ ability to gain yards after catch with physical running will continue to be utilized, but it will be worth monitoring how Royals and Allen’s role change with the absence of Tyquan Thornton now factored in. The Offensive takeaway: Emmett Johnson is the pass-down back Rookie running back Emmett Johnson played the second-most snaps (17) of his career and the most pass-play snaps (12) of the season. Johnson did not receive a handoff over his time on the field, but did catch a screen pass that gained 10 yards at one point. In the shadows of lead back Ken Walker’s 177 yards on the ground, Johnson is settling more into a pass-down role and is hogging the playing time from second-year back Brashard Smith, who only played two snaps on offense in Las Vegas. Smith has only played six snaps on offense this season. The Defensive takeaway: Chamarri Conner returns as primary starter In his season debut, safety Chamarri Conner played 75% of the team’s defensive snaps and played the same amount of snaps as starting slot defender L’Jarius Sneed (63). He was one of the two starting safeties, along with Alohi Gilman, taking over the role of third-year safety Jaden Hicks, who only played 29 snaps in Week 4. However, Hicks (13) nearly played the same amount of run-defense snaps as Conner (18), which shows that the Chiefs’ defense still values Hicks’ skills in certain situations. In previous seasons, Conner has been an every-down starter. Safety Christian Roland-Wallace (29 snaps) also saw a good amount of playing time, speaking to the team’s reliance on Dime personnel (six defensive backs in formation) against the Raiders. Before Week 4, Roland-Wallace’s season-high snap-count total was 12. Offensive Snaps Defensive Snaps Special teams snaps

full_text: (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs emerged from the Week 4 battle with the Las Vegas Raiders undefeated, with a bye week ahead. It’s well-timed, considering the short-term injury to wide receiver Rashee Rice (hamstring) and the long-term injury of wide receiver Tyquan Thornton (ankle). The Chiefs will have to adjust the game plan around these two injuries by the next time they hit the field against the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 6. However, one former Chiefs receiver is available to sign as a free agent, and the possibility feels more likely by the day. Chiefs Kingdom, bring the noise to the SB Nation app! Download the SB Nation app on your mobile device! For Apple devices, click here . For Android devices, click here . The latest Kansas City Chiefs news Chiefs interested in adding wide receiver Tyreek Hill to roster: Sources | The Athletic In the wake of those injuries, the Chiefs have already reached out to Hill’s agent, Drew Rosenhaus, to express their interest. They’d have to be satisfied with the receiver’s recovery, but there would likely be no other obstacles on the organization’s end. His tenure in Kansas City ended on reasonably good terms, and people inside the organization believe he would fit in well with the current team. After Thornton’s injury, Hill posted “hm” on his X account. Following the victory over the Raiders, several prominent Chiefs players said they’d be in favor of Hill’s return. Five things that stood out about the Chiefs’ win vs. the Raiders in Las Vegas | The Kansas City Star The special teams had special moments. The best defensive moment of the game actually came on a special-teams tackle. Jeffrey Bassa punched the ball out from Darake Young on a kickoff immediately after the Chiefs took the lead in the fourth quarter. The Chiefs scored one play later for a two-score lead. Matt Araiza, the punter, finished as the Chiefs’ second-leading rusher. How? He kept a punt and ran for 12 yards after the Raiders inexplicably dropped four players deep into the secondary to block. NFL Week 4: Big takeaways, questions and fantasy spin from Sunday’s games | ESPN This stat might seem unbelievable, but it’s true: The Chiefs haven’t sacked a quarterback in the past three weeks. This is a troubling trend since the Chiefs invested in improving their pass rush in the offseason, including selecting defensive tackle Peter Woods and defensive end R Mason Thomas in the first two rounds of April’s draft. — Nate Taylor The terrifying, unbeaten Chiefs would like you to know your predictions were wrong | The Guardian As for the 4-0 Chiefs, they are officially back to the top of the NFL after a disastrous 6-11 2025 season. Everybody who picked other teams to make the Super Bowl (and that includes just about everybody) may want to check those opinions at the door. Mahomes isn’t the force who blew away opponents at his peak, but he has been careful with the ball this season. He only has two interceptions to go alongside his seven touchdown passes, and is still unflappable on third downs. 10 Instant Observations From the Chiefs’ Thrilling Rivalry Win Over Raiders | Sports Illustrated 9. Opening-Drive Streak Comes to an End The Chiefs had scored on each of their first three opening drives this season (two touchdowns, one field goal). However, the offense began the day with a turnover on downs after Khyiris Tonga and Kenneth Walker III were stuffed up the middle on consecutive plays. It only took Vegas four plays on its opening possession to get onto the board and kick off the scoring. Surely, this is a trend that Eric Bieniemy will want to erase moving forward. Around the NFL NFL looking into official apparently cursing at Cardinals’ McBride | ESPN “This kind of behavior from an official towards a player is unacceptable,” Tretter wrote. “Players are consistently held accountable when the roles are reversed. We expect the NFL to hold officials to the same standard.” The NFL Referees Association did not immediately respond to a message seeking comment. The interaction took place with just under five minutes left after officials did not call a pass interference or illegal contact penalty on New York’s Dru Phillips, who made contact with McBride before the ball arrived from Jacoby Brissett on a third-and-2 play. Jim Harbaugh backs Mike McDaniel after Chargers fall to 0-4: ‘His job is not in jeopardy’ | NFL.com Justin Herbert threw two more interceptions and was sacked four times on Sunday. His six INTs and 12 sacks through four weeks are both tied for second most in the NFL. Herbert is the first Chargers quarterback with at least six interceptions and 10 sacks through the team’s first four games of a season since Ryan Leaf in 2000. His six INTs are the most through four games in his career, and his 12 sacks are tied for the most. Herbert continues to look uncomfortable in the offense, and his interceptions right to two different linebackers underscore that he’s not seeing or feeling things well in McDaniel’s offense. title: 8 Winners and 4 Losers from the Chiefs’ win over the Raiders
summary: Raiders week started off weird. Then it was weird in the middle. So, of course, the ending was weird. This game had everything— game-changing penalties, turnovers, a fake punt, and a controversial play at the end. The personnel decisions and short-yardage play calls were mind-boggling, and momentum shifted rapidly in Las Vegas. The unexpected should […]
full_text: (Photo by Steve Marcus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Raiders week started off weird. Then it was weird in the middle. So, of course, the ending was weird. This game had everything— game-changing penalties, turnovers, a fake punt, and a controversial play at the end. The personnel decisions and short-yardage play calls were mind-boggling, and momentum shifted rapidly in Las Vegas. The unexpected should be expected in these division rivalry games. Scores are always close, and the results can be contradictory. Here are some Kansas City Chiefs who stood out in a back-and-forth, too-close-for-comfort win over the Las Vegas Raiders : Winners Defensive end George Karlaftis: The Chiefs didn’t officially log a single quarterback sack on Sunday — but that doesn’t mean they weren’t getting after Kirk Cousins. Karlaftis played like a man possessed in the second half, finishing with 6 QB hits, a batted pass, and a huge tackle for loss. He also had a sack just before the two-minute warning, but a L’Jarius Sneed holding penalty wiped it out. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes: Mahomes took a beating all afternoon (two sacks and eight hits), but kept firing. He completed a nice deep ball to wide receiver Xavier Worthy, setting up an easy TD to Thornton. He also extended a drive with a run through a linebacker on the sideline. Mahomes is thriving in this newly-balanced offense. Wide receiver Tyquan Thornton: The heartbreaking ending doesn’t take away from what Tyquan Thornton accomplished this week. After the injury to Rashee Rice, Thornton had a career game—five catches for 111 yards and two touchdowns—all in big situations. I’m not sure the Chiefs would have stayed undefeated without Thornton. Cornerback Mansoor Delane: The kid is going to be a star. Delane remains tough in coverage, and even tougher as a tackler. He blew up a screen, then blanketed tight end Brock Bowers on consecutive plays in the first half. Mansoor finished with ten total tackles and is quickly earning respect across the league. Punter Matt Araiza: It’s not often a punter makes this list. But Matt Araiza was a serious factor in Las Vegas on Sunday. He converted a first down on a fake punt, and pinned the Raiders inside the 20 on all five of his kicks. “Punt God” is leading the NFL in gross and net yardage and would lead the NFL in yards per rush (12) if he had more opportunities. Defensive end Felix Anudike-Uzomah: Sure, Felix had a roughing-the-passer call that helped extend the Raiders’ fourth-quarter touchdown drive. But he also had several big pressures and hits, including a tackle for loss. FAU is developing into a solid rotational defensive end. Running back Kenneth Walker III: The best free agent acquisition in the NFL has been a complete and total game changer for this offense. Yes, he was stopped on a few ill-fated short-yardage runs — but he also broke free for the league’s longest run so far this season (76 yards). When it was time to put the game away, K9 helped close things out with two touchdowns in 20 seconds. Linebacker Drue Tranquill: It’s been a weakness for the Chiefs, but Tranquill really showed up against the Raiders. He was a force against the run (2 TFLs) and the pass (a PBU and a QB hit). Losers Linebacker Nick Bolton: The Raiders’ first scoring drive featured two pass plays where No. 32 was lost in space, including a TD on blown coverage. Yes, Bolton made plays in the run game as always, but teams seem to target these linebackers when they try to cover tight ends. The Raiders had tremendous success (16 catches for 200 yards and 2 touchdowns) with three of theirs (Bowers, Mayer, and Thomas). That wasn’t all on Bolton (we could give a dishonorable mention to Jack Cochrane, Jaden Hicks, Chamarri Conner, and Alohi Gilman, amongst others) Cornerback Nohl Williams: Growing pains are expected for a second-year cornerback, even one who has played as well as Nohl. On Sunday afternoon, his costly penalties helped put two FGs on the board for the Raiders. It’s likely just a bump in the road— given what we’ve seen from Williams, he’ll be someone the team is counting on all season. Offensive linemen Jaylon Moore and Mike Caliendo: In the strangest decision of the day, Andy Reid benched a steady (and improving) piece of the protection in front of Patrick Mahomes. Without their starting left guard, the staff leaned on Caliendo— and the results weren’t great. Moore didn’t fare much better on the right side—our hope is that the team can reshuffle the deck during their bye week. Note: Applying the label “losers” is not meant as a judgment on the talent or character of any of these individuals. It’s simply a way to grade their performance in a single game. No disrespect should be inferred.
author: Matt Stagner

title: Patrick Mahomes: Tyquan Thornton ‘One of the best teammates I’ve had’
summary: Although the Kansas City Chiefs remain undefeated at 4-0 after Sunday’s 30-27 victory over the Las Vegas Raiders, the win proved costly. The team entered the season with lingering questions at the wide receiver position, only to see two wideouts leave the game with injuries. On the team’s second possession, Rashee Rice hurt his hamstring […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - OCTOBER 04: Tyquan Thornton #2 of the Kansas City Chiefs is tackled by Treydan Stukes #31 of the Las Vegas Raiders during the fourth quarter at Allegiant Stadium on October 04, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Chris Unger/Getty Images) | Getty Images Although the Kansas City Chiefs remain undefeated at 4-0 after Sunday’s 30-27 victory over the Las Vegas Raiders , the win proved costly. The team entered the season with lingering questions at the wide receiver position, only to see two wideouts leave the game with injuries. On the team’s second possession, Rashee Rice hurt his hamstring on a seven-yard catch (that was ultimately nullified by penalty). Ultimately, the team described his return as doubtful . Head coach Andy Reid had no word on the severity after the game, but appreciated the rest of the room stepping up in Rice’s absence. “Rashee Rice tweaked his hamstring there,” said Reid. “I will tell you that the rest of the guys picked up the pace on things and did a nice at the receiver position, which I appreciate. The next man up jumped in, and they kept rolling.“ One of those players who stepped up was veteran Tyquan Thornton, who hauled in five catches for 111 and two touchdowns. Sadly, the best game of Thornton’s five-year career came to an end in the fourth quarter when he suffered a gruesome ankle injury while making a 55-yard catch. Reid showed no optimism on Thornton’s prognosis, although he does expect the speedster to be able to travel back to Kansas City with the team. “With Tyquan Thornton’s ankle, that doesn’t look good,” the coach acknowledged. “He’s going to fly back with us, and we’ll get further evaluation later.” #Chiefs WR Tyquan Thornton suffered a dislocated ankle that was put back into place by doctors earlier today. He did make the plane with the team. Thornton will have a full evaluation in the morning, along with a second opinion. Out indefinitely, but in good spirits. pic.twitter.com/DBvRHI3jeJ — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) October 5, 2026 Later in the evening, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported that Thornton suffered a dislocated ankle that “was put back into place by doctors.” In postgame comments, it was clear what Thornton means to his teammates and the emotions involved in seeing him suffer a major injury. “That’s a rough one,” Reid added, “especially a guy like Tyquan [who is] a great father, a great husband and all that. Just his attitude. His attitude is unbelievable. He’s great for the team and kind of a leader for that group. For that to happen, especially with the year’s he’s having — he’s had a phenomenal year to this point — and on a great play on top of that, it’s a tough one to see for all the guys.” A personal foul moved the Chiefs to the Las Vegas two-yard line on Thornton’s catch. One play after seeing his teammate carted off of the Allegiant Stadium field, Kenneth Walker punched in a key touchdown. Walker was not about to let Thornton’s incredible catch be for naught. “You never want to see that,” Walker said after the game. “It could happen to anyone. It’s kind of motivating. You have to play for your brother that much harder.” No one on the Chiefs knows more about how quickly an injury can happen than quarterback Patrick Mahomes, who suffered torn knee ligaments in December that ended his 2025 campaign early. “It’s tough,” Mahomes said in his postgame remarks. “Those guys, they put in so much work. I was in that spot last year. Everybody puts in so much work to be out there and to play the game they love. One play can change your season. For him, he’s put in all the time and all the work and had a tough play there. You hope for the best, but at the same time, you want to show him support. I know how it is when you’re in that position. It’s like the world’s closing in on you, and you want to make sure you have the support from your teammates there.” Mahomes also knows the importance of Thornton knowing his has the support of his teammates. “He’s one of the best teammates I’ve ever had,” the face of the league declared. “He truly is. He has a smile on his face every time that he’s in the building. So, we’re in his corner, and he knows that he has us behind him.”
author: Jared Sapp

title: Andy Reid on Chiefs’ offensive line change: ‘That’s between Kingsley and I’
summary: At the beginning of the Kansas City Chiefs’ 30-27 victory over the Las Vegas Raiders, a significant change in the starting lineup stood out: left guard Mike Caliendo was between center Creed Humphrey and left tackle Kahlil Benson, not Kingsley Suamataia. Suamataia, the 23-year-old starter who has manned left guard since the start of the […]
full_text: (Photo by Chris Unger/Getty Images) | Getty Images At the beginning of the Kansas City Chiefs ’ 30-27 victory over the Las Vegas Raiders , a significant change in the starting lineup stood out: left guard Mike Caliendo was between center Creed Humphrey and left tackle Kahlil Benson, not Kingsley Suamataia. Suamataia, the 23-year-old starter who has manned left guard since the start of the 2025 season, remained on the sideline for the entire contest. In the first half, the Chiefs told local media that the action was “a coaching decision.” After the game, head coach Andy Reid used part of his opening statement at the podium to make it clear that we won’t know much more about the change in the starting lineup. “Before you guys ask, that’s between Kingsley and I,” Reid said. “But we’ll figure it out and down the road, we’ll be better as a team for it and Kingsley will be better for it.” Sam McDowell of The Kansas City Star followed up with Reid, who responded snippily when asked about the major shakeup. “I might have stuttered when I said that,” Reid said before reiterating that the situation is between Suamataia and him. McDowell asked for clarification on whether the action was for disciplinary or performance reasons. ESPN’s Nate Taylor asked quarterback Patrick Mahomes about the sudden absence of one of the team’s young, ascending starters during Mahomes’ time at the podium. “Kingsley knows how important he is to the team,” Mahomes said. “We’ll get Kingsley back in the fold here soon.” Mahomes was sacked twice, and the Raiders registered eight quarterback hits against a line that was technically down two starters, considering left tackle Josh Simmons (Back) has missed the entire year so far. Early in the game, the run game couldn’t break through because of penetration from the left side. With a bye week ahead, the team may not have any more information about why Suamataia was out of the lineup in Las Vegas.
author: Ron Kopp Jr.

title: 5 things we learned from the Chiefs’ Week 4 victory over the Raiders
summary: In what was arguably the biggest game of the Kansas City Chiefs‘ early season, Kansas City struggled to keep quarterback Patrick Mahomes upright in what turned out to be a hotly contested game. It was by no means the Chiefs’ crispest game, and they left plays on the field they wish they could have back […]
full_text: (Photo by Chris Unger/Getty Images) | Getty Images In what was arguably the biggest game of the Kansas City Chiefs ‘ early season, Kansas City struggled to keep quarterback Patrick Mahomes upright in what turned out to be a hotly contested game. It was by no means the Chiefs’ crispest game, and they left plays on the field they wish they could have back in all three phases. But in the end, the Chiefs’ determination carried them on the road and helped them scrape together enough wins to open the season 4-0, beat the Las Vegas Raiders 30-27 , and take sole first place in the AFC West. 1. There is more to the pass protection concerns than Kahlil Benson The biggest worry coming into this game was whether the Chiefs’ undrafted rookie free agent left tackle, Kahlil Benson, would be exposed against edge rusher Maxx Crosby and the rest of this Raiders defense. And the answer was “kind of.” I actually thought Benson battled pretty well in this game, but left guard Kingsley Suamataia sat out this contest on what the Chiefs called a coaching decision. And while we don’t know what he did to find himself riding the pine, it had to be something bad for them to roll with Mike Caliendo, who has proven multiple times he’s not good enough to start in the NFL and was a liability this entire game. The Chiefs have said that Mike Caliendo surprise start over Kingsley Suamataia was a "coaching decision." — Nate Taylor (@ByNateTaylor) October 4, 2026 As I said, we don’t know what Suamataia did, but to miss such an important game with your replacement playing so poorly, he must have dang near murdered somebody. 2. Tyquan Thornton was the X-factor for this offense Thornton is never going to be your WR1. He will always be a role player. But Dante Hall was a role player. Jerrick McKinnon was a role player. Sometimes a role player is the difference between winning a hotly contested game against your arch rivals. And losing a game that makes you sick to your stomach because you know you should have won it. But we’re not talking about hypotheticals here, because Thornton was in the midst of playing one of the greatest games of his life when he went down with what looked like a gruesome lower leg injury. It’s not about replacing him. We can’t replace him. BACK FOR SECONDS ✌️ pic.twitter.com/wkulsAd1dE — Kansas City Chiefs (@Chiefs) October 4, 2026 Thornton didn’t just score a touchdown in this game; he had a pair of them, in moments when the Chiefs needed it the most. His most clutch play was the one that got him hurt. Get well soon, Tyquan; Chiefs Kingdom loves you, big guy. 3. It’s time for Dave Toub to go I always try to be hesitant when I call for a coaching change. But Toub has to be beyond the hot seat right now. Special teams didn’t just have a bad game today; they’ve had a bad three years, and things don’t seem to be going in the right direction. Having an illegal formation on the field is unacceptable. So is an illegal fair catch. And worst of all, they can’t cover the kick and keep giving the opposing team an advantageous field position. The lone bright spot on special teams has been Matt Arizia, who is playing like the league’s best punter. But aside from Arizia’s brilliance, the rest of the unit has been horrible. It’s not a skill problem. It’s a focus problem. It’s an execution problem. It’s a coaching problem. 4. Sack Nation should be The Republic of Pressure A lot has been made about the Chiefs’ lack of ability to get sacks. But Chris Jones, George Karlaftis, R Mason Thomas, and even Felix Anudike Uzoimah quietly made Kirk Cousins uncomfortable all day long. And while they didn’t result in sacks, they forced the Vegas quarterback to make multiple back throws in key situations. You can tell they came out in this game with fire, looking to make a point. Chris Jones said this week that he sees the sports media criticism of the Chiefs’ front four. If sports writers criticizing the Chiefs was what it took to get them to start wreaking havoc, then I hope the articles keep flowing in. But for at least one week, it won’t be coming from me. The Chiefs’ pass rush came up big against the Raiders, including hitting Kirk Cousins on Las Vegas’ final offensive play, when George Karlaftis called ballgame. Raiders' last-ditch effort falls short as the @Chiefs intercept Kirk Cousins to clinch it pic.twitter.com/0TvLTR3vsU — NFL on CBS 🏈 (@NFLonCBS) October 4, 2026 5. Kenneth Walker is built different We knew he was a stud. We knew he was built different. But Kenneth Walker III is built different in a room of guys who are built different. It’s not just his vision. It’s not his burst. His strength and his ability to break tackles. It’s not just his agility. It’s not his drive. Or his determination and the fact that he doesn’t go down until you pile on him and force him to the ground. It’s all of it. On every play. Without exception. Trying to tackle Kenneth Walker does NOT look fun pic.twitter.com/FtfvsQo2g1 — NFL on CBS 🏈 (@NFLonCBS) October 4, 2026
author: Rocky Magaña

title: Chiefs’ Tyquan Thornton carted off field, suffers dislocated ankle
summary: In what felt like a do-or-die moment for the Kansas City Chiefs in the fourth quarter of Week 4 against the Las Vegas Raiders, quarterback Patrick Mahomes launched a deep pass to wide receiver Tyquan Thornton, who heroically stretched out for it and kept running down the left sideline. It was his fifth catch of […]
full_text: (Photo by Chris Unger/Getty Images) | Getty Images In what felt like a do-or-die moment for the Kansas City Chiefs in the fourth quarter of Week 4 against the Las Vegas Raiders , quarterback Patrick Mahomes launched a deep pass to wide receiver Tyquan Thornton, who heroically stretched out for it and kept running down the left sideline. It was his fifth catch of the day — two of them touchdowns —and he accumulated 111 yards. As he got up to celebrate, Thornton noticed something wrong with his left lower leg. The highlight play turned into a somber, unfortunate moment for the 26-year-old receiver having a career day. A brief replay is available here . Tyquan Thornton carted off with a serious injury after an incredible performance: – 5 rec, 111 yds, 2 TD – massive 55-yard catch to set up @Chiefs ' go-ahead score pic.twitter.com/4rLtB3gERx — NFL on CBS 🏈 (@NFLonCBS) October 4, 2026 After some time on the field, Thornton was carted off the field following the game-changing 55-yard play. The Chiefs’ offense followed up Thornton’s effort with two touchdowns by running back Kenneth Walker, taking a 30-19 lead. WR Tyquan Thornton is out with an ankle injury. pic.twitter.com/VpmxWqLrKw — Kansas City Chiefs (@Chiefs) October 4, 2026 With less than two minutes to go, the team announced Thornton out with an ankle injury. #Chiefs WR Tyquan Thornton suffered a dislocated ankle that was put back into place by doctors earlier today. He did make the plane with the team. Thornton will have a full evaluation in the morning, along with a second opinion. Out indefinitely, but in good spirits. pic.twitter.com/DBvRHI3jeJ — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) October 5, 2026 A couple of hours after the game’s conclusion, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported that Thornton suffered a dislocated ankle “that was put back into place by doctors” either during or immediately after the game. Head coach Andy Reid confirmed that Thornton made the plan with the team.
author: Ron Kopp Jr.

title: ‘Frustration and competitiveness’ shown on Chiefs’ sideline in Vegas
summary: Just before halftime of the Kansas City Chiefs’ Week 4 contest against the Las Vegas Raiders, the Chiefs drove 70 yards in 10 plays, reaching the 10-yard line before settling for a field goal. That put Kansas City into a 10-10 tie that would be broken by the Raiders shortly after. Las Vegas took a […]
full_text: (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images Just before halftime of the Kansas City Chiefs ’ Week 4 contest against the Las Vegas Raiders , the Chiefs drove 70 yards in 10 plays, reaching the 10-yard line before settling for a field goal. That put Kansas City into a 10-10 tie that would be broken by the Raiders shortly after. Las Vegas took a 13-10 lead into the locker room. Instead of a 14-13 lead at the break, which would have been the score if the Chiefs had converted the red-zone drive, the team was down three and began the second half on defense. Patrick Mahomes having a passionate rant towards Eric Bieniemy. 🎥 @sluggahjells pic.twitter.com/yJPg2xKs9B — The Whole Delivery (@TWDTV1) October 4, 2026 After the field-goal drive, the CBS broadcast showed quarterback Patrick Mahomes and offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy in a lengthy sideline discussion. Mahomes seemed pretty amped up, while Bieniemy seemed to give his perspective and listen to Mahomes’. When the game resumed in the third quarter, sideline reporter Tracy Wolfson shared a note that head coach Andy Reid gave her about the conversation. Reid called it “frustration and competitiveness,” per Wolfson. Reid also added, per Wolfson, that “you have to score when you get down there.” The Chiefs have 10 points through five possessions in Las Vegas as of this writing. Play-by-play announcer Jim Nantz mentioned frustration on Kansas City’s sideline again after a commercial break in the second half.
author: Ron Kopp Jr.

title: Chargers-Seahawks Winners/Losers: A tale of 2 halves for Justin Herbert
summary: The Chargers really had a shot at getting their first win of the season against the reigning Super Bowl champs. They really did. Even after two bad first half interceptions from Justin Herbert, it all came down to one final drive for the Chargers. But alas, it wasn’t meant to be. There was a lot […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - OCTOBER 04: Khalil Mack #52 of the Los Angeles Chargers sacks Sam Darnold #14 of the Seattle Seahawks during the second quarter at Lumen Field on October 04, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Olivia Vanni/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chargers really had a shot at getting their first win of the season against the reigning Super Bowl champs. They really did. Even after two bad first half interceptions from Justin Herbert, it all came down to one final drive for the Chargers. But alas, it wasn’t meant to be. There was a lot of bad during Sunday’s loss. We’ve come to expect that throughout a very frustrating first month of the season. There was also some good that needs to be celebrated, but it’s unfortunate that it wasn’t enough to finally get this team over the hump. Let’s talk about it. Winners QB Justin Herbert (Second Half) It really was a tale of two halves for Herbert. In the first half, he completed less than half his passes and did not break 40 passing yards. In the second half, he topped 150 yards and a touchdown, including a few clutch throws in the fourth quarter to Quentin Johnston and Tre’ Harris. It also wasn’t a surprise that when the offense simplified itself and went into full two-minute mode, Herbert looked much more comfortable running the offense. From a down-to-down basis in the final 15 minutes, it truly looked like the Herbert of old. He looked COMFORTABLE. He looked POISED. If Mike McDaniel and Jim Harbaugh do not make a note of that going forward, then shame on them because it was night and day. EDGE Tuli Tuipulotu On the second play of the entire game, Tuli picked off Sam Darnold to get the ball right back after Herbert’s opening play turnover. Tuli followed the running back to the sideline on a swing route and when Darnold pulled the trigger, the back slipped and was not in a position to contest at the catch point. While Tuli did not record a sack, he helped bottle up the run game and created pressure to keep Darnold jittery in the pocket. His 91.6 overall game grade from PFF was also his highest grade of the young season. EDGE Khalil Mack Mack recorded his third sack of the season and is currently on pace to record his second double-digit sack season since being traded from the Bears during the Brandon Staley era. In a very disapponting season thus far, especially for all the veterans that continue to put their bodies on the line and put off their eventual retirement, Mack has been an all-around difference-maker up front. If the postseason isn’t ever going to bounce his way, then he can at least pad his career stats on the way out the door. Losers QB Justin Herbert (First Half) As mentioned above, Herbert’s first half was a far cry from his second half performance. Herbert began the game with an ugly interception where he targeted tight end Oronde Gadsden over the middle. I gave Herbert the benefit of the doubt initially because it looked like linebacker Drake Thomas was covered in his line of sight by the offensive line before showing up just after Herbert pulled the trigger. However, a Seahakws safety was also right there to undercut the pass if Thomas did not make the play. Either way you looked at that one, it was going to end up being a concerning decision. Then there was the second interception. This one looked even more concerning. After watching the replauy numerous times, there’s not reason Herbert should have thrown the pass. It was on a double slant concept and Herbert was looking to hit Ladd McConkey on the second slant. The thing is, linebacker Ernest Jones dropped back into the window of the slants and even with him sitting squarely in the passing window, Herbert threw it anyway. It could not have been an easier pick for Jones. Herbert now has six interceptions in four games played this season. DT Justin Eboigbe Eboige has been a bright spot on this defense for most of the this young season but his decision to fall on top of Darnold after he slid was nearly more catastrophic than it ended up being. With a few seconds left before the two-minute warning, Darnold was flushed from the pocket and headed towards the sideline. It was third down and the Chargers needed to get a stop to have enough time to put together a final drive to tie the game. Darnold’s slide sealed the Chargers’ chances of getting the ball back to run a two-minute drill. However, Eboigbe didn’t just touch Darnold down, he fell entirely on his head. He was then flagged for unnecessary roughness and gave Seattle a fresh set of down. The Seahawks ultimately did punt back to the Chargers with a little over 90 seconds left in the game so they had a shot nonetheless, but for Eboigbe to be that undisciplined and lack that awareness in the moment was a really bad look.
author: Michael Peterson

title: Chargers Week 4 PFF Grades: Tuli Tuipulotu, Khalil Mack ravaged the Seahawks OL
summary: In a game where the defense still played well despite the 30 points put up by the Seahawks, it was edge rushers Tuli Tuipulotu and Khalil Mack that shined the brightest. Tuli was the team’s highest-graded player with an elite 91.7 game grade, followed by Mack’s 86.1. Offensively — and you’re not going to believe […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - SEPTEMBER 27: Tuli Tuipulotu #45 of the Los Angeles Chargers on the field before a game against the Buffalo Bills at Highmark Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images) | Getty Images In a game where the defense still played well despite the 30 points put up by the Seahawks, it was edge rushers Tuli Tuipulotu and Khalil Mack that shined the brightest. Tuli was the team’s highest-graded player with an elite 91.7 game grade, followed by Mack’s 86.1. Offensively — and you’re not going to believe this — but right guard Cole Strange was that unit’s highest-graded player at 75.5. That’s surprising and also not surprising given that he was one of two healthy starters to begin and end the game. In a very up-and-down game for the Chargers, it’s a positive to see them hang around the reigning Super Bowl champs long enough to actually threaten them with a loss on the very last drive. Is that enough for fans to calm down in any sense of the word? My guess is no. Alright, let’s take a look at this week’s grades. Offense Best RG Cole Strange – 75.5 OT Joe Alt – 74.7 LT Logan Taylor – 74.6 TE Oronde Gadsden – 71.7 RB Omarion Hampton – 65.5 Strange went from being the offense’s worst-graded player to their highest-graded player in the span of a week. His 75.5 was tops among the unit and his run block grade was an elite 90.8. Alt’s 77.3 in run blocking was second best while his pass block grade of 66.3 was fifth best. Taylor’s first 28 snaps of his career ended in him earning a near-elite 86.6 pass block grade. His 66.9 run block grade was good for fourth. Hampton saw a season-low 25 snaps but looked great when he was leaned upon in the second half. The Chargers would be wise to not overthink his fumbles and continue to ride their first-round pick. Omarion Hampton finds the hole for the touchdown! pic.twitter.com/OG7eBXlegu — TSN (@TSN_Sports) October 4, 2026 Worst C Jacob Spomer – 42.2 QB Justin Herbert – 43.8 WR Ladd McConkey – 44.0 TE Hayden Rucci – 50.7 TE Patrick Herbert – 52.0 Spomer’s first 11 career snaps came against the likes of Leonard Williams and Byron Murphy. That’s a real “Welcome to the NFL” moment for the undrafted rookie. He’ll be better for being thrown to the wolves like this and I’m not too worried about how he looked in that small sample size against elite competition. Herbert had two egregious interceptions, both of which were thrown directly into the arms of a linebacker standing in front of his intended receiver. Both were indefensible. I’m not sure what he was looking at nor what McDaniel coaches him to do on those particular plays but it was really, really bad on the live broadcast. McConey dropped his first pass of the season and it happened third down to kill a promising drive. Looks like the bad vibes have now extended to the team’s best wideout. Patrick Herbert, Justin’s brother, recorded a higher grade but still wound up in the bottom five with a terrible 22.0 in pass blocking. Defense Best EDGE Tuli Tuipulotu – 91.7 EDGE Khalil Mack – 86.1 LB Troy Dye – 74.7 S Elijah Molden – 66.0 LB Marlowe Wax – 65.9 Tuli’s grade was pushed into elite territory due to high grades in every area other than pass rush. His interception gave him an elite coverage grade of 93.8 to go with an 82.0 in run defense and a 75.6 in tackling. Mack produced one sack and four pressures while leading the team with four stops. He also posted an 82.0 in run defense and a 69.6 in pass rush (second best on the team). Dye posted a team-high 72.7 pass rush grade that was reinforced with a sack on third down to force a punt by Seattle during their final drive of the game. The huge play gave the Chargers a shot at tying it up in the final 90 seconds. Tuli Tuipulotu chega na luta contra os atuais campeões! 📺: #LACvsSEA – ao vivo no SporTV2 e GE TV pic.twitter.com/tcU4LkibXb — NFL Brasil (@NFLBrasil) October 4, 2026 Worst DT Justin Eboigbe – 37.0 EDGE Bud Dupree – 37.5 S Tony Jefferson – 40.2 DT Teair Tart – 40.5 LB Del’Shawn Phillips – 41.7 Eboigbe’s unnecessary roughness penalty late in the fourth quarter almost erased any chance the Chargers had at a final drive to tie it up. His run defense of 47.0 was fourth worst on the team, as well. Jefferson’s 33.4 coverage grade was tied for worst on the team with Phillips. Phillips’ 28.5 in tackling was fourth worst on the team and his 54.3 run defense grade was middle of the pack. Tart posted a 40.5 in tackling (fifth worst) and a 51.6 in run defense (sixth worst). He had two pressures but a missed tackle.
