title: Los Angeles Chargers news: A positive takeaway from the loss to the Seahawks
summary: The Chargers lost a close one against the Seahawks on Sunday and wouldn’t you know it, but we got a little glimpse of the old Justin Herbert during the second half comeback attempt. Once the Chargers offense was pressed for time and needed multiple scores, the whole system looked to be simplified by Mike McDaniel […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - OCTOBER 04: Justin Herbert #10 of the Los Angeles Chargers reacts after a touchdown against the Seattle Seahawks during the fourth quarter at Lumen Field on October 04, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chargers lost a close one against the Seahawks on Sunday and wouldn’t you know it, but we got a little glimpse of the old Justin Herbert during the second half comeback attempt. Once the Chargers offense was pressed for time and needed multiple scores, the whole system looked to be simplified by Mike McDaniel at the drop of a hat. No more motions. No more unique handoff techniques. It simply became Herbert sitting in the shotgun dissecting the defense while STILL being chased around on every play (some things never change!). The wildest thing was that the offense looked even better once it was just a bunch of backups in the game protecting him. I can’t put my finger on it, but it just felt…normal? And that’s probably a terrible thing but it certainly looked like Herbert was able to find a groove from play to play. After suffering through the better part of the first month of the season while watching this offense, Sunday’s second half really did feel like a return to home. Herbert made hero plays, his receivers were coming through for him (even Quentin Johnston!) and they were able to move the ball consistently down the field. That’s a silver lining if there ever was one. And now for today’s links. title: Broncos vs. Chargers Opening Odds: Bolts underdogs in Week 5

title: Ladd McConkey exits Chargers vs. Seahawks game with foot injury
summary: The Los Angeles Chargers’ season is continuing to evolve into a disaster. In the team’s Week 4 matchup against the Seattle Seahawks, wide receiver Ladd McConkey was questionable all week with a foot injury, but he was active for the contest. Unfortunately for him, after playing the first half against Seattle, McConkey reaggravated his injury […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - SEPTEMBER 27: Ladd McConkey #15 of the Los Angeles Chargers tries to reach for the ball on a pass during the second quarter against the Buffalo Bills at Highmark Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Chargers’ season is continuing to evolve into a disaster. In the team’s Week 4 matchup against the Seattle Seahawks, wide receiver Ladd McConkey was questionable all week with a foot injury, but he was active for the contest. Unfortunately for him, after playing the first half against Seattle, McConkey reaggravated his injury and did not return in the second half. The team ruled him out for the remainder of the game. So far this season, McConkey leads the team with 12 catches for 183 yards and a touchdown, so not having him on the field for the second half is a massive loss. The Chargers are already playing without rookie fourth-round pick Brenen Thompson, who is dealing with a quad injury, so it continues to be a problem of emphasis for the team. With McConkey out, the Chargers will rely on second-year pro Tre Harris to lead the wide receiver room, along with Quentin Johnston and Marquez Valdes-Scantling. Other players like tight end Oronde Gadsden II and running back Keaton Mitchell are also seeing more targets on offense. The Chargers have been trailing by multiple scores for most of the game, so they have a long way to go to catch up against the Seahawks. The hope for the Chargers at this point is to be as healthy as possible going into their Week 5 matchup. Fans can watch the remainder of the Chargers and Seahawks game on CBS, or it can be streamed on Paramount Plus.

title: Chargers-Seahawks Game Recap: Bolts show life, lose to Seattle in penalty-filled contest
summary: As everyone expected, the Chargers scored a season-high in points against the Seahawks’ top-ranked defense. Unfortunately, it still wasn’t more than the Seahawks scored. And hey, the offense legitimately came to life late to make it a ball game. The Seahawks scored on the opening drive to push their lead to 27-6 which was a […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - OCTOBER 04: Kimani Vidal #28 of the Los Angeles Chargers celebrates after scoring a touchdown against the Seattle Seahawks during the third quarter at Lumen Field on October 04, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images As everyone expected, the Chargers scored a season-high in points against the Seahawks’ top-ranked defense. Unfortunately, it still wasn’t more than the Seahawks scored. And hey, the offense legitimately came to life late to make it a ball game. The Seahawks scored on the opening drive to push their lead to 27-6 which was a deficit that may have been insurmountable given what the Chargers offense has looked like all season up to this point. However, it was the Bolts who managed to outscore the Seahawks 17 to 3 the rest of the way, coming up with a real two-minute opportunity to win the game. Unfortunately all of the late-game heroics by Herbert that led to such a crunch-time moment for all for naught. On third-and-one with 1:03 remaining, Herbert dropped back and was stripped by former Chargers pass rusher Uchenna Nwosu. The Seahawks recovered and that was that. No final drive for the Herbert and the offense. Just a lot of momentum snuffed out in an instant. And that sucks, to be quite honest. After a horrid first half where Herbert threw for less than 40 yards, he bounced back in the final two quarters, throwing for 153 and a touchdown to Kimani Vidal. For a moment, he looked like the Herbert we all came into the season knowing well. It also wasn’t a surprise that he looked better the moment McDaniel stopped getting cute with his play calls. No motion. No unique handoff technique. No odd personnel formations. Just Herbert dropping back and letting it rip. Did it really take McDaniel almost four full games to realize that he doesn’t need to reinvent the wheel? And what was the deal with the running back rotation? Third-stringer Kimani Vidal played a season high in snaps while Hampton looked to become an afterthought behind him and Keaton Mitchell, the latter of which received a game-high 10 carries (Hampton got nine for a team-high 45 yards and a touchdown). Mitchell also led the offense with five receptions (tied with Oronde Gadsden) for 24 yards. It sure looked like McDaniel made a concerted effort to force the ball into Mitchell’s hands despite Hampton being much more efficient. It wasn’t until the Chargers’ feverish comeback in the fourth quarter that McDaniel decided to get Hampton more involved. At the end of the day the Bolts did score a new season high in points, and it should be noted just how many injuries they went through to get there. By the end of the game, left tackle Rashawn Slater, right tackle Joe Alt, and left guard Trevor Penning were all sidelined with various injuries. Alt left with a neck injury and was not seen on the sideline during the entire second half. Slater went out late in the fourth and was later seen with a boot on his right foot with crutches. When Hampton dove in from two yards out to make it a 10-point game, he ran behind FOUR rookies and right guard Cole Strange. Following Slater’s injury on the play before, the Chargers front five were (from left to right): Logan Taylor, Jake Slaughter, Jacob Spomer, Strange, and Travis Burke. A sixth-rounder, second-rounder out of position, a UDFA, an underwhelming veteran, and a fourth-round pick. That’s all the Chargers had left for healthy linemen who were dressed in Seattle. That’s a lot of injuries, but something seemed to create a spark inside Herbert and the offense. Maybe they just love playing with the entire deck stacked against them. Maybe they just feed on the immense pressuere. Who knows, but at least the offense has some better film to watch this week. Check out the entire recap of Sunday’s game below. First Quarter The Chargers received the opening kickoff with running back Keaton Mitchell returning it out to the 32-yard line. On the first play of the game, Herbert was picked off by linebacker Drake Thomas who was not fooled by the play action. Oronde Gadsden was the target and it was clear Herbert did not see Thomas drop back underneath the route before throwing. However, on the second play of the game, Sam Darnold threw out to his running back in the flat, but he slipped and the ball when straight into Tuli Tuipulotu’s arms for a second interception in as many plays. With the ball back, the Chargers managed to move the chains twice before the drive stalled just outside the red zone. Mitchell recorded an eight-yard reception for the team’s first first down of the game and a 13-yard pitch-and-catch to wideout Tre’ Harris for the second. The Chargers defense then followed with a three-and-out by the Seahawks offense, but punt returner Derius Davis let the punt bounce off his chest and Seattle recovered at the LA 23-yard line. On the first play following the turnover, Darnold found running back Emmanuel Wilson on a screen before taking it all the way into the end zone. The PAT was good and the Seahawks led 7-3. Herbert and the offense came out uninspired, going three-and-out before punting it away once again. The Chargers showed some life on offense again later in the quarter, starting their drive with runs of nine (Vidal) and 15 (Hampton), but it sputtered out after Quentin Johnston lost four yards on an end-around on second-and-10. Ladd McConkey then recorded his first drop of the season after bobbling the ball on a potential chain-moving reception. Chris O’Leary’s unit remained steady and forced another three-and-out by the Seahawks on the very next drive. Second Quarter After three combined punts by both teams, the Seahawks became the first offense to convert on a third down as Darnold found Jaxon Smith-Njigba for a gain of 28 yards. Three plays later, wide receiver Rashid Shaheed took an end around and raced 28 yards into the end zone to increase the Seahawks’ lead to 13-3 after Jason Myers was wide right on the extra point. Herbert was picked off for a second time on an attempt towards McConkey. Linebacker Ernest Jones looked to drop back underneath the slant route and Herbert threw it right to him. The Seahawks scored two plays later on an eight-yard run by Wilson to push their lead to 20-3. The Chargers got the ball back with 38 seconds remaining. Herbert took off on third-and-eight for a huge pickup of 26 yards down to the Seattle 38-yard line. That was the longest play of the day for the Chargers and it helped flip the field into Seahawks territory. An unnecessary roughness penalty on Seattle then pushed them 15 yards closer and Cameron Dicker came on to convert a 39-yard field goal. Both teams went into the locker rooms with the Seahawks holding a 20-6 lead. Third Quarter Darnold and the Seahawks offense came out hot to begin the second half. They marched 67 yards in eight plays, including a 20-yard completion to Smith-Njigba to begin the drive. Darnold capped the drive with a six-yard touchdown pass to Tory Horton, further piling on their lead to 27-6. For the first time all game, the Chargers offense looked like a competent group on the ensuing drive. Aided by yet another unnecessary roughness penalty by the Seahawks, the Chargers were taken from their 16 to their 31 on the very first play. On Third-and-four, Seahawks safety Nick Emanwori was then called for a face mask penalty which gave the Chargers another free 15 yards. Herbert then found Tre’ Harris for a gain of 26 that brought them just into the red zone at the Seattle 20-yard line. Three plays later, Herbert found Oronde Gadsden for four yards on fourth-and-three to keep their drive alive. Vidal was on the receiving end of a nine-yard touchdown pass from Herbert on second-and-goal and the Chargers finally found the end zone to generate some hope with the score now 27-13. kimani for 6 pic.twitter.com/SnjtqITXC4 — Los Angeles Chargers (@chargers) October 4, 2026 The Seahawks responded with another long drive that…

While most of the players are getting ready, a few members of the team will be on the inactive list. Defensive back Derwin James (hamstring), quarterback DJ Uiagalelei (emergency third QB), offensive […]
full_text: Inglewood, CA - September 20: Los Angeles Chargers safety Derwin James Jr. (3) takes the field for a game against the Las Vegas Raiders at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood on Sunday, September 20, 2026. (Photo by Jeff Antenore/MediaNews Group/Orange County Register via Getty Images) | MediaNews Group via Getty Images The Los Angeles Chargers are getting ready for their Week 4 matchup against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field in the Pacific Northwest. While most of the players are getting ready, a few members of the team will be on the inactive list. Defensive back Derwin James (hamstring), quarterback DJ Uiagalelei (emergency third QB), offensive lineman Alex Harkey, offensive lineman Kayode Awosika (fibula), tight end Charlie Kolar (forearm), wide receiver Brenen Thompson (quad) and defensive tackle Dalvin Tomlinson (hamstring). It’s unfortunate for the Chargers to be without Derwin James. This will hurt their secondary and defense quite a bit, opening the door for the Seahawks to take advantage. In lighter news, wide receiver Ladd McConkey will play despite dealing with a foot injury throughout the week. Meanwhile, the inactives for the Seahawks are quarterback Jalen Milroe (emergency third QB), cornerback Avery Smith, defensive back Ty Okada, linebacker Chazz Surratt, wide receiver Montorie Foster, Jr., tight end Nick Kallerup and defensive lineman Brandon Pili. It’s a big game for the Chargers, who are 0-3 to start the season. If they were to lose today, they would face an 0-4 start, which would put them in a major hole to start the year. If they were to make the playoffs, they would join only the 1992 Chargers as the only squad to lose their first four games and still make the postseason. That’s why this game is so important, and the Chargers have to take it as seriously as possible against the defending champions. Kickoff between the Chargers and Seahawks is set for 1:25 a.m. PT inside Lumen Field. Fans can watch the game on CBS or stream it on the Paramount Plus app.

title: Chargers-Seahawks Game Preview: 2 things to watch for in Week 4
summary: The Chargers are on the road again this week to face the Seahawks (2-1) in one of the most intimidating venues for traveling teams. It’s going to be loud, loud, LOUD for the Chargers and that’s only going to make communication more of an issue for the Los Angeles offense that’s already struggling to be […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - SEPTEMBER 27: Offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel of the Los Angeles Chargers watches play from the sideline against the Buffalo Bills during the fourth quarter of the game at Highmark Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Bryan Bennett/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chargers are on the road again this week to face the Seahawks (2-1) in one of the most intimidating venues for traveling teams. It’s going to be loud, loud, LOUD for the Chargers and that’s only going to make communication more of an issue for the Los Angeles offense that’s already struggling to be on the same page play-in and play-out. Defensively, the Chargers are tasked with putting a lid on the reigning Offensive Player of the Year in wide receiver Jaxon Smitch-Njigba. JSN is currently on an absolute tear through three games with 400+ yards and six touchdowns already to his name. No way around it, the Chargers are going to have their hands full this Sunday. While that’s happening, here are the storylines I’ll be keep a close eye on when these teams are on the field. 1.) Can the offense make…any progress at all? After scoring 14 points in each of their first two games, the offense improved in Week Three by scoring…16 points…against the Bills who were allowing 31.0 PPG on defense coming in. The whole group once again was disconnected and working against each other seemingly on every play. The run game was fine but the lack of Hampton being able to find a groove made it look a lot worse than it probably was. Through the air, receivers struggled to gain separation and Quentin Johnston unfortunately authored another third-down drop that killed a drive. So this week, can the Chargers make literally any progress as an offense? Mike McDaniel told reporters this week that he has a “much better understanding of things that lead to (Justin Herbert) making good plays.” My question is, why didn’t you already have this knowledge down before the regular season started? You had the entire offseason to watch all of his film and all of training camp to gather this knowledge, but we’re still learning how to make Herbert the most comfortable almost a month into the schedule? This is less than ideal! Mike McDaniel on Justin Herbert: “At this point I think I have a much better understanding of things that lead to him making good plays.” — Kris Rhim (@krisrhim1) October 1, 2026 In all fairness, I am not really sure what a “win” would look like this week outside of actually beating the Seahawks. Seattle has the league’s top defense and it’s likely the Chargers offense will look pretty bad once again given the circumstances. Even if Herbert and Co. are more connected and in-line with each other entering this game, the Seahawks are probably going to still make it hell on them. Most notably, that defensive front with Leonard Williams and Byron Murphy is going to be one hell of a task for the interior of the offensive line. So what will “progress” look like this week? Maybe going the entire game without a drop? Maybe Johnston records some new season highs? It’s going to be tough sledding in Seattle. 2.) What is the plan at cornerback if Donte Jackson does not play? When Jackson left the Bills game with a concussion, the Chargers were forced to play Rodney Shelley way more than they initially planned. Even with Deane Leonard healthy, the coaching staff seemed fine letting him only play special teams. I don’t necessarrily agree with that if the next best option is an undrafted rookie, but here we are. Josh Allen exploited Shelley early and often. Several of the biggest passing plays for the Bills were against Shelley who let up three completions on three targets for 66 yards while only playing 11 snaps. This came after he was beat for a touchdown on just one of his two snaps against the Raiders in Week Two. Isas Waxter was elevated for the Bills game but did not end up seeing the field. He’ll likely get another elevation this week given Jackson’s status with a concussion, but it sure seems like the Chargers could use some that isn’t currently on the team. I don’t know if that’s a future trade yet to be made or what, but the Chargers defense cannot survive this season with only three cornerbacks who can hold their own.
author: Michael Peterson

title: Rams boast elite defensive stats even without Myles Garrett
summary: The addition of Trent McDuffie in the offseason is already paying off dividends for the L.A. Rams defense, as they rank second in passing yards allowed, second in yards per pass allowed, and third in EPA per pass allowed through four weeks. Even with no contributions yet from Myles Garrett, or practically Aaron Donald, the […]
full_text: The addition of Trent McDuffie in the offseason is already paying off dividends for the L.A. Rams defense, as they rank second in passing yards allowed, second in yards per pass allowed, and third in EPA per pass allowed through four weeks. Even with no contributions yet from Myles Garrett, or practically Aaron Donald, the Rams have received the pass defensive improvements that they desperately wanted to see from last season. Now imagine how the defense could do with Garrett, Donald, and Jaylen Watson. Trent McDuffie is worth it The Rams traded a late first-round pick in 2026 for McDuffie and then paid him over $30 million per season. This was all in an effort to replace the likes of Darious Williams and company and it’s paying off. McDuffie is arguably the best cornerback in the NFL this season. Trent McDuffie has allowed a 26.7% completion percentage in coverage this season, the lowest of any cornerback to face at least 10 targets. McDuffie has recorded seven passes defensed, the most among cornerbacks, while allowing just four receptions. #RamsHouse pic.twitter.com/Meaivcw2pt — Next Gen Stats (@NextGenStats) October 1, 2026 The Rams wanted to pair McDuffie with former Chiefs teammate Jaylen Watson, but Watson missed Week 4’s win over the Eagles with a shoulder injury. And the Rams held Philadelphia to 68 net passing yards. TRENT MCDUFFIE IS ONE OF THE BEST CORNERBACKS IN THE #NFL : Trent continues to make ridiculous plays look routine and completely LOCK DOWN opposing receivers — every week since arriving in LA. One of the most dominant defensive backs in football. 🔒🔒🔒 pic.twitter.com/qr1PNmGoJ3 — MLFootball (@MLFootball) October 5, 2026 It certainly helps that Jalen Hurts didn’t have Devonta Smith to throw to this week, but Darius Cooper certainly earned some respect with his two touchdown catches against L.A.‘s defense. It took practically all he had for the first one to be completed, so credit to him for that. Only TWO cornerbacks have been targeted multiple times in man coverage and allowed a 0.0 passer rating this season. – Trent McDuffie – Travis Hunter 🤯🤯🤯 pic.twitter.com/Q4t4j6Nary — Dov Kleiman (@NFL_DovKleiman) October 4, 2026 But even so, the Rams held the Eagles to 68 passing yards with Josh Wallace starting and playing the entire game. Wallace certainly deserves more credit too: Going into Week 4, Wallace has been allowing a passer rating of 34.8 on throws in his direction. 4 games, 582 passing yards The Rams have only allowed 582 passing yards in four games, including a season-worst 205 passing yards against the 49ers in Week 1. Only the Seahawks and Rams have held all four opponents to 205 passing yards or fewer this season. L.A.’s defense is second in total yards per play allowed at 4.2, also behind Seattle. One area the Rams would like to improve is forcing more turnovers, as they only have three takeaways and have yet to recover a fumble. This is at least partly related to L.A. only having three sacks and a 19% pressure rate. By comparison, the Vikings have a 36% pressure rate. This is what Garrett was traded to help with and he has missed the last three games. He didn’t do anything in Week 1. But nobody expects Garrett to miss the entire season and his presence will change everything about the Rams’ front seven. Per Next Gen Stats, the Rams are averaging 3.1 yards of separation between the defense and the intended receivers of the offense. That ranks as the third-best in the NFL. Again, this highlights how sticky McDuffie and company have been in coverage this season, a major improvement from 2025. Rams have more on the way Garrett has to miss at least this week’s game against the Bills, and then he will be eligible to come off of IR in Week 6. However, the Rams have not indicated that they expect Garrett to return that soon . If Garrett misses the Cardinals and Raiders games, which would mean six weeks off, he’d return against the Chargers on November 1. Week 4 Defensive EPA per Play pic.twitter.com/upOftpHVWh — Gridiron Stats and Info (@GridironInfo_) October 5, 2026 Watson missed this week’s game, but McVay said that it wasn’t even up for discussion that Watson would go on IR, implying that he could return in the next two weeks. The Rams are reportedly “optimistic” that Donald will return from a back injury in Week 5, according to Mike Garafolo. Aaron Donald (back) is out for Sunday's game against the Eagles, but the Rams are "optimistic" that he'll be able to play Week 5 versus the Bills. Via @MikeGarafolo pic.twitter.com/hhDmeMUkDb — RotoWire Fantasy Football (@RotoWireNFL) October 4, 2026 Kam Kinchens returned from a hamstring injury in Week 4 and played in 70% of the snaps. This is actually typical for Kinchens, but perhaps he’d be even better next week. Overall, if the Rams had this defense and only this defense, their prospects for the upcoming schedule would already be fairly good relative to other teams. However, imagine if this was the Rams defense and then they traded for Myles Garrett, Jaylen Watson, and Aaron Donald between Weeks 5-8. That’s kind of what could happen. And as long as the rest of the team, and McDuffie, stays on track, that could mean that the L.A. Rams’ defense is as good as we thought it could be after the offseason they used toiling to make it better.
author: Kenneth Arthur

title: The Rams need to beat the Bills
summary: The NFL is only entering Week 5, but the October stakes couldn’t be higher for the NFC West based on next weekend’s games. The Los Angeles Rams salvaged potential disaster by coming back to beat the Philadelphia Eagles and setting their record at 2-2, and they’re within striking distance of the 4-0 San Francisco 49ers […]
full_text: The NFL is only entering Week 5, but the October stakes couldn’t be higher for the NFC West based on next weekend’s games. The Los Angeles Rams salvaged potential disaster by coming back to beat the Philadelphia Eagles and setting their record at 2-2 , and they’re within striking distance of the 4-0 San Francisco 49ers and 3-1 Seattle Seahawks. However, that slim margin could become a chasm if the Rams lose to the Buffalo Bills in Week 5. Worst Case: 49ers 5-0, Rams 2-3 The 49ers already have a head-to-head advantage by beating the Rams 27-7 in Week 1. So already the Rams are in a position where they are in a must-win situation when they face San Francisco in Week 14 — but a lot could change by then. Either in L.A.’s favor or against it. Starting this weekend . Week 5: 49ers at Seahawks Week 5: Bills at Rams If the 49ers beat the Seahawks, and the Bills beat the Rams, then L.A. will essentially already be four games back of first place in the NFC West. Four, not three. That’s 3 games back in the win-loss column + a head-to-head loss. Things get really, really ugly when a team is that far behind another team at any point in the season. The good news about it being early in the season is that there’s a lot of time for things to change. The bad news is that it could get that bad this early in the season? The Rams are not in must-win territory, especially when it comes to simply making the playoffs (and it should NOT be the goal for L.A. to only make the playoffs, they must do much better than that), but Sean McVay and Matthew Stafford are pushing the envelope if they lose to the Bills. And the Bills are not going to be easy to beat. Odds to NFC West if this happens: 8.5% If the 49ers end up 5-0 and the Rams 2-3, then L.A.’s odds to win the NFC West drop to approximately 8.5%. This isn’t easy to calculate because a lot depends on whether or not the Rams win the rematch. Even if the Rams win that game, the odds only go up to about 12%. If the Rams lose the rematch, then their odds to win the NFC West are almost 0 . But think of it like this based on the 5-0 vs. 2-3 scenario: If the 49ers go 10-2 the rest of the way, the Rams can’t win the division If the 49ers go 9-3 the rest of the way, the Rams have to go 12-0 If the 49ers go 8-4 the rest of the way, the Rams have to go 11-1 If the 49ers go 7-5 the rest of the way, the Rams have to go 10-2 It becomes a situation where the Rams have to be almost perfect and they need the 49ers to play significantly worse than they’ve already played this season. And that’s just looking at ONE team. The Rams also have to be better than the Seahawks to win the division. “So what? Just win a wild card!” Here we go again: The “All-In” Rams going for…a wild card? Wild Card teams don’t win The Rams haven’t won or reached the Super Bowl since 2021, when they won the division and were the number four seed. That team also had two home games in the playoffs, including the NFC Championship against the 49ers. L.A. can’t count on getting a home game if they are a wild card, and it’s exceedingly rare for teams to go 3-0 on the road in the playoffs. Like it just doesn’t happen. Since 2021’s 7-team playoff expansion, a wild card has NOT made the Super Bowl. From 2002-2020, wild card teams reached the Super Bowl only 4 times (05 PIT, 07 NYG, 10 GB, 20 TB) . So since 2002 realignment, only four wild card teams have reached the Super Bowl. And since expanding the schedule to include an extra wild card, a wild card teams has not even reached the Super Bowl. The goal NEEDS to be winning the NFC West. If the Rams lose to the Bills, that becomes extremely difficult to do. Especially if the 49ers beat the Seahawks. Bills 3-1 Buffalo dropped to 3-1 after losing to the Patriots 29-26 on Sunday. It was a close game, obviously, and needed an exceptional catch by New England’s rookie receiver to win the game in the final minute. TOUCHDOWN PATRIOTS. What a catch by Efton Chism III to take the lead! @NEvsBUF on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/DtIZoenYNL — NFL (@NFL) October 4, 2026 On offense, the Bills have Josh Allen and James Cook and they lead the NFL in points per game. On defense, the Bills are 25th in points allowed per game. Buffalo has allowed at least 29 points in three of four games, with the only exception being the hapless L.A. Chargers. The Bills are hard to beat. The Rams need to beat them. If McVay and Stafford L.A. to a win, then the Rams will be a threat to win the NFC West regardless of how Seattle vs. San Francisco goes because then we’ll know that the team is waking up. However, if they sleep through this week and lose, the odds of getting the rebound that they need to have will be dramatically deflated.
author: Kenneth Arthur

title: With Sunday’s win, Rams put themselves back in the playoff picture
summary: It’s early in the season, but the Los Angeles Rams maybe, kinda, sorta just saved their season by beating the Philadelphia Eagles and rising to 2-2 instead of falling to 1-3. Look, it’s a 17-game season, the Rams maybe, kinda, sorta could’ve come back from a 1-3 reord, but 2-2 is so much better. It’s […]
full_text: It’s early in the season, but the Los Angeles Rams maybe, kinda, sorta just saved their season by beating the Philadelphia Eagles and rising to 2-2 instead of falling to 1-3. Look, it’s a 17-game season, the Rams maybe, kinda, sorta could’ve come back from a 1-3 reord, but 2-2 is so much better. It’s gives them some breathing room. Now, there’s a lot of games to go, the Rams could falter over the next few weeks, but this win, for now, puts the Rams firmly back in the playoff conversation in a real way. It’s a week-to-week league, the Rams can be happy for this week, but they need to keep winning. That’s the trick. Happy victory Monday. Monday night game in Week 5 incoming. 2026 NFL season, Week 4: What We Learned from Sunday’s games (nfl.clom) “ Rams finally finish. Los Angeles thoroughly outplayed the banged-up Eagles at a soggy Linc on Sunday, but found itself down 10 points midway through the fourth quarter. Matthew Stafford interceptions, special teams snafus and fourth-down follies were to blame. But one week after blowing multiple leads against the Broncos, the Rams took control of the proceedings in eastern Pennsylvania and changed the narrative. After L.A. stuffed Philly at the 2-yard line as the Eagles attempted to go up three scores, Stafford led the Rams on their best drive of the day, finding Puka Nacua (who is absolutely back from injury, finishing with nine catches for 125 yards) and Tyler Higbee on the boundary to get L.A. into Philly territory. An Eagles late hit penalty and Kyren Williams TD later, the Rams were within striking distance. L.A. then stopped Philadelphia on their 11th straight third down of the day and got the ball back. The recipe was the same: Nacua and Higbee into Eagles territory, then Williams (147 total yards on 26 touches) to salt away the drive. The box score will say L.A. should have run away with this one (414 yards to 172), and perhaps Sean McVay’s side should have. But the mettle shown against a franchise that has had their number has to be rewarding for the Rams, as they avoid a 1-3 start and keep pace with the rival 49ers and Seahawks in the NFC West. This team can finish — at times, in spite of itself.“ The Los Angeles Rams saved their season with a last-minute comeback (nbcnews) “After having blown a 16-0 lead to the Denver Broncos a week ago, the Los Angeles Rams — a preseason Super Bowl favorite — looked well on their way to another dispiriting loss Sunday. The Rams were trailing 20-10 and had the ball 98 yards away from the end zone with less than eight minutes to go in the fourth quarter on a day they had already committed several mistakes against an opponent they had not beaten since 2020. Staring a 1-3 record in the face, Los Angeles instead stepped up and saved its season.“ Watch: Rams coaches and Eagles fans flip each other off at end of game (ramswire) “The Los Angeles Rams pulled off a dramatic comeback win over the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday afternoon, taking down a team that has had their number for years. Sean McVay was fired up after the win, as were his assistant coaches up in the booth. A video was taken in the stands at the end of the game showing Rams coaches and Eagles fans flipping each other off. Eagles fans could be seen shouting at the Rams’ coaches, who allegedly were banging on the window after Kyren Williams’ go-ahead touchdown. A beer was then thrown by a fan at the glass where the Rams’ coaches were sitting.“ Notable injuries, news from Sunday’s Week 4 games: Saquon Barkley (hamstring), Ja’Marr Chase (concussion) exit (nfl.com) “ Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Rashee Rice (hamstring) was injured in the first quarter and did not return to Sunday’s win over the Raiders. Head coach Andy Reid described Rice’s injury as a tweak. Wide receiver Tyquan Thornton ‘s ankle injury “doesn’t look good,” according to Reid, who said that Thornton would travel back to Kansas City with the team. Thornton was carted off in the fourth quarter and ruled out shortly after. Las Vegas Raiders wide receiver Jalen Nailor (concussion) was ruled out of Sunday’s loss to the Chiefs. Los Angeles Chargers wide receiver Ladd McConkey (foot) and offensive tackle Joe Alt (neck) were ruled out of Sunday’s loss to the Seahawks. Offensive tackle Rashawn Slater (ankle) and cornerback Donte Jackson (hamstring) did not return. Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Konata Mumpfield (shoulder) did not return to Sunday’s win over Philadelphia.“ Rams Beat Eagles, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Stafford, Hurts, Saquon, Puka, Top Players (bleacherreport) “Matthew Stafford and the Los Angeles Rams are magicians. Or the Philadelphia Eagles snatched defeat from the jaws of victory. Depends on your perspective. Los Angeles overcame a 10-point deficit in the fourth quarter for a dramatic 24-20 victory over the Eagles on Sunday at Lincoln Financial Field. Kyren Williams scored the two fourth-quarter touchdowns for the victors, while the Rams defense didn’t allow Jalen Hurts and Co. to score a single point in the second half.“ Game Recap: Rams rally for 24-20 road win over Eagles in Philadelphia (therams.com) “Trailing 20-17 with 3:59 to go in the fourth quarter after a four-yard touchdown run by running back Kyren Williams , the Rams defense had to dig in after kicker Harrison Mevis received a kickoff out of bounds penalty, spotting the ball at the Eagles’ own 40-yard line. Still, the Rams defense got the stop and forced the Eagles (2-2) to punt, putting the ball back in the hands of quarterback Matthew Stafford with just under three minutes remaining. Stafford then marched the Rams downfield on a go-ahead scoring drive punctuated by a seven-yard touchdown run by Williams to give the Rams the lead 24-20 with 1:10 remaining. Outside linebacker Byron Young ‘s two sacks on the final drive clinched the victory for Los Angeles. Williams finished with 16 carries for 80 yards and two touchdowns, plus 10 catches for 67 yards in the victory.“ Eagles vs. Rams: Philadelphia blows a ten-point lead in Week 4 loss (eagleswire) “The Philadelphia Eagles squandered a 10-point halftime lead and fell to the Los Angeles Rams , 24-20, on Sunday at Lincoln Financial Field. Philadelphia failed to convert any of its 12 third-down opportunities and did not score after halftime. Jalen Hurts threw two touchdown passes to Darius Cooper, but the Eagles finished with just 172 total yards. Kyren Williams scored twice in the fourth quarter as Los Angeles completed its comeback, dropping Philadelphia to 2-2. Andrew Mukuba and Cooper DeJean recorded the Eagles’ first two takeaways of the season, but those early defensive contributions were not enough. Saquon Barkley was ruled out with a hamstring injury, and Jonathan Greenard left with an ankle injury and did not return. Philadelphia now heads to London to face Jacksonville on Oct. 11, with an expanding injury list and major questions about its protection and second-half offense. Eagles Wire brought you live updates, scores, and highlights from the game. Check out the key moments below.“ Williams helps Rams stage comeback win over Eagles (nbcsports) “Mike Florio unpacks the Rams improbable win over the “hamstrung” Eagles, where Sean McVay got his first win over Nick Sirianni in comeback fashion thanks to a stellar showing from Kyren Williams.“ Eagles-Rams Week 4 report card: Beat-up Birds let double-digit lead – and history – slip away (phillyvoice) “The Eagles were threatening to become the first team in NFL history to win a game despite failing to convert at least one of 12 third-down attempts before predictably imploding in the fourth as the their injury situation became untenable. Had the Eagles been able to punch in a touchdown at the LA 6 with 8:57 to play, they would’ve have won the game. But they were stopped on three straight tries, including a bold 4th-and-2 pass, and then watched the Rams score go on two TD drives to win.“ NFL says it is looking into an official cursing at Cardinals TE Trey McBride…

title: 5 key plays lead Rams comeback over Eagles
summary: The Los Angeles Rams finally found a way to win in Philadelphia. After falling behind 20-10 at halftime, the Rams rallied for 14 unanswered points in the fourth quarter to defeat the Eagles 24-20 and improve to 2-2 on the season. The comeback was fueled by several pivotal moments on both sides of the football. […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams finally found a way to win in Philadelphia. After falling behind 20-10 at halftime, the Rams rallied for 14 unanswered points in the fourth quarter to defeat the Eagles 24-20 and improve to 2-2 on the season. The comeback was fueled by several pivotal moments on both sides of the football. Matthew Stafford orchestrated two fourth-quarter scoring drives, Kyren Williams delivered two critical touchdown runs, and the Rams defense repeatedly kept the Eagles from putting the game away. Puka Nacua also made an immediate impact in his return from injury, finishing with 125 receiving yards. Philadelphia had multiple opportunities to close out the game, but the Rams continually found a way to stay within striking distance. From costly turnovers and a missed field goal to a critical fourth-down stop and Byron Young’s game-sealing sacks, the contest ultimately came down to a handful of defining plays. 1. Rams D stops Eagles on 4th & Goal (7:31 left in 4th quarter) With the Rams down 20-10, the Eagles had driven down to the Rams 9 yard line. But Chris Shula’s defense stuffed Jalen Hurts on 3rd & Goal and forced an incomplete pass on 4th & Goal. It was a questionable call by Nick Sirianni (surprise) considering the Eagles offense was anemic all afternoon. The 4th down stop gave the Rams offense momentum and they did not look back. The Rams had a 3.2% win probability with 8:17 left in the 4th quarter. It's the most improbable comeback by the Rams under McVay. Stafford completed 12 of 15 passes for 140 yards on his final two drives. (Via NFL Pro) pic.twitter.com/35FgTLOYCM — Blaine Grisak (@BGMediaOnSI) October 4, 2026 2. Stafford checks down to Kyren Williams on 3rd Down & 10 It wasn’t a miraculous play by any measure. It was a simple 9 yard completion but Jonathan Jones was flagged 15 yards for hitting Kyren Williams while he was airborne and well out of bounds. The unnecessary roughness penalty on Philadelphia gave the Rams the ball inside the redzone and a fresh set of downs. Sports Highlights ( #NFL ): The Philadelphia Eagles go upstairs, downstairs on Los Angeles Rams RB Kyren Williams who gets 15 more yards added after this hit! pic.twitter.com/masu2AzFhm https://t.co/FzQFs68sOt — Justin David Kish • Sports Journalist (@JustinDavidKish) October 4, 2026 3. Kam Curl breaks up 3rd Down & 4 pass to Zach Ertz Had the Eagles managed to pick up a first down the Rams might not have had enough time to mount a comeback. On 3rd & 4 at the PHI 46, Kam Curl managed to get his hands in to breakup a pass intended for Zach Ertz. It was the Eagles 11th failed down conversion of the game and forced them to punt the ball back to Los Angeles; giving Matthew Stafford a chance to win the game… and did he. 4. Kyren Williams punches in 2nd Touchdown Kyren Williams was the hero of the game and his 2nd touchdown was impressive. Kyren fought through three defenders on his way to paydirt. After attacking the Eagles run defense inside the tackles all game, Kyren bounced a run outside the left tackle and lunged for the goal line to give the Rams a 24-20 lead with 1:10 left in the game. Kyren walks it in for the touchdown! 💪 📺 @NFLonFOX | #RamsHouse pic.twitter.com/o9EKiRkfai — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) October 4, 2026 5a. Byron Young sacks Jalen Hurts on 1st Down 5b. Byron Young sacks Jalen Hurts on 3rd Down It’s hard not to include both of these. Byron Young closed out the game for the Rams with two sacks, including a forced fumble. Even though the Eagles had no timeouts, there was still opportunity but Young ensured that the Eagles would not come anywhere close to responding. The first was a 7 yard loss and the second was an 8 yard loss. Both plays bleed the clock and the Eagles were forced to throw up a hail mary on 4th Down & 25 from their own PHI 12. Atta way defense ‼️ 📺 @NFLonFOX | #RamsHouse pic.twitter.com/YYss3Wvm5q — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) October 4, 2026

title: Four down territory: Stafford notches 40th comeback win
summary: The Los Angeles Rams (2-2) snatched the soul of the Philadelphia Eagles (2-2) at SoFi Lincoln Financial on Sunday afternoon; mounting a 10 pt comeback to win 24-20. The conditions and circumstances were far from ideal going into and throughout the majority of the game. But Los Angeles finally, and I mean finally, figured out […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 04: Matthew Stafford #9 of the Los Angeles Rams looks to pass during the second quarter of the game against the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field on October 04, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams (2-2) snatched the soul of the Philadelphia Eagles (2-2) at SoFi Lincoln Financial on Sunday afternoon; mounting a 10 pt comeback to win 24-20 . The conditions and circumstances were far from ideal going into and throughout the majority of the game. But Los Angeles finally, and I mean finally, figured out a way to win a close game. Since their Week 3 loss last year to the Eagles, the Rams had endured significant one score losses that just hampered the team from reaching the next level. The hope is that today’s win instills in the team a sense of belief that even when their best football isn’t there, they can win in any game. Here are four major takeaways from Sunday’s win… 1. Tale of Two Stafford’s Stafford single handedly gave the Eagles points when he threw two interceptions; giving the Eagles short field position. Then time and time again, Stafford was just missing his wide receivers. Some of that was the wet conditions but some of that was just trying to make something happen when he just needed to take what the defense was giving him. But…the reason that Stafford has been so great in his career and aged well into his late 30s is because of his ability to bounce back. Regardless of his box score production, Stafford is just gritty and can lead a game winning drive or 4th quarterback in any circumstance or condition. He notched his 40th career 4th quarter comeback; joining Tom Brady, Peyton Manning, and Ben Roethlisberger as the only quarterbacks to do so. Matthew Stafford (40) joined Tom Brady (46), Peyton Manning (43) and Ben Roethlisberger (41) as the only players in NFL history with 40 career fourth quarter comebacks. He also recorded his 51st career game-winning drive, trailing only Brady (58), Manning (54), Roethlisberger… pic.twitter.com/iXl5GPjNtF — Los Angeles Rams PR (@TheLARamsPR) October 4, 2026 2. Kyren Williams puts team on his back The Rams stars were very quiet throughout the majority of the contest but Kyren Williams was the gamechanger. Even though Matthew Stafford gets credit for the 4th quarter comeback as a QB, this was Kyren William’s game. He rushed 16 times for 80 yards and 2 touchdowns, including the game winner. He was also Stafford’s security blanket, hauling in 10 receptions (13 targets) for 67 yards. Vic Fangio and the Eagles defense were determined to not let the Rams get their explosives on offense but they were unable to account for Kyren all afternoon. 3. Essential NFC win & Payback The Rams could not afford to drop to 1-3 but they also could not afford to be 1-2 in the NFC Conference when they play in the NFC West division – the best division in football…again. Dropping to a 1-2 record in the NFC Conference would have probably made the Rams a wildcard team at best. Now, they are 2-1 in the NFC and remain firmly in the conversation for the NFC West divisional crown and a top seed. The other huge factor was that this win “righted” a lot wrongs that took play throughout the 2025 season and the Denver Broncos game in Week 3. The Rams just could not seem to win a one-score game. They had losses to: Philadelphia (Week 3), San Francisco (Week 5), Carolina (Week 13), Seattle (Week 16), Atlanta (Week 17), and Seattle (NFC Championship). All of these one score losses came on the road except Week 5. The Rams finally got the monkey off their back in those close contests and gave some overdue payback. Matthew Stafford (40) joined Tom Brady (46), Peyton Manning (43) and Ben Roethlisberger (41) as the only players in NFL history with 40 career fourth quarter comebacks. He also recorded his 51st career game-winning drive, trailing only Brady (58), Manning (54), Roethlisberger… pic.twitter.com/iXl5GPjNtF — Los Angeles Rams PR (@TheLARamsPR) October 4, 2026 4. Special Teams is still an Ongoing Mess Not only do the Rams coaches, players, and fans know their special teams is a circus, but the media sees it weekly too. In Week 3, it was Emmanuel Forbes drawing a penalty. This week, Harrison Mevis missed a field goal attempt, hit a kickoff out of bounds, and the Rams coverage team struggled to contain Britain Covey. It doesn’t matter who the Rams special teams coach is, the Rams just can’t ever seem to fix the issue. And it continues to show up every week.
author: Steven Ridings

title: The start of something good?
summary: It’s certainly a positive that the Los Angeles Rams were able to stop the slide and find a way to win against the Philadelphia Eagles. The more encouraging sign? That Matthew Stafford and the offense found their footing on the game’s final two possessions and are carrying momentum into next week’s primetime contest against the […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 4: Matthew Stafford #9 of the Los Angeles Rams celebrates after a touchdown during the fourth quarter of an NFL football game against the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field on October 4, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s certainly a positive that the Los Angeles Rams were able to stop the slide and find a way to win against the Philadelphia Eagles . The more encouraging sign? That Matthew Stafford and the offense found their footing on the game’s final two possessions and are carrying momentum into next week’s primetime contest against the Buffalo Bills. What changed with the offense? Well, they had been beating their head into the wall on deep passes— the exact play defenses are aiming to takeaway this season . That problem isn’t fixed from a production standpoint. It can be corrected in terms of frequency. The overly aggressive nature was cooled towards the end of the Eagles game. Stafford took his checkdowns and pass catchers found room to run. The Rams offense played within themselves. With their talented cast, that is enough. Kyren Williams accumulated 67 yards on a whopping 13 targets. Tyler Higbee was often available underneath, although he and Stafford did connect on a 20-yard back-shoulder pass along the sideline. Puka Nacua somehow flew under the radar and still put up 125 yards on nine catches. Explosive is not the expectation. Consistency and good decisions are . As evidenced over the last three weeks, LA’s defense is good enough to give you chances at the end of games . You can’t turn the ball over and hand the opposing offense advantageous field position. The last four weeks haven’t been good enough. This team never expected to be 2-2. How can the Rams keep the positive momentum going? The Bills are strangely a ‘get right’ game Josh Allen and the Bills have been one of the NFL’s best teams through four weeks. On offense they will fill up the scoreboard. You can get after their defense. Buffalo’s defense overall ranks in the lower third of the league in EPA per play, success rate, explosive play rate, points per drive, and missed tackles. They aren’t better in the run game versus the pass. They are flat out bad all the way around. We know the Rams can run the ball. They need to continue to build on their progress in the passing game. The Bills should give them an opportunity to do just that. Their pass defense ranks 26th in EPA per play, 22nd in explosive pass rate, 27th in passer rating allowed, 30th in passing touchdowns with 10, and 20th in interceptions with two. Buffalo leads the NFL in total pressures. On a percentage basis they’re currently third. The Bills can and will get after your quarterback. They’re not sticky enough on the back end for that to matter much. The mission for Stafford and the Rams is to continue on the trajectory they showed on their final two offensive possessions against the Eagles and build on that progress versus Buffalo. It’s a unique opportunity. Climbing to 3-2 from a 1-2 start would be a welcome development. The offense is the key to attaining that record.
author: JB Scott

title: Rams Winners & Losers: Kyren Williams wills LA to much-needed win
summary: While at times the Philadelphia Eagles’ lead felt insurmountable, the Los Angeles Rams come from behind for a 24-20 Week 4 victory. LA improves to 2-2 on the season. It’s their second win in the last three weeks. The defense kept the Rams alive despite the offense hanging them out to dry over and over […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 04: Kyren Williams #23 of the Los Angeles Rams celebrates with teammates in the end zone after scoring a touchdown during the fourth quarter of the game against the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field on October 04, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images While at times the Philadelphia Eagles’ lead felt insurmountable, the Los Angeles Rams come from behind for a 24-20 Week 4 victory . LA improves to 2-2 on the season. It’s their second win in the last three weeks. The defense kept the Rams alive despite the offense hanging them out to dry over and over again. It’s impressive to see the defense hold the line and not break. A late fourth down stop in the red zone gave the offense one final chance—and they drove 99 yards before punching the ball into the end zone. Williams scored his second touchdown on the ensuing possession. One can hope that these final two drives exorcise the offense’s demons and put their early season struggles in the rear view mirror. It seemed a weight came off for a team that has faced significant adversity through four weeks. Let’s analyze the individual performances that helped the Rams finish in the win column. Winners Kyren Williams, RB Kyren Williams is on a tear. The last two games could possibly be the best stretch of play we’ve ever seen from the veteran running back. He has clearly taken a step forward as a receiver. He’s the focal point of the offense right now. Williams rushed 16 times for 80 yards (5.0 average) with two scores. Matthew Stafford targeted him 13 times (!) and he hauled in 10 catches for 67 yards. That’s a complete effort. Trent McDuffie, CB At a time where nearly all of the Rams’ high-profile defensive acquisitions are injured, Trent McDuffie is the one newcomer who has been as advertised. He’s a physical tackler in the screen and run game. His coverage is sticky and he has a nose for the football. Good things will happen over McDuffie’s tenure in LA. He fits the bill to the tee. Eagles went 0 for 12 on third down against the Rams. Went 0 for 5 in the second half last week against the Bears. Their last third down conversion was over 90 minutes of game clock ago. — Benjamin Solak (@BenjaminSolak) October 4, 2026 Josh Wallace, CB Jaylen Watson’s absence was catastrophic last week. With a week of preparation for the Eagles, the Rams defense didn’t miss a beat in coverage with Josh Wallace. It helps, of course, that Philly was short-handed in terms of pass catchers . Wallace deserves praise for the quick turnaround. He was from scapegoat to value add in the span of a week. Puka Nacua, WR Nacua earned a quiet 125 yards through the air on Sunday. He caught nine of his 12 targets and was an efficient part of LA’s passing attack. With Nacua managing a soft tissue injury, it was a positive sign that he mostly looked like himself. The Rams must maximize both Nacua and Adams—at times it seems questionable whether they can co-exist and both be productive. Losers Davante Adams, WR The Rams dropped five passes on Sunday when their passing game needed all the help it could get. The quarterback wasn’t sharp. The receivers also deserve blame for execution failures along the way. Adams had at least two drops on his own, including a would-be touchdown on an amazing deep throw from Stafford. The veteran receiver continues to not be on the same page as his quarterback, as the duo missed again on a later deep connection with Adams open. It’s been a troubling and continuing trend through four weeks. Special teams… again The Eagles averaged 19.7 return yards on three punts. That’s pretty bad. Philly’s return man, Britain Covey, was waived by the Rams last year in favor of the now-released Xavier Smith. I bet LA wish they could have a do-over on that decision. Kicker Harrison Mevis also missed a 48-yard field goal, which explains why the Rams rarely let him kick from beyond 45 out. He made a 40-yard attempt. Between two offensive turnovers and poor punt coverage, the Rams handed the Eagles very favorable field position on a handful of drives. The defense did their part to stop the bleeding, but the other two phases failed to set them up for success often . Blake Corum, RB 29 plays went in Williams’ direction between rushes and targets. Blake Corum earned just 7 opportunities. This used to be as close to a 50/50 backfield as it gets. Williams has led the charge over the last two weeks and Corum is an afterthought. And, in fairness, Corum has done little in order to make the coaching staff question the rotation. He’s at risk of losing his role in the offense. An almost inconceivable loss https://t.co/0pHcC636PX pic.twitter.com/ACT8FkCtw6 — Brett Kollmann (@BrettKollmann) October 4, 2026 Matthew Stafford, QB Let’s be honest with Matthew Stafford’s performance. We must be process oriented and not only focus on outcomes. Yes, the Rams won and that is a positive. Stafford played better in the late fourth quarter. It was not a winning performance. Stafford threw two interceptions and the Eagles scored 10 points off those turnovers. The Rams only managed 10 points through the first half, went scoreless again in the third quarter, and then did their best work with less than five minutes on the clock. I’ve said recently that the defense is not the problem . Special teams and the offense are failing them, which is why their high rankings in yardage allowed does not match their lower rankings in points allowed. Football is a symbiotic game and the ultimate team sport. All three phases must work in coordination. Stafford is not playing complimentary football through four weeks of the season. This defense may be good enough for him to get by with a competent but not elite performance. They are not good enough to consistently win when he’s gifting points to the other team. Hopefully the momentum the Rams built on the game’s final two drives will re-ignite their fire moving forward.
author: JB Scott

title: Rams vs. Eagles final score: Matthew Stafford resilient in win
summary: The Los Angeles Rams beat the Philadelphia Eagles by a final score of 24-20 in Week 4, coming back from a 10-point deficit to improve their record to 2-2. Matthew Stafford rebounded from a poor game to get the Rams in position to score the go-ahead touchdown, which was a hard-nosed run by Kyren Williams, […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams beat the Philadelphia Eagles by a final score of 24-20 in Week 4, coming back from a 10-point deficit to improve their record to 2-2. Matthew Stafford rebounded from a poor game to get the Rams in position to score the go-ahead touchdown, which was a hard-nosed run by Kyren Williams, his second of the game. Puka Nacua returned from a two-game absence to catch nine passes for 125 yards. Facing early season extinction if they lost, the Rams were resilient enough to end up beating the Eagles. Kyren Williams POWERS IT IN FOR THE LEAD!! @LARvsPHI on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/LW85llHviL — NFL (@NFL) October 4, 2026 Although Stafford threw two picks in the first half (he’s thrown an interception in every game this year), and Harris Mevis missed a 48-yard kick to help Philly hold a 20-10 lead into halftime, the Rams showed life in the second half. They put up 16 unanswered points to make the score 24-20 with just about one minute left in the fourth quarter. The Rams struggled to find an exact rhythm on offense Sunday, as Stafford missed some throws while his players also failed to haul in some of his stronger passes. The special teams was a low point with penalties, poor coverage and a missed field goal by Mevis after being perfect in Week 3. But the Rams defense kept them in the game, and they were rewarded with a victory. Chris Shula bailed out Sean McVay today more the other way around. The First Half Quarters one and two ended up badly for L.A. Their defense jumped out to a hot start, sure, but the offense struggled with Stafford turning the ball over twice, and Kyren Williams getting stuffed on a third and one early in the game, forcing a punt. The rainy weather and Vic Fangio’s defense did a lot of the heavy lifting for Philly, who was without DeVonta Smith. Saquan Barkley also left this game in the first quarter, yet, Philly seemed to overcome as Jalen Hurts found Darious Cooper for two passing touchdowns before the first half came to its close. The special teams for the Rams also gave up a big return to Britain Covery who at one time had a chance to make the Rams roster. L.A. may be regretting their decision to let Covey walk after seeing his big return today and they’re lack of consistency in their own return game. Hurts had less than 100 passing yards after the first half, but still had two passing scores. Credit Hurts’s nice play to make that happen, but the Rams have to take some blame for allowing that. The Second Half The Rams came out the second half with the ball on offense and trailing 10 points. Stafford had a chance to connect with Adams deep, but overthrew the ball. To be fair, earlier in the game Stafford had hit Adams seemingly on the hands in the endzone, but Adams failed to haul that one in. Point being, there was plenty of blame to go around for why the Rams were trailing to their NFC East opponent, but the Rams kept grinding, they kept competing. Stafford and the offense failed to get anything of substance going. Seemingly anytime the Rams did put together a strong play, it was negated or pushed back by a penalty. Finally, with less than 5 minutes to play, the Rams made the score 20-17 when Kyren Williams found the endzone, but then Mevis kicked the ensuing kickoff out of bounds setting up the Eagles at the 4o-yard line. It was another example of the Rams getting in their own way, butt the Rams held as they forced a turnover on downs and Williams rush for his second score of the day. It happened fast, but all the sudden the Rams had a 24-20 lead, and they held it. The Officiating Rams’ fans are going to say the officiating was poor, the Eagles would say the same. Either way, it’s worth bringing up that for the second week in a row some very questionable calls went against McVay and his boys. Trent McDuffie was called for a weak pass interference call towards the end of the opening half when his glove became caught on a jersey. The Rams had a player run into an official on the sideline. Puka Nacua was called for what looked like a phantom blindside block. Officiating in any NFL game is typically worth discussion because calls can be so subjective. The Rams were outplayed more than not over the course of 60 minutes, but they found a way to win as good teams do. The Rams were good enough in Week 4. The Final: A “super team” this team is not. Though, through 4 weeks the Rams are 2-2 though, so they have a chance to rebound, especially after Myles Garrett, Jaylen Watson, and Aaron Donald are able to return. Puka helped power the Rams on Sunday. Maybe more reinforcements can do that this month. The season isn’t over, and the Rams will look to build off this win in Week 5 against the Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football.

title: Las Vegas Raiders lose in trenches against Kansas City Chiefs to fall short in Week 4
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders entered Week 4 with a chance to take command of the AFC West, but fell three points short, squandering the opportunity with the 30-27 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs. The difference came down to the trenches, as both teams ran the ball 26 times, but the Chiefs turned that into […]
full_text: (Photo by Chris Unger/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders entered Week 4 with a chance to take command of the AFC West, but fell three points short, squandering the opportunity with the 30-27 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs . The difference came down to the trenches, as both teams ran the ball 26 times, but the Chiefs turned that into 189 rushing yards (7.3 ypc) and the Raiders managed just 72 yards on the ground (2.8 ypc). That’s a big point of emphasis in this week’s winners and losers. LOSER: Klint Kubiak Kubiak drew plenty of praise for starting his career 3-0, but the other end of that is that he has to shoulder the blame when his team loses. Also, while it can be debatable whether or not the decision to take the field goal off the board was the right decision, the NFL is a results business at the end of the day and Kubiak’s call didn’t work out. To the coach’s credit, he took accountability for the loss after the game and admitted that he “blew it” on the final drive. There’s still plenty of reason to believe in the first-time head coach. One loss doesn’t erase how the Raiders have already exceeded expectations with a hot start to the season. However, Kubiak certainly has to figure out the offense’s running game woes since his unit hasn’t had success on the ground since Week 1. LOSER: Kolton Miller While Miller has been a steadying presence on Las Vegas’ offensive line for several years, including the beginning of the 2026 campaign, he was anything but that on Sunday. According to Pro Football Focus , the nine-year veteran had only given up five pressures in the first three games combined but more than doubled his season total by giving up six to the Chiefs. Miller struggled to handle George Karlaftis’ power in the passing game, and he had issues in the running game, getting beaten several times to log a 51.2 run-blocking grade from PFF. Again, the Raiders’ left tackle and longest-tenured offensive lineman has been playing well for most of the season. But he certainly wasn’t at his best in Week 4. LOSER: Caleb Rogers To be fair, lining up against Chris Jones in your first start of the season isn’t an easy task. However, the Raiders needed Rogers to provide more resistance than giving up five pressures and an ugly 7.6 PFF pass-blocking grade . On top of that, this was an opportunity for the second-year pro to establish himself as a regular starter moving forward with Jackson Powers-Johnson out of the lineup. But Rogers didn’t rise to the occasion, likely giving Powers-Johnson his spot back if he can return from injury next week. WINNER: Michael Mayer If you’re looking for silver linings from the Silver and Black’s tough loss, Kubiak’s ability to use the team’s tight ends is one of them. Fighting an illness, Brock Bowers did his thing by being the team’s leading receiver with six catches for 86 yards and a touchdown, while Kubiak had a great play design for Ian Thomas to score a 27-yard touchdown. On top of that, Mayer had one of the best games of his career, hauling in eight passes for 82 yards. Both of those figures are the second-most he’s had in a single game . The fourth-year pro did exactly what is expected of him in the Raiders’ passing attack: serve as a check-down option by getting yards after the catch and moving the chains (37 YAC and five first downs, per PFF ), in addition to making contested catches (three-for-three on such targets). That’s the type of performance the Raiders have been looking for since giving Mayer a contract extension right before the season. LOSER: Rob Leonard Of course, the defensive front seven shoulders some of the blame for Kenneth Walker collecting 177 rushing yards and 8.0 yards per carry, but so does the defensive play caller. Also, Leonard got burned when trying to dial up the heat on Patrick Mahomes, as three Cover 0 calls resulted in the Chiefs adding over 50% win probability, according to former director of analytics Ryan Paganetti on X/Twitter . Additionally, Mahomes was seven-of-11 for 120 yards with one “big time throw” and no “turnover-worthy plays” when the Raiders blitzed on Sunday, per PFF , and Vegas’ fourth-quarter defensive magic ran out. The Chiefs scored 20 of their 30 points in the final frame and weren’t forced into any turnovers throughout the game. Leonard did a great job of creating havoc in the first three weeks of the year, but not so much against Kansas City. The Raiders may have wished they could get some of their Cover 0 calls back against Mahomes. Three pivotal Cover 0 moments in the game: 41 yard completion to Worthy (10.6% win probability added) 2 yard TD to Thornton (5.6% win probability added) 55 yard completion to Thornton… — Ryan Paganetti (@RyanPaganetti) October 5, 2026 WINNER: Kirk Cousins Cousins certainly isn’t to blame for the loss, throwing for a season-high 365 passing yards and a pair of touchdowns. Granted, 52 attempts definitely helps with that. But the quarterback has been playing pretty well over the last three weeks. He’s tied with Brock Purdy for the most passing touchdowns in the NFL (11) so far this season, and has posted a solid 71.8 PFF passing grade . There’s no need for the Raiders to put Fernando Mendoza on the field right now because Cousins is playing well enough to keep the team in the playoff conversation through the first quarter of the season. LOSER: Kwity Paye After a solid performance in the season opener, Paye has been pretty quiet. He had six tackles, two TFLs, two sacks and four quarterback hits against the Miami Dolphins, but has five, zero, zero and one in the three games combined since then. Paye’s outing on Sunday was especially underwhelming, failing to show up on the box score while also recording zero pressures on 18 pass rushes, a missed tackle and a 43.8 run defense grade, per PFF . That’s not what the organization had in mind when it signed the free agent to a three-year, $48 million contract in the offseason. LOSER: Mike Washington Jr. Kubiak mentioned that Washington had earned more touches with his play during the first three games of the season, and the rookie received the most carries he’s had with nine against the Chiefs. However, that resulted in the second-lowest rushing yards (18) and worst yards per carry (2.0) of his young career. On top of that, Washington struggled in the passing game with one drop on two targets and was beaten for a pressure in pass protection . The Raiders may have issues in the running game, but it’s pretty clear who their top back is right now.

title: Explosive plays, special teams miscue Raiders’ undoing in loss to Chiefs
summary: When CBS Sports play-by-play man Jim Nantz called out Kansas City had generated just 18 total yards of offense with 30 seconds left in the third quarter, it was fortuitous foreshadowing for the Chiefs. What ensued was an explosive play netting a touchdown and four series later, the visiting Chiefs got another chunk play resulting […]
full_text: (Photo by Chris Unger/Getty Images) | Getty Images When CBS Sports play-by-play man Jim Nantz called out Kansas City had generated just 18 total yards of offense with 30 seconds left in the third quarter, it was fortuitous foreshadowing for the Chiefs. What ensued was an explosive play netting a touchdown and four series later, the visiting Chiefs got another chunk play resulting in another end zone visit. And after punching the ball out of Las Vegas Raiders kick returner Dareke Young, Kansas City found the end zone one play later. Yielding the two explosive plays and the special teams gaffe sunk the home Raiders and the Chiefs reign supreme in the AFC West at 4-0 after a tightly contest 30-27 win this past Sunday.4 What could’ve been a runaway win Kansas City was thwarted by Las Vegas trailing 30-19 in the fourth quarter, but unlike the previous two matchups where takeaways powered the Silver & Black, it was the opposition that showcased more complementary football. It’s the first defeat for Raiders rookie head coach Klint Kubiak — who proclaimed on the broadcast his team would win the game in a half time interview before the two teams went into the locker rooms at half time — and how his team develops and grows after this stinging loss will say a lot about this team going forward. Especially with his football team having a difficult schedule ahead of them. "[The Raiders] are going to be a pain in the butt for every team out there." @PriscoCBS #NFLPostgame pic.twitter.com/J0vgmZ2NqC — NFL on CBS 🏈 (@NFLonCBS) October 5, 2026 As longtime NFL analyst Pete Prisco noted above, this isn’t a fugazi football team and what Kubiak is doing is not fluke. How he and his coaching staff pivot after film review from the loss is something many will be watching closely — under a microscope even. Because yielding explosive plays on defense while not generating more of their own on offense can’t continue to happen, especially for a tough stretch of upcoming games that feature the New England Patriots (road), Buffalo Bills (home), Los Angeles Rams (home), and New York Jets (road) in the next four games. Las Vegas will also need to rejuvenate a run game that’s been stymied. Perhaps watching the tape of how Walker carved up the defense will provide not only answers for Rob Leonard’s defense, but Kubiak’s offense? Immediately after Nantz made note of the lack of offensive production, Walker took the hand off on the 1st-and-10 play from the Chiefs’ 11-yard line sprinted through a gaping hole for a 76-yard run. The reason it wasn’t a home run break away touchdown was because of the hustle from Raiders nickel cornerback Taron Johnson, who ran the tailback down. K9 GOES 77 YARDS 🔥 @KCvsLV on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/1d8jxbAU0C — NFL (@NFL) October 4, 2026 Two plays later, quarterback Patrick Mahomes threw a dime to wide open wide receiver Tyquan Thornton to boost the Chiefs momentarily lead to 17-13. But Thornton wasn’t done there as he hauled in a 55-yard dime from Mahomes to set up a go-ahead two-yard touchdown run from Walker, 23-19 Chiefs. Walker hit pay dirt again after the forced fumble and recovery on the ensuing kick off going around the Raiders defense for a 22-yard score and with 30-19 lead in hand and 3:02 left to play, Kansas City was comfortable. Kubiak and his Raiders weren’t going to go away quietly and made it a game again after quarterback Kirk Cousins escaped a sack and lofted a 20-yard touchdown to tight end Brock Bowers to slash the deficit to 30-27. The Las Vegas defense rose to the occasion to force a punt but the Raiders’ last gasp on offense ended with Cousins firing an interception on a play that Kubiak admitted he didn’t get quickly enough to his quarterback, hence its haphazard nature and turnover. Let’s hit the quick slants as fast as both Walker and Thornton torched the Raiders defense on their respective big-play efforts: —Losing by three points put Kubiak’s decision to go for it on 4th-and-2 instead of keeping the made field goal on the board in the third quarter under the spotlight. To his credit, the rookie’s aggressive decision is something to be done against the high-powered Chiefs, and Kubiak noted he didn’t regret the decision, just regretted the team couldn’t convert and turned the ball over. —Bowers and fellow tight end Michael Mayer paced the Raiders air attack with six catches for 86 yards and a touchdown and eight receptions for 82 yards, respectively. Reserve tight end Ian Thomas hauled in the other touchdown — a beauty of a 27-yard pass from Cousins where Kubiak schemed the tight end wide open. KIRK COUSINS MAGIC FOR THE TOUCHDOWN! @KCvsLV on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/ADaylXSjLZ — NFL (@NFL) October 4, 2026 —While the tight ends produced 200 yards and two touchdowns on 16 receptions, the wide receivers didn’t produce as much. Tre Tucker had four grabs for 44 yards while Cody White had two receptions for 32 yards. Jeanty did haul in six passes for 68 yards, but the lack of a standout wideout is glaring. —In the battle of quality punters, the Chiefs’ southpaw Matt Araiza outperformed the Raiders’ AJ Cole III with five boots for 238 yards and all five landing or downed inside Las Vegas’ 20-yard line. Cole had three punts for 142 yards with only one being downed or landing inside the Chiefs’ 20-yard line. —Walker’s impressive 2026 season continued as he churned out 177 yards on 22 carries (8.0 yards per carry average) with two touchdowns. —CBS Sports color analyst and likely future hall of fame defensive end J.J. Watt called out that Crosby was on the sideline during Walker’s long 76-yard run for a breather. And just like Watt noted, giving up that kind of explosive play with your best defender taking a rest likely is the catalyst for Crosby to once again play near 100 percent of snaps. —In comparison, the Raiders’ entire run game rushed for 72 yards on 26 carries (2.8 yards per carry) with Ashton Jeanty leading the group with 58 yards on 15 carries. Rookie running back Mike Washington Jr. added 18 yards on 9 totes while fullback Connor Heyward had two carries for negative four yards. Ashton Jeanty talks about how he is feeling health wise and what the #Raiders offense needs to do in order to get the run game going again pic.twitter.com/qh3XqgFVsI — Raider Nation Radio (@RNR920AM) October 5, 2026 Quotes of Note “I took three points off the board, and we were going to be aggressive going into the game. I don’t regret it. I regret not getting it.” —Las Vegas Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak on going for it on 4th-and-2 in the third quarter instead of taking the made field goal. “That’s a good football team. You know they had a few people defensively come over for them. They added to the talent they had. The D line and secondary were playing together. That’s a good team. When Kirk’s dealing like that it’s hard to stop. And they have a guy like Brock Bowers. We have to keep getting better but I’m sure they will do the same.” —Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes on the Las Vegas Raiders after the win. Up Next Las Vegas (3-1) preps for an East Coast trip to face New England (2-2) next Sunday. The Patriots head into Week 5 after a big win over the Buffalo Bills in their AFC East clash. The Raiders are 2-0 on the road so far this season and will need similar strong performances the team had at the Los Angeles Chargers and New Orleans Saints. Unlike the two previous away games, however, this is the first for the Silver & Black that’s an early 10 a.m. (Pacific Standard Time) matchup.

Last meeting: Last season, these two teams reminded the NFL and its fan base just how wild and unpredictable Week 1 of every NFL season can be. Like Carrol, Mike Vrabel was in his first game as the head coach of his team. The Raiders went on to earn the No. 1 overall pick in the draft and Carroll was fired the day after the season ended. Vrabel was named the AP NFL Coach of the Year and led New England to the Super Bowl. So, yeah, Week 1.
