title: Klint Kubiak takes accountability for Las Vegas Raiders falling short against Kansas City Chiefs
summary: Klint Kubiak is no longer perfect as an NFL head coach. The Las Vegas Raiders entered Week 4 undefeated and with a chance to take command of the AFC West with a win against the Kansas City Chiefs, who also entered the game without a loss. However, the Raiders fell just three points short, losing […]
full_text: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images Klint Kubiak is no longer perfect as an NFL head coach. The Las Vegas Raiders entered Week 4 undefeated and with a chance to take command of the AFC West with a win against the Kansas City Chiefs, who also entered the game without a loss. However, the Raiders fell just three points short, losing to the Chiefs 30-27 , giving Kubiak his first loss. As is customary on Monday morning sports talk shows, the head coach will likely face a lot of criticism for two plays/decisions. The first game was during the opening possession of the third quarter. Las Vegas kicked a field goal to extend its lead to six points. However, an illegal formation penalty by Kansas City left the head coach with a decision to make: leave the points on the board, or gamble by taking the penalty and going for it on fourth and two. In typical Vegas fashion, Kubiak put all of his money on black, and the roulette ball landed on red, with the Chiefs making a big stop to keep it a three-point game. Hindsight being 20/20, that’s a tough pill to swallow in a three-point loss. But the Raiders still had a chance to pull off a miraculous comeback. However, the offense scrambled to get a play off with 10 seconds left and looked completely disjointed, leading to an interception from Kirk Cousins to seal the Silver and Black’s fate. Kubiak discussed both situations during his post-game press conference, taking accountability by saying he “blew it,” as the internet reacts to Las Vegas’ first loss of the 2026 campaign. Klint Kubiak on the Raiders final offensive play and what led to the disjointed Kirk Cousins interception: “I didn’t get the play call in fast enough to the quarterback and total missed opportunity. I blew it.” — Sam Warren (@samwarren83) October 5, 2026 #Raiders HC Klint Kubiak on the decision not to get kick the FG and go for it on fourth down in the third quarter: “I took three points off the board, and we were going to be aggressive going into the game. I don’t regret it. I regret not getting it.” — Ryan McFadden (@ryanmcfadden_) October 4, 2026 Klint Kubiak on what was different between the decision to go for it in the third quarter and the one to kick the field goal with 5 minutes to go in the fourth to take a two-point lead. “Just wanted points. Fell short the first time, wanted to get the points.” https://t.co/V7p3naHJbs — Sam Warren (@samwarren83) October 5, 2026 “I don’t regret it.” Raiders coach Klint Kubiak on his decision making and “We’re going to win” statement at halftime after a 30-27 loss to the Chiefs. 🎥: By @Sean_Zittel pic.twitter.com/E3AGSrFGL9 — Vegas Sports Today (@VegasSportsTD) October 5, 2026 Kirk Cousins on what went wrong on the Raiders final offensive play and Klint Kubiak taking blame for it: "That's Klint. He's always gonna point the thumb at himself and how he can be better. I think there's a lot going on there. We're trying to get to the optimum play, clocks… — Sam Warren (@samwarren83) October 5, 2026 “It’s our job to execute and make the coach right. I feel like I probably could’ve squeezed it to Cody on 4th down. That’s one of the plays on the drive, I’m gonna be thinking about.” Raiders QB Kirk Cousins on Klint Kubiak’s 4th down decision making after a 30-27 loss to the… pic.twitter.com/3SDqQwkmVS — Vegas Sports Today (@VegasSportsTD) October 5, 2026 THE NUMBERS SAY KICK pic.twitter.com/LIPPzJhV5f — Seth Walder (@SethWalder) October 4, 2026 The Raiders have also been struggling to run the ball over the last three games, Sunday included, with just 72 rushing yards and 2.8 ypc as a team. Kubiak was asked about that as well. Kubiak on finding more consistency in the run game: “We got to find that answer because that’ll be a big factor in us being a better team.” — Ryan McFadden (@ryanmcfadden_) October 5, 2026 The Raiders certainly let this one slip through their hands, but this team is already exceeding expectations if we’re upset about a three-point loss to a Super Bowl favorite for first place in the AFC West. The Raiders had it. They really had it. Barely even a minute of game clock later, Chiefs essentially seal it. Unreal. — Brett Kollmann (@BrettKollmann) October 4, 2026 Brutal loss but if you told me a month ago that the #Raiders would be in a dog fight with the Chiefs for 1st place in the AFC West, I’d be ecstatic — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) October 4, 2026 I don’t care if they won. I love this Raiders team. — Andrew Perloff (@andrewperloff) October 4, 2026 "[The Raiders] are going to be a pain in the butt for every team out there." @PriscoCBS #NFLPostgame pic.twitter.com/J0vgmZ2NqC — NFL on CBS 🏈 (@NFLonCBS) October 5, 2026 A few thoughts from our community chat (click the links/quotes below to join the conversation): Chiefs played a helluva game and we still made it competitive to the end. Finally losing the turnover battle was the downfall. But this team is obviously on the right path for the first time in 25 years. I can’t even be mad. — ResDog In the end it’s not about beating KC, it’s about winning SB. Beat KC next time and in AFC title game if so. But might never see them again too aside from the next game. Beat New England Cheatriots next. That’s what’s important, atm. — Njccc Game of inches, right? The punt returner should have gone straight then down, Laube should have fair caught-too much distance to go, Tucker-catch the ball. Despite all of this we had a chance and shoulda/coulda won. 175 yards rushing indeed killed us plus they made more deep plays. Either way, great effort by our Raiders. Let’s see how they respond next week against those darn Cheats. — NC Hellrazors The game was won and lost in the run game and kicking game and the points we took off the board, im concerned about the Oline not run blocking good enough, cant win that way, need a road grader to open holes up in the middle, where is it? title: Raiders-Chiefs: 18 things we learned
summary: We were going to learn something about the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 4 against the Kansas City Chiefs as they faced increased competition. And, in the process of seeing Klint Kubiak’s team lose 30-27 to drop to 3-1, we certainly did learn something. First, we learned that this outfit isn’t a phony. The Raiders […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - OCTOBER 04: Kenneth Walker III #9 of the Kansas City Chiefs runs the ball against the Las Vegas Raiders during the first quarter at Allegiant Stadium on October 04, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Chris Unger/Getty Images) | Getty Images We were going to learn something about the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 4 against the Kansas City Chiefs as they faced increased competition. And, in the process of seeing Klint Kubiak’s team lose 30-27 to drop to 3-1 , we certainly did learn something. First, we learned that this outfit isn’t a phony. The Raiders can play. Sure, they didn’t make enough plays (for the first time this season) to win and the Chiefs, in the end, were the better team. But the Raiders showed they belonged in a game that had serious playoff-game vibes. They showed that they will likely be an AFC playoff contender and it with the first game of a tough eight-game stretch in the books, Las Vegas gave Kansas City and the rest of the league something to think about. They weren’t 3-0 just because they beat bad teams. They nearly pulled off a second straight late double-digit comeback, but fell short. Moving forward, the Raiders proved that, while they are not going to go undefeated, Yes, they re for real in the first year of Kubiak’s tenure: Here are some key aspects of the game: Turnovers not there: The Raiders led the NFL with nine takeaways after the first three weeks. They didn’t get any Sunday and they committed two turnovers themselves both in the fourth quarter. Last week, the Raiders got four takeaways in the fourth quarter. The line between winning and losing. No fourth-quarter magic: The Raiders outscored their first three opponents 22-0 in the fourth quarter. Sunday, the Chiefs scored right away in the quarter and outscored the Raiders 20-14 in the quarter. Another line between winning and losing. Run attack struggles for much of the game: The Raiders’ running attack has suffered since Week 1. Sunday, they struggled most of the game and ended up with 72 rushing yards. Ashton Jeanty, who looks like he’s still dealing with ankle issues, had 58 yards on 19 carries. He did add 68 yards on six catches. Rookie Mike Washington had 18 yards on nine carries. Kubiak said after the game figuring out the ground game is vital and he’s right. Kenneth Walker crushed them: The Raiders got their first look at Kenneth Walker in a Chiefs’ uniform and they didn’t like it. Walker was the star of the game as he had 177 rushing yards on 22 caries and two scores. He had a 76-yard run that turned the game in the Chiefs’ favor on the final play of the third quarter. Walker is a big reason why the Chiefs are 4-0. Cousins pressured: The Chiefs didn’t have any sacks Sunday, but they hit Kirk Cousins often. Yet, the 38-yaear-old hung in there threw for 365 yards and he threw two touchdown passes. He now has 11 on the season. Cousins wasn’t the reason why the Raiders’ lost. So was Mahomes: The Raiders were all over Mahomes and they had two sacks. He did hurt them with some deep passes, but Maxx Crosby and company made Mahomes work. Taking points off the board: The Raiders went down the field and converted a 41-yard field goal to make it 16-10 to open the second half. But the Chiefs were called for a penalty and the Kubiak went for it on fourth and two. The play failed at the Chiefs 18. Taking points off the board hurts. But the aggression by Kubiak was understandable. You have to get in the end zone to beat Mahomes. Kubiak said he didn’t regret the move in the eventual threee-point loss. Tight ends take over passing game: The Raiders’ passing game revolved around ight ends Brock Bowers (who played despite being ill), Michael Mayer and Ian Thomas. They combined for 16 catches for 200 yards and two touchdowns. That may have to continue. The Raiders’ receivers aren’t producing much and Jalen Nailor suffered a concussion. With Jack Bech and Dont’e Thornton on the injured reserve, this won’t quiet rumors about the Raiders trading for a receiver before the November 10 deadline. Penalties not a problem again: The Raiders entered the game leading the NFL in fewest penalty yards at 90. They had six penalties for 30 yards while the Chiefs were flagged eight times for 59 yards. Gay has been perfect: Free-agent kicker Matt Gay has been terrific. He was four-for-four on field-goal attempts Sunday and is 10-for-10 on he season. Not bad for a journeyman. Kwity Paye quiet again: Free-agent addition, defensive end Kwity Paye had a great Week 1, but he hasn;t made much of an impact since. He didn’t appear on the initial post-game stat sheet. What a start: The Raiders ‘ defense forced a 3-and-out on the first drive, but the Chiefs ran a perfect fake punt on a re-punt after a penalty. Yet, the Raiders then stopped Kansas City on fourth and 1 at the Las Vegas 49. Then, the Raiders turned around and connected on a long pass play for a score with Cousins hitting tight end Ian Thomas. It was a hell of a play call by Kubiak and it was Thomas’ first score in six years. It was a great answer from Las Vegas to Kansas City’s aggression and got the crowd in the game. Laube is balling: Returner Dylan Laube had a 53-yard kick return in the fourth quarter. He is leading the NFL witha 33.4 yard return average on kickoffs. Streak continues: The Raiders have not allowed a score on their opponents opening drive for seven straight games dating back to last season. It’s the second longest current streak in the NFL. This is the first team the Raiders have started the season allowing no scores on the opening drive in the first four games since 2018. Kelce surpasses Raiders’ legend: Kansas City star tight end Travis Kelce entered the game tied with Raiders’ Pro Football Hall of Fame tight end Tim Brown for seventh place with 1,094 all-time catches/ Kelce surpassed Brown in the first half. Overall, the Raiders contained Kelce, a noted Raiders’ killer who started this season hot. He had just two catches for 15 yards. Rice hurt: Chiefs receiver Rashee Rice hurt his hamstring in the first quarter. That was a loss for the Chiefs. Too many Chiefs fans: Ys, opposing fans often take over Allegiant Stadium, especially Chiefs’ games. So, the sea of red was expected. But this was a huge game. The Raiders fans must keep their tickets. Expect a similar takeover attempt when the Raiders come back home in two weeks to play the Buffalo Bills. Bills Mafia travels well and this will be Buffalo’s first game in Las Vegas with fans allowed to attend. Laulu inactive: In a surprise, defensive tackle Jonah Laulu was a healthy scratch. Second-year defensive tackle J.J. Pegues was active for the first time this season. Laulu was a key rotational player his first two seasons with the Raiders. Laulu played 30 percent of the snaps this season after playing 67 percent last season. So, he is falling out of the playing rotation, at least, for now.

title: Raiders fight hard, but lose to Chiefs
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders are hosting the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday. Here is everything to need to know about the contest: First quarter:The Raiders won the coin toss and deferred. The Las Vegas defense and forced a three and put in a loud Allegiant Stadium. But after a penalty, the Chiefs called a fake […]
full_text: (Photo by Steve Marcus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders are hosting the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday. Here is everything to need to know about the contest: First quarter : The Raiders won the coin toss and deferred. The Las Vegas defense and forced a three and put in a loud Allegiant Stadium. But after a penalty, the Chiefs called a fake punt and converted. Then, the Raiders defense stopped the Chiefs on fourth down, getting the ball at their 49, giving them much better field position had the Chiefs punted. The Raiders quickly struck as Kirk Cousins hit wide-open tight end Ian Thomas for a long touchdown. The place is going crazy. The Chiefs responded with a long touchdown drive to tie the game at 7-7 with just more than two minutes to go. The scoring drive was fueled by a long pass from Patrick Mahomes to Zavier Worthy. Second quarter: . After getting a first down, the Raiders have to punt. After forcing the Chiefs to punt, the Raiders drove down for a 32-yard Matt Gay field goal to take a 10-7 leaf with 3:19 to go in the half. The Chiefs drove down the field but had to settle for a short field goal after Quay Walker sacked Mahomes. 10-10 game with more than a minute to go. The Raiders zipped down the field and Gay converted a 48-yard field goal at the buzzer to give the Raiders a 13-10 lead at halftime. Las Vegas gets the ball to start the second half. Third quarter: The Raiders went down the field and converted a 41-yard field goal to make it 16-10, but the Chiefs were called for a penalty and the Kubiak went for it on fourth and two. The play failed at the Chiefs 18. Taking points off the board hurts. The Chiefs had to punt for this second time this quarter and have nine plays for 18 yards this quarter. After a Raiders’ punt, Kenneth Walker ran 76 yards to the Raiders’ 6 on the final play of the quarter. Fourth quarter: The Chiefs take a 17-13 lead with 14:50 to go. It’s the first time the Raiders have allowed an opponent to score in the fourth quarter this season. Dylan Laube had a 53-yard return on he kickoff to put the Raiders at the Chiefs; 45. A huge boost. On third and 11, Cousins hit Brock Bowers for a huge 21-yard gain. Another Matt Gay field goal. It’s 17-16 Chiefs lead with 11:12 to go. Raiders get ball on their own 10 after punt with 9:36 to go. They made some big plays and rode a another Matt Gay field goal, from 48, to take a 19-17 lead with 4:53 to go. On third and five, the Chiefs hit a big 55-yard pass play down to the Raiders’ 5. The Chiefs scored and missed the two-point conversion. They lead 23-19 with 3:21 to go. Dareke Young fumbled the kickoff. The Chiefs recovered and Walker scored on the next play. Kansas CIty is is up 30-19 with 3:02 to go. The Raiders come back and score on a touchdown pass from Cousins to Bowers, down 30-27 with 1:46 to go after two-point conversion. It’s not over. A bad decision by Mahomes and the Chiefs are punting. Raiders getting ball at their 16 with 47 seconds left. The Raiders got the ball into Chiefs’ terrority, but Cousins was picked off the end the game. Final score: Chiefs 30, Raiders 27 Now that the game is over, let’s take a look at the key aspects: Team records: The Las Vegas Raiders are 3-1. The Kansas City Chiefs are 4-0. What the win/loss means for the Raiders: They are no longer undefeated and they are in second place in the AFC West. Mahomes has never lost in Las Vegas. Turning point of the game: The Raiders fought back, but that two-touchdown late swing by Kansas City was too much to overcome. Injury report: Rookie offensive lineman and special teamer Trey Zuhn hurt his knee in the first quarter. He returned in the second half. Wide receiver Jalen Nailor suffered a concussion in the second quarter and did not return. Running back Ashton Jeanty walked off the field with trainers in the third quarter. He returned in the fourth quarter. What’s next for the Raiders: The Raiders are playing at the 2-2 New England Patriots next Sunday. Kickoff is at 10 a.m. PT. Raiders Week 4: Meet the Chiefs

title: Fins Up, Fins Down | Winners and losers from Miami Dolphins week four loss
summary: The Miami Dolphins fell to the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday by a score of 15-10. While keeping it close only really counts in horseshoes and hand-grenades, as they say, it was Miami’s narrowest defeat of the season through four tough contests. This team is getting better, despite the considerable limitations they are under regarding the […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - OCTOBER 04: Miami Dolphins defensive tackle Zach Sieler (92) tackles Minnesota Vikings running back Demond Claiborne (21) during the second half of the NFL game between the Miami Dolphins and the Minnesota Vikings on October 4th, 2026, at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis, MN. (Photo by Bailey Hillesheim/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Miami Dolphins fell to the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday by a score of 15-10. While keeping it close only really counts in horseshoes and hand-grenades, as they say, it was Miami’s narrowest defeat of the season through four tough contests. This team is getting better, despite the considerable limitations they are under regarding the mammoth amount of dead cap they are currently dealing with, and I don’t think it’s long before they steal a victory to finally get into the win column this year. Of course there are still glaring problems on this team — covering tight ends has been one of those problems. T.J. Hockenson was targeted 13 times yesterday — he caught all 13 passes for a game high 119 yards receiving. Special teams is another — with multiple errors leading to fantastic starting field position for the Vikings on numerous occasions. FINS UP Our Fins Up player from Miami’s week three loss is defensive tackle Zach Sieler. It had been a rough start to the season for Miami’s veteran defender, however, on Sunday against the Vikings, Sieler unleashed his frustrations on Minnesota quarterback Kyler Murray — sacking the diminutive passer twice on the afternoon to account for half of Miami’s four sacks on the day. Sieler hadn’t sacked an opposing quarterback since Week 16 of last season. He finished last season with just 5.5 sacks after having 10 sacks in both the 2023 and 2024 seasons. If he can continue the momentum he began building on Sunday, Miami’s monster in the middle could easily surpass last year’s sack total in short order. FINS DOWN This week’s Fins Down personality is once again special teams coordinator Chris Tabor. Tabor, a respected coach in the National Football League, has now been named in our Fins Down section twice this season — also earning the dubious distinction after week one’s dismal performance from his unit. All afternoon long, Minnesota’s offense was treated to great starting field position due to Miami’s inability to cover kick returns with any competency. Tabor is working with what he has — and what he has is a bunch of young, inexperienced football players trying to make their mark on an undermanned Dolphins squad. However, it is his job to coach them up and maximize their abilities. Unfortunately, he isn’t doing such a great job at that just yet… His next opportunity to show that he should remain on Miami’s staff will come this Sunday when the Dolphins host the Cincinnati Bengals at Hard Rock Stadium.

title: The Good, Bad & Ugly from the Miami Dolphins Week 4 loss to the Minnesota Vikings
summary: The Miami Dolphins traveled to Minnesota to take on Kyler Murray, Aaron Jones Sr., T.J. Hockenson and the rest of the Vikings in week four of the 2026 season. Jeff Hafley’s bunch once again battled hard throughout the entire contest — but ultimately fell to the undefeated Minnesota squad by a score of 15-10. Without […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - OCTOBER 04: Jacob Rodriguez #10 of the Miami Dolphins warms up before kickoff against the Minnesota Vikings during an NFL football game at U.S. Bank Stadium on October 4, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins traveled to Minnesota to take on Kyler Murray, Aaron Jones Sr., T.J. Hockenson and the rest of the Vikings in week four of the 2026 season. Jeff Hafley’s bunch once again battled hard throughout the entire contest — but ultimately fell to the undefeated Minnesota squad by a score of 15-10. Without their top weapon, running back De’Von Achane, and rookie standout receiver, Caleb Douglas, Miami’s offense was stagnant for most of the afternoon. Their defense, however, played their best game all season. The Dolphins may be 0-4 in the standings, but they are getting better each week. It won’t be long until they claim their first victory of the year. But, before we look too far into the future, let’s take a look back at the good, bad and ugly from Miami’s week four loss to the Minnesota Vikings. GOOD Dolphins keep Vikings out of endzone; hold Minnesota offense to nothing but field goals If there was one positive to take away from Sunday’s loss, it was the performance of Miami’s defense. For a team that entered Week 4 searching for answers, holding a 3-0 Minnesota Vikings team without a touchdown is no small accomplishment. Sure, they were without stud receiver Justin Jefferson, but the Dolphins limited Minnesota to just 15 points, forcing kicker Will Reichard to account for every single point on the Vikings’ scoreboard via five field goals. Miami’s defensive front deserves plenty of credit for making life uncomfortable for quarterback Kyler Murray. The Dolphins generated four sacks and consistently applied pressure — preventing Minnesota from finding the rhythm it wanted offensively. Rookie linebacker Jacob Rodriguez finished the tilt with 18 total tackles! Miami’s pass rush was particularly encouraging, with Zach Sieler, Josh Uche and Chop Robinson contributing to a defensive effort that looked considerably more disruptive than what we had seen through the first three weeks — repeatedly finding ways to make Minnesota scrap and claw for its points. The defense gave Miami a legitimate opportunity to steal a road victory. It created stops, generated pressure, and kept the opposing offense out of the end zone for four quarters. Unfortunately, the offense couldn’t return the favor. BAD Miami’s passing offense nearly nonexistent in loss The Dolphins’ passing offense was simply not good enough on Sunday. Malik Willis finished the afternoon completing 9 of 17 passes for just 85 yards, with no touchdowns — accumulating a paltry 67.0 passer rating. Throughout the entire game, Miami struggled to generate anything resembling a legitimate passing attack. That effort is not going to cut it. Miami’s inability to consistently threaten Minnesota through the air allowed the Vikings to remain comfortable defensively. The Dolphins struggled to sustain drives, failed to capitalize on opportunities, and ultimately put far too much responsibility on a defense that was doing everything it could to keep the game within reach. There was a moment when it appeared Miami had finally found the explosive play it desperately needed. Willis connected with rookie wide receiver Chris Bell for what looked like a dazzling 68-yard touchdown. Unfortunately, the play was erased by an illegal-touching penalty after Bell was ruled to have stepped out of bounds (by a toenail) before making the catch. It was a devastating, yet appropriate moment for a Dolphins offense that seemed incapable of getting out of its own way all game. The Dolphins cannot expect to win football games while producing fewer than 200 total yards — they had 198 yards on Sunday. At some point, the offense has to become part of the solution rather than another problem for the coaching staff to address. UGLY Both teams combined for 20 total penalties; 15 in the first half alone If you enjoy watching football games interrupted by yellow flags, Sunday’s first half was practically your Super Bowl. For everyone else, it was an unmitigated nightmare. The Dolphins and Vikings combined for 15 penalties before halftime, turning what should have been a competitive NFL contest into an exercise in frustration. That’s an astonishing amount of self-inflicted nonsense, particularly for two teams attempting to establish offensive rhythm and control the game. False starts, holding calls, and other costly infractions repeatedly disrupted the flow of the afternoon. Drives became longer than necessary, promising situations disappeared, and both teams struggled to establish any kind of consistency. There is a difference between playing aggressively and playing undisciplined football. Sunday’s first half featured far too much of the latter. The final penalty totals told the story. Miami finished with nine penalties for 55 yards, while Minnesota was flagged 11 times for 85 yards — 20 combined penalties for 140 yards over the course of the afternoon. Let’s hope the Dolphins can clean things up on the penalty front when they take on the Cincinnati Bengals next Sunday. __ The Dolphins find themselves sitting at 0-4 to begin the Jeff Hafley era in Miami , but they are showing improvements in certain areas. Do you think a victory is on the horizon for the boys in aqua and orange? Let me know in the comments below or on Twitter at @MBrave13 . Fins up.

(Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins dropped to 0-4 in the 2026 season after losing to the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday. It was an ugly game, filled with penalties, mistakes, and offensive struggles for both teams. It also showed growth from the Dolphins, the league’s youngest team, as they start turning experience into development. Miami is not going to suddenly become an AFC contender, but they are at least showing signs that this rebuild is headed in the right direction. One of the biggest questions Miami must answer this year is the role of quarterback Malik Willis next season and beyond. Is Willis, who signed as a free agent with the Dolphins this offseason, the franchise quarterback who can continue to lead the team for years to come? Is he a short-term rental to start the rebuild, with Miami needing to use an early 2027 draft pick to land their true long-term starter? After the first four games, Miami Herald reporter Barry Jackson says Willis’s play is simply “not good enough.” He does, however, add, “during fleeting moments, tantalizing enough to not totally rule out the possibility that he could become [a franchise quarterback].” There have been moments, some snapshots, where you see the dynamic arm strength, or the escapability, or the high-end athleticism, or the ability to throw on the run — NFL-specific skills that make you resistant to give up totally on the hope of Willis becoming a franchise quarterback. You can’t determine anything definitively after four games, particularly when several of the players around Willis are underperforming or simply not good enough. But we’re still waiting for the game where the Dolphins have reason to emerge saying “we have our guy!” Or at least “I think we do.” A month in, that game hasn’t happened. Jackson went on to break down Willis’s play in the team’s loss to Minnesota and his statistical standing after the first four games this season. title: Dolphins vs. Vikings final score, immediate reactions
summary: The Miami Dolphins faced the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday as part of the NFL’s 2026 Week 4 schedule. The game was ugly, but in a way different than some of Miami’s previous games. This one never felt like a blowout. Instead, it was a sloppy game marred by penalties and mistakes. In the end, however, […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - OCTOBER 4: Malik Washington #6 of the Miami Dolphins is tackled as he carries the ball by Joshua Metellus #44 of the Minnesota Vikings during the second quarter of the game at U.S. Bank Stadium on October 4, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins faced the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday as part of the NFL’s 2026 Week 4 schedule. The game was ugly, but in a way different than some of Miami’s previous games. This one never felt like a blowout. Instead, it was a sloppy game marred by penalties and mistakes. In the end, however, the Dolphins could not get it done. They had a chance in the fourth quarter to take the lead – which would have marked the first time in the season they led a game – but a three-and-out gave the ball back to the Vikings. The defense could not get a stop, letting Minnesota run out the final 5:41 in the game. The Dolphins look much better than they did in Week 1. They look like a team that can compete and keep up with a team that is positioning itself for a playoff run. Miami falls to 0-4, but they are continuing to grow as a team, gain experience, and work their way toward a victory. Teams have to learn not to take the Dolphins for granted because this team is not going to just roll over. Final Score Dolphins 10 – 15 Vikings Snap Winners and Losers Winners Zach Sieler, defensive tackle: The Dolphins’ veteran defensive tackle got the game started the right way for the Dolphins – recording the team’s first sack of the year on the opening snap of the contest. He then recorded another at the end of the first half. Miami would add two more sacks from other players, but it was Sieler who set the tone. He is starting to look the like the dominant player of a couple years ago – and the Dolphins need him to fill that role. Ollie Gordon, running back: The loss of De’Von Achane to an ACL tear was a massive blow to the Dolphins’ offensive system. Gordon took the reins and led the team on Sunday. He ran for 100 yards with a touchdown on just nine carries. Losers Note: “Losers” is not a judgment on the talent or character of any individual. It is simply a categorization of the play in one game – no disrespect is intended or should be inferred. Special teams : The game opened with the Vikings returning the opening kickoff 47 yards. After holding Minnesota to a three-and-out, the Dolphins muffed the punt return and (luckily) fell on the ball in the endzone for a touchback (with a penalty then enforced). On Miami’s following punt, they allowed a 36-yard return, leading to a Vikings field goal. Then on the kickoff, the Dolphins could not field the ball cleanly and were flagged for an illegal formation. Austin Jackson, right tackle: I have said many times that Jackson is a solid right tackle when he is healthy – he is someone you can choose to upgrade when you have the opportunity, but he will be fine if you choose to have him as your starter. I may have to move off that stance. Jackson has been bad against speed rushers this year. He is constantly being pushed backward and off balance. We have seen way too many times – including multiple times today – when Jackson bites on the initial move, then struggles to react when the rusher cuts back the other direction. Jackson is a liability right now. Immediate Reactions Pass rush finally getting home : Miami entered the game as the only team that had not recorded a sack this season. The pass rush showed life against the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 3 but could not finish the job. This week, it took one snap to end the storyline. Defensive tackle Zach Sieler burst through the line on the Vikings’ first snap and brought down quarterback Kyler Murray. The second quarter started with Josh Uche adding a sack of his own on Murray before Sieler picked up his second in the final minute of the half. Chop Robinson got in on the fun in the third quarter to force a Vikings punt. If nothing else, this Dolphins team plays with heart: The 2026 season is not about wins and losses for the Dolphins, but do not tell them that. This team is out there fighting on every snap, playing hard and trying to push through the mistakes and misplays that come with a young team. Penalties, penalties, and penalties: Wow, was that rough. This referee crew was very flag-happy. Some of the penalties were deserved. Some of them were extremely light. It made it hard to watch at times, with every play seeming to have some penalty being called. The good news is, the penalty calls were balanced, with both teams getting flagged throughout the game. The game ended with 20 enforced penalties – nine for Miami, 11 for the Vikings – for 140 yards. Tight end coverage issues : The Dolphins have struggled for years to cover tight ends, and on Sunday, that storyline was back. T.J. Hockenson caught 13 passes for 119 yards. He should have had 120 yards and a touchdown, but he chose to slide down at the one-yard line in the fourth quarter to allow the team to kneel out the clock rather than take an easy score. The Dolphins had no answer to Hockenson, no matter who they had in coverage.

(Photo by Jordon Kelly/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Miami Dolphins and Minnesota Vikings kick off a Week 4 showdown at 4:05 p.m. Eastern this afternoon. Both teams have released their inactive player lists for the game, dropping down to the league-mandated 48-man gameday roster limit. Miami’s inactives include wide receiver Caleb Douglas and edge rusher Robert Beal Jr., both listed as out on Friday’s injury report. Cornerback Marcellas Dial Jr., guard DJ Campbell, tackle Chukwuebuka Godrick, and tight end Justin Joly were also listed as inactive. Joly was active last week for the first time, but returns to an inactive status this week. Miami elevated offensive lineman Mazi Smith and edge rusher Rodney McGraw from the practice squad. The headline for the Vikings is wide receiver Just Jefferson, who was ruled out on Friday with an ankle injury. Also ruled out ahead of the game were cornerback Charles Demmings and punter Brett Thorson. Minnesota elevated punter Johnny Hekker from its practice squad to replace Thorson. The Vikings listed safety Jakobe Thomas, quarterback Max Brosmer, and defensive lineman Elijah Williams as inactive, alongside Jefferson, Demmings, and Thorson.

title: The Phinsider Mailbag: Offense changes following Achane’s injury, young players, and 2027 Draft in Week 4
summary: The Miami Dolphins kickoff against the Minnesota Vikings later today. Before we get to the game, however, we empty The Phinsider Mailbag to answer your questions about the team. Today’s mail bag looks at the changes Miami has to make with the injury to running back De’Von Achane, the young players stepping up, and what […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MD - AUGUST 14: Quinn Ewers #14 of the Miami Dolphins hands the ball off to Jaylen Wright #5 during the first half of a preseason game against the Washington Commanders at Northwest Stadium on August 14, 2026 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins kickoff against the Minnesota Vikings later today. Before we get to the game, however, we empty The Phinsider Mailbag to answer your questions about the team. Today’s mail bag looks at the changes Miami has to make with the injury to running back De’Von Achane, the young players stepping up, and what the team could do in the 2027 NFL Draft. It is time to jump into the mailbag and give you our thoughts. Let us know if you agree or disagree in the comments. MB: I think we’ll see the offense lean on more of a power running game with Ollie Gordon and Jaylen Wright taking over running back duties now that Achane is out for the season due to his ACL tear. I’d like to see Malik Willis continue to use his mobility — and I think more play-action passing could benefit this offense moving forward. KN: I think Wright is the more direct replacement of Achane and will be the primary option out of the backfield, but the position will rely on more of a rotation than they may have with a healthy Achane. Gordon should see plenty of playing time and the coaching staff needs to stick with the hot hand. The short passing game probably becomes more important. And, we might see more reliance on tight end Greg Dulcich as a safety valve. MB: Regarding Miami’s young talent, I think there’s a lot to like. Kadyn Proctor has been really solid since the start of the season. Chris Johnson has had his ups and downs, but there’s a lot to be excited about regarding his game. The rookie receivers — Chris Bell and Caleb Douglas — have both flashed. Will Kacmarek has been a difference-maker as a blocking tight end. I think Jon-Eric Sullivan nailed it with his first draft in Miami. KN: The Dolphins definitely appear to have hit on many of their draft picks – at least in a very small sample size. Rodriguez looks like a star in the making, Douglas and Bell have had moments and will continue to grow. Proctor is settling in and may be a very strong guard for years to come for the Dolphins. Safety Michael Taaffe and Johnson have both flashed in the secondary, fighting through rookie mistakes and adjusting to the speed of the game. As for second-year players, Jordan Phillips has been very good in the middle of the defensive line. Dante Trader Jr. has paired well with Taaffe. And we cannot overlook Jonah Savaiinaea, who has been solid at right guard. MB: The Dolphins could go a lot of different directions if they do land the #1 pick in the 2027 Draft — although I’m still not fully convinced that comes to pass. As far as quarterbacks go, it’s still early, but there isn’t really a suitable one standing out from the pack in the collegiate ranks at the moment. I don’t think Arch comes out next year, but even if he does, he hasn’t played like a #1 overall pick this season at all. Jeremiah Smith is the next “can’t miss” wide receiver prospect from Ohio State — and for good reason. If Miami picks first next April, he should be the pick unless you can trade down a spot or two to a quarterback-hungry team and still get Smith plus a haul of picks to boot. KN: I think it all comes down to Malik Willis. Do the coaches see him as their quarterback for 2027 and beyond? If he plays well enough to earn that trust, then they can do just about anything they want with the pick. I think this quarterback draft class is not going ot be as strong as people thought – in large part because Arch Manning still needs to develop; his last name is not going to be enough to be a true franchise quarterback in the NFL. I think the Dolphins have two options if they land the first overall pick: trade back to a team desperate for a quarterback and add a ton of picks, or make Jeremiah Smith just the fourth wide receiver ever taken with the number one pick. If Miami does not take Smith, or they trade back and see him come off the board before they can make their pick, edge rusher is probably the biggest focal point in the first round.

title: A Couple Doses of Bad News for the Vikings’ Offensive Line
summary: Despite their 4-0 record, the Minnesota Vikings have had their share of issues on offense in the early phases of this 2026 NFL season, and they’ve gotten a couple of doses of bad news on this Monday morning that could, somehow, make things a little bit worse. Both members of the left side of the […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 27: Donovan Jackson #74 of the Minnesota Vikings lines up against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the game at Raymond James Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Despite their 4-0 record, the Minnesota Vikings have had their share of issues on offense in the early phases of this 2026 NFL season, and they’ve gotten a couple of doses of bad news on this Monday morning that could, somehow, make things a little bit worse. Both members of the left side of the Vikings’ offensive line are now dealing with injuries, and one could be out for an extended length of time. We’ll start with left tackle Christian Darrisaw, who had a couple of different issues in Sunday’s victory over the Miami Dolphins. Darrisaw left early in Sunday’s game with a neck issue and was listed as questionable to return, but did come back into the game. Later on, he left the game again and was replaced by Ryan Van Demark, who finished things out in Darrisaw’s spot. In his press conference today, Kevin O’Connell told reporters that Darrisaw is now in the league’s concussion protocol, putting his status for Sunday’s game in New Orleans in doubt. That’s, obviously, something that we’ll be monitoring throughout the course of this week. Unfortunately, the news is much worse for his tag team partner, guard Donovan Jackson. Jackson has a torn meniscus that will require surgery and, in all likelihood, end his sophomore season after just four games. Jackson went out in the first quarter of Sunday’s game and went to the locker room, where he was ruled out for the afternoon relatively quickly. He was replaced by Joe Huber at the left guard spot. Jackson, the Vikings’ first-round pick in the 2025 NFL Draft, had really come on strong in the early portion of this season, and his absence is definitely one that is going to be felt for a Vikings’ offense that is already having problems getting points on the board. The week is already not off to a great start on the injury front for a Vikings team that is already wondering about Justin Jefferson’s status as they head into their Week 5 matchup in New Orleans. We’ll have more news on Christian Darrisaw’s status as the injury reports come out through the week, and here’s hoping that Donovan Jackson’s upcoming surgery is a successful one and he comes back fully ready to go for 2027.

title: Vikings Week 4 Stock Market Report
summary: The Minnesota Vikings improved to 4-0 after beating the Miami Dolphins 15-10 with the same successful but frustrating formula: top notch defense and special teams and just good enough offense. It came against one of the worst teams in the league, so the fact that the win wasn’t more decisive was disappointing, especially at home. […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - OCTOBER 04: Minnesota Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson (87) celebrates getting a first down during the second half of the NFL game between the Miami Dolphins and the Minnesota Vikings on October 4th, 2026, at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis, MN. (Photo by Bailey Hillesheim/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings improved to 4-0 after beating the Miami Dolphins 15-10 with the same successful but frustrating formula: top notch defense and special teams and just good enough offense. It came against one of the worst teams in the league, so the fact that the win wasn’t more decisive was disappointing, especially at home. But the Vikings still achieved the key weekly objective while Justin Jefferson recovered from his ankle injury. The Vikings offense never really threatened to score a touchdown until the end of the game, when TJ Hockenson opted to go down on his own accord on the 2 yard line so the Vikings could take the victory formation and secure the win rather than score a touchdown and give the Dolphins maybe a 1% chance of a comeback victory. That fits with Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell’s new found philosophy of focusing on doing what it takes to get the win and not worry about stats. The Vikings offense had its best outing in terms of total yards (336) and first downs (20), but went 0-3 in the red zone including Hockenson’s aforementioned slide to allow the Vikings offense to run out the clock in victory formation. But they did not turnover the ball either, allowing the Vikings to win the turnover battle which 90% of the time leads to a Vikings victory in the KOC era. And so it was. Stock Up T.J. Hockenson . Hockenson had what amounted to a post-knee-injury breakout game. He had 13 receptions (tying a career high) on 13 targets for 119 yards and looked more dialed in and dynamic than he has for a couple years. A rejuvenated Hockenson is the perfect underneath complement to Addison and Jefferson down the field and a way for Kyler Murray and the Vikings offense to win when the opposing defense is focused on taking away the deeper part of the field. Kyler Murray. He wasn’t outstanding by any means, and sacks continue to be a problem, but he had his most productive outing as a passer with the Vikings while avoiding turnovers or turnover-worthy plays. He adapted to the Dolphins playing a lot of two high safety coverages (which they hadn’t previously this season) to take away deeper strikes to Jordan Addison by targeting Hockenson underneath. He finished 27/37 (73%) for 247 yards and a 90.7 passer rating. His adjusted completion percentage (accuracy) was 90.6% according to PFF, which is elite. It appeared that there were not receivers open downfield on several of Murray’s dropbacks, which led to four throwaways. Dallas Turner. He led the charge against Malik Willis, racking up 2 sacks on 5 pressures. He also forced the only turnover of the game, which Blake Cashman recovered, and had a tackle-for-loss as well in run defense. Will Reichard. Perfect once again, going 5-5 on field goal attempts and accounting for all of the Vikings points. He has now made 31 straight field goals without a miss, the longest active streak in the league. He also landed a couple kickoffs in the landing zone in such a way that it caused the Dolphins to muff the return on two occasions. Myles Price. He had 121 yards on five kick/punt returns, averaging 35 yards per kickoff return an 17 per punt return, both excellent numbers. Aaron Jones. He had 94 yards on 20 carries (4.7 ypc) which helped move the chains on many occasions. He also had three explosive (10+ yard) carries. Stock Down Jauan Jennings. He played all but four snaps on offense and had one reception for eight yards. His blocking wasn’t great either. Harrison Smith. His tackling effort on the two biggest Dolphins plays (one negated by penalty) left much to be desired. Johnny Hekker. He shanked a couple punts later in the game that gave the Dolphins significantly better starting field position. Buy The Vikings ability to play championship football consistently on defense and special teams over the first four games. Sell The Vikings ability to win a championship without the offense showing significant improvement. Buy The Vikings winning games over racking up stats. Sell The rise in Vikings penalties. After having just 3 penalties in each of their first two games, the Vikings have committed 20 penalties over their last two games. Follow me on X/Bluesky @wludford

title: Offense Disappears Again, But Vikings Still Hold Off Dolphins
summary: For the second time in three weeks, the Minnesota Vikings did not manage to score an offensive touchdown. And for the fourth time in four weeks, the Minnesota Vikings did enough to come out of their game with a victory. Behind five Will Reichard field goals and a career-high 13 catches from T.J. Hockenson, as […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - OCTOBER 04: T.J. Hockenson #87 of the Minnesota Vikings celebrates against the Miami Dolphins in the second quarter at U.S. Bank Stadium on October 04, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images For the second time in three weeks, the Minnesota Vikings did not manage to score an offensive touchdown. And for the fourth time in four weeks, the Minnesota Vikings did enough to come out of their game with a victory. Behind five Will Reichard field goals and a career-high 13 catches from T.J. Hockenson, as well as yet another dominating defensive performance, the Minnesota Vikings managed to hold off a very game Miami Dolphins team at U.S. Bank Stadium on Sunday afternoon, winning by a score of 15-10 to push their record to 4-0 on the 2026 NFL season. The Vikings won the opening coin toss and elected to receive, and Myles Price picked up right where he left off after being named the Special Teams Player of the Week for Week 3, taking the opening kickoff out to near midfield. But the Vikings did nothing with it, as the team’s first play from scrimmage resulted in the first sack of the year for the Miami defense, as Kyler Murray was taken down by Zach Sieler for an 8-yard loss. The Vikings punted the ball away, and the return was muffed by the Dolphins’ returner into the end zone for a touchback. After a penalty, the Dolphins started their first possession at their own 10-yard line. The Dolphins managed to pick up one first down on their first possession, but eventually wound up punting it away. That meant Price got another chance with the ball, and he returned the punt 36 yards to set the Vikings up in Miami territory at the 38-yard line. But the Vikings’ offense couldn’t do much with it after one first down, as a couple of penalties pushed them backward. Of course, that meant they could call on Will Reichard, who did what he usually does and drilled a 47-yard field goal to give the Vikings an early lead, 3-0, with just under eight minutes remaining in the first quarter. Miami put together a fairly solid drive on their next possession, pushing themselves into Minnesota territory before having their drive ended by a sack from Dallas Turner, a takedown that gave him 4.5 on the young season. That gave the Vikings the ball at their own 21-yard line to start their next drive. The penalty bug struck the Vikings again as a 21-yard gain from Murray to Jordan Addison was negated by a penalty on rookie Caleb Tiernan, and the Dolphins officially ended the drive by sacking Murray again, this one coming from Josh Uche. The Vikings dodged a major bullet on the Dolphins’ next possession, as Willis scrambled around and avoided enough Vikings defenders to get a pass away to rookie Chris Bell, who ran away from the defense for what appeared to be a 68-yard score. However, the officials ruled that Bell had stepped out of bounds prior to catching the pass, making his reception illegal and taking the points off the board, forcing Miami to punt the ball away. Minnesota moved the ball into Miami territory on their next possession, almost despite themselves thanks to a couple more offensive penalties. But, as is their wont, the Vikings’ offense stalled again after Murray was nearly sacked a third time, and again Will Reichard came on to add points for the Vikings. He connected on a 50-yard field goal to extend the Minnesota lead to 6-0 with seven minutes left before halftime. The Dolphins’ next drive started with a penalty, as Willis scrambled and rookie Domonique Orange was called for a late hit for tackling him out of bounds, even though it appeared the hit was initiated in the field of play. That put the Dolphins quickly near midfield, but things quickly went the Vikings’ way thanks to Turner. He got pressure on Willis, and when Willis attempted to throw the ball, his hand hit Turner’s helmet and jarred the ball loose. The initial ruling on the field was an incomplete pass, but the Vikings challenged the call, and it was reversed because the loose ball was clearly recovered by Blake Cashman. That meant the Vikings got the football back at midfield on the turnover. Unfortunately, the Vikings’ offense did nothing with the turnover, as they quickly went three-and-out and got just a 20-yard punt from Johnny Hekker, meaning the turnover didn’t hurt the Dolphins much at all. The Dolphins returned the favor with a three-and-out of their own, and the Vikings got the ball to midfield at the two-minute warning. Murray then found T.J. Hockenson to get the Vikings down to the Miami 26-yard line, but then took another sack from Sieler. Passes to Tai Felton and Hockenson put the Vikings at the Miami 15 with ten seconds left, and the Vikings took their last timeout. The final play of the half was, once again, Will Reichard adding to the Minnesota lead, as he connected from 33 yards out to make it 9-0 heading into the locker room. Miami got the football to start the second half, and they got their biggest play of the afternoon in short order as Ollie Gordon took a handoff from Willis and rumbled 53 yards to the Minnesota 11-yard line to put Miami into the red zone for the first time on the day. After that, the Vikings’ defense got their bearings back and forced the Dolphins to settle for a 27-yard field goal from Riley Patterson for their first points of the day, cutting the Minnesota lead to 9-3. The Vikings answered with a fairly solid drive, as they mixed some nice runs from Aaron Jones with some connections between Murray and Hockenson to push into Miami territory. Once they got near the 20, however, penalties started to bite them again as Jauan Jennings got called for offensive pass interference. The drive stalled out, which gave another opportunity to Reichard, and he once again made the most of it, connecting from 41 yards out to push the lead back to nine points at 12-3. Miami quickly went three-and-out on their next possession, and the Vikings responded with a three-and-out of their own that saw Murray get sacked for the fourth time on the afternoon, this time by Chop Robinson. The Dolphins then put together their best offensive possession of the day, as Willis found Malik Washington for a couple of connections to get the Dolphins into the red zone, and Ollie Gordon then took a handoff and went into the end zone practically untouched for a 13-yard score to make it 12-10 right at the end of the third quarter. The Vikings then went on a lengthy drive that encompassed 15 plays, but only traveled 60 yards and took over eight minutes off the clock. In the end, however, the result was the same. . .another field goal from Will Reichard. This one came from 29 yards out and increased the Minnesota lead to 15-10 with just over six minutes remaining in regulation. After the Vikings forced the Dolphins to punt it away, the Minnesota offense managed to put together another long drive. Minnesota forced the Dolphins to burn their timeouts, and on a 3rd-and-5 play from the Miami 10-yard line, Murray found Hockenson near the goal line. Rather than going into the end zone, Hockenson slid down in bounds at the 1-yard line at the two-minute warning. With no timeouts left for Miami, all the Vikings had to do was kneel out the victory, and that’s what they did. Hockenson wound up having a huge day with Justin Jefferson out of the lineup. He tied a career high with 13 catches, picking up 119 yards. Jordan Addison and Aaron Jones each caught four passes on the day. Murray wound up completing 27-of-37 passes for 247 yards. For the second time in their last three games, the Vikings did not score an offensive touchdown. It’s obviously not sustainable, but it was effective enough to get the Vikings’ record to 4-0 on the 2026 NFL season. At some point, they’ll have to get the offense moving, but given that the Vikings did not have star wide receiver Justin Jefferson in this one, they did a fairly solid job coming out of this one with a victory.…

title: Mack Hollins injury set to open door for more Efton Chism III
summary: The New England Patriots saw wide receiver Mack Hollins depart Sunday’s game early with a calf injury.  While the Patriots await more information to determine the severity of the injury, head coach Mike Vrabel is preparing to potentially be without the veteran in the short term. “I think we’ll probably know more here in a […]
full_text: The New England Patriots saw wide receiver Mack Hollins depart Sunday’s game early with a calf injury. While the Patriots await more information to determine the severity of the injury, head coach Mike Vrabel is preparing to potentially be without the veteran in the short term. “I think we’ll probably know more here in a little bit,” Vrabel said Monday morning. “I don’t know if he’ll be able to practice here for a couple days. But again, I don’t have every detail. I’ll get in there with [the training staff] afterwards and kinda see where we are, and make sure we have guys that are ready to go and everybody is preparing as a starter. We know the energy that Mack brings. The next guy has to be ready to go.” In Hollins’ absence Sunday, wide receiver Efton Chism III played a season-high 34 offensive snaps in relief. Chism made the most of the opportunity, hauling in two catches for 42 yards and the game-winning touchdown. The performance could set Chism up for a larger role moving forward. “Of course. That’s what happens. Guys continue to take advantage of their opportunities, they get more opportunities,” Vrabel said. “We’ve been finding ways to work Chiz in there previously. It’s a balance, but certainly did a lot of things well and I know that he’ll continue to do things well for us and continue to know a bunch of different spots.” The Patriots are already without A.J. Brown in the wide receiver room, as the veteran remains on injured reserve through at least next week. Hollins’ absence would leave just Romeo Doubs, DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams, and Chism on the active roster. Undrafted rookies Cameron Dorner and Kyle Dixon, in addition to Chandler Brayboy, are currently on the practice squad. Vrabel did not rule out the Patriots searching for external additions at the position. “Sure. Anybody that can help us, we’ll go exploring here shortly,” Vrabel said.

title: Patriots vs. Bills: Fan observations from Week 4 win
summary: Covering the NFL, in any capacity, is like being a weatherman. You don’t know a damn thing and you’re wrong more often than you’re right. But since nobody else knows anything either, you get a pass each and every week. The New England Patriots, who have been struggling all season and were without their best […]
full_text: Covering the NFL, in any capacity, is like being a weatherman. You don’t know a damn thing and you’re wrong more often than you’re right. But since nobody else knows anything either, you get a pass each and every week. The New England Patriots, who have been struggling all season and were without their best cornerback and best interior linemen on both sides of the ball, took the best team in the AFC to the wire yesterday in a game that should give us all a lot of optimism going forward. It’s kind of fitting that Buffalo’s first-ever loss in their new stadium came at the hands of the Patriots, the team that won the most games ever at the old Bills stadium. I feel like everyone, yours truly included, had the Patriots sitting at 2-2 through four weeks. Lo and behold, here we find ourselves. Did I think New England would get slapped around by Jacksonville only to beat Buffalo on the road? Of course not. But that’s why we watch this nonsensical sport. If there’s a larger chasm that separates a 2-2 team from a 1-3 team, I don’t know what it is. It’s technically only one game, but teams sitting at 1-3 this morning are taking a long, unshaven, hungover look in the mirror right now, while the 2-2 teams are motivated to position themselves for a strong October. So, this game meant more than just getting a divisional win on the road, for a lot of reasons. But before I get into why that is, I’ll own my blatant sports fan hypocrisy by admitting that I would have spin-zoned the hell out of this game if Buffalo had won it. Drake Maye looked more poised. They hung with one of the best teams in the AFC. Lots to build on. Maybe they win if everyone is healthy. It’s a long season. This was the best the team has looked. We all know the platitudes. Luckily, though, I don’t have to do any of that, as New England outcoached and outplayed Buffalo to find themselves half a game out of first place in the AFC East. And this iteration of the Bills has never, at any point, defeated a defending AFC Champion. Let’s start with the offense, because that has been the team’s biggest weakness thus far. Sure, Maye had a fumble and a pick, but in a nice change of pace neither of them were on him. He probably should have felt the pressure on the strip sack and tucked the ball instead, but that was a strong pass rush against a new member of the offensive line. For the most part, Maye was decisive, poised, and clutch when he needed to be. I also have to point out that if T.J. Parker’s hands had been any more illegally to the face on that strip sack, he would have found himself on a split screen on MSNBC at some point this week being asked some questions. He also outrushed Josh Allen by 50 yards, which I didn’t expect (more on Allen’s legs and the defensive strategy surrounding that in a minute). And all of his runs were the right kind: receivers were covered, or the protection broke down, so he tucked and ran. He also got out of bounds or went right to the ground in the face of contact, which was even more enjoyable than watching him scramble. As for his leading receivers, it was a nice mix of old and new. Hunter Henry finally got involved in the passing game, and Romeo Doubs is getting more and more comfortable by the week. The bobble-to-interception wasn’t the best look for him, and he seems good for one drop per game. But if he can make up for it with two scores per game, I’ll certainly allow it. It’s wild to me how excited I was about the New England wide receiver room coming into this season. Brown, Doubs, Boutte, Douglas, Hollins, Chism, Williams… there just seemed to be so many weapons. Then Brown got hurt right away, Boutte got traded, Williams continues to be an absolute ghost, and a guy who should be thriving as WR4 was somehow pulling WR1 duty. And then that guy goes down too. “Man, if Mack Hollins can’t play for an extended period, this offense is really screwed” 100% went through my head yesterday. Football. What a ride! But in Hollins’s absence, seven different Patriots notched at least one reception. And Kyle Williams got two whole targets! I don’t want to get into too much turd in the punchbowlery in the wake of a big win. But what in the name of Tebow do the Patriots have to do to take a receiver early in the draft and have that receiver work out? And while I appreciate the universe balancing things out by consistently gifting the team with short, explosive, white slot receivers in the later rounds or through free agency, it would be nice if Kyle Williams could join the likes of Deion Branch and… um… Deion Branch… instead of Bethel Johnson, Chad Jackson, Brandon Tate, Taylor Price, Aaron Dobson, N’Keal Harry, Tyquan Thornton, and Ja’Lynn Polk. That said… I don’t want to pull the plug on Kyle Williams yet. He still has value and a skillset that could make him a strong contributor. But I also kind of feel like I’m at the point where, from this moment forward, if the Pats are thinking about targeting a WR in the draft, instead they should just trade that draft pick for a receiver who has already proven that he can produce at the NFL level. Speaking of producing… poor Tyquan Thornton. He had carved himself out a nice role in that Chiefs offense, which is a point in favor of the “it ain’t the player, it’s New England’s development” side of things. Hopefully that injury looks a lot worse than it is and he’ll be back on the field before too long. OK, enough with the negativity. One receiver being nonexistent just opened the door for the latest New England folk hero, Efton Chism III, who has made the catch of the year so far. This was shortly after high-pointing a crosser for a 19-yard gain to move the ball into Bills territory. There wasn’t anything complicated about the route; it looked like a simple out-and-up. Maye had to throw it a little earlier than he probably would have liked as the pressure came around the left side, and the coverage was perfect. Chism just made an absolutely absurd catch, and the legend was born. I was a little surprised to see that New England rushed for 143 yards yesterday. But then you realize that it’s less than 100 without Maye’s scrambles, and since TreVeyon Henderson seems to eat primarily off of long runs, it makes a lot more sense. Which means that this game was more or less won on the shoulders of the QB who had really been struggling through three weeks. And if he had laid another huge egg yesterday, there would be some conversations happening right now. Of that, I have no doubt. But this whole thing was just what everyone needed. There’s still a ton to clean up. This game could have gotten out of hand late in the first half with all the shenanigans that went down. But I’d rather need to clean up than start thinking about cleaning house. Speaking of cleaning house, the cupboard was pretty bare for the Patriots defense, who were without both Christians and a wildly depleted LB corp. They still held Allen to four yards rushing and should have recorded a safety. Seriously, what the hell was that? I guess a random, no-look throw to nobody while both still in the pocket in the end zone doesn’t meet the standards for grounding somehow. The best part about that play, though, was Gabe Jacas, who steamrolled Dion Dawkins and created immediate pressure. He’s still raw, but given the serious questions he was raising for everyone during the preseason, Jacas has been a beast. My only real gripe with the defense is that, at times, they seemed so concerned with Allen running that they broke into a lot of soft zone, which gave Allen plenty to choose from. But it was mostly effective, so hard to get too mad. I absolutely love it when the defense, any defense, celebrates an open receiver dropping a pass. As someone who has taken more than my fair share of credit for group projects in which I did zero work, it resonates with me on a personal level. I still remember being in 10th grade and, having done exactly nothing for our group report on FDR’s New Deal,…

title: Mike Vrabel fires back at Bills safety after postgame rant
summary: If you ask C.J. Gardner-Johnson, the better team lost during Sunday’s New England Patriots game against the Buffalo Bills. It was one of several dubious claims the Bills safety made in the postgame locker room following his team’s 29-26 defeat. Gardner-Johnson complained about the Patriots’ apparent lack of confidence, about their offensive output, and about […]
full_text: If you ask C.J. Gardner-Johnson, the better team lost during Sunday’s New England Patriots game against the Buffalo Bills. It was one of several dubious claims the Bills safety made in the postgame locker room following his team’s 29-26 defeat. Gardner-Johnson complained about the Patriots’ apparent lack of confidence, about their offensive output, and about the game-winning touchdown being scored by an apparent practice squad player who won’t be able to repeat that feat any time soon. For New England head coach Mike Vrabel, that final part was particularly interesting. “For a guy who’s been on eight teams in four years, I guess he knows the drill,” Vrabel said about the Bills defender during an appearance on WEEI’s The Greg Hill Show on Monday. As with the totality of Gardner-Johnson’s statements — the Patriots outperformed Buffalo by multiple statistical metrics — there also was no truth to the practice squad player claim. The pass catcher in question, after all, was second-year wide receiver Efton Chism, who has been on New England’s active since joining the organization as an undrafted free agent in 2025. While Chism only saw extended playing time after fellow wideout Mack Hollins exited with a calf injury, he made the most of his opportunity. The sophomore caught two passes for 42 yards on the Patriots’ game-winning drive, including the 23-yard touchdown on third down to cap it off. For Vrabel, that was more noteworthy than any trash talk coming out of Buffalo. “Nobody works harder,” he said about Chism. “You love to see players take advantage of opportunities and help the team win. He is very well-respected. He practices — on show team, he takes a million reps. Nobody runs more miles or yards or whatever we track than Chiz.” With Hollins’ injury status unclear as of right now, and with A.J. Brown ineligible to return from injured reserve until next week, Chism might find himself playing more snaps on offense this week against the Las Vegas Raiders. If so, there is a chance he will put more big plays on tape for Gardner-Johnson and the Bills defense to study ahead of the rematch in early December.
