title: Real Drake Maye shines through in Patriots’ win over Bills
summary: There was talk about a shoulder injury. There was talk about a rift with head coach Mike Vrabel. There even were comparisons with Mac Jones. And yet, when he left the field at Highmark Stadium on Sunday, all the speculation and exaggeration surrounding Drake Maye was suddenly a thing of the past. At least for […]
full_text: There was talk about a shoulder injury . There was talk about a rift with head coach Mike Vrabel . There even were comparisons with Mac Jones . And yet, when he left the field at Highmark Stadium on Sunday, all the speculation and exaggeration surrounding Drake Maye was suddenly a thing of the past. At least for one game, the New England Patriots’ third-year quarterback looked like the MVP candidate again that he was just last season. Maye had just led his team to a 29-26 upset win over the previously-unbeaten Buffalo Bills, and doing so in style. He was efficient as a passer, productive as a runner, and most importantly avoided the back-breaking mistakes that cost the Patriots in their previous losses to the Seahawks and Jaguars. He looked like vintage Drake Maye. “I think it’s relieving a little bit,” the 24-year-old said during his postgame press conference. Entering 2026 off a Super Bowl berth and one of the best individual seasons in Patriots franchise history — a history, mind you, dominated by the greatest quarterback of all time — Maye and the team had high expectations. The first three games, however, tempered those expectations. Maye looked insecure, made questionable decisions, and was one of the least effective QBs in the NFL. In those three games, two of them losses, the turned the ball over a league-worst seven times. But while he did add two more giveaways to his tally on Sunday in Orchard Park, his performance as a whole was much more in line with the pre-season expectation. Not only did he go toe-to-toe with one of the NFL’s best quarterbacks, Josh Allen, he statistically out-performed his Bills counterpart. Welcome back, good Drake Maye. — Bernd Buchmasser (@berndbuchmasser.bsky.social) 2026-10-05T10:43:28.202Z Maye looked particularly good during the Patriots’ game-winning drive in the late fourth quarter. Taking possession of the ball down five points with 4:27 left on the clock, he completed passes to Hunter Henry, Romeo Doubs and Efton Chism before again connecting with Chism on a 23-yard touchdown; he also added two more points on a subsequent conversion to Rhamondre Stevenson. In total, Maye went 4-for-7 for 68 yards and a touchdown on the final possession. “We definitely got to build off it,” he said after the game. “I’m just proud of the way the guys fought. Nobody blinked when we were over there on the sideline and they scored and went up 26-21. We just did what we do and just thankful for those guys stepping up. Everybody’s stepping up.” For his head coach, Maye’s performance on Sunday did not come as a surprise even after his slow start to the season. “He’s extremely prepared and focused and had a good week of practice for the most part,” Mike Vrabel said. “I thought that there was some protection. I thought he was decisive.” There was a lot to feel good about for the Patriots coming out of Sunday’s game. But despite playing his best football of the season in a hostile environment and without two of his top targets — A.J. Brown (IR), Mack Hollins (third-quarter calf injury) — Maye was not entirely happy with the performance on Sunday. Besides the two turnovers, he lamented missed opportunities to close out the game sooner than the late fourth quarter. “We still have some work left out there. We left our defense in some bad positions. We got the ball back twice in that third quarter, where we got a chance to really put it on them,” he said. “You’re 1-2, we come to this game and just earned a second win, 2-2. You can’t hang your hat. This is the league, and I know I have to play better and still left some stuff out there today. So, we have to build on it and know that this isn’t a point in the season where you can end the season on this. You have to get back and keep going.”
author: Bernd Buchmasser

title: Craig Woodson, Patriots defense step up in upset win over Bills
summary: The New England Patriots bounced back on Sunday. And while it was Drake Maye’s late 73-yard fourth-quarter drive that resulted in the game-winning touchdown to Efton Chism III, putting New England ahead in its Week 4 upset on the road against the previously unbeaten Buffalo Bills, its defense helped seal the victory nearing the final […]
full_text: The New England Patriots bounced back on Sunday. And while it was Drake Maye’s late 73-yard fourth-quarter drive that resulted in the game-winning touchdown to Efton Chism III, putting New England ahead in its Week 4 upset on the road against the previously unbeaten Buffalo Bills , its defense helped seal the victory nearing the final minute of regulation. On 2nd-and-6 from his own 40-yard line, Josh Allen stiff-armed his way out of a would-have-been Dre’Mont Jones sack before uncorking a deep ball down the left sideline towards his receiver Joshua Palmer. But second-year safety Craig Woodson cut in front of Palmer and high-pointed the ball, intercepting Allen. That turnover put the Patriots’ offense back on the field, where Maye found Hunter Henry for a first down to end the contest. However, earlier in the quarter, Buffalo wide receiver Keon Coleman scored the Bills’ go-ahead touchdown, slipping past Woodson and cornerback Charles Woods by running a post on his way to the end zone. “I trust Craig (Woodson) with everything we got,” head coach Mike Vrabel said. “He’s very mature, and I just love his demeanor. I love the way that he prepares, and that’s what happens. We choose our ability to respond and how we’re going to do it. I’m sure he was disappointed in the play before, and [he] came back to make a huge play to seal [the game]. “So all the credit to him, and being able to understand that the game isn’t over, and we’re going to come back and we’re going to need [him].” Woodson was just one player from an entire defensive unit that stepped up amidst crucial injuries, leaving key players absent from the matchup. Though outside linebacker Dre’Mont Jones returned, both standouts Christian Gonzalez and Christian Barmore sat out. After New England regained its advantage 21-17 shortly after halftime, the offense grew stagnant, with its next three drives resulting in punts through half of the final frame. Still, it took Buffalo four offensive series to find Coleman in the end zone, punting twice and only notching a field goal on its third drive. Though allowing 26 points isn’t labeled a “shut down” defensive performance, it could be considered as such against a Bills offense that led the league averaging 33.7 points per game entering the divisional matchup. Buffalo’s production also includes a statistically top-five rushing offense. Even though their run defense bent a little more in the second half, the Patriots held that unit 64 yards below its weekly average and running back James Cook to just 16 yards on the ground in the first half. “I thought we were excellent against the run … So, [I’m] extremely proud of the way the defensive staff, but most importantly, the players,” Vrabel said. “All the credit goes to those guys for being out there.” With players like recent practice squad elevation Kindle Vildor contributing and making appearances on the field that afternoon, Woodson described the team’s approach as a “next-man-up mentality” before adding that the group was “ready today.” “Everyone has to believe they are going to be the answer for why we’re going to get back in this thing,” Vrabel said of his messaging heading into the contest. “… That’s what the message will continue to be … You have to prepare every week as a starter, and you have to believe that you are the reason. Whether you make one play or 15 plays, that you’re the reason we’re going to win.” New England, heading into Highmark Stadium 1-2 on the season, now adds another tally to the win column, placing itself just one game behind the Bills in the conference standings. “We knew that we were in a little bit of a storm when it came to our record, losing games and especially how we last [to the Jacksonville Jaguars],” Woodson said. “I think we all just wanted to rally together … We know we can go make plays, and that was the only thing we told each other, like, ‘Go be you out there and go make a play.’ We already put it on tape before. Just go do it again, and that’s what happened today.”
author: Andrew Guindon

title: 10 things we learned from Patriots vs. Bills
summary: The New England Patriots celebrated a massive win in Buffalo on Sunday, beating their division rivals 29-26 and improving to 2-2 on the year. It’s still early and a lot will happen, but this one victory may have just saved their season. Let’s get into the lessons we learned from the game. This is a […]
full_text: The New England Patriots celebrated a massive win in Buffalo on Sunday, beating their division rivals 29-26 and improving to 2-2 on the year. It’s still early and a lot will happen, but this one victory may have just saved their season. Let’s get into the lessons we learned from the game. This is a mentally tough team The Patriots heard all the talk this week, they couldn’t have missed it. People say they were done. They said Drake Maye was broken. They claimed that there was a rift between him and Mike Vrabel . They said the team hated Vrabel. They had the Patriots ranked 31st in the league. None of it mattered. When the Patriots’ backs were against the wall, they responded with a huge win in Buffalo — becoming the first road win to celebrate a victory at the new Highmark Stadium. From the 97-yard drive to start the game to the fourth-quarter drive to win it, the Patriots competed their posteriors off, and won despite four of their best players — CB Christian Gonzalez, DT Christian Barmore, WR A.J. Brown, RG Mike Onwenu — being out with injury. In doing so, they might have pulled their season back from the brink of collapse. A 2-2 record looks a lot better than 1-3, and with a win over the Bills, and only being one game behind them now, they have a shot at competing for the division once again. There is a long way to go, as mentioned above, but this win last year served as a springboard for the team. Maybe it does the same this season. Drake Maye answers the critics Of all the people who were criticized this week, no one was criticized harder than Drake Maye. For him to play the way he did on Sunday was therefore impressive. It wasn’t perfect, and I didn’t like the fumble just outside the red zone, but he played his best game of the season and did it all for the team, running for 54 yards as well as passing for 269 and three touchdowns. If Maye continues to play the way he did in Buffalo on Sunday, the critics are not going to have much to say. In fact, if he plays this way every week, he’ll be back in the MVP conversation in no time. EF-Yeah Chism When Mack Hollins went down with an injury in the third quarter, the Patriots were left with a hole on their wide receiver depth chart. Efton Chism stepped up to fill that hole, and he made two monstrous catches on the final drive, the second one being a one-handed touchdown on third down that won the Patriots the game. The severity of Hollins’ injury remains to be seen, and it will be seen how effective Chism can be if asked to step into his role on a full-time basis. At least on Sunday, however, the second-year wideout stepped up when the Patriots desperately needed him to. It was exciting to see, and potentially a sign of good things to come from him. Injuries are piling up Speaking of guys who are injured, the depth at the receiver position is being tested with Hollins now banged-up as well. Add the fact that A.J. Brown is also not eligible to return until Week 6 against the Jets, and the team might have to rely on the likes of Efton Chism and Kyle Williams — or rookie tight end Eli Raridon — at a higher rate than normal. Young edges continue to impress The Patriots are banged up along the defensive line right now, but they have gotten some solid play out of their two young edge defenders, Elijah Ponder and Gabe Jacas. Both of them showed some real flash and power, and they constantly seem to be around the ball making plays. Jacas helped force what could have been a safety, while Ponder had a sack and a fumble recovery. They are not blue-chip players at this current moment, but they both look to be competent starters, and that’s huge considering that Ponder was a UDFA last season and Jacas looked awful in camp and preseason. The Patriots needed them to play well with Harold Landry out and will continue to count on them until the team captain is able to return from the PUP list. Romeo Doubs has a good day, but leaves more to be desired Since we are talking about the receivers, let’s talk about the guy who has been New England’s default WR1 since A.J. Brown went down, Romeo Doubs. On the one hand, he had two touchdowns and two fourth-down conversions on Sunday; on the other, he dropped a pass that ended up being an interception that gifted the Bills three points before the end of the half. The throw was not a perfect one by Drake Maye, but you would still like to see a $68 million receiver bring it down. Doubs needs to continue to improve if the Patriots are going to continue to win games with A.J. Brown on IR and Mack Hollins’ outlook unclear, but he took a step in the right direction on Sunday. In total, he finished with six receptions for 58 yards and those two TDs. Defensive masterclass on Josh Allen Josh Allen is one of, if not the very best quarterback in the NFL. He had an okay day throwing the ball on Sunday, but the Patriots were able to almost completely shut him down as a ball-carrier. He did have a tush push touchdown, but finished with only 4 rushing yards for the day. Every time he broke the pocket or stepped up, there were multiple guys waiting for him to stop him from running. The Patriots also did a nice job not leaving guys open while doing that, honing in on the “second play” element that makes Allen such a dangerous player. They made it difficult for the Bills to generate explosive plays — at least when they weren’t throwing to Keon Coleman — and forced them to string together long drives to score. Considering the injuries the Patriots were dealing with, it was an impressive performance. The Patriots look better running the ball, but still can’t run with big personnel The Patriots want to establish the run, and they brought in a bunch of players this offseason to help them do just that. They have already lost Julian Hill for the season, and Reggie Gilliam has been banged up as well, but you would still like the Patriots be able to run the ball more effectively especially out of heavy personnel. The good news is that the Patriots were able to run fairly efficiently out of lighter packages. The bad news is that they still can’t line up and run it down your throat like they would seemingly like to do. They need to simply accept what they are, and what injuries to multiple players, including Mike Onwenu, have made them. That might mean that they are going to have to pass the ball more, and run out of some lighter formations, but based on what we saw Wednesday, that is perfectly fine and might be a recipe for success for this team. Not a banner day for officiating It was far from a banner day for the refs around the league, with multiple bizarre interactions between players and coaches and the officials. One of those came in the Patriots game. Seemingly without warning, Mike Vrabel was hit with an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty for arguing over a ticky-tack holding call on Marcus Jones. In addition, the holding call on Will Campbell was suspect as well, and that the Bills had worse calls that were missed, including an egregious hands-to-the-face flag that should have been thrown on the Drake Maye strip sack. Based on what we saw around the league, the officiating should be called into question, and the way that some of them have been acting leaves quite a bit to be desired. Raiders up next, in the throwbacks The Patriots are hoping to build off of the momentum of their win in Buffalo next week, when they welcome the Las Vegas Raiders to Gillette Stadium. The Raiders are coming off a season where they were the worst team in the league, but are playing very well right now and look like they are for real. They are 3-1 and almost pulled off the upset of the Chiefs on Sunday. This looked to be an easy win when the schedule came out in May, but it’s not looking so easy anymore. The Patriots are going to look good in their red throwback jerseys, and the hope is that the old Deion Sanders quote proves true, and that they play as well as they look.
author: Pat Lane

title: 5 winners and losers from Patriots win over Bills
summary: The New England Patriots got back in the win column on Sunday with a 29-26 win over the Buffalo Bills. Here is who caught our eye for better or worse upon live-viewing the Week 4 contest. Winners QB Drake Maye: After a well-documented slow start to the season, Maye turned things around on Sunday out-dueling […]
full_text: The New England Patriots got back in the win column on Sunday with a 29-26 win over the Buffalo Bills . Here is who caught our eye for better or worse upon live-viewing the Week 4 contest. Winners QB Drake Maye: After a well-documented slow start to the season, Maye turned things around on Sunday out-dueling Josh Allen in the win. Maye seemed more comfortable from the start leading a 97-yard scoring drive to start the game, which set the stage for him to lead four total scoring drives. There still were a pair of turnovers, but Maye overall looked more comfortable and decisive in the pocket while carving up the blitz and pushing the ball downfield. He made an impact as a scrambler too, where he led the team with 54 yards on the ground. WR Efton Chism III: With Mack Hollins leaving the game with a calf injury, Efton Chism III saw an increased workload down the stretch. Chism took advantage of those opportunities, hauling in a pair of passes on the Patriots game-winning drive including the winning touchdown — an incredible one-handed snag. ARE YOU EFTON KIDDING ME!!!!!!! 📺 CBS pic.twitter.com/dRQyU4Vbca — New England Patriots (@Patriots) October 4, 2026 WR Romeo Doubs: It’s been an up-and-down start to the season for the Drake Maye-Romeo Doubs connection. A low pass that Doubs could not haul in resulted in an interception on Sunday, but there was plenty more good from the duo in Buffalo. Doubs caught six passes for 58 yards and a pair of touchdowns — one a goal-line fade which the receiver hauled in with one hand through contact — to go along with two big fourth-down conversions. CB Carlton Davis III: Filling in for the injured Christian Gonzalez, it was a strong day for cornerback Carlton Davis. He held up well in coverage against D.J. Moore before the receiver left with an injury and was involved on a forced fumble in the first half. Davis also was on scene to again blow up another screen pass and logged two run stuffs against James Cook. Losers OT Will Campbell/Pass Protection: Drake Maye was under pressure on 42.9% of his dropbacks on Sunday, with left tackle Will Campbell being the main culprit surrendering six pressures (three hits), which included three on seven matchups against Greg Rousseau. Guards Alijah Vera-Tucker and Ben Brown were also charged with three pressures each and were pushed backwards on Drake Maye’s strip sack. Honorable mentions While the Patriots short-yardage run game had some struggles, the ground game as a whole took a step forward. Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson broke off several plus rushes as they finished with a 45% rushing success rate (75th percentile). Most productive game of the season for tight end Hunter Henry (5 catches, 62 yards), who then iced the game with a third-down conversion on the last possession. Jared Wilson and Morgan Moses had cleaner performances up front being tabbed with just one pressure allowed each. It continues to be a promising start to the year for Gabe Jacas and Elijah Ponder. The duo had three pressures a piece while the rookie showed off his power with a bullrush against Dion Dawkins, while Ponder also recovered a fumble. The Patriots defense largely played zone coverage on Sunday, but a rare man-to-man rep late in the game led to Craig Woodson’s interception on Josh Allen. New England’s run defense faltered down the stretch, as James Cook ended the day averaging 6.3 yards per carry while Buffalo posted an 89th percentile rushing success rate.
author: Brian Hines

title: Mike Vrabel reacts to Patriots win over Bills: ‘It gets us back in the race’
summary: Even though the season was only three weeks old, it felt as if the New England Patriots already had their backs against the wall entering Week 4. And while their upset win over the Buffalo Bills only gets them back to .500 and a game closer to the division lead, it might just end up […]
full_text: Even though the season was only three weeks old, it felt as if the New England Patriots already had their backs against the wall entering Week 4. And while their upset win over the Buffalo Bills only gets them back to .500 and a game closer to the division lead, it might just end up a turning point in their season. Head coach Mike Vrabel would not call it that. He did, however, acknowledge that the victory “gets us back in the race” — a sentiment he shared with both his team in the locker room, and with the media during his postgame press conference after the 29-26 victory. “Our guys worked extremely hard this week, and we knew that it was going to be a battle,” Vrabel said. “I mean, Josh [Allen] is unbelievable. I felt like Drake [Maye] went toe-to-toe with him. We had a couple of turnovers that we have to continue to eliminate, but we knew that if we took advantage of some opportunities we’d get some too. They have an excellent football team, great staff, excellent players, and we’re lucky to get out of here with a win. But it does get us back in the race.” Now at 2-2, the Patriots are still trailing the 3-1 Bills in the standings. However, Vrabel’s team does not only own the head-to-head tiebreaker over their AFC East rivals now, it also has built some much-needed momentum coming out of a relatively lackluster September. And if the 2025 Patriots have taught us one thing, the momentum built by beating a talented Bills team on the road can sustain a club for quite some time and boost some confidence. The Patriots, fresh off a 35-6 blowout loss in Jacksonville, were in dire need of just that this week. Vrabel’s post-game messaging expressed that thought as well. “Everyone has to believe that they’re going to be the answer for why we’re going to get back in this thing each and every day that we come to work,” he said. “That’s what the message was and that’s what the message will continue to be. And whether that’s the examples that we can show them — other guys stepping up, other guys stepping in — but you have to prepare every week as a starter. You have to believe that you’re the reason — whether you make one play or 15 plays — that we’re going to win.” On Sunday, several players answered that call. Whether it was Efton Chism catching the game-winning touchdown or Ben Brown going wire-to-wire despite being the third-string option at right guard. “A lot for us to correct,” said Vrabel, “but I really just appreciated the way we competed and that we fought against a good, veteran football team.”

full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - JANUARY 04: Head coaches Raheem Morris of the Atlanta Falcons and Kellen Moore of the New Orleans Saints meet after the Falcons beat the Saints 19-17 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on January 04, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New Orleans Saints will return to the Caesars Superdome on Monday night for their first NFC South matchup of the season as they host the Atlanta Falcons on Monday Night Football. New Orleans enters Week 4 looking to bounce back from a frustrating 35-27 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders, while the Falcons come to town for another chapter in one of the NFL’s longest and most heated rivalries. Monday night’s matchup carries even more significance as the Saints and the NFL commemorate the 20th anniversary of the historic “Domecoming” game. On Sept. 25, 2006, New Orleans returned to the Superdome for the first time following Hurricane Katrina and defeated Atlanta 23-3 in a night that became about much more than a football game. Now, 20 years later, the Saints and Falcons will once again meet again in primetime with a national audience watching. For the Saints, their focus will be to put last week’s loss behind them and get back on track. Tyler Shough has continued to show promise through the first three games of the season, but the offense needs to be more consistent and avoid the mistakes that proved costly against the Raiders, WR Chris Olave remains one of Shough’s most dangerous weapons and will once again play an important role against Atlanta. Establishing an offensive rhythm early will be especially important as New Orleans looks to take advantage of what should be an energetic home crowd. Defensively, the Saints will face another difficult test against a familiar division opponent. Games between these two teams have rarely been predictable, and limiting explosive plays while creating pressure will be key if the Saints hope to slow down a Falcons offense led again by quarterback Michael Penix Jr. The Saints must capitalize on their opportunities. In a rivalry where games are often decided by only a few plays, turnovers and red-zone execution could ultimately make the difference. But Monday night will have a different feel inside the Superdome. Between the national spotlight, the rivalry and the emotions surrounding the anniversary of one of the most important nights in franchise history, the atmosphere should be electric. The Saints will have a loud and proud home crowd behind them as they look to bounce back, earn their first NFC South win of the season and add another memorable game to the Saints and Falcons history. Prediction: Saints 34 – Falcons 27 It’s Monday Night Football, the Saints are back in primetime, and the Superdome will be rocking. With all of the emotions surrounding the 20th anniversary of “Domecoming”, I think the atmosphere gives New Orleans an extra edge. In what will be a close game, I think the Saints can feed off that energy and come away with the win. title: Week 4 Film Preview: Highlights from the All 22
summary: Falcons 35 – Packers 14 The Packers couldn’t do much on the offensive side of the ball last Thursday night and it led to Atlanta’s first win of the season. In Michael Penix first game of the season back from injury, Atlanta was able to control the line of scrimmage on both sides of the […]
full_text: Falcons 35 – Packers 14 The Packers couldn’t do much on the offensive side of the ball last Thursday night and it led to Atlanta’s first win of the season. In Michael Penix first game of the season back from injury, Atlanta was able to control the line of scrimmage on both sides of the ball and dominate the Packers for most of the game. While Atlanta deserves the credit for going into Lambeau and getting the win against the favored Packers, this game was more about the Packers not executing than Atlanta doing something special. For the Saints to get a win this Monday night, it must start with taking control of the line of scrimmage, something they couldn’t do in the 4th quarter against the Raiders. Set the Edge Atlanta’s offense starts and ends with their ability to get their best player, Bijan Robinson, the ball with room to run. Their playbook is centered around their ability to run outside zone with Robinson and the Packers never found a solid answer for this as Robinson rushed for 194 yards and 2 touchdowns on Thursday night. Outside zone is a very hard play to stop as it is tiring for the defensive line and offers many possible cut-back options for the running back so defenders must be discipline in their gap assignments. If the Saints can set the edge and limit Atlanta’s ability to let Robinson round around the edge, the Falcons will not have similar success on the ground that they had in Green Bay. Take Advantage of Personnel Mismatch The Falcons defensive response to 12 personnel can be seen below and will be an area the Saints can take advantage. When the Packers put 2 tight ends on the field, the Falcons reacted by getting into a bear front (Image below) out of a base personnel package that include 3 lineman and 4 linebackers. This is an area where the Saints offense can take advantage as they can present having 2 tight ends in their personnel package while using either Noah Fant or Juwan Johnson in more of a receiver role. While they Packers weren’t able to take advantage of the mismatches the Falcons 12 personnel response would create due to poor OLine play, the Saints seem very comfortable so far this season with 2 tight ends on the field. This leads me to believe we will see another big day for Juwan in the receiving game and more effective in the run game as the Falcons front 7 on paper is the weakest one they have faced yet. Limit Drake London Explosives Similar to the Ravens, the Falcons offense will give the Saints defense a hefty sample of boot action to stop on Monday night as they use the play as a compliment to their zone rushing scheme. The Falcons boot play is unique as they move Drake London (most dangerous receiver) around to involve him in the concept in multiple ways. Unlike the Ravens, London will run every route in the concept and offers a unique ability to be dangerous at every level of the defense. The Packers where never able to reach a real answer for the Falcons zone rushing which led to London gashing them on boot and play action plays. While I trust Staley’s ability to stop the Zone/Boot combo teams after his showing against the Ravens, Drake London will be the best receiver he has been tasked with stopping yet this year in that type of scheme. Though I don’t expect London to be running wide open across the field, the Saints must have an answer for when he catches the ball on short flat routes that can be found as check downs – which is where the Raiders constantly found easy yards for their tight ends. This area is where London is most dangerous as he can turn a short competition into an explosive play for the Atlanta offense. Keys to Victory Set the Edge (Stop Outside Zone) Take Advantage of Personnel Mismatch (Utilize 2 tight end packages) Limit Drake London Explosives (Stop Boot)

title: NY Giants to place KR/WR Braxton Berrios on IR, per report
summary: Braxton Berrios is being placed on injured reserve by the New York Giants after suffering a foot injury in Sunday’s 36-24 victory over the Arizona Cardinals, according to a report from ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter. It is unclear when Berrios was injured, though his last play was a late-second quarter punt return on which […]
full_text: Braxton Berrios | Getty Images Braxton Berrios is being placed on injured reserve by the New York Giants after suffering a foot injury in Sunday’s 36-24 victory over the Arizona Cardinals, according to a report from ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter . It is unclear when Berrios was injured, though his last play was a late-second quarter punt return on which he lost 2 yards. Berrios was just added to the 53-man roster last week after the Giants released Odell Beckham Jr . Considering Beckham’s weekend rant after his release, he may have taken himself out of the running for a return to the Giants. The Giants have wide receivers Dalen Cambre and Jalin Hyatt on the practice squad. They cut ties with veteran wide receiver Darius Slayton, now a member of the Indianapolis Colts, early in the season. Berrios has returned five kickoffs for an average of 27.6 yards and four punts for an average of 2.5 yards this season. Charlie Jones , an experienced NFL kick returner, replaced Berrios on kickoff returns Sunday. He averaged 23.0 yards on three returns. He took over for Berrios on punt returns after the injury, averaging 14.5 yards on two returns.

title: Giants-Cardinals ‘things I think’: First-place Giants just keep ‘throwing punches’
summary: EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — The flawed but feisty New York Giants woke up Monday morning with a 3-1 record and sole possession of first place in the NFC East. That is a pleasant, but absolutely unexpected development. Just for fun, and because we know it may not stay this way over the next 13 games, […]
full_text: John Harbaugh and Giants players talk to an official during Sunday’s game. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — The flawed but feisty New York Giants woke up Monday morning with a 3-1 record and sole possession of first place in the NFC East. That is a pleasant, but absolutely unexpected development. Just for fun, and because we know it may not stay this way over the next 13 games, a look at the Week 4 NFC East standings: New York Giants — 3-1 Dallas Cowboys — 2-2 Philadelphia Eagles — 2-2 Washington Commanders — 1-3 How did this happen? Let’s take a look. The John Harbaugh effect The veteran head coach’s impact has been central to the Giants’ early-season success. Harbaugh made players — many of them used to losing with the Giants — believe they could win if they earned the right to win. He drove them hard during the spring and especially in the summer, harder and longer than most were accustomed to as NFL players. Harbaugh made them believe that the hard work, and the bond they developed through their shared effort, would callous them and help build the toughness to earn the opportunity to win. Be truthful, Giants fans. Would the team have won either of the Week 3 and Week 4 games it was victorious in last season? Almost certainly not. A year ago, the Giants blew five fourth-quarter leads. In each of the last two weeks, they have won games that felt as though they were about to be lost. That maybe should have been lost. “You have to play the next play, which is what they do. You gotta keep believing, and then you got to do. Keep believing, keep doing, keep believing, keep doing, keep believing, keep doing,” Harbaugh said after Sunday’s game. “That’s really what life is. Football is a metaphor for life, and that’s the way a football game goes. Sometimes it doesn’t go your way. But the last two times it did go our way, and they were rewarded for that.” Defensive tackle D.J. Reader is in his 11th season in the NFL. He knows what he sees and feels. “We fightin’, man. We out there throwing punches, and we know our brother beside us is throwing punches with us,” Reader said. “That’s all that matters. “It might not be as conventional as everybody’s looking for it to be, but shoot, we care about each other. There’s nothing really you can do to replace camaraderie. When people care about each other, a lot of things can happen.” The Giants are not the most talented team in the NFL. They are not the most talented team in the NFC East. They have lost their young star quarterback for the season in Jaxson Dart. They have lost their defensive leader in Brian Burns for the season. There are plenty of flaws to pick at. Yet, they believe. It is, again, resilience and toughness born from the work they have done. “You shouldn’t be out there playing if you don’t believe,” Reader said. “We put a lot of work in in camp. New coaches, new coordinators, new systems. If you believe in the work you put in, you just gotta keep believing.” Significantly, the winning plays were made the past two weeks by players who are having resurgent seasons. A week ago it was Jevon Holland, who was disappointing in his first season with the Giants in 2025, but earned NFC Defensive Player of the Month honors after getting three interceptions in three games. Sunday, it was Tae Banks , who looked like a bust three years after the Giants made him a first-round pick. Harbaugh gave Banks a shot at redemption, and from the beginning, Banks has taken advantage of it. Teammates lauded Banks’ resilience on Sunday, making two plays on the final goal line stand after a questionable pass interference call against him put the Arizona Cardinals at the Giants’ 4-yard line with :22 to play. Banks said after the game that the important thing is to “keep going.” He and his teammates have been doing that. “That’s real hard,” said Arvell Reese . “After you make a mistake like that, some people would probably get down. He still held his head high, chest up. Man made a play; he won us the game. That’s very hard. Tip my hat to him.” Abdul Carter is another player who had a rough rookie season in 2025, but who had a big hand in Sunday’s victory. “I think it just shows what we’re made of,” Carter said. “In those critical situations, that’s where you’ve gotta be at your best. The last two weeks we’ve been at our best in those situations. “It’s really hard to win in this league. It just reminds me of last year so much because in these situations we didn’t get it done, but obviously this year has been a change. I credit the coaches, I credit the players, I credit everybody in the building. It takes everybody.” It started with Harbaugh setting the standard, and convincing the players they could do it if they worked hard enough to earn it. The Jameis-coaster I think that is what we have to call the Jameis Winston Experience. There is great. There is ugly. There is everything in between. In some cases, all at the same time. I don’t know about anyone else, but every time Winston drops back to throw, my immediate thought is “Oh, God, what is going to happen this time?” Sometimes it is great. Sometimes it is disastrous. Every time he starts to move around in the pocket or his feet start to bounce around, I cringe. Yet, some of his best plays occur when that happens. Some of his worst, too. If I’m an offensive lineman, sometimes I love Winston. Sometimes, I hate him for making me look bad. Winston threw three touchdown passes. He threw two interceptions. He made plays that kept the Cardinals in the game. Yet, in the end, he made plays the Giants don’t win the game without. The Giants are 2-0 with Winston starting games. It isn’t pretty with Winston, and never will be. Still, could this be the start of a heater like the one Winston was on when he went 5-2 as a starter for the New Orleans Saints in 2021? Even Winston’s post-game press conference sounded like Jameis being Jameis. “I’m just grateful for the opportunity I have now. And right now, I get to smile and say I’m the starting quarterback for the New York Football Giants,” Winston said. “So, focusing on what I would love is winning games with my team, being the best that I can be. And I just feel like that, man, I’m heating up and I’m starting to get better, better, and better. “Last week, I was questioning if I could even throw. This week, I’ve got people talking about the Jameis Winston experience again. So, I’m just still so curious, and I’m so inspired to be the best me every single day. And that alone pushes me. Not another man, not another teammate, just my desire to be what I would love.” Honestly, I’m not exactly sure all of that makes sense. But sometimes watching Winston doesn’t make sense. Which, right now, with the way things are going for this Giants team, might make him the perfect quarterback for an imperfect team that has so far turned the NFC East upside down. A monster is rising In retrospect, it seems appropriate that the first question Arvell Reese was asked after Sunday’s game was about playing so well in front of Lawrence Taylor as the Giants honored the 1986 Super Bowl team. I’m kind of mad that I didn’t think to ask the question. “Oh man, that means a lot, bro,” Reese said. “With a guy like that in the building, him setting the standard for how that position is supposed to be played back in the day. It definitely means a lot to play a decent game like that.” Let’s not put Reese in the same category as Taylor just yet. Actually, not for a long while. Maybe never. Still, the 21-year-old rookie had a Taylor-esque game on Sunday. He had nine tackles. He had a pressure that led to an interception when he hit Jacoby Brissett’s arm. He had an interception of his own. He had a tackle for loss. He had three passes defensed. He made one-on-one tackles in the open field. Still, he only called his play “decent,” because there were “a bunch of plays I left out there.” Reese said in the celebratory post-game locker room that he wants to…

title: 3 NY Giants players injured in victory over Arizona Cardinals
summary: The New York Giants suffered a trio of injuries during Sunday’s 34-26 victory over the Arizona Cardinals. Bryan Hudson starts at center Bryan Hudson played well in his first NFL start at center. Head coach John Harbaugh said that Hudson started in place of John Michael Schmitz because the latter missed practices at the end […]
full_text: Jason Pinnock | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The New York Giants suffered a trio of injuries during Sunday’s 34-26 victory over the Arizona Cardinals. Safety Jason Pinnock , splitting time early in the game with Tyler Nubin , left the game with a concussion. Pinnock played 17 snaps. Kick returner/reserve wide receiver Braxton Berrios left the game with a foot injury. Berrios had been replaced on kickoff return at the beginning of the game by Charlie Jones . Jones took over as the punt returner after Berrios was injured. Defensive lineman Chauncey Golston left the game with a neck injury. That led to an uptick in snaps for Darius Alexander . Bryan Hudson starts at center Bryan Hudson played well in his first NFL start at center. Head coach John Harbaugh said that Hudson started in place of John Michael Schmitz because the latter missed practices at the end of the week due to the birth of a child. Per Pro Football Focus, Hudson was the fourth-highest graded center in Week 4, and had a perfect 100.0 pass-blocking efficiency score in 33 pass-blocking snaps. Harbaugh did not anoint Hudson as the new starting center. “JMS had missed a couple days of practice, and Huddy had been doing so well,” Harbaugh said. “We kind of felt like he’s got the reps. He’s made the calls, and we were kind of thinking about starting to work him in a little bit here and there, even some extra line stuff, if possible. And it just made sense. I mean, JMS, he’d been up, his wife had the baby. He didn’t have a lot of rest. It just made sense, and I think it paid off. It’s not a long-term thing. I mean, we just have two centers we really like.” 3-0 at home Sunday’s victory marked the first time since 2008 that the Giants have started a season 3-0 at home. MetLife Stadium opened in 2010, so that is the first time in their current building. “It means a lot. I think all of us, all of us, the players, coaches, we’re all very, the organization,” Harbaugh said. “I know Mr. Mara, talked to him after the game, everybody’s very proud of that, very proud of that. All right, now, next time we come back home, we got to extend it. We got to win the next one.”

title: Giants-Cardinals: 5 plays that led to the Giants’ victory
summary: The New York Giants defeat the Cardinals 36-24 in an exciting, sloppy game that showcased a resilient defense that dialed up the pressure. Arizona set the tone early, taking a 14-3 lead with a heavy rushing attack that exploited the Giants’ edge. However, Dennard Wilson’ unit stabilized and only allowed 138 total yards after those […]
full_text: Arvell Reese | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The New York Giants defeat the Cardinals 36-24 in an exciting, sloppy game that showcased a resilient defense that dialed up the pressure. Arizona set the tone early, taking a 14-3 lead with a heavy rushing attack that exploited the Giants’ edge. However, Dennard Wilson’ unit stabilized and only allowed 138 total yards after those first two Cardinals’ possessions. Both teams turned the football over three times. Both teams were sloppy with consequential penalties throughout the game. It was a wild experience, but New York is now 3-1 at the top of the NFC East; here are the five plays, or sequence of plays, that got them there. Play(s) 1: Goal line stand Deonte Banks played a HUGE role in the Giants’ win over Arizona. 1 INT, 1 TD, 4 PD, 3 AST vs Cardinals A huge win for New York as they try to stay right in the NFC East race. https://t.co/03EtvopKuc pic.twitter.com/zvcIU9pS0k — Football Performances (@NFLPerformances) October 4, 2026 I’m here for the Tae Banks redemption arc. The Giants relied heavily on man coverage, including at the end when Arizona had a fresh set of downs with 22 seconds on the Giants’ four-yard line. Banks made TWO elite plays: a pass break-up against Tre McBride and the epic pick-six to secure the Giants’ victory. Banks was beaten earlier in the game for a touchdown, but bounced back with game-saving work, as you can see in the post above. Below is just the pick-six, which capped a resilient effort by the defense: PICK SIX TO SEAL THE GAME! 🤯 Deonte Banks intercepts Jacoby Brissett and takes it to the house to secure the win for the Giants pic.twitter.com/xlEssRkJcq — NFL on CBS 🏈 (@NFLonCBS) October 4, 2026 DOTS of the Deonte Banks game-winner pic.twitter.com/KDnI8qIWkI — Doug Analytics (@Doug_Analytics) October 4, 2026 Play(s) 2: Controversial — or correct — call! ? Dominic Zvada booted his third field goal of the game, as yellow laundry found its way onto the field. It was a defensive holding penalty that extended the Giants’ drive: Refs said this was a hold on Dante Stills 😭😭😭😭😭😭😭😭😭 pic.twitter.com/YmCTSpaoUn — mervin (@MervinBusanut) October 4, 2026 Mike LaFleur was upset, and the Giants took advantage of the call with another peak of the Jameis Winston roller coaster: Theo Johnson up the seam for the go ahead score! pic.twitter.com/y7ThBuOmC5 — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) October 4, 2026 Out of an EMPTY formation, Winston found Theo Johnson up the seam for a touchdown in tight coverage, which gave the Giants a 25-24 lead. New York went for two by running the football off-tackle to the left; Najee Harris punched it in, and the Giants took a three-point lead. Play(s) 3: Reckless and sloppy football The Giants seized momentum with two touchdowns in two minutes of game time. However, the Jameis Winston experience can be quite reckless. Winston threw two interceptions on the next two Giants’ drives: We see you 29 ‼️ 📺:CBS pic.twitter.com/d2ABjyKyGD — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) October 4, 2026 Budda Baker interception! 🙌 AZvsNYG on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/fSRBXz7KKr — NFL (@NFL) October 4, 2026 The Giants got the ball to start the second half, and they responded by committing a false start penalty and throwing an interception – this is not winning football. The Winston interception led to the Cardinals scoring a go-ahead touchdown at the tail end of a 10-play, 37-yard drive, where Greg Newsome II was called for a defensive holding penalty in the end zone against Marvin Harrison Jr. Brissett 🎯 Higgins for the TD AZvsNYG on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/zm1iLz07Rw — NFL (@NFL) October 4, 2026 The touchdown and extra point gave the Cardinals a five-point lead with 7:20 left in the third quarter. The Giants may have put the Cardinals away early, but the reckless, sloppy football made for a much more competitive — and exciting — game. Play(s) 4: Arvell Reese continues to impress Arvell Reese has established himself as one of the better young defensive weapons in the NFL, after some coverage lapses in the first two weeks of the season. Wilson mentioned Reese’s development when talking with the media, and he had his best game to date. Reese was heavily involved in Wilson’s blitz package. He hit Jacoby Brissett’s arm, which resulted in this Greg Newsome II interception: Arvell Reese on the blitz hits Jacoby Brissett's arm, which led to this Greg Newsome INT… The #Giants defense NEEDED this. pic.twitter.com/kgaIzFQ5Hn — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) October 4, 2026 Winston and the Giants offense went three-and-out, but Winston found Malik Nabers in the end zone after Reese secured his own interception toward the end of the second quarter: Excellent turn around by the #Giants defense, led by rookie Arvell Reese. Shelby Harris gets his paw on a pass and Reese is there to secure the INT. pic.twitter.com/8JCBR0y22p — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) October 4, 2026 Malik Nabers scored a few plays later to give the Giants a lead. Reese also had several big tackles and knocked other balls out of the air: Arvell Reese is putting the Giants' defense on his back. Blitz PBU to force a third-and-long where the #Giants got off the field. pic.twitter.com/9zpNn5zVKo — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) October 4, 2026 Reese finished with nine tackles, a tackle for a loss, and three passes defensed. Play (s) 5: Abdul Carter is a stud The Giants felt the loss of Brian Burns early, as Arizona averaged nine yards per play on their first two drives. The Cardinals had a lot of success rushing outside, but Carter’s presence was felt on the third drive with a tackle for loss. He then took over the game in the second half, but no sequence of plays was more important for Carter than his two quarterback hits: Abdul Carter with TWO QB hits on consecutive plays to force a Cardinals punt. Both Carter and Arvell Reese have put the defense on their backs at different points of the game. Great effort by the young #Giants defenders. pic.twitter.com/rXczrhL85L — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) October 4, 2026 Najee Harris fumbled the football after the Giants’ defense forced a four-and-out. Arizona received the ball near midfield, down by three with 11:08 left in the game. Carter hit Brissett on second-and-12, but the pass was incomplete and well covered by Newsome. Carter then rushed Brissett and hit him on a third-and-12 pass that went for just five yards. Arizona was forced to punt, as New York’s defense kept the momentum. Carter also had his hand in on Tremaine Edmunds play vs. Brissett in the second half: Abdul Carter wins inside and forced Brissett into the arms of Tremaine Edmunds. Dennard Wilson has DIALED up the blitz/pressure against the Cardinals. pic.twitter.com/7qSo77fZvi — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) October 4, 2026 It was excellent to see both Reese and Carter play as well as they did against Arizona. Both young players were integral parts of this Giants’ victory.

summary: The leading New York Giants enter their Week 5 match-up as 3.5-point underdogs on the road against the Washington Commanders, per Fanduel. The Giants come into the game with a 3-1 record and sole possession of first place in the NFC East, while the Commanders are carrying a 1-3 record as the last place team […]
full_text: ﻿The New York Giants’ defense lines up against the Washington Commanders. | Getty Images The leading New York Giants enter their Week 5 match-up as 3.5-point underdogs on the road against the Washington Commanders, per Fanduel . The Giants come into the game with a 3-1 record and sole possession of first place in the NFC East, while the Commanders are carrying a 1-3 record as the last place team in the division. The Commanders are coming off of a 30-13 drubbing at the hands of the Indianapolis Colts in London. The Giants, meanwhile, are the Cardiac Kids. They’ve won the game on the last play each of the last two weeks, with a pair of Red Zone interceptions against the Titans and Cardinals. The good news for the Commanders is that they might be getting starting quarterback Jayden Daniels back for this game after he suffered a dislocated elbow back in Week 2. His return would be incredibly timely, as Marcus Mariota was knocked out of their loss against the Colts. It was initially believed that Daniels might need season-ending surgery, but decided to forego it to return this year. The Giants, meanwhile, finally saw their defense click against a good Cardinals offense, limiting Arizona to just 4 of 12 on third down, and taking the ball away three times — including Deonte Banks’ walk-off Pick 6. This will be the fourth time in five games that 3-1 Giants will come in as underdogs. Can the Giants prove the oddsmakers wrong and climb to 4-1 on the season? title: Deonte Banks called his shot, and delivered a game-winning play for the Giants
summary: EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — Deonte Banks looked like he might be the unfortunate goat of a game it seemed like was going to slip away from the New York Giants in the closing seconds on Sunday. With :27 left, Banks was called for a seemingly bogus pass interference penalty with the Arizona Cardinals facing third-and-6 […]
full_text: Deonte Banks heading to the end zone on Sunday with a game-winning interception. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — Deonte Banks looked like he might be the unfortunate goat of a game it seemed like was going to slip away from the New York Giants in the closing seconds on Sunday. With :27 left, Banks was called for a seemingly bogus pass interference penalty with the Arizona Cardinals facing third-and-6 from the New York 22-yard line. Head coach John Harbaugh called the penalty “crazy”, for which he might end up getting fined, and added “I thought you had to touch the guy for it to be pass interference.” After three incompletions, one caused by a Banks pass breakup, the Cardinals were still sitting at the 4-yard line facing fourth-and-goal with :11 remaining on the clock. Arizona quarterback Jacoby Brissett fired a slant toward wide receiver Michael Wilson near the goal line. It never got there. Banks, sitting inside and waiting for the slant he had been expecting the entire game, jumped in front of Wilson, caught the ball and raced 98 yards for a game-sealing score. “They was giving me a tight end and a receiver set all day. I’ve been thinking a slant all day and they haven’t been giving it to me,” Banks said. “That time I just knew they were going to give it to me. It was just a matter of time because they kept running it. “I knew I was going to take it. I’ve been calling it all week. I’m going to pick a slant this week.” Banks called his shot. And, he delivered. Banks picked off the pass, his first interception since 2023, and ran uncontested to the end zone as teammates and a jubilant MetLife Stadium crowd erupted. The Giants are 3-1 and in first place in the NFC East. Amazing and completely unexpected. The same has to be said for Banks having a starring role. After a promising rookie season, things went sideways for Banks the past two seasons. Poor play and maturity issues that led to what looked like poor effort on the field, and made you wonder if Banks was destined to be a kickoff returner and emergency cornerback for the remainder of whatever was left of his NFL career. Now, he is a hero. And, he might be the best cornerback on the Giants’ roster. “I got a bad pass interference in the first call, I did,” Banks said. “Two plays later they went at me again with McBride. He got another PBU. I just keep going. The main thing is just to keep going. Finish.” Banks admitted that has not always been easy for him. “I feel like I always had a problem with sometimes going to the next play,” Banks said. “I just think about what I did last time. Sometimes you just got to flush it. Keep going. That’s what I’ve been doing. “I just try to keep going. Alright. Let’s go. Keep going. Keep going. The game ain’t over until it’s over.” The Giants have now won back-to-back games in which a defensive back made a game-saving interception in the final seconds. Last week it was Jevon Holland with a last-second end zone interception against Cam Ward and the Tennessee Titans. “It just shows our relentlessness,” Banks said. “We’re going to keep going and keep going until the game’s over.” Harbaugh said he was “crying inside” when the pass interference call was made on Banks. “Was it crying? Was it rage? Maybe it was rage. It’s kind of a mix of those two things, right? You have to play the next play, which is what they do,” Harbaugh said. “You gotta keep believing and then you got to do. Keep believing, keep doing, keep believing, keep doing, keep believing, keep doing. That’s really what life is. Football is a metaphor for life and that’s the way a football game goes. Sometimes it doesn’t go your way. But the last two times it did go our way and they were rewarded for that.” Defensive tackle D.J. Reader wasn’t around for Banks’ struggles the past couple of seasons. He wasn’t surprised by what he saw Banks do at the end of the game. “That’s the only Tae Banks I know, man. Very confident player,” Reader said. “You get a BS PI call, whatever. You know how ballsy it is to undercut an out for the game? That’s confidence. That’s a ballsy thing to do, but when you’ve trusted your technique, you’ve watched the tape, and you see it, you can break on it and return it for six.” Banks said after the game he never doubted his ability despite the struggles of the past two seasons. “I just know what I’m capable of. Let me just prove myself right. I’m going to just keep proving myself right. That’s all,” Banks said. “I really don’t care about last year. We got a new coaching staff, new coaches, new players. I’m just happy to get going.” The Giants are certainly happy that he has.
author: Ed Valentine

title: NY Giants-Arizona Cardinals winners and losers: Deonte Banks the hero, Arvell Reese the star
summary: EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — The New York Giants are — somehow — 3-1 without quarterback Jaxson Dart and star edge defender Brian Burns. They lead the NFC East. Let’s examine the game in our unique ‘Kudos & Wet Willies’ style. Kudos to … Deonte Banks — In case you didn’t know, this is what happened […]
full_text: Tae Banks celebrates Sunday after his game-clinching interception. | Getty Images EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — The New York Giants are — somehow — 3-1 without quarterback Jaxson Dart and star edge defender Brian Burns. They lead the NFC East. Let’s examine the game in our unique ‘Kudos & Wet Willies’ style. Kudos to … Deonte Banks — In case you didn’t know, this is what happened on the final play of the game with the Giants desperately trying to hold a 30-24 lead: BANKS CALLS GAME!!! pic.twitter.com/P5TuEOvjxH — NFL (@NFL) October 4, 2026 That is a Banks’ game-saving house call four plays after being called for a phantom pass interference call that gave the Cardinals first-and-goal at the 4-yard line with :22 seconds left, seemingly dooming the Giants to a depressing loss. “I thought you had to touch the guy for it to be pass interference,” said head coach John Harbaugh of the penalty call. No matter. The Cardinals never gained another yard. Three straight incompletions, including one on a pass breakup by Banks, set the stage for the final play. Banks undercut a slant intended for Cardinals’ wide receiver Michael Wilson and took the ball to the house as a jubilant crowd at MetLife Stadium erupted. Banks had four passes defensed in addition to his game-winning interception. It’s been an amazing turnaround for Banks, a 2023 first-round pick who had miserable seasons in 2024 and 2025 and not long ago seemed destined to be a backup cornerback and kickoff returner. Not anymore. Arvell Reese — The No. 5 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft is getting better each game, and quickly turning into a star. Reese filled up the stat sheet on Sunday with nine tackles [one for loss], an interception, three passes defensed and a pressure that helped Greg Newsome get one of the Giants’ three interceptions of Brissett. Reese wasn’t satisfied, saying he “left a lot of plays out there.” Reese said he wants to be a “game changer” and a “dominant player” but that he’s “nowhere near” being the player he wants to be. Maybe not, but after what we saw Sunday that is a scary thought. He’s pretty darn good right now. Malik Nabers — Nabers gave everyone a scare when he stayed down on the field briefly after a 39-yard reception in the first quarter. He popped up and ran off the field, though. Nabers finished with a big day, six receptions in seven targets for 112 yards (18.7 yards per catch), including that 39-yarder and a 25-yard touchdown catch. This was easily Nabers’ best game of the season, and the explosive plays bode well for a Giants’ offense that desperately needs them. Abdul Carter — The second-year edge defender told Big Blue View this week that he was “disgusted” by the team’s pass rush productivity through three games. Sunday, he did something about it., Carter did not have a sack, but he did make Cardinals’ quarterback Jacoby Brissett feel his presence for the entire game. Without Brian Burns in the lineup against the Cardinals, Abdul Carter led the Giants with nine pressures, including eight coming in less than 2.5 seconds. No other Giants pass rusher had more than two pressures on the day. #AZvsNYG | #BigBlue pic.twitter.com/Q0rNXiMXwT — Next Gen Stats (@NextGenStats) October 4, 2026 Special teams (except for kickoff coverage) — There is so much to love about what the Giants did on special teams Sunday, and what they have done all season. Except for Sunday’s kickoff coverage, which we will get to. Rookie placekicker Dominic Zvada is now 9 of 9 after connecting on three field goals on Sunday. He his from 39, 50, and 52 yards — the last two being the longest kicks he has been asked to attempt thus far. Tyrone Tracy had a 55-yard kickoff return that set up a Zvada field goal. Punter Jordan Stout did not hit any 70-yard bombs on Sunday, but he did average 44.7 net yards and drop two of his three punts inside the 20-yard line. His best punt was a 47-yarder with the Giants clinging to a fourth-quarter lead that pinned Arizona at its own 3-yard line. Charlie Jones replaced Braxton Berrios on kickoff return, and eventual on punt return after Berrios was ruled out with a foot injury. Jones contributed a 23-yard punt return that prevented the Giants from starting a fourth-quarter drive in the shadow of their own end zone. Dennard Wilson — There are a couple of reasons to praise the Giants’ defensive coordinator after Sunday’s game. First, even without Brian Burns Wilson found a way to finally get the Giants’ pass rush cranked up. Check this nugget from NextGenStats: The Giants blitzed on 53.8% of dropbacks in their victory over the Cardinals in Week 4, the highest blitz rate by a Giants defense since the start of last season. Jacoby Brissett completed 6 of 18 pass attempts for 55 yards, two touchdowns, and two interceptions against the Giants’ blitzes while facing pressure on 52.4% of dropbacks (2 sacks). The Giants have called more blitzes with Brian Burns off the field, who suffered a season-ending injury in Week 3, blitzing on 47.1% of dropbacks with Burns off the field and just 23.7% with him on the field this season. As noted above, Carter and Reese were fantastic. Tremaine Edmunds and C.J. Okoye has sacks — the first official sack of Okoye’s career. They made Brissett uncomfortable, contributing to the three passes they intercepted. More subtly, look at the run defense. After two drives, the Cardinals had a 14-3 lead and had run the ball — mostly to the edges of the Giants’ defense — nine times for 81 yards (that’s 9.0 yards per carry). For the remainder of the game, they ran 17 times for 42 yards, 2.5 yards per carry. I don’t know what adjustment Wilson made, but whatever it was it worked. And it changed the trajectory of what looked like it might be an Arizona route. Bryan Hudson — Hudson got his first start in place of John Michael Schmitz, and appeared to play well. There were no obvious breakdowns in the middle of the line. John Harbaugh said the switch isn’t permanent, with Schmitz having missed time during the week for the birth of a child. Still, Hudson’s play might give the Giants something to think about. Wet Willies to … Kickoff coverage — The Giants allowed kickoff returns of 39 and 27 yards, uncharacteristic breakdowns for special teams coordinator Chris Horton’s group. Kayvon Thibodeaux — Getting the start with Burns out for the year, Thibodeaux was mostly non-existent. He had two assists on tackles. That’s it. Odell Beckham — Beckham created lot of good will during the summer as he worked to come back to the Giants after a year away from football. He made the team, but in the end the Giants cut him. In my view, Odell washed away all the good will he created with his social media tirade . Kwillies to … Jameis Winston — I think we probably just need to get used to the idea that Winston is going to be in this category every week. There was, as is the way of the world with Winston, a lot of good and a lot of bad. There were three touchdown passes. A couple of those came on brilliant plays. A 25-yard strike to Nabers. A play where he scrambled and got Malachi Fields open for a score. A tight-window TD to Theo Johnson. There were two interceptions. One of those, created a six-point swing at the end of the first half, taking the Giants out of field goal range and giving the Cardinals a chance to add three points. The other one, on the first possession of the second half, was “allegedly” thrown to Darnell Mooney. It missed the receiver, though, by about 10 yards. That pick put the ball at the Giants’ 37-yard line and set up a touchdown that put Arizona ahead, 24-19. There were four sacks. I’m not sure what the tape will show, but I would venture an educated guess that Winston either could have avoided or actually caused all of them. In the end, though, Winston has started two games for the Giants, they have won both, and they lead the NFC East. That is the bottom line.

title: Odell Beckham Jr. breaks silence after being cut by Giants
summary: The New York Giants ended their reunion with Odell Beckham Jr. earlier in the week by cutting him after three games. The move wasn’t a huge surprise, as Beckham had played minimal snaps to start the season. Braxton Berrios was viewed as a more valuable player for the roster, given his special teams expertise, which […]
full_text: The New York Giants ended their reunion with Odell Beckham Jr. earlier in the week by cutting him after three games. The move wasn’t a huge surprise, as Beckham had played minimal snaps to start the season. Braxton Berrios was viewed as a more valuable player for the roster, given his special teams expertise, which is what prompted the decision to move on from OBJ. Beckham took to Instagram comments in a fan-made video to air out his grievances. “Im super smart !!!! But I didn’t see this one my brotha! They got me!!! They won on top of the money u talkin bout I made tnem I came in HUMBLY took vet min then EARNED my spot n didn’t say nothing bout no $$$ which I kno make for everybody 🤑🤑… Ima tell u this ima grown man and this Shxt didn’t hurt me but it did when they cut me like that cause part of me is like I shoulda known better,” Beckham commented. “Now let me tellllll u the realllll deal truth what hurt my heart to the core is comin home and seeing my son and how happy he was with no idea of what happened and talkin bout my job n jersey number 13 broke me tf down.. funny thing about that is he said he likes 3 better n I find that very interesting .. “but again there was no real pain till u get home and ur son gives u that hug like idc what happened daddy ur the best and I love u… nothing better than tht.. but yea idk why they even gave me the run along I coulda really been playing this year somewhere and making a impact and I mean that from a person whose humbled by God and life, so all im doin is gettin ready for whatever God has for me and spreading luv n meantime.” It isn’t all doom and gloom for OBJ, as he still is supporting his teammates from afar during their Week 4 matchup against the Arizona Cardinals. After Malik Nabers caught a touchdown pass from Jameis Winston, Beckham took to social media to celebrate the score. YAAAEEE LEEK! — Odell Beckham Jr (@obj) October 4, 2026 Beckham came on board after several injuries to the wide receiver core shook the team. OBJ stuck around and worked hard, but it was clear after the first segment of the season that there isn’t a large role for him like he once had. Big Blue View community, what do you make of OBJ’s comments? Let us know in the comments section below.
