After terrorizing old team, 49ers’ Dre Greenlaw said he was fueled by Sean Payton’s ‘disrespect’ (paywall) “Greenlaw was blacking out and seeing red Sunday because Payton, he said, ignored him last year, starting around late November. After he signed a three-year, $31.5 million contract in March 2025, Greenlaw missed Denver’s first six games with a torn quadriceps. He missed the final two games with a hamstring strain. The Broncos released him in March after Greenlaw had made 43 tackles in eight games. Greenlaw said Payton began ignoring him – he said he hadn’t spoken to him since Week 12 — because he was frustrated by the return the Broncos were receiving on their investment. “He definitely was, for sure,” Greenlaw said. “He would walk by – I would walk by – and he wouldn’t even look at me because of my injury. So I just knew what it was (with him) there.” Greenlaw, a longtime enforcer and energizer who spent his first six seasons with the 49ers before his lone season in Denver, said his relationship with Payton is why he was “1,000 percent” more amped than usual for Sunday’s game. Greenlaw said his agent was the one who informed him the Broncos were parting ways with him. “The disrespect,” Greenlaw said of Sunday’s motivation. “He couldn’t be man to man and call my phone and say, ‘We’re going to cut you.’” …..“I told him after the game, ‘I could tell you were about 98% blacked out,’” Williams said. “But he kept his cool with that other 2%.” Defensive end Romello Height added, “Every time he came to the sideline, he was tweaking out. It was good to see that, and it was good to see him kind of get revenge on an old team.” Dre Greenlaw had ‘a little extra’ vs. the Broncos, his ex-team “I was half blacked out, but I just know my teammates just had my back, and they just told me to be smart,” Greenlaw said. “I’m thankful to have the teammates that just have my back and just understand me. … They helped a lot.” Asked what happened in the moment, Warner, with a smile creeping across his face, said the moment was “blurry” in his mind. “There was definitely something a little extra for him this week,” Warner said. “He had extra emotion going in this game. I told him just to use it wisely, which he did. I was proud of him and played a heck of a game. He’s played great all year, continuing to play great for us. I’m glad he’s on our side now.” 8 Winners, 3 losers, and 1 IDK from the 49ers win over the Broncos “Sumer Sports has a “pressure to pocket attempt” stat, and the 49ers had 57.9%, 6.6% above league average. They moved Nix off his spot. Credit Nix for making plays off schedule, but the lack of sacks doesn’t mean the 49ers gave Nix all day to throw. Nix’s 40.5% passing success rate (34.5% before the final drive) was 21st among all quarterbacks in Week 4. He was pressured 43.2% of the time, despite a 29.5% blitz rate. That pressure rate was the 11th-best this week. My takeaway from this game was that Morris went out of his way to take away anything over 10 yards. He forced Nix to dink and dunk down the field, hoping the offense would either get impatient or Denver would shoot itself in the foot. The latter proved to be true multiple times. Osa Odighizuwa had four pressures. Gracen Halton and Sebastian Valdez had one apiece. Keion White had four. Ogbo Okoronkwo and Romello Height also had two. In fact, Height had a team-high 22.2% pass-rush win rate. White was at 18.2%. They didn’t turn them into sacks, but it felt like Nix was flustered enough during the game that it impacted his decision-making to throw the ball downfield.” Kyle Juszczyk (knee), two more 49ers injured in win over Broncos “Juice … they’re thinking it was probably a knee sprain,” Shanahan said. “[The] ACL and stuff looked intact, but we’ll have to find out tomorrow. Stout, they’re guessing an AC [sprain], but we won’t know for sure until tomorrow. And Sigle, they’re not sure. They just thought an ankle.” What Kyle Shanahan and others said after 49ers’ 24-14 win vs. Broncos “Yeah, I grabbed [Brock] and said, ‘Don’t throw any more incompletions.’ And he listened. I should have told him at the beginning (laughter). No, I think he had some better looks. Didn’t get any tipped balls. I think he had better looks and was awesome there.” Kawakami: The Kyle Shanahan era keeps going and going — stronger than ever (paywall) “But right now, Shanahan and general manager John Lynch are the two unquestioned power sources in this franchise. Underline that 10 more times now that Paraag Marathe has left to run the 49ers’ European soccer interests and Jed York has been suspended and moved to Ohio before that. Who’s going to overrule Shanahan and Lynch now? Who would want to? The whole rational point of the Shanahan era is that nobody ever has to pull him from doing crazy things.” What we learned as huge second half fuels 49ers’ win over Broncos, 4-0 start “The 49ers entered the game with a 63-percent success rate on third downs, but their short-yardage offense was a problem on Sunday.” Grades for Brock Purdy, 49ers’ gutsy Week 4 win over Broncos to stay undefeated “The 49ers’ run defense had been one of the areas of concern through the first three games. But they did a good job on Sunday against J.K. Dobbins and R.J. Harvey. Dobbins had 11 carries for 40 yards (3.6 average), and Harvey managed just 25 yards on seven carries (3.6 average). The 49ers also did a good job of limiting Bo Nix on his scrambles. He gained just 10 yards on two rushing attempts.” 49ers’ Upton Stout reminds Raheem Morris of a Hall of Fame cornerback (paywall) “The 49ers grade each college prospect on what they call “Game WIT,” an assessment of their on-field demeanor, aggressiveness, mentality and strain. Area scout Warren Ball gave Stout the highest “Game WIT” grade he ever has assigned a prospect, saying he had a “heart of a lion.” Head coach Kyle Shanahan shows his players highlights from the previous week in a team meeting the night before games. The greatest hits from the victory over the Dolphins? Tight end George Kittle said, “It was mostly an Upton highlight film.” ….Stout has never lacked confidence. At Western Kentucky, he sometimes acted like a coach, barking at his teammates for missed assignments or effort that didn’t meet his standards. His position coach, Da’Von Brown, raved about Stout last year, but also conceded: “Every day wasn’t cream and cookies.” The 49ers did their homework and felt comfortable that Stout’s rough edges reflected his passion, not bad character. Eighteen months after Stout was drafted, it appears they came to the correct conclusion.”
author: Yinon Raviv

title: 8 Winners, 3 losers, and 1 IDK from the 49ers win over the Broncos
summary: It was the kind of win that proves your mettle as a San Francisco 49ers player. This is what an NFL game looks like. You can’t expect everything to go your way. You’re not going to score on every drive against a playoff-caliber team. It took the offense a half to heat up, but once […]
full_text: (Photo by Santiago Mejia/San Francisco Chronicle via Getty Images) It was the kind of win that proves your mettle as a San Francisco 49ers player. This is what an NFL game looks like. You can’t expect everything to go your way. You’re not going to score on every drive against a playoff-caliber team. It took the offense a half to heat up, but once they started cooking, they scored three consecutive touchdowns. Conversely, the defense did its part for three and a half quarters. The Niners never looked back after a Broncos special teams miscue, which is where we’ll start this week’s Winners and Losers. Winners Siran Neal The offense was stagnant. They looked lifeless. Neal had a fantastic individual effort on a punt to put himself in a position to make a tackle. The returner attempted to juke Neal, but couldn’t. Then, he went down and fumbled. That play was all Neal and flipped the game on its head. Deebo Samuel Deebo scored the first touchdown of the game. He had the longest carry of the game. Samuel’s first three attempts resulted in 44 yards, including 31 of those coming after contact. He is a tank, and somebody who defenses have no idea how difficult he is to tackle until it’s too late. That’s how you force four missed tackles. Samuel’s receiving line won’t impress, with five receptions for 26 yards, but offense needed every one of those to stay on the field. He has the perfect skill set for the role the 49ers are asking of him, and Samuel capitalized on his opportunities against the Broncos. George Kittle Kittle had the game-winning touchdown. He was less than two-hundredths of a mile per hour away from reaching 20 miles per hour. Kittle finished with four receptions for 70 yards, and a +1.41 receiving EPA. Kittle caught all three of his targets against man coverage. Losers Upton Stout Stout was picked on in coverage. The first six times he was targeted, it was a completion. A few of those resulted in first downs, including the play that resulted in a 30-yard gain for the Broncos. Stout’s seventh target was also completed for a first down. Stout left the game with a shoulder injury. Before he left, he occasionally got lost in coverage, especially when Bo Nix scrambled. Stout missed one tackle, which leads us to our next point. Tackling Stout’s injury paved the way for Jack Jones to see the field. Denver went at Jones, forcing him to tackle. Jones was 0-for-2, with one resulting in a touchdown and the other an 18-yarder that preceded the score. Not all missed tackles are created equal. Sometimes, the defender slows the ball-carrier down while the rest of his teammates rally. Week 4 didn’t feel like one of those times. The 49ers’ missed tackle rate of 16.18% offset an afternoon that was full of sound coverage on the back end. That number is a little more than four percent above league average, and not something you can expect to get away with next week if you want similar results. Third downs The 49ers defense looked fortunate early, as the Broncos committed penalties on seemingly every other third down to turn a 3rd and 1 into a 3rd and 5 or longer. Denver started the game 3-for-4 before they faced a 3rd and 17. After getting off the field on the next two third downs, Nix scrambled for the next first down. That was the start of three of the next four conversions for Denver. They finished the game 8-for-17, but without self-inflicted wounds, the Niners would’ve faced more than one red zone trip. It was the opposite for the offense, who started slow before finishing 6-for-15 on late downs. It looks bad in hindsight, but the fourth-down sneak was the right call. Kyle Shanahan admitted they got the look that they wanted after the game, but it just didn’t work out. The offense started the game 1-for-5 on late downs before they converted a 3rd and 1. They missed their next three before another 1-yard opportunity. Once Denver’s starting cornerbacks left, it flipped. But the offense has to be better on early and late downs in the first half. IDKs The pass rush The 49ers got no sacks, and only Sebastian Valdez and Keion White hit Bo Nix on 42 attempts. It wasn’t for a lack of effort. Raheem Morris only blitzed Nix 13 times. Nix is the definition of a check-down merchant. You won’t generate much pass rush when the quarterback is playing hot potato. Running back R.J. Harvey had 10 targets. Sumer Sports has a “pressure to pocket attempt” stat, and the 49ers had 57.9%, 6.6% above league average. They moved Nix off his spot. Credit Nix for making plays off schedule, but the lack of sacks doesn’t mean the 49ers gave Nix all day to throw. Nix’s 40.5% passing success rate (34.5% before the final drive) was 21st among all quarterbacks in Week 4. He was pressured 43.2% of the time, despite a 29.5% blitz rate. That pressure rate was the 11th-best this week. My takeaway from this game was that Morris went out of his way to take away anything over 10 yards. He forced Nix to dink and dunk down the field, hoping the offense would either get impatient or Denver would shoot itself in the foot. The latter proved to be true multiple times. Osa Odighizuwa had four pressures. Gracen Halton and Sebastian Valdez had one apiece. Keion White had four. Ogbo Okoronkwo and Romello Height also had two. In fact, Height had a team-high 22.2% pass-rush win rate. White was at 18.2%. They didn’t turn them into sacks, but it felt like Nix was flustered enough during the game that it impacted his decision-making to throw the ball downfield. Winners Raheem Morris He’s awesome. I don’t know if the 49ers could have found a better fit for this team than Morris. Despite the injuries, he has a great grasp of the team’s strengths. We’re seeing free runners when Morris dials up a blitz. This time last year, and up until he was benched, how many times did we see Marques Sigle or Jason Pinnock 1-on-1 in coverage? They were hung out to dry, and offenses made them pay. Ji’Ayir Brown and Sigle were targeted a combined four times for 14 yards against Denver. The 49ers are allowing the lowest explosive play rate (3.5%) by any team through 4 games since 2000 They've allowed only nine 10+ yard runs & 20+ yard catches this year. — Doug Clawson (@doug_clawson) October 5, 2026 This passing defense does not give up the big play. They just don’t. That’s Morris’s scheme. You can’t blame the coach for missed tackles. But you can credit him with devising a plan that kept the Broncos in check on the ground and through the air. Us getting through a game without mentioning the safeties is a testament to Morris. The offensive line Another above-average week for the offensive line in the yards-before-contact area. The running backs had 41 total yards before contact, good for the 10th-best mark of the week. Broncos defensive coordinator Vance Joseph blitzed Purdy 41% of the time, but the line yielded only a 35.3% pressure rate. Shanahan doesn’t drop back to throw on four of the final five plays to end the game if he isn’t confident his line will hold up. When Purdy scanned the field on the final drive and came back to Christian McCaffrey, it was his third read. Connor Colby allowed three pressures. Colton McKivitz and Jake Brendel had two. Dominick Puni had one, while Trent Williams had a clean sheet. There were zero false starts or holds. We know those penalties ended drives for the Broncos offense, as they committed three pre-snap penalties. Fred Warner and Dre Greenlaw Together, they missed four tackles, but they had nine impact plays and 19 tackles between them. Dre had a pair of run stops. They each stuffed a run. The damage came in coverage. Greenlaw and Warner gave up 27 yards on seven targets. Warner broke up two passes, including one where the Broncos tight end was shell-shocked that Warner hit him as hard as he did. Greenlaw was close to a sack or a tackle for loss on multiple plays. He had four pressures and forced a fumble — Denver had a Johnny on the spot there to recover it. Morris put this game on his…
author: Kyle Posey

title: 3 quick takeaways from 49ers win over Broncos: Timely plays put Niners on top for 2nd straight week
summary: The San Francisco 49ers beat the Denver Broncos 24-14 to start the season 4-0 on Sunday and cap off a three-game home stretch with another quality win. Over the first three weeks, the 49ers offense dominated, but it took a while to get things going on Sunday, as San Francisco had just 10 points through […]
full_text: (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers beat the Denver Broncos 24-14 to start the season 4-0 on Sunday and cap off a three-game home stretch with another quality win. Over the first three weeks, the 49ers offense dominated, but it took a while to get things going on Sunday, as San Francisco had just 10 points through three quarters in a low-scoring affair. However, timely plays at the end led the 49ers to another double-digit victory, and they stand atop the NFC West a quarter into the season. Here are three quick takeaways from the 49ers win over Denver on Sunday. Finishing games strong The 49ers have faced some adversity the last two weeks in the fourth quarter, as they’ve found themselves in close games after holding double-digit leads. Last weekend, after the Arizona Cardinals pulled within two, the 49ers were aggressive offensively, and a touchdown drive sealed the game. This weekend, after the Broncos got a touchdown and two-point conversion to cut the lead to three, the 49ers had the ball with just over four minutes left and a chance to finish the game. And that’s exactly what they did. After getting a first down that inched the 49ers near midfield, San Francisco got the explosive play they had been searching for all game as Brock Purdy hit George Kittle, who outran the defense for a 56-yard touchdown to put the 49ers up 10. On the following drive, the 49ers forced Denver into multiple fourth downs, and the Broncos looked to kick on 4th & 5 at the 40-yard line to try and bridge the gap for an onside kick. However, a Will Lutz field goal sealed the deal and the 49ers came away with yet another impressive win. This wasn’t the prettiest win for the 49ers. They did not look great offensively, as the Broncos defense neutralized explosive plays and kept the run game in check for the most part. But in games like these, they need timely plays at the end, and Kyle Shanahan’s squad delivered. Defensive Line stops the run The Broncos have generally been a pass-heavy team under Sean Payton and Bo Nix. But with the 49ers’ shorthanded defensive line, stopping the run was a priority. Well, San Francisco’s unit did a pretty good job of that, holding Denver’s running backs to 3.6 yards per carry. Moreover, the 49ers contained explosives, as the Broncos had no carries for 10 or more yards. Of course, a big part of that was also linebackers Fred Warner and Dre Greenlaw swarming to the ball. They had 19 tackles combined. Now, San Francisco’s defensive line is clearly lacking a pass rush. While Bo Nix has generally been one of the NFL’s best quarterbacks at avoiding sacks, he had a ton of clean pockets on Sunday. Credit goes, though, to the 49ers secondary for locking up well in coverage, limiting explosive plays through the air. We’ll see if the 49ers can get players back or look for reinforcements over the next couple of weeks, but it was a good sign that players showed up in run defense on Sunday. Playing clean football As simple as it sounds, one of my keys to the game for the 49ers was playing clean football. Why? Well, San Francisco entered the game as one of the least-penalized and least turnover-prone teams, ranking in the bottom five in both categories. Meanwhile, the Broncos were in the middle of the pack, and penalties have especially been a recurring theme for Denver. In a close game like Sunday’s, I thought those two factors could tilt things in the 49ers’ favor, and they did. The Broncos were penalized seven times on Sunday, compared to just one for the 49ers. Additionally, Marvin Mims’s fumble on the punt led to the 49ers first touchdown of the game, opening things up for the Niners offense. Even when they may be struggling in some facet of the game, playing clean football can keep the 49ers ahead, and it did on Sunday. Next up, the 49ers get another big challenge, as they take on the Seattle Seahawks on the road next week at Lumen Field. But 4-0, the 49ers are in a great spot through the first quarter of the season.
author: Rohan Chakravarthi

Kyle Shanahan said, “We don’t know for sure,” about Juszczyk’s injury. “They’re thinking […]
full_text: (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images Here are the San Francisco 49ers injury updates after their Week 4 win against the Denver Broncos: S Marques Sigle (ankle) FB Kyle Juszczyk (knee) CB Upton Stout (shoulder) Sigle returned to the game, but left again after suffering an injury on a kickoff. Kyle Shanahan said, “We don’t know for sure,” about Juszczyk’s injury. “They’re thinking it’s probably a knee sprain. His ACL and stuff looked intact. We’ll find out for sure tomorrow.” As for Stout, Shanahan said, “We’re guessing an AC [sprain], but we won’t know for sure until tomorrow.” The team is unsure about the specifics of Stout’s shoulder injury. All three players will have MRIs on Monday. Linebacker Fred Warner dealt with stomach pain during the first half, but he returned. Mike Evans made it through the game after dealing with a rib injury all week. Shanahan said Evans wasn’t on a specific pitch count, “But we knew how much pain he was in. So we were just trying to limit the percentage of hits he has to take.” Shanahan said he didn’t think it was possible for Evans to play throughout the whole week, going as far as saying he wasn’t counting on Evans. “The way he was at walk-through on Friday, I knew how much pain he was in. But he never grimaced, never changed his stride. It was really, really impressive today what he did.”

title: Buccaneers Week 4 Top Performers vs. Green Bay Packers
summary: It was always going to be long odds, and sadly the Buccaneers couldn’t surmount them as they dropped their fourth straight loss Sunday. The 17-14 affair against the Green Bay Packers basically killed the season for a Tampa Bay team that needed a savior — an ask unfairly delegated to an undrafted rookie quarterback making […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 4: quarterback Jalon Daniels #10 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers runs for a first down in the second quarter against the Green Bay Packers at Raymond James Stadium on October 4, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Parker S. Freedman/Getty Images) | Getty Images It was always going to be long odds, and sadly the Buccaneers couldn’t surmount them as they dropped their fourth straight loss Sunday. The 17-14 affair against the Green Bay Packers basically killed the season for a Tampa Bay team that needed a savior — an ask unfairly delegated to an undrafted rookie quarterback making his first career start in Jalon Daniels. But so the dice roll, and the Bucs’ front office and coaching staff have come up snake eyes. At 0-4 and facing an extremely difficult next draw with the Dallas Cowboys on the road on a short week this Thursday, it’s hard to see the Bucs’ first win coming any time soon. All we can do is try to muster some positives as the season fades further and further in obscurity. Offensive Top Performer: QB Jalon Daniels The statline won’t be remarkable to anyone with the context of it belonging to a UDFA, but truly Jalon Daniels deserves praise for the difficult circumstances into which the coaching staff inserted him. Daniels threw two bad picks, but nothing uncharacteristic of a young player making his first start against a deceptive defensive scheme. He also kept the team in a close game with resiliency and grit. He completed 19-of-27 passes for 148 yards and score, along with 8 rushes for 56 yards — a single-game record for a Bucs rookie QB. His offensive coordinator Zac Robinson, who’s now proven that he is in fact quite bad at his job, largely failed to give him easy answers to the test nor good chances to create chunk plays. The longest play through the air was 21 yards. Daniels is a good kid who showed why he deserved a spot on an NFL roster, but it just wasn’t enough on Sunday. It happens. Jalon Daniels' first career TD! 🙌 @GBvsTB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/MKQijt4XeA — NFL (@NFL) October 4, 2026 Who else do you really praise here? Bucky Irving is great when the team decides to actually use him. He carried the ball 16 times for 61 yards but got no looks in the passing attack and was often neglected for long stretches. Sean Tucker got his first action of the year and got a touchdown, that was cool I guess. The hyper fixation on Cade Otton (6 targets) is extremely strange, he caught 4 passes for 37 yards but also dropped yet another easy one. Said focus is hampering the team’s ability to actually use its young receivers (Emeka Egbuka and Ted Hurst combined for 4 catches and 38 yards). There were continued issues with untimely penalties, not getting playcalls to the QB efficiently, and having some piss-poor protection plans. It’s pretty clear at this point there is no quick or easy fix coming. Defensive Top Performer: CB Jacob Parrish Parrish completely balled out on Sunday and continued to show how big of a hit he was as a 2025 third-rounder. Parrish recorded 5 tackles (1 for loss), a pass defensed, and a critical red zone interception that kept his team in the game — a turnover he went off-assignment to secure, by the way. He also could’ve logged a forced fumble if an official review went his way in the first half, but so it goes. Rookie LB Josiah Trotter experienced a few more growing pains but largely showed up in a positive way with 9 total tackles. His football instincts and physicality are clearly there, which are the essential building blocks. David Walker flashed again with one of the team’s only QB pressures and a run stop. More of the same from everyone else though. ANOTHER TAMPA BAY TAKEAWAY 🔥 @GBvsTB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/VVfqSCPHii — NFL (@NFL) October 4, 2026 Special Teams Top Performer: No One There’s no point of stretching to praise Chase McLaughlin’s two extra points. A strong argument could’ve been made he was the better choice to attempt a 65-yard-field goal (which he did last year) on 4th down rather than letting Daniels try to get 11 yards, but so it goes. Now that the Bucs have actually needed to punt the last couple weeks, we can renew the conversation that Riley Dixon is one of the league’s worst punters. He averaged a paltry 40 yards per kick on 4 punts. A conversation needs to be had about replacing him (again).
author: Mike Kiwak

title: Week 4 Game Recap: Daniels’ flashes not enough as Bucs fall 0-4
summary: First Quarter: Winless, with no starting quarterback. That was Tampa Bay’s situation as they took field for the opening series. Two runs, a sack, and a punt. Blessed by a third down drop, the Buccaneers’ defense got off the field, still the empty scoreboard. Tampa’s second drive was a slightly more productive rendezvous with a […]
full_text: Oct 4, 2026; Tampa, Florida, USA; Green Bay Packers safety Xavier McKinney (29) sacks Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Jalon Daniels (10) during the third quarter at Raymond James Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Matt Pendleton-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect First Quarter: Winless, with no starting quarterback. That was Tampa Bay’s situation as they took field for the opening series. Two runs, a sack, and a punt. Blessed by a third down drop, the Buccaneers’ defense got off the field, still the empty scoreboard. Tampa’s second drive was a slightly more productive rendezvous with a similar result— No points, Packer’s ball. Jalon Daniels’ first career completion would come on the game’s second drive but so would his second career interception. On a pass intended for Emeka Egbuka, Daniels instead found Evan Williams. Carrying their drive till the first quarter’s end, Green Bay began heating up and stacking positive plays. Second Quarter: At the start of the game’s second 15 minutes, Green Bay had the ball deep in Tampa territory. After a dropped touchdown pass, a pass interference on Jacob Parrish placed the ball at the one yard line— A sequence that Tampa’s defense managed to stretch out to a fourth and goal. That fourth down would be where Buccaneers’ fans would want to look away. Jordan love dropped back against a heavy blitz and found a very open Matthew Golden for game’s first points. 7-0, Packers. Two drives of ineffective offensive football later (Featuring a Cade Otton drop, something that feels like tradition by this point and startling Zyon McCollum praise when Jonathan Vilma mentioned that he regarded him as one of the league’s best corners) The Buccaneers’ next possession would officially end the missing persons case involving Sean Tucker. Tucker, a remarkable no-show throughout the first three games of the season finally saw his first opportunity to touch the ball. Those opportunities were multiple and as has been the speculation of many, led to good things. Tucker ran hard, pushing his way for a conversion on fourth and short which he used to set himself for a touchdown— His first score of the season and Tampa’s first of the day. 7-7, evened up. With three minutes remaining in the first half, it seemed Zac Robinson remembered that the strength of Tampa Bay’s offense was projected to be its depth at receiver. Jalon Daniels was spotted actually targeting his top two receivers. A few catches by Godwin, and pass interference drawn by Emeka Egbuka and Tampa Bay was threatening points before the half. Unfortunately, that threat would turn out be empty. Jalon Daniels tossed his second interception of the game and set the Packers up for lead-taking 58 yard field goal before the half. Matching most of this season for the Bucs, Todd Bowles iced Trey Smack which took his miss off the board and gave him another swing, which Smack smacked through. 10-7, Packers. Third Quarter: Green Bay took the opening drive of the second half right down the field 80 yards and wide open touchdown— What should have been Tucker Craft’s second of the day. A drive that just ran the football right at Todd Bowles’ ego stomped through tackles attempts and subsequent missed tackles all the way to the end zone. 17-7, Green Bay. The Buccaneers’ offense would not boast that level of efficiency with their halftime adjustments— Run, run, third down sack. The script of starting drives with Bucky Irving running the football up the middle is reaching near Adam Gase New York Jets’ levels of play calling (ask former Buccaneer Le’Veon Bell). Tampa would punt, Green Bay would match and the final six minutes of the third quarter would begin with Jalon Daniels finding Chris Godwin for a first down and his third catch of the game. Moving, inside of the Packers’ 15-yard line, the Buccaneers’ offense ran the ball into the fourth quarter. Fourth Quarter: Jalon Daniels started the fourth quarter by placing an exclamation point on the Tampa Bay’s best drive of the day, one of their best of the season— That exclamation point being his first career touchdown— The recipient Kenny Gainwell, snatching his first score in red and pewter. Green Bay’s ensuing drive was not one for Todd Bowles’ trophy case. Jordan love, with a healthy variety of passes scooted his offense right down the field. Aided by a questionable Alex Anzalone penalty, the benefit of bounce out of bounds on a forced fumble, and some questionable The Buccaneers would get the ball back, but that possession would unfortunately start with them backed up pretty significantly inside of their own five yard line. Although Daniels would find Egbuka for a first down, the team would still ultimately wind up nearly saftied when the group’s next third down snap hit Graham Barton in the rear and never made it off the ground. Following Daniels’ recovery of the on- hop dribbler, the Bucs had to punt from their own end zone. That punt would lead to phenomenal starting field position for the Packers still up three. Green Bay’s fantastic field position would lead to a fantastic Buccaneers play Jacob Parrish. Parrish, who has shown consistent scrappiness thus far in 2026, left his zone to jump a route down the middle of the field and give Tampa Bay the ball back, marking consecutive drives where the Bucs’ defense forced a turnover in the red zone to give the Buccaneers a chance to steal a late win. Tampa, with the ball back, just under four minutes, in the Jalon Daniels’ first start, would have a moment— A chance at glory. All preseason it was Daniels’ ability to bring the team from behind that was so wow-ing for fans and also a heavy factor in the organization eventually deciding he deserved to make the team. Daniels, however, would not be able to pull off a similar feat Sunday. The game would, as it often does, come down to a Todd Bowles decision. Foregoing a 65-yard field goal to tie, Bowles chose to leave his undrafted rookie free agent quarterback on the field for a fourth down and long attempt. That fourth down conversion attempt would feature what far too many plays have for the 2026 Buccaneers, an unblocked blitzer charging at their quarterback— Incomplete pass, turnover on downs, game over, 0-4.

summary: UPDATE: Mutliple reports have confirmed what Dan Quinn stated after Sunday’s loss to the Colts, that Marcus Mariota suffered an MCL injury to the same knee that got hurt during the preseason. He missed roughly a month with the last ailment, and it’s fair to expect he’ll miss the same amount of time this time […]
full_text: UPDATE: Mutliple reports have confirmed what Dan Quinn stated after Sunday’s loss to the Colts, that Marcus Mariota suffered an MCL injury to the same knee that got hurt during the preseason. He missed roughly a month with the last ailment, and it’s fair to expect he’ll miss the same amount of time this time around. Commanders QB Marcus Mariota suffered an MCL sprain Sunday in London, per source. This is his second MCL sprain, the first coming in the preseason. pic.twitter.com/GHYVOTApqP — Jeremy Fowler (@JFowlerESPN) October 5, 2026 Here’s the play where Mariota got hurt: #Commanders rookie RG Matt Gulbin gets manhandled here on the play that Marcus Mariota got injured on pic.twitter.com/hOEiNE3lcX — brandon (@JayDanielsMVP) October 5, 2026 As previously mentioned, it’s expected that top Commanders QB Jayden Daniels will start and play in a Week 5 contest against the Giants after suffering a left elbow dislocation in Week 2. Jayden Daniels was formally ruled out of Sunday’s game against the Indianapolis Colts, yet they felt good about their quarterback situation. That was due to veteran backup, Marcus Mariota, a proven commodity capable of winning games at this level. We saw proof of that last week, when he was darn near perfect in a Week 3 victory over the Seahawks. He validated that point over the first few drives, until he went down awkwardly during a quarterback sack. Here’s the play that Marcus Mariota got hurt on. He’s now headed to the locker room. pic.twitter.com/DszMaJu5mq — Jordan Schultz (@Schultz_Report) October 4, 2026 Mariota went into the blue medical tent and then into the locker room and did not return to the game. Rookie Athan Kaliakmanis entered the game and ended up playing out what became a 30-13 loss to the Colts. After the game, Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said that Mariota suffered an MCL injury, and would be evaluated, with additional imaging, once the team returned to the DMV. “I’m just gutted for him,” Quinn told on-site reporters in his postgame press conference . “…The team thinks it’s an MCL injury and he’ll have scans tomorrow (Monday) and we’ll have further knowledge with the length (of absence) and all those things.” Mariota missed a few weeks when he injured his MCL in the same knee during the preseason , so it’s probably fair to expect the veteran to miss some weeks (at least) in this case. Quinn said that Daniels expects to be a full participant in practice leading into a Week 5 contest against the New York Giants, creating the belief that he’ll be able to return for that contest. If Mariota will miss some weeks, as expected, the Commanders still have some depth issues at quarterback. Kaliakmanis was 15-for-33 passing for 186 yards , one touchdown and one interception despite taking few reps during the practice week. Does that influence whether the Commanders add another quarterback to the roster? Mariota’s prognosis will impact that, but it seems likely they’ll add someone should Mariota miss some time. The Commanders have Sam Hartman on the practice squad, and it will be interesting to see if they consider him a viable option. Should the Commanders sign another quarterback? title: Commanders vs. Colts (London) – Studs and Duds
summary: Washington took on Indianapolis over the pond and, although they hung tough early on, the injuries (playing their third string quarterback), inconsistent play calling, poor coaching and having to play not only against the Colts but also the refs, ultimately doomed the Commanders in the end and resulted in a 30-13 loss. full_text: Washington took on Indianapolis over the pond and, although they hung tough early on, the injuries (playing their third string quarterback), inconsistent play calling, poor coaching and having to play not only against the Colts but also the refs, ultimately doomed the Commanders in the end and resulted in a 30-13 loss. Washington is now 1-3 on the season with a division game against the Giants on the horizon. Dan Quinn’s seat continues to get even hotter and Adam Peters’ draft and free-agency strategy have fans questioning his qualifications. Although there is a great chance both quarterback Jayden Daniels and receiver Terry McLaurin return next week, it’s going to take a miracle for Washington to make the postseason at this rate. Below are my Studs and Duds of the game, followed by some notes. Studs: CB Amik Robertson: Mik led the team in tackles (nine total, seven solo) and had a beautiful pass defended on a deep shot down the left sideline, allowing just two passes completed in coverage. He continues to be the bright spot on this defense. Perfect coverage by Mik! pic.twitter.com/XUrA76pvha — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) October 4, 2026 Amik with great tackle short of the sticks on 3rd and 5! pic.twitter.com/p9CGbMr6Bv — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) October 4, 2026 DL Javon Kinlaw: Kinlaw has been playing some really good football, and that continued over the pond. He recorded three tackles (two of them stops), had two batted passes and two pressures. Kinlaw‘s second batted pass of the game pic.twitter.com/wzyvldbqbZ — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) October 4, 2026 Kinlaw with the batted pass pic.twitter.com/oTmc2FwiMI — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) October 4, 2026 CB Rasul Douglas: Douglas had a nice game against Indy’s wide receivers. He recorded an interception on an errant pass by Jones and had a big hit to prevent a first down on a third-and-short. He had six tackles and a pass defensed. Pressure comes – Jones with the errant pass, Douglas picks it off! pic.twitter.com/62Vz8yf3me — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) October 4, 2026 Douglas with a great tackle on 3rd and 2 pic.twitter.com/4akIoyHgdH — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) October 4, 2026 Duds: Alan Eck and his crew: This was easily the worst officiated game I have seen in quite some time, and I have seen some bad ones throughout the years. This crew, led by the Pennsylvania guy who grew up an Eagles fan , called a completely one-sided game that saw Washington get hit with 10 penalties for 84 yards and had a touchdown by Antonio Williams erased, while the Colts had just one penalty for five yards. But it wasn’t just what was called. It’s also what wasn’t called, including two pretty blatant pass interference calls against the Colts defensive backs. The “crew” needs to be investigated by the NFL. This is who the @NFL sent to ref the game in London. Alan Eck (Williamsport, PA native) grew up an Eagles fan and despised Washington. Penalties today by his crew: Washington: 10-84yds and one TD called back INDY: 1-5yds pic.twitter.com/wZsRYP7WBp — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) October 4, 2026 @NFLOfficiating really called offensive pass interference here. 9 penalties against Washington 1 against the Colts pic.twitter.com/ocDfop0Vjd — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) October 4, 2026 NFL field Judge – Anthony Fleming looking right at this infraction @NFLOfficiating https://t.co/7eY5Bxx0UZ pic.twitter.com/89FZPMZKBr — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) October 4, 2026 Just notice in this still shot at the goal line, the ball has not yet arrived. Let me repeat – THE BALL HAS NOT YET ARRIVED!!! pic.twitter.com/GuaxifPy1v — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) October 4, 2026 UNBELIEVABLE that this was not pass interference 😡 pic.twitter.com/qMeTDEEHBP — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) October 4, 2026 ABSOLUTELY TERRIBLE call by the refs here on Amik Robertson after a great 3nd and long stop by Washington😡😡😡 Ridiculous to call this BS!!! This is FOOTBALL! pic.twitter.com/dbukYjes0i — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) October 4, 2026 HC Dan Quinn/OC David Blough: The fourth-down run with none other than CRAIG REYNOLDS behind the weak spot on our offensive line was mind-blowingly STUPID! Also, why are we not using our tight ends in the passing game? I still like Blough and know he’s being hamstrung by who/what he’s being given, but as for Quinn, his time is running out. 4th and 1 – this had ZERO chance pic.twitter.com/z1zoxJ5dBj — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) October 4, 2026 G Matt Gulbin: It was a rough start for the rookie at right guard (and this speaks to just how bad Nick Allegretti has been playing), and although his play did improve some as the game went on, it wasn’t nearly enough to keep him off the Duds list. His lack of blocking is what got Mariota injured early on. This may be the first time he’s made my Duds list, but he definitely deserved it. full_text: The Daily Slop – 5 October 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles NFL.com Commanders QB Marcus Mariota suffers knee injury in loss to Colts Mariota suffered the knee injury on a third-down sack midway through the first quarter when Indy defensive end Laiatu Latu landed on the veteran QB’s right leg. Mariota went to the locker room and was replaced by Kaliakmanis, with Washington leading 6-0. This was Kaliakmanis’ first NFL regular-season game appearance. The 23-year-old is the first QB drafted out of Rutgers to attempt a pass in the NFL since the 2005 season (Mike McMahon). Kaliakmanis is also the first rookie QB from the 2026 draft to take a regular-season snap; he was the eighth QB taken at No. 223 overall. Commanders coach Dan Quinn said after the loss that Mariota is feared to have aggravated an MCL injury that sidelined him in 2022. The vet QB will undergo testing to confirm the nature of the injury. JP Finlay Making sense of the London mess The Commanders went to England for a weird week and came back 1-3 But as bad as the refs were, they did not lose Washington the game. Washington lost the game, and a major portion of that belongs to Quinn. The decision in the first half to go for it on 4th down from about midfield, with a third-string rookie QB in the game and a defense that was dominating, was curious. It was an aggressive call at a time when discretion might have been the move. To go for it not just with Kaliakmanis under center but with practice squad call-up Craig Reynolds at running back made even less sense. Quinn did his best to explain the decision, yet, it still lacks clarity. Dan Quinn on the 4th down attempt to Craig Reynolds – we have to be able to get that. It was less than a yard. We can’t overthink it. pic.twitter.com/TUhTAdIP0c — JP Finlay (@JPFinlayNBCS) October 4, 2026 The failed 4th down attempt completely swung the momentum of the contest. Quinn’s decision in that spot gave the Colts life. For Commanders fans the offensive line moves provide whiplash. After the team cut Tyler Biadasz last winter and tried to sign Tyler Linderbaum with no success, that’s when the Allegretti hype train began from AP and DQ. They love Nick. Nick is the smartest guy in the room. Nick can get the job done. Well, to the Commanders brass, don’t pee on our leg and say that it’s raining. And by the way, Gulbin was quite bad against the Colts and got his lunch money taken by DeForest Buckner . It’s quite possible Sam Cosmi returns next week and the Allegretti/Gulbin conversation dwindles but that doesn’t mean the process was correct. Benching Allegretti made no sense against the backdrop of months of praise, and makes even less sense after watching the Colts defensive line hurt Mariota, abuse Kaliakmanis and shut down the Commanders run game. So to add it all up: bad refs, bad injuries, bad 4th down decision, bad personnel decision, and a loss to a Colts team that doesn’t seem very good. The result? An 8-hour flight home and a 1-3 record. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Too Deep Zone 3rd-string QB renders all other injury conversations a little asymmetrical Sunday’s Week 4 action began in London, where the Colts faced a Commanders team without Jayden Daniels and Terry McLaurin, among many others. Marcus Mariota got hurt early in the first quarter, entrusting the Commanders offense to seventh-round Rutgers rookie Athan Kaliakmanis, previously best known for sometimes looking halfway decent while tossing RPOs in the first quarter against Ohio State. Kaliakmanis, the Piscataway Popgun, spent the first half being treated like a blueberry scone by Laiatu Latu and other Colts defenders. In the third quarter, however, he completed bombs to Treylon Burks and Dyami Brown – with Sauce Gardner in coverage on both plays – to throw a scare into the listless-since-2016 Colts. The Colts were also banged up, most notably at wide receiver, where Alec Pierce, Keenan Allen and Darius Slayton were unavailable on Sunday. But a third-string quarterback renders all other injury conversations a little asymmetrical. Also, a team that’s relying on Keenan Allen and Darius Slayton to play significant roles in 2026 is just asking for trouble. Fortunately for the Colts, Jonathan Taylor can carry their offense against weaker opponents, Laquan Treadwell is having the best season of his decade-long career, and it’s only a matter of time before Marquez Valdes-Scantling, Dante Pettis, Denzel Mims and Jalen Reagor all find their way to Indianapolis. The Colts prevailed in a 30-13 victory against Kaliakmanis’ Upside-Down Golden Gophers (the Commanders rookie also played for the University of Minnesota) to achieve their preferred flavor of unsweetened tapioca .500 blandness. Mariota may be out a while, but Daniels will return next week To read more of this article, CLICK HERE A quick reader poll ESPN NFL Week 4: Big takeaways, questions and fantasy spin from Sunday’s games Can the Commanders recover from all these injuries? As the saying goes, it’s getting late early for the Commanders. They were already playing minus their top four offensive players — tackle Laremy Tunsil, receiver Terry McLaurin, quarterback Jayden Daniels and guard Sam Cosmi — and then they lost backup QB Marcus Mariota. The good news for them? They’re hopeful Daniels can return in Week 5, but they need McLaurin ( hamstring ) and Cosmi (concussion) and their returns remain uncertain. And the worst part for Washington: After facing the Giants next Sunday, they play at San Francisco and then host the Eagles and Rams. Injuries plus that schedule equals trouble. What to make of the QB performance: Athan Kaliakmanis, who was filling in for Mariota, has a big arm and plays with poise, but he’s also inexperienced and playing behind a patchwork line. Bad combo. He completed 15 of 33 passes for 186 yards, with a touchdown and an interception. With Mariota injuring the same knee that sidelined him multiple weeks in training camp, the Commanders need to consider signing a veteran to back up Jayden Daniels. However, the line needs to provide more help or it won’t matter. — John Keim To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Bullock’s Film Room (subscription) Commanders Film Room: Run Game Struggles vs Colts The Washington Commanders fell to perhaps their most disappointing defeat of the season so far. In London, the Commanders faced off against a very beatable Colts team and they started off well but things quickly fell apart as Marcus Mariota was injured on the second drive and seventh round rookie quarterback Athan Kaliakmanis, the Commanders third string quarterback, was forced into the game. Kaliakmanis performed admirably in his first NFL action, but the team struggled to support him. The obvious thing to do with a young and inexperienced quarterback in the game is to run the ball and take the pressure off him. title: Commanders report card: Team grades in NFL Week 4 loss vs. Colts
summary: Well, that didn’t go according to script.   The Commanders worked with a rookie quarterback in Athan Kaliakmanis for most of Sunday’s game, so it’s no shock that Washington suffered a 30-13 loss to the Indianapolis Colts at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London.   That doesn’t describe everything that happened on Sunday, and this report card is […]
full_text: Well, that didn’t go according to script. The Commanders worked with a rookie quarterback in Athan Kaliakmanis for most of Sunday’s game, so it’s no shock that Washington suffered a 30-13 loss to the Indianapolis Colts at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London. That doesn’t describe everything that happened on Sunday, and this report card is an opportunity to discuss different facets of the game and how Washington fared on a granular level. Let’s go into that here, after things went sideways from an injury perspective and after the Colts were able to wear the Commanders down and send Washington to a disappointing 1-3 start to the season. Rushing offense The Commanders started this game without Rachaad White (shoulder) exposing Bill Croskey-Merritt and his influence on this season as a feature back. What we saw was not encouraging. He finished with 15 yards on nine carries (1.7 ypc). I mean, yikes. We know the line factors into the equations here, but Austin Ekeler averaged 7.3 yards per carry on four rushes. Overall, the run game wasn’t good. But Croskey-Merritt’s sophomore slump is on. Sure seems like he’s going to start losing carries, especially when White returns. Grade: D Passing offense We aren’t grading on a curve here, but we’re adjusting grades based on quarterback expectations. With that in mind, Athan Kaliakmanis did just fine considering the circumstances. He completed roughly half his passes and seemed comfortable tossing it deep, almost over the natural flow of the offense. That’s a complete difference from how David Blough’s likes to run, and the pass operation wasn’t great at times. The Commanders clearly missed Terry McLaurin in this situation, and Stefon Diggs wasn’t ideal on this day as a marked man, with nine targets and just five catches. Also, Chig Okonkwo was virtually invisible. To this early point, he’s not the dominant force the Commanders paid for. Grade: C-plus Rushing defense The Commanders entered Week 4 as one of the NFL’s top run defenses, and for good reason. They held Jonathan Taylor to just 4.0 yards per carry in the first half , which is a relative win. The overall totals look worse, with him totaling 95 yards and two touchdowns on 20 carries. The defense just looked worn down at the end of this one, when it got out of hand. The injury to Charles Omenihu should not be discounted in this effort. Overall, defense should be graded independent of what happens offensively. We still see this is a good run defense. The game just got into a situation where the Colts could run a ton and the yardage totals got out of hand. Grade: C Passing defense The Commanders are starting to sort the secondary out and realize that Mike Sainristil is unplayable. Colts quarterback Daniels Jones was just 19-for-34 for 143 yards , no touchdowns and an interception. Cornerback Amik Robertson continues to show that he’s the best bargain in football, with nine tackles and a pass defenses. Rasul Douglas had a pick and the linebacker corps looked just fine while watching the game live. Daron Payne had a spur in his saddle, too. Grade: B Special teams The injury to Jaylin Lane (ankle) is going to be a big one, even if it only influences the special teams. Drew Stevens seems to be fine. Tress Way dropped three of five punts inside the 20, which has become (somehow) ho-hum. Grade: B Coaching We’re sure a vote of confidence in Dan Quinn and the coordinators he hired won’t be welcome after a loss that puts the Commanders at 1-3 and where Washington gave up 30-plus points for the third time in four weeks, but it’s clear that the culture and the schemes remain strong. The talent and the execution is not great. We generally deal in As or Fs here based upon the result, but coaching kept this team afloat and should continue to do so without Daniels and an unreal number of injured players. UPDATE: After watching the film and listening to what was said about crucial decisions in this game, I have changed my mind. The coaching was not good in any way, despite the injuries. Those critical of my ‘B’ grade were accurate. I can own that. New coaching grade: F Grade: B How would you grade the Commanders performance on Sunday? Give us your letter grades for the Commanders performance in the article comments below.

title: How Athan Kaliakmanis fared in Washington Commanders loss to Colts
summary: The Commanders drafted Athan Kaliakmanis with the expectation that he wouldn’t play a meaningful snap this season. There wasn’t even a guarantee the seventh-round selection would even make the 53-man roster, a position he earned with a solid preseason despite competition from the well-liked Sam Hartman.   The Rutgers product was and should’ve been viewed […]
full_text: The Commanders drafted Athan Kaliakmanis with the expectation that he wouldn’t play a meaningful snap this season. There wasn’t even a guarantee the seventh-round selection would even make the 53-man roster, a position he earned with a solid preseason despite competition from the well-liked Sam Hartman. The Rutgers product was and should’ve been viewed as a developmental prospect in 2026 and beyond, with his career seemingly mapped out to be a trusted backup throughout his rookie contract. Yet there he was despite all that, charged with guiding the Commanders for most of Sunday’s Week 4 contest against the Indianapolis Colts. That’s what happens when a quarterback situation goes pear-shaped. Jayden Daniels was unavailable with a left elbow dislocation suffered in Week 2. Then veteran backup Marcus Mariota went down with an MCL injury during the game’s second series. That put the Commanders in a bind, turning to Kaliakmanis in a time of need. He was good at times and showed his lack of experience (and practice reps) at others, producing an uneven performance with highlights and an inability to keep Washington afloat versus the Colts. We saw moments of brilliance and an inability to sustain drives. This throw to Treylon Burks was a thing of beauty. ATHAN'S FIRST TOUCHDOWN PASS 🎯 📺 #INDvsWAS @nflnetwork pic.twitter.com/RR2QfNZVdi — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) October 4, 2026 Then we saw some operational issues, which is commonplace when you’ve got a new quarterback. That led to an offensive slowdown and an inability to score efficiently enough to compete. The Commanders were in Kaliakmanis’ corner, with him getting advice from Daniels and injured receiver Terry McLaurin and more. He was ultimately able to complete just 15-of-33 passes for 186 yards , a touchdown and an interception. Kaliakmanis was far from perfect, but was serviceable considering the situation. “I feel like Athan came in and showed a lot of confidence and some fearlessness with that,” Quinn told on-site reporters in a postgame press conference. “He made some of the throws to highlight where he is where he is. As far as the full team, I don’t think we did enough around him in that spot.” Quinn was right to say that Kaliakmanis showed no fear, attacking a difficult situation with vigor. The rookie balanced the combination of excitement at his opportunity and disappointment at the outcome in his postgame press conference with on-site reporters. “I was preparing for this all week,” Kaliakmanis said. “…I have to be honest; I’m just thinking about the loss. It’s not about me. It’s about this team. There were some very blessed moments today for me but, at the end of the day, I’m a winner and today we did not win. It stings. It definitely stings.”

title: Dan Quinn: The goal is to have Jayden Daniels start vs the Giants
summary: The Washington Commanders jumped out to a 6-0 lead over the Indianapolis Colts, taking advantage of some early turnovers. The game quickly turned when QB Marcus Mariota left the game with a knee injury. Dan Quinn told Molly McGrath during the broadcast that the team believes Mariota re-injured the MCL he had injured during the […]
full_text: The Washington Commanders jumped out to a 6-0 lead over the Indianapolis Colts, taking advantage of some early turnovers. The game quickly turned when QB Marcus Mariota left the game with a knee injury. Dan Quinn told Molly McGrath during the broadcast that the team believes Mariota re-injured the MCL he had injured during the preseason, and they didn’t have a timetable for his return. Quinn said he’ gutted for Mariota after the work he put in to replace the injured Jayden Daniels. The team also lost WR Jaylin Lane to a serious ankle injury that caused him to be carted off the field. Quinn said OLB Charles Omenihu suffered a groin injury that will need imaging. Terry McLaurin was pushing to play this week, but the team decided to hold him out to recover from the hamstring injury. Quinn gave an update on Jayden Daniels, saying the QB will be a full participant in practice this week, and the goal will be to have him start when they host the Giants. Daniels traveled with the team and was a limited participant in practice all week. He has a new, bulkier brace on his left elbow, and he spent the week getting used to the brace he will be wearing the rest of the season. Mariota will likely miss some time with the knee injury, and Daniels return comes as Washington falls to 1-3 on the season. The team’s decision to start Matt Gulbin got a lot of scrutiny during the game as he had a few Welcome to the NFL moments, and Mariota’s injury. Quinn said that Nick Allegretti was banged up at the end of the Seahawks game, and he would have been limited if he played today. Quinn was also criticized for the decision to go for it on 4th and 2 at Washington’s own 46-yard line. title: Key takeaways from Washington Commanders loss to Indianapolis Colts
summary: BOX SCORE The Commanders had to deal with some adversity trying to reach an even record during Sunday morning’s game against the Indianapolis Colts.   Jayden Daniels practiced some this week and then wasn’t able to go, as expected after a dislocated left elbow suffered in Week 2. Washington felt super comfortable with Marcus Mariota […]
full_text: BOX SCORE The Commanders had to deal with some adversity trying to reach an even record during Sunday morning’s game against the Indianapolis Colts. Jayden Daniels practiced some this week and then wasn’t able to go, as expected after a dislocated left elbow suffered in Week 2. Washington felt super comfortable with Marcus Mariota calling offensive signals and could hold a similar game plan with mobile quarterbacks capable of making all the pre-snaps checks required of David Blough’s offense. Then the Commanders had to handle another quarterback blow. Like, playing a seventh-round pick in Athan Kaliakmanis in a real-life NFL game. So, yeah, Washington had to deal with some adversity. They eventually succumbed to it. It was easy to imagine a path to victory for the Commanders had the quarterback situation been normal, but it most certainly was not. That led to a 30-13 loss to the Colts on Sunday at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London. Here are some key takeaways from Washington’s contest with the Colts after watching it live: Commanders refuse to quit We learned a ton about the Commanders’ character in this game, where so much went wrong from an injury perspective. We’ve talked a ton about the quarterback situation and will discuss it a lot more lower in this story, but Sunday’s game remained competitive (for a while) due to some big plays on both sides of the ball. The coaching staff (somehow) kept this group together and involved in a game where things could’ve fallen apart. The Commanders were down two scores when Kaliakmanis found Treylon Burks deep for a touchdown. ATHAN'S FIRST TOUCHDOWN PASS 🎯 📺 #INDvsWAS @nflnetwork pic.twitter.com/RR2QfNZVdi — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) October 4, 2026 The Commanders also looked confused at times offensively. That’ll happen with a quarterback who didn’t see many reps with Daniels working towards a return while Mariota was planning to start. Kaliakmanis is a gunslinger type of guy, who connected with Dyami Brown on the play you’ll see below, but the operation wasn’t clean and the run game was stilted by the Colts’ emphasis on stopping it. can we introduced you to the Baklava Bomber 💣 📺 #INDvsWAS @nflnetwork pic.twitter.com/TIQjaWsIQX — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) October 4, 2026 While Kaliakmanis was successful on the explosives he wasn’t great in a consistent operation of the offense, which ultimately cost the Commanders down the stretch. That led to a deficit that couldn’t be overcome, as the Colts expanded their lead and eventually put the Commanders in a bind from which they couldn’t recover, considering all the injuries incurred in this game and before. Quarterback adversity reaching insane heights Jayden Daniels was ruled out of this game on Friday due to a dislocated left elbow. Marcus Mariota looked like himself early in Sunday morning’s game, validating the decision to play it safe/smart to start the veteran backup. Then the unthinkable happened. Mariota left Sunday’s game with a knee injury, leaving this game to seventh-round rookie Athan Kaliakmanis. Here’s the play where Mariota got hurt: Here’s the play that Marcus Mariota got hurt on. He’s now headed to the locker room. pic.twitter.com/DszMaJu5mq — Jordan Schultz (@Schultz_Report) October 4, 2026 Mariota did not return. That was obviously not part of the game plan. The Commanders were humming with Mariota, even with just a pair of field goals as the end results. Adding Kaliakmanis slowed some things down, as you’d expect. Then it all got worse in the second half, as the offense stalled at crucial times. This isn’t on the offensive line or the run game here. The Colts were able to make life hard on the rookie quarterback. Even with Kaliakmanis showing some spark, you’d think a veteran needs to come in. Most reports assume that Daniels will be able to return for a Week 5 contest against the New York Giants. Whether that Daniels return happens is ultimately uncertain, but Washington will probably be in the quarterback market this week while trying to establish a better cadence of passers. Kaliakmanis had some good moments, but the Mariota injury provides some pause and reports suggest he could miss some time. #Commanders QB Marcus Mariota aggravated his MCL injury and now will have tests, per @MollyAMcGrath . Expect him to miss some time. That said, there is hope that QB Jayden Daniels (elbow) is back next week. — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) October 4, 2026 The Commanders can’t deal with what they handled on Sunday from a quarterback depth perspective, so it’s probably prudent to add another passer to the group. Daronte Jones’ system taking shape The Commanders defense started super hot. Need proof? Here are the results of the first five series: fumble recovered, punt, punt, punt, interception. The only reason why the sixth series ended in a touchdown was a bogus unnecessary roughness call on Amik Robertson. Coordinator Daronte Jones had an excellent game plan dialed up that built on the excellent run defense established over the first few weeks. We saw much of the creative pressures and exotic look everyone should expect, but Colts quarterback Daniel Jones started to adjust. While the quarterback situation didn’t directly impact what was done on defense, there was an influence. The lead-expanding touchdown scored by Taylor in the third quarter came off a Kaliakmanis interception deep in Washington territory. There’s only so much a defense can do without breakage, and it eventually gave way and lost an early lead and was eventually part of a double-digit, second-half deficit. Taylor was explosive at times, especially late, and the defense was far from perfect, but you can see this system taking shape. That said, there are things to fix after a third game allowing 30-plus points. That’s a problem, man. No matter the result, you can see Jones’ scheme coming to life and being an effective path to sustainably quality defense. Washington’s defense had zero margin for error with the third-string quarterback playing and still allowed points in the 30s, but you can see what Jones is trying to do. And it’s encouraging. Commanders injuries becoming cruel joke The NFL Network broadcast showed a graphic of all the Commanders players out with injury, and it was most of those listed on our offseason top 10 ranking. Laremy Tunsil. Jayden Daniels. Nick Cross. Sam Cosmi. Terry McLaurin. Trey Amos. And that doesn’t even count important depth pieces like Jaylin Lane or Leo Chenal or Charles Omenihu or Rachaad White or Tyler Owens. And that’s not even an exhaustive list. The Commanders have been dealt some serious blows on the injury front. That’s not an excuse. It never is, but it’s a valid point of important context for why the Commanders find themselves in a difficult spot.

title: How active NFL players continue to redefine all-time sack list
summary: Myles Garrett's torrid pace up the all-time sack list paces active players making their moves among the greats.
full_text:
Last season, defensive end Myles Garrett won his second Defensive Player of the Year award after setting the NFL's single-season record with 23 sacks with the Cleveland Browns . 
 
 This season, he'll continue his climb up the NFL's all-time sack list as a member of the Los Angeles Rams  after a blockbuster trade  in June -- making the Rams favorites to win the Super Bowl, according to DraftKings Sportsbook, heading into the season. 
 
 Garrett entered the season with 125.5 career sacks, which was tied for 20th in NFL history and third among the other six active players --  Von Miller  (No. 9), Cameron Jordan  (No. 17), Calais Campbell  (No. 25), T.J. Watt  (No. 26), Danielle Hunter  (tied for No. 27) and Khalil Mack  (T-29th) -- in the top 30.  
 
 Joining the top 30 soon could be  Aaron Donald ,  who unretired  to join Garrett on the Rams' defensive line. Donald's 111 sacks currently sits two behind 30th.  
 
 As for Garrett, he entered his 10th season in the NFL averaging approximately 14 sacks per season. If he were to replicate that production, he would tie Pro Football Hall of Famer Jason Taylor, who currently sits at No. 7. If Garrett were to have another historic season, he would surpass Michael Strahan (No. 6) and approach career top-five territory. 
 
 
 
 Miller, who signed with the  Dallas Cowboys  in August, can also pass Strahan in his 15th season -- as he sits only three sacks behind him.   
 
 But Garrett's 125.5 career sacks heading into the season was 10.5 more than any other player since his rookie season in 2017, according to ESPN Research. The pass rusher recorded at least 14 sacks in each of the past five seasons, the longest such streak by any player since 1982. 
 
 If Garrett has 18.5 or more sacks this season, he will hold the record for the most over a two-season span since 1982, according to ESPN Research, and his current ascension up the career list ranks as the second-fastest pace among the top five all time behind only Reggie White's.  
 
As we look at how the sack list is redefined this season, we'll highlight milestones across the NFL landscape 
 We will update this file as the active players move up, and we'll add nuggets and milestones throughout the season. 
 

 

 Week 4 update 

 Watt kicked off things in Week 4 on "Thursday Night Football" in an impactful way. He had one sack, one forced fumble and a fumble recovery to move his total to 4.5 sacks on the season. Other than that, there wasn't much activity with Garrett continuing to be on IR. 

 Week 3 update 

 There wasn't much movement on the list this week with only Mack (1) and Hunter (.5) recording sacks. Watt, Campbell, Hunter and Mack (in that order) now make up 25 to 28 on the all-time list. Along with Campbell, the three top active leaders -- Miller, Jordan and Garrett -- have yet to record a sack this season.  

 Week 2 update 

 The second week of the season saw little movement near the top of the career list, but Watt's hot start continues, with the defensive end recording 1.5 sacks to now put him at 3.5 through two weeks (No. 2 in the NFL this season) and break a tie with Campbell to move to 25th. 

 Hunter (27th) and Mack (29th) also recorded one sack apiece over the weekend to break ties and move up one spot on the list. 

 Donald (33rd) made his  season debut on "Monday Night Football" against the Giants after taking two years off. He finished with three tackles, one for a loss, but did not record a sack. 

 

 

 Week 1 update 

 Of all the active sack leaders, Watt was the only one to record a sack, finishing the game with two to move to a tie with Campbell for 25th. 

 And while Donald was held out of the Rams' Week 1 game, Garrett will be out for at least the next four after failing to record a tackle in Australia and landing on injured reserve after having to have arthroscopic surgery on his knee.

 After the Rams' opening loss, Garrett said this was " the worst version of myself that I've put out there."

full_text:
The 2027 NFL draft is still months away, but with the 2026 season underway, we're starting to track pick order in Round 1. Which teams are in position to add elite prospects in the top 10 next April? What about the top five ... or even at No. 1?

 What follows is not the current draft order based on records. It is a projection of what ESPN's Football Power Index thinks the order ultimately will be by the end of the season. Each week during the season, the FPI projects the draft order by simulating the remainder of the season 10,000 times. Game probabilities are based primarily on the model's team ratings and game locations. The draft order is determined by the records the model projects for each team after 17 games, as well as each team's average draft position across the simulations.

 So where do things stand? Here are the full sortable projections, complete with each team's chances to pick in the top five, in the top 10 and at No. 1.

title: NFL Week 4: Big takeaways, questions and fantasy spin from Sunday's games
summary: Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering the biggest questions coming out of each Sunday game. Here's what we learned from Week 4.
full_text:
The Sunday slate for Week 4 of the 2026 NFL season  kicked off in London between the Colts and Commanders. After a slow start, the Colts recovered to secure a victory abroad.

 Back in the United States, the road team won six of eight matchups during the early window. That included a bounce-back performance by Patriots QB Drake Maye  in a win over the Bills. The Cowboys won a shootout in Houston, and the Rams pulled off an improbable comeback against the Eagles.

 In the late window Sunday, the 49ers, Chiefs and Vikings all maintained their perfect records. Minnesota defeated the Dolphins despite having kicker Will Reichard  score all of the team's points. And the Seahawks bounced back from last week's loss with a close win over the Chargers. The Panthers capped off the night by beating the Lions in a high-scoring affair.

 Our NFL Nation reporters reacted to all the action, answering lingering questions coming out of each game and detailing everything else you need to know for teams that played Sunday. Fantasy football analysts Matt Bowen and Tristan Cockcroft also have fantasy takeaways from each matchup.

 Let's get to it with the biggest lessons from Sunday's games.

 
 Jump to: 
 DET-CAR | LAC-SEA 
  KC-LV | DEN-SF |  MIA-MIN 
 NE-BUF  |  LAR-PHI |  JAX-CIN 
 DAL-HOU  |  ARI-NYG |  TEN-BAL 
 GB-TB  |  NYJ-CHI |  IND-WSH 

 Catch up on Thursday's game: 
 PIT-CLE 

 
 

 

 Carolina 32, Detroit 26 
 Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap 

 

 Panthers 
 Can Bryce Young be a QB who can carry a team to the playoffs? Young completed his first 11 passes against Detroit, and his established chemistry with wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan was apparent throughout the game. With Jalen Coker (quad) sidelined and Xavier Legette (knee) on injured reserve, Young sparked the passing game to win a back-and-forth aerial showcase against Lions quarterback Jared Goff . Young made excellent decisions throughout the night, leading six scoring drives and completing 70.7% of his passes (29-of-41) for 329 yards and two touchdowns. Young's nine passing touchdowns are a team record for the most through a season's first four games.

 Key stat to know: McMillan feasted against Detroit's faulty pass defense, catching 14 passes for 192 receiving yards and two touchdowns. He was one catch and 9 receiving yards shy of tying franchise records in both categories. McMillan is only the third Panthers player to record 150 or more receiving yards and two touchdowns in a game, according to ESPN Research. Steve Smith Sr. did it three times, and Patrick Jeffers did it twice.

 Best quote from the locker room:  Young on MVP chant: "I heard it. In the moment you just focus on executing and trying to move the team. Obviously a huge blessing - the support. And I mean the Bank [Bank of America Stadium] tonight was electric. They caused some false starts. They made it hard on them. And when the Bank's rocking like that we take a lot of pride in that. I'm super, super grateful for the fans."  -- Mike Kaye 

 Next game: at Eagles (Oct. 18, 1 p.m. ET)

 
 

 

 Lions 
 How aggressive should the Lions be at the trade deadline to bolster their leaky secondary? Extremely. The secondary needs help immediately, as it took another hit when CB Rock Ya-Sin was ruled out during the second half with a hamstring injury. But even before that, Detroit's defense struggled and has now allowed 127 total points through the first four games. The Lions had no answers for McMillan, who torched them with 14 receptions for 192 yards and two touchdowns. Last week, coach Dan Campbell confirmed that Detroit was engaged in trade talks for CB Joey Porter Jr . Porter ended up in Dallas, but the Lions were "very much on" the pursuit of him for secondary help. Sunday's loss is the most recent example of why they need immediate help in the defensive backfield.

 Key stat to know: Lions WR Jameson Williams logged his first 50-yard game of the season. After a slow first three games, Williams was unlocked Sunday, as he produced his best game of 2026 with six catches for 102 yards, including a 49-yard reception from Goff that set up a game-tying field goal at the end of the second quarter. -- Eric Woodyard 

 Next game: at Cardinals (Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET)

 
 

 Fantasy football takeaway: With Jalen Coker out, Tetairoa McMillan saw heavy volume in a very friendly matchup against the Lions' defense. McMillan produced a career-best 45.2 points, catching 14 of 16 targets for 192 yards and two touchdowns. Big-time numbers. The Panthers head into the bye before returning in Week 6 to play the Eagles. If Coker is back in the mix, managers can play McMillan as a high-end WR2. -- Bowen 

 

 

 Seattle 30, L.A. Chargers 23 
 Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap 

 

 Seahawks 
 Can Seattle's backfield continue to withstand Jadarian Price 's absence? So far, so good thanks to Emanuel Wilson . A day after the Seahawks put their top pick on IR, Wilson contributed 120 rushing yards and two touchdowns on 24 touches. He averaged 3.9 yards per carry against a top-10 Chargers run defense. Receiver Rashid Shaheed added a 28-yard rushing touchdown on a toss play, which showed one way Seattle can replace Price's explosiveness. He will miss at least three more games, but Zach Charbonnet is now eligible to come off PUP from his ACL injury. He returned to practice Thursday, but it's unclear if he's ready to play.

 Most surprising performance: The defense took a while to slam the door on Los Angeles. That didn't happen until Uchenna Nwosu 's strip sack in the final minute. The Seahawks led by as many as 21 points in the second half and had the Chargers on the ropes -- in dropback mode in a loud stadium without their No. 1 receiver and three of their starting offensive linemen. Thanks largely to Seattle penalties, Los Angeles made it a one-score game with three straight scoring drives.

 Best quote from the locker room:  The Seahawks committed 14 penalties for 150 yards. That includes seven 15-yard penalties, four of which came on the Chargers' two second-half touchdown drives. Said coach Mike Macdonald: "To have seven personal foul penalties is unacceptable on any level, however you slice it. That's not us and that's not going to be how we play football around here."  -- Brady Henderson 

 Next game: vs. 49ers (Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET)

 

 

 

 Chargers 
 Were Justin Herbert 's late-game heroics an encouraging sign? Herbert started this game terribly, throwing an awful interception on his first play and another one just as bad later in the first half. He ended the first half with just 36 passing yards, the fewest in his career, according to ESPN Research. Despite playing behind an offensive line of almost all backups in the second half, Herbert looked like the elite player he typically has been. He completed 13 of 16 pass attempts for 144 yards and a touchdown before being strip-sacked on the Chargers' final drive.

 Trend to watch:  Running back  Omarion Hampton 's role is decreasing. Hampton was the lead back in Weeks 1 and 2, but his carries have diminished in the past two weeks. He had just nine carries Sunday, second to Keaton Mitchell . Two weeks ago, Hampton had a career-high 23 carries but lost a game-deciding fumble. The difference in carries could be a result of that error. -- Kris Rhim 

 Next game: vs. Broncos (Sunday, 4:05 p.m. ET)

 
 

 Fantasy football takeaway: A second-round fantasy pick, Chargers RB Omarion Hampton's stock has slipped to the flex-play tier for upcoming matchups against the Broncos and Chiefs. One week after being outscored by Keaton Mitchell, Hampton played fewer snaps (32% share) and had fewer rushing attempts (nine) than Mitchell (38%, 10).  -- Cockcroft 

 

 

 Kansas City 30, Las Vegas 27

 Chiefs
